Apart from ranked battles, today I also got something pretty interesting from the Frontier wheel. I landed on the rare Pit Challenge reward and fought my very first Pit Challenge battle. I decided to choose the easy difficulty mode and honestly the battle went smoothly. I used the Water Archon lineup combined with multiple magic attackers and managed to defeat the boss without much trouble while also collecting a decent bunch of Sparks along the way.

 --- 


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mango-juice/23wWni5BtsxwoVoc4fYACasuXawwBR2QEx6sQrYZ57WK3VPnqUMq1HeuF31BXKjRHPMRA.png)

![Screenshot 2026-06-03 at 12.03.43 AM.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mango-juice/EoniZFh4L4svGpiDizQyK6Nj16nZ96Q2n994XpLo5Vuy1uSWFuixCRpUTUfo4E3FX5N.png)

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mango-juice/EogKrdEAA4wiJes5ZR2QejxDCuJVNHarKoNDpJgf2y6arc4TNwDqfPnxu3zHqqvJSHU.png)

 --- 



On the other hand, if we take a look at the weekly Frontier raffle, I currently hold 18 entries and there are still around 5 days and 17 hours left before the raffle draw takes place. This time once again I will try to grind toward around 54 to 57 entries before the timer runs out. Apart from that, today I also opened a whopping total of 9 Foundation packs that I had earned from the last 3 days of daily rewards. The pulls honestly turned out amazing because I managed to get 3 Epic cards, 2 Gold Foil Rare cards, 7 Rare cards including 2 Archons, and the rest Common cards.

 --- 



![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mango-juice/AJhUpdEss1rgWwQheKE2NM8wxf4etd6w18YXSXbgPiydhkcdU5HWZEfNdqNxtu8.png)


 --- 



### Snippet

Now moving forward, let us come to the main topic of this post, as today I will be discussing another interesting monster from the newest Escalation mini card set. As you have already seen in the title and thumbnail above, today I will be talking about Snippet. So if you are interested in learning more about this monster card, let us take a deeper dive without any further delay.

Snippet is a monster-type card that was introduced in the game with the newest Escalation mini card set. This monster belongs to the Life element and comes from the Mundane Beast bloodline. By rarity, this card is an Epic monster, so you will require a total of 46 CC cards in order to upgrade it to its maximum level. One of the biggest highlights of this monster is definitely its tiny mana cost of only 3, which makes it extremely flexible for almost every type of battle, especially low mana limit matches and Little League rulesets. The attack type of this monster is Melee, and despite its small mana cost, it still carries decent stats along with several unique support abilities. At its maximum level, this monster gains a total of three abilities that make it both offensive and supportive at the same time. Let us now take a closer look at its league-wise stats and abilities below to find out more.

 --- 


![Screenshot 2026-06-03 at 12.42.57 AM.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mango-juice/EoyM3BSMTnr5nXYij1Xbxq2rGYar78N88nnqfeBwpCM6RqKSzGUfkpEgKKJhPR28hXX.png)


 --- 



#### BRONZE

At level 2, this monster already possesses decent stats that consist of 2 melee attack power at 2 speed with 1 armor and 3 health. Apart from these stats, it also gains one of the most popular melee abilities in the game, Sneak. This ability is extremely useful because it allows the monster to directly attack enemy backline units and weaker support monsters hiding at the rear.


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mango-juice/23vsBsTEboeXNNgPiXWTpwNuCFhj7CdS7apERBwQvTBMLBphXovRzwoQAVSbEEJ1g2VTx.png)


`SNEAK` – Targets the enemy unit in the last position.


#### SILVER

When you upgrade this monster further to level 3, its stats remain the same, but it unlocks another interesting ability called Bloodline Tribute. This ability becomes very useful if you intentionally build a lineup using multiple monsters from the same bloodline.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mango-juice/AK6VVYjBFRPWApFLovjpuLTk8xaLPqwCGMXfr9b58ZfLrgEaUuy5o8CeKyJ5iSN.png)



`BLOODLINE TRIBUTE` – When defeated, all allied units of the same bloodline gain +1 health, speed, and armor, along with +1 power to each shared bloodline.



#### GOLD

As this monster gets upgraded further and reaches level 5, its stats improve and it now carries 3 melee attack power at 3 speed with 1 armor and 4 health. Even though it does not gain any additional abilities at this level, the improved attack and speed make it significantly more dangerous during battles.

#### DIAMOND / CHAMPION

Finally, when you upgrade this monster to its maximum level of 6, its stats remain the same as the previous level, but it unlocks another useful ability called Kindred Spirit: Relentless Strike. This ability can become extremely deadly when combined with proper Kindred monsters because Relentless Strike helps attacks deal true damage even against heavily protected enemies.


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mango-juice/AKLoFXLgq6xjqnCxrhYfr7ysL5DGNspdwvLZBW2oWLNmoBiSTxcBNaR5THWePEH.png)


`KINDRED SPIRIT: RELENTLESS STRIKE` – At the start of battle, an adjacent unit with Kindred gains Relentless Strike.



Last but not least, I think the biggest strength of this monster is definitely its tiny mana cost. For only 3 mana, you get a monster with decent stats, Sneak attacks, and several useful support abilities. This makes it extremely usable in almost every type of battle, especially low mana matches and Little League rulesets. Personally, Sneak remains one of my favorite abilities in the game because it directly targets enemy backline monsters unless interrupted by Taunt or frontline targeting effects. This makes Snippet very effective at hunting weak support monsters hiding behind enemy tanks. Another very interesting ability is Bloodline Tribute. If you intentionally build your lineup around the same bloodline, this monster can provide huge stat boosts to allied units once it gets defeated, which can completely shift the momentum of battle. Finally comes the Kindred Spirit: Relentless Strike ability. If you use proper Kindred monsters adjacent to this card, they gain Relentless Strike and become much stronger against heavily protected enemies. The only difficult part is deciding which monsters you want to sacrifice space for in order to fully utilize these Kindred combinations. Overall, I think Snippet is a very cool and flexible low mana sneaky monster that combines decent attack power with several strategic support abilities. What do you think?

#### I hope you enjoyed reading my post about SNIPPET. Let me know your thoughts about today's post in the comments section below, and I look forward to seeing you all in my next post.

body.title: Can Your Profession Last For Another Decade?
body.body:
>The world is on a steady evolution, each day a better and improved version of things is springing up. The trend of today has little to no value in the face of tomorrow, and honestly, this is good. Life has been made easy; things that were difficult to access before are now at our fingertips. The workload on humans is gradually shifting to machines. Gone are the days when people had to stress their bodies and risk their lives to get certain jobs done. Nowadays, there are machines that are well specialized in those fields. Jobs that take days to accomplish can now be done within a small time. I must commend the growth and advancement. However, with this advancement, there is a huge disadvantage: every day, people are losing their jobs. Since the coming of AI and other forms of technology, life has become very difficult for people. Many companies and organizations prefer to use machines rather than human resources to get their jobs done. Take, for instance, the popular one occurring recently, content creation that people do to get paid is now done by artificial intelligence. Since AI can easily create content, what do you think of content creation between now and the next few decades? Do you think human authentic content would still be valued? In several fields, gradually, certain things are being replaced, and the sad part of it is that as soon as the thing is replaced by a machine, the humans in that space automatically lose their jobs. For my field of teaching, I am very confident that even in the next two decades, the service of a teacher will still be required in society. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmW6kAfZKA21LSHjtunhHedZxiGuXcWQFmq7ZFnznjASoo/1780429789377.jpg) Going back in history, teaching has been in place for many years; it transcends from generation to generation, although there are many upgrades, but still, an instructor is always required to make learning take place. But this is not a yardstick for me to pitch my tent in one place. No matter how essential our fields are to society, we must never relent on one thing. The world is crazy; we never can tell what can happen between now and the next moment. It's better that we stay prepared and avoid being carried away unexpectedly. body.title: Business and Entrepreneurship: What Makes Entrepreneurs Successful and Customers Stick Around
body.body:
Business and Entrepreneurship: What Makes Entrepreneurs Successful and Customers Stick Around

Entrepreneurship has always fascinated me really. It is not just about starting a business,  it is about turning ideas into something real, solving problems, and creating value for people. But if you look closely at successful entrepreneurs, there are some common traits that make them stand out.

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmQGVS3DPrKP8JMkfyYa6QpzyRvK2pDda7dPD1Qfet5WRk/1000223514.jpg 

[Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/office-notes-notepad-entrepreneur-620817/)

I think the first thing an entrepreneur must have is passion and vision, this two are non-negotiable. When you truly care about what you are doing, it shows in the result. Passion keeps you going when things get tough and trust me, they always do. And vision, it will give you a direction, a goal to work toward, even when the path isn’t clear. Without these, it is easy to get lost or give up at the first sign of trouble.

Another big one is adaptability. Every entrepreneur knows that that Markets change, technology evolves, and customer preferences shift. And any entrepreneurs who cling to a single idea or way of doing things often struggle. But those who are willing to learn, pivot, and try new approaches are the ones who survive and grow. And if this is  Pair with resilience, and you have a recipe for long-term success. Mistakes and setbacks aren’t failures, they are lessons if they are handle the right way.

And also leadership and communication skills is very important for an entrepreneur. Even if you have a great idea, you can’t do everything alone. A successful entrepreneur knows how to motivate a team, communicate clearly, and create an environment where people feel valued and inspired. Leadership isn’t about bossing people around, it is about helping everyone move toward a common goal.

When it comes to attracting and keeping customers, I think it all boils down to value and relationships. People stick around when they feel they are getting something worthwhile and when they feel understood. Businesses need to know their customers and not just demographics, but their needs, frustrations, and dreams. Personalized service, listening carefully, and genuinely caring about customer satisfaction go a long way.

Innovation also plays a key role. Standing out in a crowded market means offering something unique, whether it is a product, a service, or just an experience that makes people feel it specialty. And as a business grows, it is easy to lose sight of the customer. The brands that keep paying attention, adapting, and delivering value are the ones that maintain loyalty over time.

 Entrepreneurship is a mix of heart, grit, and smart strategy. It’s about pursuing your vision, learning along the way, and building something that people truly care about. And if you focus on these qualities while keeping your customers happy, the business won’t just survive, it will thrive.





**Thanks for checking on my blog and have a wonderful day**

After the battle, a yellow bird guided me to a peaceful haiku spot. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUw2TTbUjUuhGLhvrfhU7CzgQgjjUrvBm28Gqv5VWstYM/screenshot_1_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWdxBTc6grS92caUUBuyQa8UibyK2JdDud5c4afVw5BDt/screenshot_2_.png) I was just about to head toward the cemetery to begin the next mission, but Ryuzo stopped me to ask how Jin had managed to survive the initial Mongol invasion. After Jin shared his story, he turned the question back to Ryuzo to ask how he and his men had escaped the slaughter, to which Ryuzo simply replied that they ran. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbTksp4gbKXsoj8aXvV8916v8nBKDgwkVk1VctM8K3DAu/screenshot_3_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZtAGBMvqt5NJSBvdRgfLk3HNnKQG1i2B4tsqQBPcT5AA/screenshot_4_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmanxgpQjokDvtuftrWELBn8eDMJYhapepWNxPysJdm8Yu/screenshot_5_.png) I began riding my horse toward the cemetery to meet Ryuzo for the new objective, but I suddenly encountered a Mongol patrol blocking my path. I took one of them down immediately in a formal standoff and then began running backward to lure the rest of the group. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZHjy4gLX3j2QUEUtrzSqNvKDw9XF4654wYwsuecyUic5/screenshot_6_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUkCLBdEM7AGX7WzgBPv5mXNTxeRUUa5jvPeX8hFpjmLk/screenshot_7_.png) I eventually stopped once I reached the straw hat camp, as it was my specific intention to draw those Mongols directly into the heart of the camp so the Ronin could get some combat practice against actual people. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNwJB3eb2HGkPbt262JbPK1KCPDVgihhpps4E1aJDcSPC/screenshot_8_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNQVAiv6mCCE2xL6Wk68vQbNCVCt746uJnqZkVYTcVfNQ/screenshot_9_.png) Upon reaching the camp, the Mongols appeared strangely hesitant and scared, refusing to launch an attack even though I was standing well within their reach. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVeoHzpiNWV8Ry7NgDLo6o5SS9furLYmcGAMyEHWpiG2h/screenshot_10_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmer2FK3j6qqSmhJ3WihFoiXzFhobeeZWMQ3FvFnMkzrve/screenshot_11_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbsZhVrcHtUGhAmNZjZPvQc3ERWsCt5mrDhVUYWdgwq4a/screenshot_12_.png) To my surprise, the Ronin also failed to engage, leaving the Mongols to simply try and escape the area. I moved ahead and managed to cut one of them down while the rest of the group scrambled away. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUPe4s3sBLwCN3MmebhAypYmEyZaErjTnzpXCzSbn3hdg/screenshot_13_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUnxokZ2kAUcmiZ8eScuGQegQV8PqxqadMEidFEMKFzRx/screenshot_14_.png) I chased the fleeing survivors, and after a short distance, the Mongols finally stopped their retreat and turned back to attack me, forcing me to draw my blade and fight back. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdHBQbKTn49QnPAn5hJTk9zXZ9ex5SBqNcGzemYxhC9W4/screenshot_15_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdiRRNrCcDyJ9szWngMNpYNaF2kkx9cPCdrBXeAeM1CGX/screenshot_16_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYnKNdFMynPTe53BCou5WZfXXfCeiSAoKFtRwXFgWLT6q/screenshot_17_.png) I began taking the enemies down one by one until only a single heavy soldier remained on the field. Utilizing my mastery skills, I dismantled his defense and took him down as well to finish the battle. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTQVKzTV1Bm8Aa5WLrBiKkgD9oZGjcKSJ1nLGxSmRv9ZB/screenshot_18_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmR7AJEzk4oWhwKziqiiL6DpZ98BRMimB8igzHBPavNGjc/screenshot_19_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSXB1GwiFJqEPyHigU4FRy1QwQWeZyZ1tM8Z4BFUAJFvg/screenshot_20_.png) Suddenly, I noticed a bright yellow bird fluttering nearby, seemingly trying to lead me somewhere important. I decided to follow the bird's flight path, hoping it would lead me to a hidden side quest or a point of interest. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSHcitt5Va9U5YMrVZpPiKHyf2Wq41YqjuTBV4AZqKuss/screenshot_21_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNMDd9u2ss22TvWCPHN45YXPDRc85hkJQCUGB5rPpwTEy/screenshot_22_.png) The bird eventually led me to the Tsutsu Haiku spot, a quiet place where I could sit and compose haiku. As I looked around to reflect, I chose to focus on the theme of death, visualizing a tree growing from a broken past toward its inevitable end, which rewarded me with the headband of death. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSYEZEjM3mJP9ESMCYZ5L1sMsvdXCcJ3LUpfV8ohee5bQ/screenshot_23_.png) After completing the haiku, I took a moment to look out over the fishing village situated right by the ocean, where a beautiful sunset provided the perfect backdrop to pass some quiet time before moving on. --- If you like the post, feel free to like, comment & share. Welcome back, Chinito. I'm very pleased to see another comment from you. In this post, I'm talking about Heisenberg's uncertainty principle. An intuitive example comes to mind right now. Imagine you want to photograph a fly in a dark room.
To see it, you have to shine a flashlight on it. But the light hits it and makes it move.
The stronger the light used to see exactly where it is, the more you alter its motion.
Heisenberg explained to us that something similar happens with electrons, but not because of limitations of the instruments: it's a fundamental property of nature.
!hiqvote

body.title: Iran – kraj, o którym świat przypomina sobie dopiero podczas wojny
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYYN6E1krP9df5haLJbLZS9sQ9aN87F1BsmkKQRAcTo3E/1780429364133.jpg)


Kiedy w mediach pojawia się temat Iranu, najczęściej słyszymy o rakietach, napięciach na Bliskim Wschodzie albo kolejnych konfliktach. Mało kto jednak zastanawia się, czym naprawdę jest ten kraj i dlaczego od tylu lat pozostaje jednym z najważniejszych punktów zapalnych świata.

Iran to nie jest małe państwo gdzieś na pustyni. To ogromny kraj z wielką historią, liczący prawie 90 milionów mieszkańców. Dawna Persja była jedną z najpotężniejszych cywilizacji świata jeszcze wtedy, gdy wiele dzisiejszych państw nawet nie istniało.

Dzisiejszy Iran znajduje się jednak w bardzo trudnym położeniu. Z jednej strony posiada ogromne zasoby ropy i gazu, a z drugiej od lat jest objęty sankcjami gospodarczymi i znajduje się pod presją Zachodu. Konflikt z USA i Izraelem trwa praktycznie od dekad i co jakiś czas wybucha z nową siłą.

Najciekawsze jest jednak to, że wojny XXI wieku coraz rzadziej wyglądają jak klasyczne starcia armii. Dzisiaj równie ważna jak rakiety jest informacja, propaganda, cyberataki i wpływ na gospodarkę. Iran bardzo mocno rozwija swoje technologie wojskowe, szczególnie drony, które stały się symbolem nowoczesnych konfliktów.

Wiele osób zastanawia się, czy świat stoi przed większą wojną na Bliskim Wschodzie. Problem polega na tym, że każdy większy konflikt w tym regionie wpływa praktycznie na cały świat — ceny paliw, inflację, giełdy czy nawet zwykłe życie przeciętnych ludzi w Europie.

Internet sprawił też, że wojny oglądamy dziś niemal na żywo. Jeszcze kilkanaście lat temu informacje docierały po wielu godzinach lub dniach. Dzisiaj nagrania z dronów, rakiet czy alarmów pojawiają się w sieci po kilku minutach. Czasami trudno już nawet odróżnić prawdziwe informacje od propagandy.

Niezależnie od polityki jedno jest pewne — zwykli ludzie zawsze płacą najwyższą cenę za konflikty wielkich państw. Historia pokazuje, że wojna bardzo rzadko kończy się tak, jak planują to politycy.

Świat zrobił się bardzo niestabilny i mam wrażenie, że żyjemy w czasach, gdzie napięcia globalne są największe od wielu lat. Pozostaje mieć nadzieję, że kolejne konflikty nie wymkną się spod kontroli.

body.title: Traveling Back to the 1960's for Some Psychedelic Rock on this Three Tune Tuesday
body.body:
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmUJq6iaSTbLTHaWMTHUoF65APVgcpYZJKWSnjLrgKEhG1/image.png


Recently in the mail I got a very nice surprise from my good friend @bulliontools . Sometime back he put together a raffle with some silver items as the prizes to the winners. The tickets could be bought with Hive, and so I went ahead and purchased some tickets for the chance to win. Lo and behold,  I came out the lucky winner of one of the prizes. One of the offered prizes was a Morgan silver dollar, so I jumped at the chance.  I don't have my old coin photography setup assembled anymore so I just snapped a couple shots with the old cell phone! They aren't great but they could be worse...

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmVTn88pQYPbRN4h2989DTJh9kyeGSkr8QDaikBNwKYC7X/Screenshot%205156.png 

Pretty isn't it? And I won it here on Hive! Thank you @bulliontools for the great raffle!

Moving on to the main purpose of today's post, since it's Tuesday and you already saw the header (and title) you know what's coming. So without further ado let's get started! But first off, I want to say thank you to @ablaze for starting and continuing to sponsor this fun weekly event where you can share three songs that you enjoy. One lucky participant will win some HSBI units, you can't have too many of those! So if you don't already participate feel free to jump in, just use the tag #ttt or #threetunetuesday and it's never a bad idea to do a shoutout to @ablaze .







 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmay1VYGkPJEY33bsAi1nuUzULQm6S8t8TyP1hRRzVVmaX/image.png 


## **Cream**

Cream was short lived band from 1966 to 1968, formed in London. The three man project included Eric Clapton, Jack Bruce, and Ginger Baker, and is often considered the first supergroup in rock history. They featured psychedelic rock mixed with hard rock and blues producing some of the most memorable songs of the late 1960's in their short run. The band was inducted into the Rock Hall of Fame in 1993. An interesting fact for the curious, Eric Clapton is the only person to have ever been inducted into the Rock Hall of Fame three times, once as a solo artist, once as a member of Cream, and once as a member of The Yardbirds.

This song came off their third album Disraeli Gears and is called: \

https://youtu.be/Bwmf58-GkG0?si=abj65_k-qsJrZRr4






 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmay1VYGkPJEY33bsAi1nuUzULQm6S8t8TyP1hRRzVVmaX/image.png 

## **The Doors**

One of my favorite bands from the 1960's has always been The Doors. They formed in Los Angeles, California in 1965 with the iconic front man Jim Morrison.  In 1967 they released their self titled debut album that launched them into fame. Over the next several years until 1971 they produced a total of six albums with Morrison that are considered some of the best in rock history. However, the good times came to an end when Morrison suddenly passed away in Paris, France on July 3, 1971.  No cause of death was ever determined and no autopsy ever done, although a drug overdose has been suspected. 

The band did try to carry on with a couple albums without Morrison but failed to do well, so they disbanded in 1973. But this song came off their debut and is called \

:



https://youtu.be/gdnzBNMfZfo?si=YEuQujlHyl-hb-kA

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmay1VYGkPJEY33bsAi1nuUzULQm6S8t8TyP1hRRzVVmaX/image.png 


## **Iron Butterfly**

This band from San Diego, California formed in 1966. They had their years of biggest fame in the late sixties  and had a blend of psychedelic, acid, and hard rock. Their biggest hit by far was one that led toward the development of hard rock and heavy metal, which may not have happened  quite the same without it. This song is of course  \

, a true classic. This is the single version for radio and television, versus the full version which ran some eighteen minutes in length!


https://youtu.be/d5ghW7OxiLs?si=dgzIqt5JRRBo1ZaN


 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmay1VYGkPJEY33bsAi1nuUzULQm6S8t8TyP1hRRzVVmaX/image.png 




That will wrap up this Three Tune Tuesday, I do hope you enjoyed it! Sometimes it's fun to do some music from way before my time, just like today. There was some great rock n' roll music from the 50's and 60's that often goes goes underappreciated. Please feel free to leave any comments or questions below, and as always thank you for all of your support. It's great appreciated! Have a great day everyone!

body.title: Obra de Toma. Memoria Descriptiva. Fin del Proyecto Hidráulico. Octavo día de trabajo/  Intake Works. Descriptive Memory. End of the Hydraulic Project. Eighth day of work.
body.body:
Buenas tardes, Hive.
​Aquí les comparto la memoria descriptiva final del proyecto, específicamente la parte hidráulica. Afortunadamente, ya se tienen los valores en cuantía de los otros especialistas (tanto del estructural, el mecánico y el eléctrico), por lo que pudimos incluir en la memoria el costo total de la obra.

​La memoria descriptiva, es la parte explicativa del proyecto. En ella se plasman los objetivos, la situación actual, la composición de la obra, los cálculos hidráulicos, el proceso constructivo, el impacto ambiental, el costo de la inversión y las normas técnicas utilizadas.
​Todo debe estar muy, muy claro, porque es un documento auditable; es decir, cualquier auditor interno o externo revisará la memoria en busca de alguna falla o mala concepción de la obra por parte del proyectista. Por tal motivo, las empresas siempre someten sus proyectos a sistemas de gestión de la calidad para corregir cualquier error en el proceso de realización del proyecto.

​En la memoria, se explican con claridad los procedimientos y normativas con los que se realizaron los cálculos, así como los software empleados. Se le detalla al constructor cómo debe proceder durante la construcción, los impactos ambientales que genera esta obra y cómo mitigar esos efectos. También se plasma el resumen de la inversión, o sea, el costo total desglosado por renglones (en una de las imágenes lo pueden apreciar). Esta obra costará más de 9 millones de pesos en CUP (el peso cubano). Exactamente $9 970 983.62.

​En el primer post de este tema, mencionamos el reto de hacer el trabajo en no más de 20 días, por exigencias de la inversión. Hoy es el octavo día y ya se concluyó la parte hidráulica. Para el estructural, el eléctrico y el mecánico quedan alrededor de una semana de trabajo según el pronóstico, así que en total serían 14 o 15 días, por lo que se cumplirá a tiempo con las exigencias del inversionista.

​Hasta aquí, la exposición de este trabajo. Próximamente comenzaremos con un nuevo proyecto; en este caso, se trata de una conductora. Los detalles aún no están listos, pero será algo interesante.

​Hasta la próxima. GRACIAS a los que prestaron su atención, comentando o apoyando de otra forma.

--------------------------------------------------

​Good afternoon, Hive.

​Here I share with you the final descriptive memory of the project, specifically the hydraulic part. Fortunately, we already have the cost estimates from the other specialists (structural, mechanical, and electrical), so we were able to include the total cost of the work in the report.

​The descriptive memory is the explanatory part of the project. It outlines the objectives, current situation, composition of the works, hydraulic calculations, construction process, environmental impact, investment cost, and the technical standards used.

​Everything must be very, very clear because it is an auditable document; meaning, any internal or external auditor will review the report looking for any flaws or misconceptions in the design by the planner. For this reason, companies always submit their projects to quality management systems to correct any errors during the project development process.

​The report clearly explains the procedures and regulations used to perform the calculations, as well as the software used. It details how the builder should proceed during construction, the environmental impacts generated by this work, and how to mitigate those effects. It also includes the investment summary—the total cost broken down by line items—which you can see in one of the images. This project will cost more than 9 million pesos in CUP (Cuban Peso). Exactly $9,970,983.62.

​In the first post on this topic, we mentioned the challenge of completing the work in no more than 20 days due to investment demands. Today is the eighth day, and the hydraulic part is already finished. According to the forecast, the structural, electrical, and mechanical parts have about a week of work left, so it will take around 14 or 15 days in total, meaning we will meet the investor's requirements right on time.

​That’s all for the presentation of this project. Soon we will start a new one; in this case, it's a water pipeline. The details are not ready yet, but it will be something interesting.

​Until next time. Thanks to everyone who paid attention, commented, or supported in any other way.

body.body:
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmNxCYqJy7giMj9h8mW5bZTUhduwW5HN9YZBLVhfNeqDCR/IMG_9058.PNG 

Today was one of those days when I felt like dressing up a little, taking a mirror photo, and appreciating how far I've come.

For a long time, I thought confidence was something people were born with.  
Now I realize it's something we build little by little, through experiences, mistakes, and lessons.

There are still days when I doubt myself.  
There are still goals I haven't reached yet.

But every time I look back, I see a stronger version of the girl I used to be.

That's why I try to celebrate the small victories too.  
A good mood, a nice outfit, a positive mindset, or simply having the courage to keep moving forward.

Life doesn't have to be perfect to be beautiful. 💫

And today, I'm choosing to enjoy the journey.

body.title: Why Marketing will be critical to Holozing's Success
body.body:
![d802dff0-24bc-44f8-b521-54a522f6419a.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cocacolaron/23tviN3uM7vPC25mPhB4Hg6axVcBTTisLNBphyJv8dg3yfGgxtgR9EXbKikMaPoLVMwj7.png)


---

The success of a modern video game does not depend solely on its quality or technical specifications (which is a shame). In the entertainment industry, marketing is often the deciding factor between making it and failing to do so; let's talk a little about this, as it is indeed a fascinating subject.


In the case of Holozing a title that combines elements of collecting, exploration, and blockchain technology marketing efforts must focus both on attracting new users and on strengthening relationships with the existing community.

---


![93795a69-f9bb-484b-a856-c7eff76fafa7.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cocacolaron/23wqiLR8gF6LgKCKxa3f61sANBEbvzU96s6CBFtUd29EV7vy7Pzf9LBQzD1pacuUEobUW.png)


---

One of the fundamental pillars for promoting Holozing is the consistent creation of content on social media. Platforms such as X (my favorite), Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube allow the team to showcase development progress, creature designs, gameplay mechanics, and updates related to the ecosystem.


Short-form videos tend to achieve a wide reach—especially when they feature eye-catching animations, battle sequences, or visual elements that pique the curiosity of potential players. The key lies in maintaining a consistent presence and offering content that fosters engagement.

Another important strategy involves collaborating with content creators and influencers. Many players discover new projects thanks to streamers, YouTubers, or well-known figures within the video game and blockchain communities. It is not always necessary to collaborate with major celebrities within the industry. ---



![main.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cocacolaron/23uR5PsXRUVfrA6hEC1dv7XX5Tq9B5a7x7gzFTyKFx5sqzGEEsvRRp2ApvWSuY25JchzK.jpg)



---


In many cases, micro-influencers possess more engaged audiences and can generate better results at a much lower cost. A campaign in which several creators try out Holozing, share their impressions, and explain its features could significantly boost the project's visibility.

Communities are especially important for a game like Holozing. Therefore, it is essential to strengthen existing spaces for interaction and create new opportunities for user participation.

---



![imagen.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cocacolaron/23uQfkr5Gb4fNc7ZYJQ38EWS1CHJfyYtpSYXGGsmpfnxMNpTCkohxpNut5rh964QnoJ1u.png)



---


Discord servers, Telegram groups, and Reddit communities can become hubs of activity where players share ideas, strategies, and feedback. Furthermore, developers can organize Q&A sessions, contests, giveaways, and special events to maintain community interest.

Content marketing can also play a crucial role. Publishing articles about the game's development, interviews with the creators, stories related to the Holozing universe, and explanations of its mechanics helps build a compelling narrative around the project. ---

![imagen.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cocacolaron/23w2sW6ZB1kki7hkyH3foTAUNdUoUcqZtVUzJf1u1NjbYgEWKDKvDg2UVe17y7d442PJD.png)



---

This type of content not only improves search engine visibility but also provides valuable material for the community to share across various platforms.

Referral programs represent another intriguing tool for driving growth. Rewarding players who invite new users can organically accelerate the community's expansion. When people receive incentives for recommending a project they enjoy, the promotion becomes far more natural and effective than traditional advertising.

---

body.title: Shelter progress and a new life by the stream
body.body:
I realize I tend to write and post the hard stuff on my blog, the uncomfortable inner development I go through. It's actually the most useful stuff to write about for me as this leads me to organize my thoughts and keep focused on these abstractions. But many other things are happening in my life, and they are mostly positive. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZ2RFYRbtNFqaLdX3sbVQJfTTsKCAUPb5cAsm2cJk1Rx7/1780424370443.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXBesuveozMJxn15nbkuQAsyLzWyXq8JbcDTizajSxjfH/1780424370523.jpg)

I've been living the last months in this magical place that was presented by a friend where people come to camp and enjoy during the hot days. Since it's gotten colder, people are not coming so much, and I've been focused on building a shelter to hold out during the winter.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNxwVrp4XmLPVJD688NoAakVBFNef6mp5GfEenRSqzdNK/1780424370602.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmX1yvbocYYefTqQerEXeaEvJnLYkxsctvXo5XuUrxEj4T/1780424370657.jpg)

It was always a possibility to keep moving to a warmer area when the cold arrived but I've made plenty of friends here and there is a sense of community that I hadn't experienced in other places, mainly because I wasn't ready for it. Now, there's plenty of things going on and I'm learning new things all the time which keeps things exciting.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTuQjEH7g5b8139dU8c9RYZdjamg7sQjgVmsZvNsSD8w3/1780424370709.jpg)


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmW5SPUAQgJxaJ55YviQwFevFqffdryP6rAE1i4BGBZBLG/1780424398472.jpg)

Recently, a friend arrived and he's helping me to build the shelter as well as gardening at another friend's house, so most days are busy between the earthly tasks, music, and meditative practices.

Overall, enjoying the whole process, with few worries and celebrating each little step towards the new life that approaches each day.

![zig.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaHuB6qTWHaSpJHQ1S8FCCRmNQuUxTcPZdU4yKHsJ7vEP/zig-banner.png)

### What will I learn
- How Unix signals work as an asynchronous notification mechanism for processes;
- How to register signal handlers using POSIX sigaction via Zig's C interop;
- Why signal handlers must only call async-signal-safe functions;
- How the self-pipe trick converts asynchronous signals into synchronous I/O events;
- How to use signal masks to block and unblock signals during critical sections;
- How SIGCHLD notifies parent processes when children exit;
- How to implement graceful shutdown with SIGTERM and SIGINT;
- How to build a multi-worker server that shuts down cleanly on termination signals.

# Learn Zig Series (#67) - Signal Handling Deep Dive

## Solutions to Episode 66 Exercises

**Exercise 1: Multi-producer shared ring buffer**

```zig
const std = @import(\

, .{});

    _ = c.munmap(ptr, @sizeOf(Blackboard));
    _ = c.close(fd);
    _ = c.shm_unlink(shm_name);
}
```

The `.release` ordering on publish and `.acquire` on subscribe form a release-acquire pair. This is sufficient because we only need the subscriber to see the data that was written before the sequence number was bumped -- we don't need a total global ordering between unrelated channels. This is cheaper than `.seq_cst` on architectures like ARM where sequential consistency requires full memory barriers.

---

Last episode we covered shared memory and semaphores -- the fastest IPC mechanism for processes on the same machine. We could map physical pages into multiple address spaces and coordinate access through atomics and semaphores. But there was one thing we didn't really address: what happens when a process gets rudely interrupted from the outside?

That's what signals are. Every Unix program has been dealing with them since the day it first ran -- you've been sending SIGINT every time you press Ctrl+C. But actually **handling** signals correctly is one of the trickiest parts of systems programming. Signal handlers run asynchronously, at arbitrary points in your program's execution. They can interrupt system calls, corrupt data structures, and deadlock your program if you're not careful. Most programs get signal handling subtley wrong, and most of the time it doesn't matter because programs usually just die on signals anyway.

But when you're building long-running services -- the kind we've been building in this OS programming arc -- getting signal handling right is the difference between a server that shuts down gracefully (finishes in-flight requests, flushes buffers, closes connections) and one that just dies mid-write and corrupts your data.

Here we go!

## What signals actually are

A signal is a software interrupt delivered to a process by the kernel. When a signal arrives, the kernel suspends whatever the process was doing, runs the signal handler (if one is registered), and then resumes the original code. Think of it like a hardware interrupt but at the process level.

There are about 30 standard signals on Linux. The important ones for application developers:

- **SIGINT** (2) -- sent when you press Ctrl+C. Default action: terminate.
- **SIGTERM** (15) -- the polite \
signal. Default action: terminate. This is what `kill <pid>` sends by default.\n- **SIGKILL** (9) -- the forceful \

signal. Cannot be caught or ignored. The kernel terminates the process immediately.
- **SIGCHLD** (17) -- sent to a parent when a child process exits. Default action: ignore.
- **SIGPIPE** (13) -- sent when writing to a broken pipe. Default action: terminate.
- **SIGALRM** (14) -- sent when an alarm timer expires. Default action: terminate.
- **SIGUSR1** (10) and **SIGUSR2** (12) -- user-defined signals. No default meaning.
- **SIGSTOP** (19) and **SIGCONT** (18) -- stop and continue a process. SIGSTOP cannot be caught.

You cannot catch SIGKILL or SIGSTOP. Everything else is fair game ;-)

```zig
const std = @import(\

, .{});
}
```

The `linux.SIG.IGN` constant tells the kernel to silently discard the signal. The opposite is `linux.SIG.DFL` which restores the default action. Notice we're using `linux.sigaction` here -- Zig's standard library exposes the Linux sigaction syscall directly through `std.os.linux`, which is exactly what we need. No C interop required for this part.

## Registering signal handlers with sigaction

The old `signal()` function from C is broken in several ways (it resets the handler after each delivery, it doesn't let you control which signals are blocked during handling, and its behavior varies between Unix variants). The proper interface is **sigaction**, and Zig gives us direct access to it:

```zig
const std = @import(\

, .{signal_count});
}
```

A few important things happening here:

1. The handler function has `callconv(.c)` -- signal handlers must use the C calling convention because the kernel expects it.

2. The `SA.RESTART` flag tells the kernel to automatically restart interrupted system calls. Without this, a signal arriving during a `read()` or `write()` would cause it to fail with EINTR, and you'd have to retry manually. With `SA.RESTART`, the kernel handles the retry for you. Almost always what you want.

3. The `mask` field controls which signals are blocked while this handler runs. `empty_sigset` means no additional signals are blocked. We could fill this with other signal numbers to prevent nested signal delivery.

4. The global `signal_count` variable is modified from the handler. This is **technically a data race** -- the handler and main code both access it without synchronization. For a simple counter it mostly works, but this is NOT safe in general. We'll fix this with atomics shortly.

## The danger zone: async-signal-safe functions

Here's where signal handling gets truly tricky. When a signal arrives, your handler runs in the context of the interrupted code. If your main code was in the middle of `malloc()`, and your signal handler calls `malloc()`, you've got a deadlock -- `malloc` holds an internal lock, and the handler tries to acquire the same lock on the same thread.

The POSIX standard defines a list of **async-signal-safe** functions that are safe to call from signal handlers. The list is surprisingly short. What you CAN do in a signal handler:

- Set a global `volatile` flag (or use an atomic)
- Call `write()` (the raw syscall, NOT stdio `printf`)
- Call `_exit()`
- Call signal-related functions (`sigaction`, `kill`)

What you CANNOT do:

- Call `malloc()` or `free()` (Zig's allocators)
- Call `printf()` or any stdio buffered I/O (includes `std.debug.print`)
- Call `std.io.getStdOut().writer().print()` -- this uses buffered I/O
- Lock mutexes (unless you locked them in the main code AND the signal can't arrive while held)
- Pretty much anything that manages internal state

This is why most real signal handlers are tiny -- they just set a flag:

```zig
const std = @import(\
, .{iteration});\n    // flush buffers, close files, save state, etc.\n    try stdout.print(\

from the main code's perspective, so atomics are necessary for correctness.

## The self-pipe trick

The flag-checking approach works when your main loop is busy doing computation. But what if your main loop is **blocked** on I/O? If you're sitting in a `poll()` or `read()` call waiting for data, a flag set by a signal handler won't be checked until the I/O completes.

The **self-pipe trick** (invented by Daniel J. Bernstein in the 1990s) elegantly solves this. You create a pipe, and the signal handler writes a byte to it. Your main loop includes the pipe's read end in its `poll()` set. When a signal arrives, the write wakes up `poll()`, and you can check which signal was delivered:

```zig
const std = @import(\

process. The parent forks a child that does work (simulated with sleep). The parent sets a SIGALRM alarm for 2 seconds using the `alarm()` syscall (via `@cImport`). If the child finishes before the alarm fires, cancel the alarm and print success. If the alarm fires first (child is taking too long), the SIGALRM handler should kill the child with SIGTERM, wait for it, and print a timeout message. Test with both a \

child (sleeps 5 seconds).

2. Implement a signal-driven log rotator. Write a long-running process that writes numbered log lines to a file (`/tmp/zig_log_test.log`). When it receives SIGUSR1 (via self-pipe), it should: close the current log file, rename it to `zig_log_test.log.1` (moving the old `.1` to `.2` if it exists), open a fresh log file, and continue writing. Use `kill` from another terminal to send SIGUSR1 and verify the rotation works. The signal handler must NOT do the rotation itself -- it must only write to the self-pipe, and the main loop does the actual file operations.

3. Build a process pool with signal-based lifecycle management. The parent process starts 4 worker children. Each worker does simulated work in a loop (sleep 200ms per \
). The parent handles three signals: SIGUSR1 means \
(fork one more, up to a max of 8), SIGUSR2 means \
(send SIGTERM to the most recently spawned child), and SIGTERM means \

(send SIGTERM to each child, wait for all, then exit). Track all child PIDs in an array. Handle SIGCHLD to detect when workers exit unexpectedly and print a warning.

## Wat we geleerd hebben

- Signals are asynchronous notifications delivered by the kernel -- they interrupt whatever your process is doing and run a handler function
- The `sigaction` syscall (via `std.os.linux.sigaction`) is the proper way to register handlers -- the old `signal()` function is broken and non-portable
- Signal handlers must ONLY call async-signal-safe functions -- no allocators, no buffered I/O, no mutexes. Set an atomic flag or write to a pipe, and do the real work in the main loop.
- The self-pipe trick converts asynchronous signal delivery into synchronous I/O events -- write a byte in the handler, poll for it in your event loop. Used by nginx, libuv, asyncio, and every serious event-driven server.
- Signal masks (`sigprocmask`) block signal delivery during critical sections -- blocked signals are queued (one per signal number) and delivered when unblocked
- SIGCHLD notifies parents when children exit -- always use `waitpid` with WNOHANG in a loop because multiple children can exit between SIGCHLD deliveries
- Production servers ignore SIGPIPE (a disconnecting client should not kill your server), handle SIGTERM/SIGINT for graceful shutdown, and support escalation (second signal forces immediate exit)

Signals are one of the oldest Unix APIs and also one of the most misunderstood. The rules are strict (async-signal-safety) but the patterns are well established (self-pipe, atomic flags, graceful shutdown). Now that we've covered fork, pipes, shared memory, and signals, we have most of the foundational IPC and process management primitives. The next steps in this OS programming arc will take us into Unix domain sockets for local networking and the machinery that turns a regular process into a background daemon.

body.title: PANTAN TERONG PEAK // Exploring an old tourist Destination with stunning natural views
body.body:
## Good night to all my beloved hive friends ❤️ ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmW8px5tLvj7PTw97ZC25P6NFwe1ZRejHQf2VX6k4mEXAV/1780399632784.jpg) In this post, I would like to share an exciting experience and memorable moments from my trip to the top of Pantan Terong in Aceh Tengah. This is one of the oldest tourist destinations in the area,according to information I received from the staff there, this place was officially opened on August 17, 2002, which means it is now around 24 years old. Successfully reaching this destination brought me a great sense of happiness and satisfaction, because to get to the top,we had to pass through a very challenging route with extremely steep roads. The difficult road access became one of the reasons why this tourist destination was abandoned several times. In fact, I also visited this place back in 2023, and at that time it was already neglected,many buildings that were once beautiful and magnificent had become abandoned and damaged,and now, let us take a look at the changes that have taken place at this place. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbzbbTKDtXZaMYmeymzcskzCRrddXnPXKzkRneCvAumSz/1780399632860.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmT8ton49qMki4uS1NVdzYWmEX3Wkx4ee7M5w6imhHni5k/1780399632979.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYJCRpY8oFHDUeXZpdsuiZWZ46pPPiju6N5CyyhkdmDss/1780399633070.jpg) At the top of Pantan Terong, we can find many food stalls, cafes, and other natural tourist destinations. The change that I immediately noticed was that there were already many new kiosks and food stalls along the roadside,of course, that is quite a good thing, considering this tourist destination is already quite old and needs a lot of support. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWT9W7Jt4FUkioEj4So2RMpuAddngH8XGXXdHAsALqXeq/1780399633153.jpg) Many stalls and food vendors have been built along the roadside, and some of them are even located right on the edge of the cliff. There are so many people who decide to stop by these places to rest or enjoy a meal,what is even more amazing is that from this place, we can witness such breathtaking natural scenery. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTwRkGSkL9RZMieufqtEA1PnCNuMxyhr8dYNr3govTUwi/1780402005261.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRSwhEQwhtC45GMpNqVuukV41xCyarGio74P3Y5DS6xWL/1780402005357.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWFLnyHorQZehhm5SiscVd4GeLo7XGEQXhSX6ofX9vB5H/1780402005466.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWcs379FNRvbQVb5k8WVCR9VoriJTVBStSNZgNijQWAgC/1780402005572.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYWBfQLpxiQoRVdojw3KvmcgNg37UUTqxx5pJWZ3zDsLs/1780402005651.jpg) This tourist destination is located on highland terrain, so even a little rain can create thick fog. Therefore, to enjoy beautiful natural scenery like this, we must check the weather conditions first. Many people also call this place “the land above the clouds,” because from the top we can see a sea of clouds quite clearly,however that view can only be enjoyed in the morning, and that is a very difficult time for me to reach this place. The natural scenery here is still quite natural and well preserved,many areas are still filled with lush trees, and that is very good news. However, from this view we can also see that some parts of the mountains have experienced severe landslides, and that happened purely because of natural factors. At that time, I had quite a lot of time, so I also took the opportunity to stop by a food stall to rest,I felt very happy because I was able to enjoy a cup of coffee while being accompanied by the beautiful natural scenery right in front of my eyes. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZrzn55Doc7DUZ8mQ3LhqDF6S81NrLYQaGMbssz5EUpm4/1780402802863.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmevfjZ9PVZ1aoqVmynyXPVpPmwVzosoZkQ6btqY2U2QV9/1780402802986.jpg) Puncak Al Kahfi is one of the most popular tourist destinations at the top of Pantan Terong. In this area, a viewpoint has been provided where visitors can enjoy the natural scenery clearly and to the fullest. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRsoohJ9gKWUu7dXDdtV27N3LfcwvdJYGVzgiTKAk3XY8/1780402803103.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUzxaBi3oZMobPdLr6Kf9DRjBFuL4Y2dCw25Z68uXDw1V/1780402803183.jpg) There are many abandoned buildings in this area, such as this building that I have managed to capture, if I'm not mistaken it used to be a cafe building, the building still looks abandoned and there are no signs of renovation. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRVDmSwiCQ2gR3FhQEfDnvnsdngGV299UqBHRsb4q3UcN/1780402830754.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmU6HChpMWQRb9kQQfcajodH247PkayPTrXTDzjypWcaSt/1780402830825.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbij1XQaEnHkxi749HAmMQMz7LAMtdLJd2XYqXTNh6C5U/1780402830898.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdingAPWqzc7RXrLC1G2fkSAzmDsvz3jdCwt684SHnh4K/1780402830959.jpg) The Viewpoint area is also very spacious and has two floors, that is good news because this place can accommodate many visitors. However, it is very unfortunate that the weather at that time was very hot and in this area there were very few places to take shelter except for a few trees on the side of the road. At that time there were a lot of visitors who came to this place and that is normal considering that yesterday was the Eid al-Adha holiday. ----

Life is a responsibility Be yourself, keep learning and don't hesitate to start😉

If you like other travel posts, you can see them on [Worldmappin Community](https://v3.ecency.com/created/hive-163772) and you can also participate there. If you are curious about the places I have visited so far, you can see them on [my personal worldmappin map](https://worldmappin.com/@riyat) And you can also find me on [Ecency Discord](https://discord.com/invite/m9MyMSWx)

----

Thank you very much for reading my post till the end, I am here to say thank you very much 🙏

---- ----

All images are mine, I took the photos using the Infinix 10 pro cellphone and I edited the images using the Lightroom application. I'm @riyat. See you again in my next post ♥️

body.title: The BlockTunes A&R Program: Bring In Artists, They Mint Music, You Get Paid
body.body:
![arprogram.png](https://images.blocktunes.net/DQmQsLiv9Vi8YiSAuGyQZVpwXq5XGuPwztuXfyoVVPbyXfU/arprogram.png)



In the traditional music industry, A&R stands for Artists and Repertoire. It's the job of finding talent and bringing it to a label. The people who do it well are the ones who heard greatness before anyone else did, who spotted the artist in the small venue and sent them on the journey to their sold-out arena runs.

In the traditional industry model, A&R reps get paid by the label. They take a salary, maybe a bonus, and the artist they signed sometimes never sees them again.

BlockTunes has a different model. If you find an artist and bring them to the platform using your referral code, you earn a percentage of their streaming revenue automatically, on every qualifying play, forever. No label involved. No boss to ask for your cut. The protocol handles it.

---

## How It Works

Every BlockTunes user has a referral link:

```
https://app.blocktunes.net/listen?ref=yourusername
```

Share that link with an artist. When they visit it before they log in or sign up for the first time, your Hive username is stored as their A&R rep. That association is permanent and on-chain.

From the moment they mint their first track, **5% of every streaming payout from every track they ever mint comes directly to you** on every qualifying play. Automatically. No claiming. No check-in. It just arrives in your Hive wallet.

---

## The Math

An artist you referred mints a track and it gets 100 qualifying plays a day.

Each qualifying play sends **0.005 HIVE** directly to your wallet as the A&R rep.

100 plays a day: **0.5 HIVE per day.** Just from that one artist.

Now imagine you referred 5 artists, each with 100 plays a day: **2.5 HIVE per day.** From sharing a link.

That HIVE is real value you can take anywhere. Swap it for Bitcoin, cash out, power up your Hive account, it's not locked to the platform. It just lands in your wallet.

The rate is fixed. There is no halving schedule, no expiration, no fine print. What you earn per play today is what the protocol pays.

---

## Your A&R Dashboard

Log in and find the **A&R Dashboard** under your profile menu. It shows:

- Every artist you've referred
- Their total play count
- Your total earnings from each one
- A complete history of every individual payout

Every streaming reward transaction is broadcast on-chain with a memo that identifies exactly what track triggered the payout. Full transparency. No black box.

---

## What Happens If No One Referred the Artist?

If an artist signed up without going through anyone's referral link, the 5% A&R share routes back to the artist instead. They earn 55% of every streaming payout until someone legitimately earns that slot, which, once set, doesn't change.

---

## Who Should Be Doing This


![Join Us Help Me GIF by Pudgy Penguins](https://media1.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTkwMGEwNzc0ZDR1M3J3ejZjcWc5ZXhwYXBtd3ltZGV1Z25tcTd6Yzc0dHMzcmZrNSZlcD12MV9naWZzX3NlYXJjaCZjdD1n/rttviCZfFJGENqxKbx/giphy.gif)



**Music curators and influencers.** If people already follow your recommendations, you're already doing A&R work for free. Now there's a revenue stream attached to it.

**Community builders.** If you run a Discord, a Telegram, a music blog, or any community where artists hang out, your referral link belongs in your bio right now. Oh and we have a Discord server too that we are building some really cool things for... Just FYI...

**Artists referring other artists.** If you're already on BlockTunes and you know musicians who should be here, send them your link. You earn from their plays while they earn from their music. Everyone benefits.

**Anyone who believes in the platform.** You don't have to be a music industry insider. You just have to know people who make music and be willing to tell them about a place that pays them fairly.

---

## There's No Limit


![agencylife advertisement GIF by MX Player](https://media0.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTkwMGEwNzc0OGNiMHFxdm8yZ21nN2tid2w2eXdtaDZmZDE0aGtncnV4Y2U4c3YyYSZlcD12MV9naWZzX3NlYXJjaCZjdD1n/VJZOUrQSXfGOtYSudu/giphy.gif)


There's no cap on how many artists you can refer. There's no cap on how long your A&R relationship with an artist lasts. There's no way for the platform to reassign your slot once it's established. If you referred them, you earn from them, for as long as they're on BlockTunes.

---

## One-Click Sharing With Your Referral Link Built In

We just shipped a feature that makes this even easier. When you mint a track in the Studio, a **Share Your Release** button appears the moment the mint succeeds. It opens a share panel pre-filled with a ready-to-post message and your referral link already embedded in the URL. You can edit the copy, hit **Enhance** to have the AI punch it up, or post straight to X in one click.

Every Masters series page also has a Share button. So if you hold masters of a track you love, or you don't even have to own it, you can just love it and want to share, you can share it the same way, your referral link in the URL, your cut of streaming rewards on every new listener who signs up through it.

This was a direct feature request from community member @elementm, who asked the right question and pointed us toward something the platform needed. That's how this gets built,  people in the community telling us what would make it better, and us shipping it. This person even did it using Harmony and submitted a feature request the way we designed it to work! So it's a win win all the way around! It means we built something that works!



![Doc Brown GIF by Back to the Future Trilogy](https://media1.giphy.com/media/v1.Y2lkPTkwMGEwNzc0MmthMGJpcXdlOXZhc3lrMm5mMGQyNWlqNjkzOWdxNWtrczl5aDdrNyZlcD12MV9naWZzX3NlYXJjaCZjdD1n/i9kwklipMwIusrsaA4/giphy.gif)



---

## Get Your Referral Link

Log in and go to the **A&R Dashboard** under your profile menu, or find your referral link at [app.blocktunes.net/affiliate](https://app.blocktunes.net/affiliate). Put it everywhere you'd normally promote music. Every artist who clicks it before signing up becomes part of your A&R roster.

**[Launch the App](https://app.blocktunes.net/listen)**
**[Create Your Free Account](https://app.blocktunes.net/signup)**


Posted using [BlockTunes](https://app.blocktunes.net/@blocktunes/the-blocktunes-a-and-r-program-bring-in-artists-they-mint-music-you-get-paid)

body.title: To be a successful entrepreneur
body.body: There are a lot of factors to be considered for one to be a successful entrepreneur, and the interesting thing is, one does not have to input all the factors; it's just a matter of picking the most important ones as applicable to the kind of business, the target audience, the environment and a few others.\n\n

/>

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

Two years ago, I heard that the salon shop close to my workplace was moving out. And just before I knew it, the same business as mine packed into the place. I won't lie; I was scared because it meant a high level of competition. At that moment, I understood why some people use voodoo to run their businesses. Lol

_Their(the newly packed in) business started well, some of my clients moved to the new place, and I was shaken a little. But I remained calm because I still had a good number of my customers intact.  
The owner of the business wasn't stable, so he employed a staff, the staff worked for a few weeks and quit, another one was employed, he managed to work for a month and quit too. Another got employed, and this guy stayed consistent for a while. That was when the competition hit me so bad, but before I knew it, the guy stopped too, and the shop was being opened once a week and was moved to once every two weeks._

_The owner of the business usually comes around, but it gets difficult for him to attend work, and that's maybe he's not used to the kind of work. That was how the business collapsed within a year. The rent of the shop was a complete waste because they didn't make consistent use of the place. The guy packed out, and when I was looking for a shop to pack in, I saw it was vacant, and I rented the place._

**Now, look at it;**

One can open a small-scale business and employ someone to look after it, that's for sure, and that's what the guy did, but the business failed. And it was so bad that the owner didn't know or didn't have the strength for the technicality of the work.  
If he had known or made himself available for the business, it would have survived, but he decided to hire people, and maybe the pay he offered wasn't good, or maybe his T&C were too tough for the employees he hired. Just maybe.

Another point he failed to look into was the high level of competition. Come on, I was there already with the same business; he just opened the next block. I knew there was going to be a balance, but that would have taken time for him to catch up due to the fact that I had dominated the area already.

So you see, maybe he went on to consider other things, especially getting involved with aesthetics; he didn't consider the most basic and simplest.

Thanks for reading.

Photo used is mine

body.title: THE STANGER WHO SAVED ME BY WALKING AWAY__DAILY PROMPT 2ND JUNE
body.body: \n\nThree words that sound like betrayal. Like knife in the back. Like \

is the loudest form of love?

The man in the cafe was not my ally. 
He didn’t clap when I talked about my \
like everyone else. \nHe didn’t share my posts. He didn’t like my ideas. \nHe looked at my business plan and said: \

Not an ally. 

My friends called him bitter. My family called him hater. 
\

They asked. 
Because allies cheer. Allies say yes. Allies clap even when you’re running into fire.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbfBEKxpasU2ntov9XXr3Gw8kQB6TLiJZX2f6GT3gH6uB/1780427761808.jpg)



He was not an ally. He was a mirror.

When I failed 6 months later - debt, tears, empty shop - he was the only one who didn’t say \
. \nHe just slid a notebook across the table. Blank pages. \n\

he said. Then he left. 

Not an ally. He didn’t walk with me. 
But because he didn’t lie to me, I learned to walk alone. 
And walking alone taught me strength that fake allies never could.

Freewriters taught me this: Not every hand that refuses to hold you is an enemy. 
Some hands refuse because they know you must learn to hold yourself. 

So today I’m not cursing the \

. 
I’m thanking him. The stranger who saved me by walking away. 
The one who chose truth over comfort. Silence over fake support. 

    5-Minute Timer Question for Freewriters👇  
Who was \

in your life… but ended up saving you? 
Drop their story below. Let’s thank the people who didn’t clap, but taught us to stand.

body.title: Nvidia Send Intel , AMD and Qualcomm To Red
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQvsdtNV6NkBAa8Z2aETkWVYZfUMxcTXQbpFRHJkkxwq7/img_8035.jpg)
Yesterday, Jensen Huang, the CEO of Nvidia, took the stage at Computex in Taiwan and announced that Nvidia is officially entering the market for personal computer processors.

A market that, for decades, had been dominated by just two names: Intel and AMD. The market reacted immediately. Shares of both Intel and AMD fell into the red within hours.

WHAT EXACTLY DID NVIDIA ANNOUNCE?

Nvidia unveiled a new processor called the RTX Spark Superchip, also known as the N1X. It was developed in partnership with Microsoft and will launch this fall as part of a brand-new lineup of Windows PCs. It will appear in laptops from Dell, HP, ASUS, Lenovo, and MSI.

So what exactly is it? Put simply, it combines two of Nvidia’s most advanced technologies into a single package. On one side is a Blackwell graphics processor. On the other is an Arm-based CPU designed by Taiwan’s MediaTek. The entire system is paired with 128GB of unified memory and manufactured using TSMC’s 3-nanometer process technology, which is currently available only in Taiwan.

Huang described the development by saying: “This reinvention of the computer is as significant as the transformation of the phone into what we now know as the smartphone.” He also added that this is the first time in 40 years that a computer platform has been redesigned from the ground up.

And this is where things become even more interesting, because behind this announcement lies a battle of architectures that has been brewing for years.

For decades, PC processors were built around the x86 architecture, originally developed by Intel in the 1970s. Now, however, more and more companies are moving toward Arm architecture, which is significantly more power efficient. It is the same architecture that powered the first iPhone in 2007.

Why is Arm suddenly gaining so much momentum?

Because Arm offers a major advantage: it consumes far less power. That allows manufacturers to build laptops that are both extremely powerful and remarkably thin and lightweight. The first laptops using this chip will be only 14 millimeters thick.

It is also important to note that Nvidia is not entering this market from a position of weakness. It is entering as arguably the most powerful technology company in the world today. Thanks to the enormous profits generated by its data center business, Nvidia can invest more resources into this effort than virtually any competitor, whether that competitor is Intel or Qualcomm with its Snapdragon processors.

THE MARKET’S REACTION

How did investors respond? Quickly and aggressively.

Intel shares fell about 4.6%, at one point dropping nearly 6%.

AMD lost more than 1.1%, while Qualcomm, another company that could be affected by Nvidia’s move, dropped roughly 8.8%.

On the other side, there was strong enthusiasm. Arm shares surged around 15%. Nvidia moved higher. MediaTek gained more than 5%. PC manufacturers such as Dell, HP, and Lenovo also advanced.

So what does all of this mean?

It represents a classic story: established leaders facing a new challenger.

Just a few years ago, Intel was the undisputed king of the PC industry. The company that helped create the architecture that powered personal computing for decades. Today, Nvidia is knocking on its door and taking a share of its home market.

Technological leadership is never permanent. The company that dominates today can quickly find itself in second or even third place tomorrow.

There is also an interesting irony here. Nvidia is not only a competitor to Intel. It is also an investor and partner. Last September, Nvidia invested $5 billion in Intel as part of a broader collaboration to manufacture chips together.

That alone shows how interconnected and complex the technology industry has become.

body.title: Another Ankara Adventure: This Time it Was Sunny, Light, and Very Joyful
body.body:
I had another short but wonderful Ankara adventure. This time, I stayed in Ankara for two days. It wasn’t a long time, but it felt so good. Sometimes, even a short trip to a city can refresh your feelings. Ankara is that kind of city for me. It’s a place where I lived and worked for years, walked its streets, sat in its cafes, met my friends, and collected many memories. That’s why every time I go back, I feel like I’m visiting my old memories, not just a city.
I had also come to Ankara about twenty days ago. It was colder back then. It had that gray, cloudy, classic Ankara weather. But this time, a completely different Ankara welcomed me. The weather was beautiful, sunny, and the sky was bright blue. I can say I saw Ankara in my favorite way. There was no gray Ankara this time. Instead, it was an Ankara that cheered me up, made me want to walk, and brought back good memories.


![IMG_3242.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/Eou8JaEYgPYaifBNibQeC87sFvha1qvEkFBR6bU52HP3wkCtJ8482tS9XdaxepRPePd.jpeg)

Of course, I acted cautious again and brought my trench coat with me. A friend living in Ankara had told me, \

So I brought it just in case. But honestly, I regretted it a bit later. The weather was so hot that the trench coat just became a burden. On top of that, I was wearing a suit jacket. A jacket in one hand, a backpack getting heavier, and a trench coat in my other hand... It really started to get exhausting after a while. You feel the weight even more when it’s hot outside. But still, even these little tirements became a part of the journey.


![33103F44-923C-4E4B-8115-EBEEE890EA4B.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/23wMajggzc4x1WJVPnnS6BLqFnwg7KhHoeb6WWDeoZtEkyLBdCoZK38WYz9oMrnwN4kmQ.jpeg)

The main reason for my visit to Ankara was an exam. I came for the exam and started studying from my very first day. I sat in a cafe, opened my notes, solved questions, and reviewed. Sometimes you get distracted while studying at home, but studying in a different city, in a nice cafe with your tea or coffee, can be more motivating. That’s exactly what I experienced on this trip. I came for the exam, but I also tried to make this process enjoyable.


![IMG_3150.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EoK5nbSZwddAm1SoeiZPikyDNGkVmVv3X6MH6bbJiyRHHQgACD7TBNKPYDspkqbHXh9.jpeg)

![IMG_3153.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EppJpFQFwcmKLNF4BXZp5ex8PF3ifYoqmFy7jxZuqoV5XXLfoCTz6An8NYSnB4eEj2B.jpeg)

![D30C201A-3B9B-4CA1-9EE7-D58AB775EEE8.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/23xp8JYAVNCGV6soDMoBTyCKGaNHvxCvJsK3GAD1srwKzmcBE5FgST9opWTLNNPBnaLwS.jpeg)

I met up with the same friends again in Ankara. This did me a lot of good. Because some friendships are like that—even if time passes, you just pick up where you left off. That’s how we were. We met at a cafe, ate börek, drank tea, and talked a lot. We didn’t just talk about the past; we also talked about the future. We spoke about new business ideas, what we could do together, and possible startups. These kinds of conversations motivate me so much. Because when you talk to your friends about the things you think about on your own, they start to feel more realistic and exciting.
Later, I met another friend and her sister at a very nice cafe. The ambiance of the cafe was beautiful. It was one of those new-generation coffee shops that have become very common in Turkey in recent years. In these types of cafes, there is usually no table service; you go and get your order yourself. People are very used to this system now. I tried a different, cold watermelon drink there. I really loved it. My friend tried the lemon one. I loved mine so much that I want to drink it again on my next visit to Ankara. Sometimes, the things that remind you of a city aren't just big memories; sometimes a drink, the table you sat at, the color of the sky, or the conversation at that moment stays in your mind.

![IMG_3180.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EoGyTmdBqShGUnV8cBL3RjSNXMniUtYFM8wGB9C6BcNk5CY28J7HcKoH44NGdz1pMXa.jpeg)

![IMG_3181.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EoK7HLnmwHg8ooTtjpQBHkNbJFquWoXeLEASg4KZoZjtWBzcMTYYANoJAxdNAZHZ22K.jpeg)

![IMG_3182.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/Eos2jYaVzdFzkbam8rrXYyXNGJbtn46GTybEb6CpRvhdjiGGeGadU8GiNmSi6mpXov9.jpeg)


One of the things I liked most about Ankara this time was that the old places were still there. I lived and worked in Ankara about ten years ago. I stayed in this city for about five years. There were some cafes I used to go to very often back then. On this trip, I went back to one of them, and seeing that it was still there made me very happy. After a fast-changing city like Istanbul, this side of Ankara feels different. In Istanbul, everything can change even in a place you haven't visited for a few months. A place might close down, another opens up, or a street changes completely. But Ankara isn’t like that. Ankara is a more stable, calmer, and steady city.


![IMG_3202.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EogMsMi4EWNwC38YeTWDApehHc2wXQ6WpTEBrgUY8WCrQFmYJxwCwgLpnHEWgc33N4r.jpeg)

I felt the same way while walking around Tunalı. The places we used to go for lunch with my friends, the spots we sat at, and the streets we walked were still there. When I saw some of the places, I said to myself, \

I also realized something nice about myself on this trip. I think I am no longer resentful towards Ankara. I really felt this inside. I used to feel a bit bitter when I came to Ankara. Maybe there was some tiredness from the past, some disappointments, or the weight of certain periods. But this time was different. I was more peaceful. My mind was more at ease while walking the streets. I said, \

But still, I realized once again that Istanbul is much more beautiful for me. Istanbul's energy, dynamism, sea, streets, and crowds make me feel better. I love Ankara, but Istanbul has a different place in my heart.

![IMG_3266.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EoiVkqpBjuj7cfdNZAyMPy4aAY4jREAS1D8xh2CmM72RgSvFmyhQwt7ehnmVKqXxQKX.jpeg)

![IMG_3267.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EoK5uVatwRbH4RgyPzS7pho59iXzERzqAK9bu5VmGY9mYz6znV5oCoByu9uYGG5ZW6W.jpeg)

![IMG_3269.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EprRjBEqCwDQ4jsf92mQrVrMcwucYrRbbrtjnCZ1TLLipcqiqLSZ6HyWRT9ojAZcAeh.jpeg)

![IMG_3270.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EpvhxD9o9LFLWaZaJ89JjqeeFzn7bJYZaD1EDHnRLK1pNvqiTVYioNXWmRaJfSncV72.jpeg)

![IMG_3271.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EoiX8nLZGgt44v32bgVx8vQoQDjH2pGUnrax5aYxvA9yhPazFERrBhCMS7m3BobXRqP.jpeg)

Still, this visit showed me that I should come to Ankara more often. Because I still have friends here whom I love to see. There are still streets that take me back to the old days. There are still cafes where I feel good sitting down. There are still places where my memories are hidden. Sometimes, instead of turning your back completely on your past, you learn to remember it from a better place. And I think that’s exactly what I experienced with Ankara.


By the way, the food part of this trip was also great. We ate very delicious things in Ankara. I especially loved their döner. I won’t explain them in detail in this post because I think they deserve a separate post. I think Ankara is a unique city when it comes to food and drink. The taste, atmosphere, and order of some places really attract people. That’s why in my next post, I will talk a bit about the delicious food we ate in Ankara.

![IMG_3272.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EoCgG8fr6r25EKLDnc4z4xUkGYRfsNXPNV9Fpb3zSa7wGPStrUXHD3takCc7aY8M6xA.jpeg)

![IMG_3273.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/Eou8Bid5cT6YuH5Gv67p5fgnaj9PWCApfvnggEUxMS9mhKW1VjKmQDoAz1wqXD3nJat.jpeg)

![IMG_3278.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/oneplanet/EoK4TpGCNUShKDUcaiytnqsJywi5obNHY6uu19eSZrHqj3VecQXHCQ6toiBCosFULPu.jpeg)

Right now, I am at the airport, waiting for my flight back. Our plane is delayed by a full hour and a half. I have to wait. But even this wait gave me a good time to think about this short Ankara trip. My exam is over, I saw my friends, walked on old streets, sat in nice cafes, saw a sunny Ankara, and most importantly, I developed a softer, more beautiful feeling about Ankara.
In short, this two-day Ankara adventure did me a lot of good. I studied, took my exam, spent great time with my friends, and remembered my old memories from a more peaceful place. Ankara opened a door from the past for me again, but this time, my mind was calmer as I walked through it. I think I am no longer resentful towards Ankara. I love Ankara. But I still have to confess: I think Istanbul is still more beautiful.
My new Ankara food post is coming soon. Especially döner lovers, stay tuned! 😊

body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdMiKCSNe25pK3hSmoti9vdRuBSw6jTgdMzQGb6RYmeHM/20260602_180921.jpg)

| Latin Name | Observation Date | Location |

| ***Spilarctia bisecta,*** | Jun 02, 2026 | Purulia, Natore, Bangladesh |


Hello Nature Observer friends. Hope everyone is well and having a great time with nature.

​I always love to see small insects and their details in nature through the camera lens. There are many such beauties hidden in the grass or bushes that escape our eyes. Today I am going to share with you the detailed information of a wonderful moth or insect that I captured on my camera.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXwhB99FncN8LssYZxbQBU9LLFnNnzcVuqTG6vPyeXoDf/20260602_180909.jpg)

​Common name and scientific name: In common language, it is known as a moth of the Tiger moth species. Its scientific name is ***Spilarctia bisecta,*** which was first described by John Henry Leach in 1889.
​Family and Genus: The moth belongs to the **Erebidae** family and is part of the Arctiinae subfamily. Its genus or genus is Spilarctia. However, historically it was classified under the Spilosoma genus.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNMDbqLyX99DmZLdCsaevitricnoWaHeGW5LeR8f7pdyW/20260602_180821.jpg)

​Native and Habitat: This moth is mainly found in Asia. They are distributed in various regions of China (such as Shanghai, Hong Kong, Sichuan, Jiangxi, Shandong, Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Hubei, Hunan, Fujian, Guangdong, Guangxi, Guizhou, Yunnan, Tibet, etc.).
Size and physical characteristics: Their wingspan is approximately 47 millimeters. The front wings are light buff in color, with a distinct and discrete row of black spots from the middle to the tip. Their hind wings are also light buff in color and also have black dots.
Diet and reproduction: Like ordinary tiger moths, their larvae or caterpillars survive by eating the leaves of various plants. However, adult moths mainly drink nectar from flowers. In reproduction, they lay eggs and the eggs hatch into caterpillars. The caterpillars later go into the pupa stage and from there such beautiful full-fledged moths are born.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRAkPvoFUeie2ePMz4WSZFPBjDV8vTGEsaEqcJ6C2Let5/20260602_180801.jpg)

​Benefits and disadvantages: They play a great role in maintaining the balance of the environment. At night, they help pollinate various flowers. In addition, they are an important part of the food chain or ecosystem as food for frogs, lizards and various birds. Speaking of disadvantages, full-fledged moths do not directly harm us or nature. However, the caterpillars that hatch from the eggs sometimes eat the leaves of agricultural land or garden plants, which can cause minor damage to the crops in some cases.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQme2UAcCaqX9VU4wrZqhK424NJcjC826GJQ8nDXdP5CWgW/20260602_180825.jpg)

​There is infinite beauty hidden among these small creatures of nature. I hope you liked the pictures and information I took. Don't forget to share your constructive opinions in the comments.

  I learned about them from various sites including iNaturalist, Wikipedia and Google.
