Greetings lovely members of the community. I hope you all are doing great and enjoying quality time with your loved ones.

>समुदाय के प्यारे सदस्यों को नमस्कार। मुझे आशा है कि आप सभी अच्छे होंगे और अपने प्रियजनों के साथ गुणवत्तापूर्ण समय का आनंद ले रहे है।


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmazLqooRxiZqskwDXYkFoChQSLULWs2GHMGntTvnbwM9V/img_4663.jpg)


This photograph is my entry for the contest. The subject is an old plastic bottle that once contained oil but is now completely empty. It was sitting on the side table beside my bed, something so ordinary that I usually wouldn’t give it a second glance. One evening, as I was lying down, I noticed sunlight streaming in through the window and falling directly onto the bottle.

>यह तस्वीर मेरी प्रतियोगिता के लिए प्रविष्टि है। इसका मुख्य विषय एक पुरानी प्लास्टिक की बोतल है, जिसमें पहले तेल रखा जाता था, लेकिन अब वह पूरी तरह खाली है। यह मेरे बिस्तर के पास रखी साइड टेबल पर पड़ी थी। यह ऐसी साधारण चीज़ थी जिस पर आमतौर पर मेरी नज़र भी नहीं जाती।


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYEWAqCECs5ifRjfiQdE1kCKUNc55CyHqPp9HT2HkeDDk/img_4662.jpg)


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRtUX5YDo2N96mYFt3x4qBtvCC9AGXcGpdx8wcA6hDcLH/img_4660.jpg)


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUdCL5e7yP8aQR2MkaBEnB6NVj7j8d2BXQ7Y398w6xuhX/img_4661.jpg)

Next to it was a paper takeout shopping bag, and the bottle’s silhouette appeared on it with remarkable clarity. The shadow mirrored the bottle’s shape almost perfectly, from the cap at the top to the curved body below. 

> उसके ठीक बगल में एक पेपर टेकअवे शॉपिंग बैग रखा था, जिस पर बोतल की परछाईं आश्चर्यजनक रूप से स्पष्ट दिखाई दे रही थी। यह छाया बोतल के आकार को लगभग पूरी तरह प्रतिबिंबित कर रही थी ऊपर लगे ढक्कन से लेकर नीचे के घुमावदार हिस्से तक।


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcKkkGSK2AhKSfWUatTkSVXpvehLyqSZS6rfpTY4tzvuV/img_4664.jpg)


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaVZCFZJBhYYgfFh2WgpgKDCN1YZ9DKN2jrkpW9FFzRbQ/img_4665.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcKkkGSK2AhKSfWUatTkSVXpvehLyqSZS6rfpTY4tzvuV/img_4666.jpg)

I found it fascinating how an everyday object that had outlived its original purpose could still become the center of an interesting photograph.

>मुझे यह बात बेहद दिलचस्प लगी कि एक साधारण रोज़मर्रा की वस्तु, जो अपने मूल उपयोग से आगे बढ़ चुकी थी, फिर भी एक आकर्षक और रोचक तस्वीर का केंद्र बन सकती थी।


That's all for today folks. Happy snapping. 💜💙

links.title: Digital Popularity: The Crisis of Students Identity in the Online Platform.
links.body:
Today's generation is far more advance than our presistors. They have more technology support, quick transport services and online markets. So that they can trade easily from any where in the world. But they don't have a things which their presistor had. That is passion. The inventions we see around us all are the results of their patient research. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcZdFmq4vk1p5cVTByq3yKHMDs3aZ3u1PmMEGGAFpTBbA/1780424480395.jpg)

They felt to invent new things to make easier their life. Such as mobile phone was invented Martin Cooper which can carry anywhere but telephone was invented first by Graham Bell which was not portable. Charles Babaje invented modern computer. Now we use smartphones which contains all these features amd more. But there is a question is eveyone using technology for betterment of their life. The answer is 'NO'. But why? I observed that millions of people around the world using technology only for earning money.  It is not bad but the way they earn is not always fruitful. Many of them are creating bullshit content and they have a large number of fan followers. A lot os students are involving with this. They are making content like illiterate people even in educational institutions. They forget their student identity and become online celebrity by making low class content. Other students influenced by see this and they are also build the dream to become online celebrity by doing anything in online platform. Our parents are not conscious about this. 

They think that their kids earning money, supporting their family from student life. It is a big success for them. But they dont know which is actual success of life.There are a vast source of knowledge in online platform. Today's students can gather knowledge from online and can develope their skills to establish themselves. But a large number of students are going backward for earning money which they can earn by changing their tastes and learning other graceful skill.

appy to share my first #blog #articleEmergency Medical Services: The Foundation of Rapid and Life-Saving HealthcareIntroductionEmergency Medical Services (EMS) play a vital role in modern healthcare systems  https://img.leopedia.io/DQmQ6taFar1h6BcX8tyBKgCrDYMofxKSXAgdZm4Saihu8f5/IMG_7210.png 

by providing immediate medical care to individuals suffering from sudden illness, injury, or life-threatening conditions. EMS serves as the critical link between the scene of an emergency and definitive hospital care. The primary goal of EMS is to preserve life, prevent further injury, promote recovery, and ensure safe transportation of patients to appropriate healthcare facilities.EMS professionals work in highly demanding environments where quick decision-making, clinical expertise, effective communication, and teamwork are essential. Whether responding to road traffic accidents, cardiac emergencies, strokes, respiratory distress, or natural disasters, EMS personnel are often the first healthcare providers to interact with patients during their most vulnerable moments.This article explores the importance of Emergency Medical Services, the role of teamwork, patient care principles, emergency management strategies, and an overview of stroke and cardiac arrest management.Understanding Emergency Medical ServicesEmergency Medical Services encompass a coordinated system of healthcare professionals, communication networks, ambulances, emergency medical technicians (EMTs), paramedics, nurses, physicians, and healthcare facilities working together to provide urgent medical assistance.The EMS system generally includes:1. Emergency call reception and dispatch.2. Rapid response by trained personnel.3. On-scene assessment and stabilization.4. Safe patient transportation.5. Communication with receiving healthcare facilities.6. Continuity of care upon hospital arrival.The effectiveness of EMS depends on timely intervention. In many emergencies, especially cardiac arrest and stroke, every minute can significantly affect patient outcomes. Therefore, EMS professionals must be prepared to act efficiently under pressure.Importance of Teamwork in Emergency Medical ServicesTeamwork is one of the most essential components of successful emergency medical care. Emergency situations often involve multiple healthcare professionals working together in dynamic and stressful environments. Effective teamwork improves patient safety, enhances communication, reduces errors, and increases the efficiency of care delivery.Key Elements of Teamwork in EMSCommunicationClear and concise communication ensures that all team members understand the patient’s condition, treatment plan, and responsibilities. Accurate information exchange prevents misunderstandings and supports coordinated patient care.LeadershipA designated team leader helps organize tasks, make clinical decisions, and maintain overall control of the situation. Strong leadership promotes confidence and efficiency during emergencies.Role AllocationEach team member should understand their specific responsibilities. One provider may manage the airway, another may administer medications, while another monitors vital signs and documents interventions.Mutual SupportEMS professionals rely on one another for assistance, feedback, and problem-solving. Supporting fellow team members enhances overall performance and patient outcomes.Situational AwarenessTeam members must continuously monitor the environment, patient status, and available resources. Situational awareness allows teams to anticipate complications and adapt to changing circumstances.Effective teamwork not only improves operational efficiency but also contributes significantly to patient survival and recovery.Patient Care in Emergency Medical ServicesPatient care is the cornerstone of EMS practice. Every patient deserves compassionate, respectful, and evidence-based care regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, socioeconomic status, or medical condition.Principles of Quality Patient CareRapid AssessmentEMS providers must quickly identify life-threatening conditions while maintaining a systematic approach to patient evaluation. The primary assessment focuses on:• Airway• Breathing• Circulation• Disability (neurological status)• Exposure and environmental controlCompassion and EmpathyPatients experiencing emergencies often feel frightened, confused, or distressed. Demonstrating empathy and professionalism helps reduce anxiety and fosters trust.Patient SafetyEnsuring patient safety involves proper lifting techniques, infection control practices, medication verification, and continuous monitoring throughout transport.Pain ManagementPain is a common symptom in emergency situations. EMS providers should assess pain levels and provide appropriate interventions when indicated.DocumentationAccurate documentation ensures continuity of care and provides a legal record of patient assessment, treatment, and response.Patient AdvocacyEMS personnel serve as advocates for patients by ensuring their needs, concerns, and preferences are communicated to receiving healthcare providers.High-quality patient care extends beyond medical interventions and includes emotional support, dignity, and respect for every individual.Emergency Management in EMSEmergency management refers to the organized approach used to prepare for, respond to, mitigate, and recover from emergencies and disasters. EMS agencies play a critical role in all phases of emergency management.PreparednessPreparedness involves planning, training, and resource allocation before emergencies occur.Examples include:• Disaster drills• Staff education• Equipment maintenance• Emergency response planning• Community awareness programsPreparedness ensures that EMS teams can respond effectively when emergencies arise.ResponseThe response phase begins immediately after an emergency occurs.Key response activities include:• Dispatching resources• Patient assessment• Emergency treatment• Rescue operations• Transportation to healthcare facilitiesRapid and coordinated response minimizes morbidity and mortality.MitigationMitigation focuses on reducing the impact of future emergencies.Examples include:• Public health initiatives• Injury prevention programs• Road safety campaigns• Community CPR trainingThese measures help reduce emergency incidents and improve community resilience.RecoveryRecovery involves restoring normal operations after an emergency or disaster.Activities may include:• Patient rehabilitation• Community support services• Equipment replacement• Staff debriefing and mental health supportA comprehensive emergency management strategy strengthens healthcare systems and improves patient outcomes.Stroke Management: A Brief OverviewStroke is a medical emergency that occurs when blood flow to part of the brain is interrupted or when a blood vessel in the brain ruptures. Brain cells begin to die within minutes of oxygen deprivation, making rapid treatment essential.Common Signs and Symptoms of StrokeThe FAST assessment tool is widely used:F – Face DroopingOne side of the face appears uneven or droops.A – Arm WeaknessOne arm becomes weak or numb.S – Speech DifficultySpeech may be slurred or difficult to understand.T – Time to Call Emergency ServicesImmediate medical attention is required.Additional symptoms may include:• Sudden confusion• Vision changes• Loss of balance• Severe headache• Difficulty walkingEMS Management of StrokeEMS providers focus on:1. Rapid recognition of stroke symptoms.2. Determining symptom onset time.3. Assessing airway, breathing, and circulation.4. Monitoring blood glucose levels.5. Providing oxygen when necessary.6. Establishing intravenous access if indicated.7. Prompt transport to a stroke-capable hospital.8. Pre-notification of the receiving facility.Early recognition and rapid transport significantly improve the chances of successful treatment and recovery.Challenges Faced by EMS ProfessionalsEMS providers encounter numerous challenges in their daily practice, including:• High-stress situations• Long working hours• Exposure to traumatic events• Limited resources• Environmental hazards• Emotional and psychological strainDespite these challenges, EMS professionals remain committed to delivering high-quality emergency care and protecting public health.The Future of Emergency Medical ServicesAdvances in technology continue to transform EMS practice. Modern developments include:• Telemedicine support• Portable diagnostic devices• Advanced cardiac monitoring systems• Electronic patient care records• GPS-enabled dispatch systems• Artificial intelligence-assisted decision supportThese innovations enhance response times, improve diagnostic accuracy, and support better patient outcomes.Furthermore, ongoing education and evidence-based practice ensure that EMS providers remain prepared for emerging healthcare challenges.ConclusionEmergency Medical Services are an indispensable component of healthcare systems worldwide. EMS professionals provide immediate assessment, treatment, stabilization, and transportation for patients experiencing medical emergencies. The success of EMS operations relies heavily on teamwork, effective communication, strong leadership, and patient-centered care.High-quality patient care remains the primary mission of EMS, requiring compassion, professionalism, and clinical excellence. Emergency management principles guide preparedness, response, mitigation, and recovery efforts, ensuring communities remain resilient during crises.Stroke and cardiac arrest are among the most time-sensitive emergencies encountered by EMS providers. Rapid recognition, early intervention, and coordinated care can dramatically improve survival and recovery outcomes.As healthcare continues to evolve, Emergency Medical Services will remain at the forefront of emergency care, serving as a lifeline for patients in critical need and contributing significantly to the health and safety of communities worldwide.

links.body:
![1000768931.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ubglo17/242Y9vP3cQZTPGkJdqL4j6PY2uQVQ6VenRj3Sh2xPCsBjJZwX5osh9mqzszRwZfCD5w9C.jpg)[source](https://www.pexels.com/photo/happy-couple-looking-at-each-other-4918475)
This is my post on #freewriters3122 #dailyprompt not an ally hosted by @marinnewest's.
The sun hung low over the savanna, casting long, jagged shadows across the landscape where cattle tracks met the red dust of the village path. Hamma, a Fulani herdsman with a staff resting on his shoulder, stood silently as Adamma approached.
​They were not allies. Their worlds were separated by the ancient, unspoken friction between the nomadic migration of the cattle and the settled permanence of the farms. Hamma saw the encroaching fences as a cage for his tradition, while Adamma saw the stray herds as a threat to the yam harvest that fed her family.
​\
Adamma said, her voice steady but sharp, like the blade of a hoe. She did not look at him, but at the trampled earth.\n​Hamma adjusted his hat, his eyes scanning the horizon. \

she countered, finally meeting his gaze. There was no warmth, only the cold recognition of necessity. They stood like two tectonic plates pressing against one another, neither willing to yield ground.\n​They remained there for a long moment, bound by a shared land they both needed but could never quite share. When Hamma finally whistled to his cattle, turning away toward the horizon, Adamma walked toward her crops. They remained neighbors, yet they were forever, by the nature of their survival, not allies.

links.title: I Fixed My Windows Battery Health Dashboard and Open-Sourced It
links.body:
Windows shows whether a laptop is charged, but it does not make battery wear
easy to understand. I built a small Python dashboard that reads the capacity
data already available on a Windows PC and turns it into a simple health grade.

The first version needed cleanup before I shared it. I fixed the portable
setup, aligned the grade scale with the code, corrected the discharge display,
and rewrote the guide so every command matches the actual tool.

The dashboard now includes:

- an A-F battery-health grade
- local SQLite history
- degradation estimates after enough snapshots exist
- `--watch` and `--export` modes
- an optional Groq summary

The DIY source is MIT licensed:

<https://github.com/thefinalmilkman/digital-downloads/tree/main/battery-dashboard-v1.1>

If it saves you time and you want to support more small utilities, a
$10-equivalent tip is appreciated:

Ready-to-run tipware package:

<https://redkings-battery-dashboard.netlify.app>

- Base USDC: `0x0eAFF975a4823c823cfE0c77E9110Ba47291E72A`
- SOL: `9Ga6JioPVtGCiuvWfc2VCCbN61WLNCkm6S1qFRVn38sG`

I would rather share a small tool honestly than pretend a rough draft is a
finished product.

links.title: The Tale of Bernie - ENG- SPA
links.body: > It was 7:00 AM, and in the northern part of the city, the final preparations were underway for the concert that afternoon at 4:00 PM. A very successful singer was scheduled to perform, and the whole city was eagerly awaiting the concert to have a good time. They were especially excited to see a singer who had come from a distant place; it wasn't very common for such a visit to happen. Therefore, it was going to be a huge event, drawing a large crowd. The singer had already arrived and was staying at a hotel about 70 kilometers away. From his window high up in the hotel, he could see the long line of cars heading north. Many people had arrived early in the morning to secure their spots and get the best seats. Tourists were coming from all over, along with locals and many fans from various places. This singer called himself HUJ, and the city was plastered with signs announcing that everyone shouldn't miss the concert of the great HUJ. Since the concert was at 4 pm, there was plenty of time to get ready and leave, but HUJ hadn't counted on how massive the event would be. All the streets were jammed and full of traffic. There were people outside the hotel and on the streets waiting for the motorcade to pass so they could greet it. When they were about to leave around 2 pm, which was more than enough time in theory, they realized that the traffic had worsened and they wouldn't be able to drive properly or arrive on time.

> Eran las 7 de la mañana, en la parte norte de la ciudad se estaban ultimando los detalles para el concierto de esa tarde a las 4. El concierto lo iba a dar un cantante muy exitoso que venía de gira. Toda la ciudad estaba deseosa que llegara esa hora para pasarla bien, y les hacía mucha ilusión ver a un cantante que venía de otro lugar lejano, eso no era muy normal que pasara, no venían muchos. Por tanto sería un evento muy grande en donde iría mucha gente. El cantante ya había llegado, estaba en un hotel cercano a unos 70 kilómetros. Él desde la ventaba en lo alto del hotel veía la cantidad de autos que iban en fila para la parte norte de la ciudad. Muchas personas iban desde por la mañana para poder marcar su sitio y poder estar en lo mejores lugares. Venían turistas de varias partes, la misma población de la ciudad y muchos fans de diversas partes. Este cantante se hacía llamar HUJ, así que se podía ver la ciudad llena de letreros anunciando que no ser perdieran el concierto del gran HUJ. Como el concierto era a las 4 había bastante tiempo para prepararse y salir, pero HUJ no contó con lo masivo que sería el evento. Todas la calles estaban atascadas y llevas de tráfico. Había gente fuera del hotel y las calles estaban esperando a que pasara la caravana para saludarlo. Cuando se disponían a partir a eso de las 2 de la tarde, lo cual era tiempo más que suficiente en teoría, se dieron cuenta de que el tráfico había empeorado y así no podrían conducir bien o llegar a tiempo.
![jens-herrndorff-8osoVBQWWHc-unsplash.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nelsoncu/23tmBccDgnqP8iPsNB9SBTpiLLuEZf1PuxqXppSuRtS8tRVH5UkoTMKeiLHvRVN7t6M7E.jpg) ...Free image from Pixabay...

> Since going by car would be very difficult, it was decided that the best option was to rent a helicopter. For this mission, they called Bernie. He was a very experienced pilot with a long career, having worked for the army and now for the local police. So he was the perfect person to take them to the concert and avoid all the traffic jams. They called him, and he immediately accepted. They left at 3 p.m., just an hour away. But there was nothing to worry about; by helicopter, it would take less than 10 minutes. A sense of calm filled the air. They sped off to the venue. From the helicopter, they could already see the huge crowd gathered in the distance and the many lights of the event. HUJ was excited; this might be one of his biggest concerts ever. This trip would truly be unforgettable for everyone. Just when everything was going smoothly, a loud crash was heard in the helicopter. One of the propeller blades had come loose, destabilizing the entire aircraft. There was a real risk of an air accident, but since they were far from base, they couldn't return to try to land. Therefore, the only option was to land anywhere nearby, but there was nowhere to land. It was full of people and houses.

> Dado que sería muy difícil ir en auto se decidió que lo mejor era alquilar a un helicóptero para ir volando. Y para esa misión llamaron a Bernie. El era un piloto de mucha experiencia y llevaba mucho tiempo volando, trabajó para el ejército y ahora trabajaba en la policía local. Así que era alguien perfecto para cumplir la misión de llevarlo hasta el concierto y de esa forma evitar todos los atascos. Lo llamaron y el enseguida aceptó. Salieron a las 3 de la tarde solo faltaba una hora. Pero nada de qué preocuparse, en helicóptero esos serian menos de 10 minutos. Había calma en el ambiente. Salieron a toda prisa para el lugar, desde el helicóptero ya se podía ver la cantidad de gente amontonada a lo lejos, y las muchas luces del evento. HUJ estaba emocionado, este quizás pudiera llegar a ser uno de sus conciertos más grandes. La verdad este viaje sería inolvidable para todos. Cuando todo iba de lo mejor se sintió un fuerte estruendo en el helicóptero, y era que una de las palas de la hélices se había zafado de su lugar desestabilizando todo el aparato. Había un riesgo real de accidente aéreo, pero como estaban lejos de la base no podían regresar para intentar aterrizar. Por lo tanto lo que había que hacer era aterriza en cualquier lugar cerca posible, NO había donde hacerlo. Estaba lleno de gente y de casas.
![austin-neill-4pHcmcPsP8A-unsplash.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nelsoncu/244oWtEDWPNPNoL5LDNdsVxxHwC44BEnSg5ZN9iuAwXWHMpTcDDU8h3XKk5V9m37j1yxk.jpg) ...Free image from Pixabay...

> \n\nLuckily for everyone, Bernie was at the controls, so he was able to maneuver and land on one of the rooftops. It was a difficult task, and he lost more helicopter blades in the process. But he made it, and that's what mattered. HUJ didn't believe they were alive. Bernie splashed water on his face and asked, \

After confirming that he was, he told him his mission wasn't over. He borrowed one of the cars from the owners of the house where they had landed on the rooftop and drove HUJ to the concert. They arrived on time, and HUJ, still a little shaken, was able to sing, and everyone had a great time. No one in the audience knew what had happened. But when the concert ended, he publicly thanked Bernie for making the event possible and for looking out for his life. Without him, he wouldn't have been there to tell the tale. It will all remain an interesting story for the grandchildren and the fans.

> Por suerte para todos Bernie iba al mando de los controles por lo que pudo maniobrar para aterrizar en una de las azoteas de los edificios. Pero hacerlo le costó mucho, y perdió mas palas del helicóptero en el proceso. Pero lo logró y eso es lo importante. HUJ no creía que estuvieran vivos. Bernie le echó agua en la cara y le dijo, ¿estás bien? Tras confirmar que si, entonces le dijo que su misión no había acabado. Pidió prestado uno de los autos de los dueños de la casa en donde había aterrizado en la azotea y llevó a HUJ hasta el mismo concierto. Llegaron a tiempo al concierto y HUJ aún un poco sobresaltado pudo cantar y todo el mundo lo pasó bien, nadie sabía lo que había pasado en el publico. Pero cuando el concierto se acabó el agradeció púbicamente a Bernie por haber hecho el evento posible y por cuidar de su vida. Sin el no hubiera estado allí para contarlo. Todo quedará como un interesante relato para los nietos y para los fans.
![redd-francisco-qMFSP1xYVTQ-unsplash.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nelsoncu/23tRvScp35QUmCo9kWp2UsvVhWjzRnbECMg2VM2z4FXoQV4BnHDWHUquN9uyuQYAbEUsD.jpg) ...Free image from Pixabay...

links.title: Television Review: Riverworld (2010)
links.body:
![(source:imdb.com)](https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMjMzOGI1MzEtYzM2Zi00OGQ4LTliODAtNDViMDQ0NDdmMmU1XkEyXkFqcGc@._V1_FMjpg_UX1000_.jpg)



The *Riverworld* cycle of science fiction novels by Hugo Award-winning author Philip José Farmer has long captivated readers with its audacious premise—the post-mortem resurrection of every human who ever lived along the banks of a seemingly endless river on an alien world. This concept, rich with philosophical potential and boundless narrative possibilities, has not only amassed a devoted following but has persistently tantalised those imagining its translation to the screen. Prior to 2010, there had been but a single, faltering attempt: the [2003 Sci-Fi Channel television film](https://peakd.com/hive-166847/@drax/television-review-riverworld-2003), directed by Kari Skogland, which served as a pilot for a series that never materialised. That production, as noted in contemporary critiques, was a profound disappointment, reducing Farmer’s intellectually curious saga to a generic telefantasy adventure. Seven years later, the same channel embarked on another, more ambitious adaptation: a two-part miniseries directed by Stewart Gillard. On paper, the expanded format promised a more faithful and nuanced exploration of Farmer’s creation. In practice, the 2010 *Riverworld* stands as a stark testament to how greater length, without concomitant vision, budget, or respect for the source material, can result in an adaptation even more frustrating and ultimately more forgettable than its predecessor.

The miniseries transplants the narrative to a contemporary setting, opening in Kuala Lumpur where photojournalist Matt Ellman (Tahmoh Penikett) is about to propose to his girlfriend, Jessie Machalan (Laura Vandervoort). Their moment is obliterated by a female suicide bomber, killing them both. Ellman awakens, disoriented, in the titular river, and upon reaching shore discovers he is not alone. He encounters others who died in the blast, including an elderly woman now mysteriously rejuvenated. This initial mystery effectively establishes the core conceit: all here are dead, resurrected by inscrutable beings known as the Caretakers, provided with basic sustenance via “grails,” and left to forge a new society. Ellman soon learns that this fresh start has merely replicated old tyrannies. The strong prey upon the weak, epitomised by the infamous Spanish conquistador Francisco Pizarro (Bruce Ramsay), who has established a brutal empire. Aiding him is the English explorer Sir Richard Francis Burton (Peter Wingfield), a figure whose presence will incense any reader of the novels, where Burton is the charismatic, complex protagonist. Here, he is reinvented as a scheming villain in league with a sinister, renegade Caretaker (Alan Cumming). Escaping Pizarro’s clutches, Ellman embarks on a quest to find Jessie, aided by the legendary Japanese female samurai Tomoe Gozen (Jeananne Goossen) and Samuel Clemens, aka Mark Twain (Mark Deklin), who has constructed a riverboat to explore this strange world.

The most immediate advantage the 2010 version holds over the 2003 film is its miniseries format. With roughly twice the runtime, the script by Robert Hewitt Wolfe and Randall M. Badat does manage to incorporate more elements from Farmer’s literary universe. Most notably, it introduces the concept of repeated resurrections—characters who die on Riverworld can be “recycled” back to life—a fundamental mechanic of the novels that adds a layer of existential stakes absent from the earlier adaptation. This suggests an intention to engage more deeply with the source material’s mechanics. Yet, this solitary fidelity only serves to highlight the myriad other ways in which the production fails, and often more catastrophically than the 2003 effort.

The most palpable deficiency is the glaring lack of budget. Where Skogland’s film was shot amidst the striking, unfamiliar landscapes of New Zealand, Gillard’s miniseries is confined to the well-trodden, temperate forests of British Columbia—a location so ubiquitously used for North American television science fiction and fantasy that it instantly shatters any illusion of an alien, awe-inspiring world. The setting feels generic and earthbound, lacking the visual grandeur the premise demands. The marginally improved CGI, which allows for the inclusion of a zeppelin alongside Twain’s riverboat, is a paltry compensation. It cannot mask the overall cheapness of the production design, from the unconvincing armour of Pizarro’s conquistadors to the underwhelming realisation of the climactic Dark Towers.

This budgetary constraint is exacerbated by Stuart Gillard’s pedestrian direction. Where a skilled director might use clever cinematography and editing to disguise financial limitations, Gillard’s handling of action, particularly the battle sequences, only accentuates their scale-less, televisual cheapness. The performances he elicits are similarly lacking. Bruce Ramsay’s Pizarro is a one-note, snarling antagonist, devoid of the chilling, cultured menace that Jonathan Cake brought to Nero in the 2003 version. Far more egregious, however, is the character assassination of Sir Richard Francis Burton. Peter Wingfield plays him as a standard-issue, duplicitous schemer, a decision that fundamentally misunderstands and disrespects Farmer’s work. In the novels, Burton’s brilliant, irascible, and deeply human nature is the engine of the story; his reduction to a secondary villain is an unforgivable betrayal of the source material that alienates its core audience. Tahmoh Penikett strives for gravitas as Ellman but is shackled to an uninspired, everyman protagonist whose journey feels generic. Laura Vandervoort is regrettably sidelined, her role as Jessie amounting to little more than a damsel-in-distress plot device and eye candy, a wasted opportunity for meaningful characterisation.

Gillard’s narrative choices further undermine the miniseries. Lengthy, repetitive flashbacks to Ellman’s past as a war correspondent in Chechnya feel like tedious filler, inserted to pad the runtime rather than to illuminate character or theme. They disrupt the pacing and contribute to a sense of narrative lethargy. Even more curiously regressive is Gillard’s approach to a foundational element of the premise: the nudity of the resurrected. The 2003 film, for all its faults, had the courage to depict the raw, unsettling vulnerability of hundreds of people awakening naked on the riverbank, a powerful visual metaphor for rebirth and existential nakedness. The 2010 version, in a display of inexplicable prudishness, has characters appear already clothed. This sanitisation strips the scenario of its visceral, disquieting impact, making the resurrection feel safe, sterile, and unimaginative. The irony is acute: Gillard began his directorial career with the 1982 film [*Paradise*](https://peakd.com/hive-166847/@drax/film-review-paradise-1982), a romantic period adventure whose marketing heavily featured the nudity of its young leads. Here, whether due to network pressure or personal choice, he lacks the will or skill that Kari Skogland demonstrated in navigating such content for television, resulting in a tamer, less daring production.

The miniseries lumbers towards a climax at the mysterious Dark Towers, culminating in a spectacular, apocalyptic showdown that the protagonists conveniently survive via yet another resurrection. This provides a neat cliffhanger, clearly designed to tee up potential sequels or an ongoing series. However, by this point, any narrative momentum or viewer investment has long since dissipated. The Sci-Fi Channel, and the audience, had lost interest. The failure feels particularly pronounced when viewed in the broader television landscape. By 2010, series like *Lost* had conclusively demonstrated how a mysterious, character-driven saga with a sprawling ensemble and deep mythological underpinnings could captivate a global audience. *Lost* proved that a premise akin to Farmer’s—people stranded in a strange world confronting mysteries of existence—could be executed with ingenuity, originality, and emotional resonance. The 2010 *Riverworld*, in contrast, feels like a relic, a clumsily executed adventure story that misunderstands its own source material and fails to learn from either the mistakes of its 2003 predecessor or the successes of its contemporaries.

The 2010 *Riverworld* miniseries is a profoundly disappointing endeavour. It squanders the expanded canvas of its format, offering only superficial gestures towards the novels’ complexity while succumbing to crippling budgetary constraints, uninspired direction, and a deeply misguided approach to character and tone. It is less an adaptation of Philip José Farmer’s visionary work and more a bland, televisual fantasy that uses the *Riverworld* name as a shallow backdrop. Its failure is twofold: it neither satisfies fans of the books nor succeeds as compelling standalone television. This second attempt at resurrecting *Riverworld* for the screen only succeeded in proving that some literary worlds, no matter how fascinating, remain stubbornly beyond the reach of inadequate interpretation.


RATING: 2/10 (-)

links.title: Splinterlands-Awesome combination of Dread Tafarian and Time Bandit.
links.body:
‎Hello everyone. I am @naturaluttom, I would like to share with you some of my experiences about my two favorite cards from my favorite game Splinterlands, Dread Tafarian and Time Bandit. I play these two cards regularly and have had good results in many matches.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVqsdzo2v5uKTum36MuFsk9Rf88rHJtr7xmPa2upEq7N2/1780423613591.png)



[‎The image was created with AI.]()

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSZztvzURKTdS9QiX5QmGGCs6HpLCBQssbNSKLTrbdLs2/1779301832564.png)


First, let's talk about the Dread Tafarian card. It is a powerful card with 9 mana. At level 1, it has 1 Melee Attack, 1 Armor, 2 Speed ​​and 6 Health. The best part of this card is its Heal ability. It can recover some of its Health every round. So it is not easily defeated. I usually keep this card in front, because it can withstand a lot of damage and survive on the field for a long time.



![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWmwKDX9Eekg7oL65dDS9BkbJBr6jX5BgBsvqFka7Dsa2/1780423447797.jpg)



On the other hand, Time Bandit is an 8 mana Magic Attack card. At level 1, it has 1 Magic Attack, 1 Speed ​​and 7 Health. Since it is a Magic Attack, it can avoid the opponent's Armor and directly hit the Health. So in matches where the opponent's Armor is high, this card is quite useful. I often put Time Bandit behind Dread Tafarian, so that he can attack from safety.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmP4ncEWzegqdWmteP9yL8HtcyYVE8WmeY5BdqtNYcf82G/1780423448003.jpg)



I really like the pairing of these two cards. Dread Tafarian deals damage from the front, and Time Bandit deals Magic Damage from the back. I have had good results with these two cards in many matches. Especially in long fights, Dread Tafarian's healing ability helps a lot.

Overall, Dread Tafarian and Time Bandit are two of my favorite cards. So I use these two cards whenever I get the chance. I'm ending it here like today. I hope you like my little experience.

Thank you all.























![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSZztvzURKTdS9QiX5QmGGCs6HpLCBQssbNSKLTrbdLs2/1779301832564.png)

links.title: CCC's Street Art Contest #303 - Our National Identity / Nuestra Identidad Nacional
links.body:
> ***English*** ###
**Our National Identity**
Greetings to all my friends in the StreetArt community. Undoubtedly, a country's identity is shaped by its history, culture, traditions, values, and its people—a legacy passed down through generations. It's essential to showcase these values ​​to understand how the society we live in has been formed. In our country, we always keep these elements in mind because we find them expressed in various forms, one of which is art, which, with just a single painting, speaks volumes. >***Español*** >###
**Nuestra Identidad Nacional**
>Un gran saludo amigos de la comunidad de StreetArt. Sin duda, la identidad de un país se constituye por su historia, cultura, tradiciones, valores y su gente, ese legado que se transmite a través de la generación. Y es necesario mostrar estos valores para comprender cómo se ha formado la sociedad en que vivimos. En nuestro país siempre tenemos presente todos estos elementos porque los encontramos plasmados en diferentes formas y una de ellas es el arte, que, con solo una pintura, ella habla por sí sola. ![IMG_20260523_093601~2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lanoican/23ywq2gimcoBFna7y4MZNqoY22CVixzUUy3DiAvEWCzMiEhtGD9A4QfQ68NN1DZ8yPTQy.jpg) For example, this mural depicts the cultural traditions of dances and musical instruments, each with its own story, accompanying the dance troupes in many cities across our country. It also showcases the flora that typically adorns our gardens and the traditional costumes worn for these dances. A wealth of elements that constitute the essence of a nation. >Como ejemplo, este mural donde está plasmada la tradición cultural de los bailes, los instrumentos musicales que son historias y acompañan las comparsas de muchas ciudades de nuestro país. En él también se muestra la flora que usualmente adorna nuestros jardines y el traje típico para esos bailes tradicionales. Toda una cantidad de elementos que constituyen la esencia de una nación. ![IMG_20260523_093551~2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lanoican/242NejEKk8hDRy4KuD9KzkqhDHRKR3hGZ52bkzKzgKja1Th4aUUEZZG2cMUvUpFpzbfjU.jpg) This vibrant mural captures the pure essence of a people who live by their values ​​and traditions. It's located in a space where it's admired by all passersby. Sharing and cultivating our cultural values ​​allows us to strengthen our roots. This mural is located at the exit of the Petare Metro station in Caracas. >Este mural tan colorido plasma la esencia pura de un pueblo que se mueve al ritmo de sus valores y tradiciones. Se encuentra en un espacio donde es admirado por todos los transeúntes que pasan por el lugar. Dar a conocer y sembrar nuestros valores culturales nos permite consolidar nuestras raíces. Este mural está ubicado en la salida de la estación del Metro de Caracas, Petare. ![IMG_20260523_093622~2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lanoican/241tX7yx8apmKBb9J4BuSqURKzn5k4vtQwzfmCmaSKrK1uHRDaVsQ9FZkq8UqS3f4KZ1d.jpg) ![5s4dzRwnVbzGY5ssnCE4wXzkeAEXyVtgk1ApQTwHMTp6y5PvEo1yennAbzQkJ9G8uVvM1WjDyTeCvUuTiNFbfpF1J9yKTEBESC7RtqAxoD6Bxcoo9NaddDxcS5uE8yY95UEuz59CpRNk6DkRm9KA8gUJKK44W396P5RhjnE.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lanoican/23tvASVrTgFFPYz1s62q3C9eFbkQRo9rWE2uxH6GMt4TsfTQCNqzbmpm3djenunLN6PA8.png)

> Hello everyone, how are you doing today? Hope you are having a great time. This will be *Week 220 Edition 01* of our Weekly Featured Content. ![Copy of Copy of Copy of TPEP's Friday Feature (1).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kronias/23zH3ihhxgjN5Ydxs9LGWWgZQUHDtgcBQZCamdrWRF3q1gTuNQiUs4P42GSHPa55aRRqb.png)
Made With Canva
So, last Saturday we had our hangout as usual, and it was just so much fun that we did not want it to end. We are currently on the first topic for this week, which is “THE SCHOOL YOU GO TO”. But before we proceed with the details of the topic, let us take a look at the winners of the last topic, which was “A WHITE LIE”. This topic was geared toward each member of the community, telling us their thoughts on white lies and the effects they could have on us. We saw the need for white lies told from time to time, because in the end, the reason for the lies we tell will decide just how bad the act of lying really is. We got to see that indeed, we all tell lies, and there can be valid reasons why people will resort to white lies. But then, we still have to be careful, because once it starts becoming about deceiving the other person, it becomes a major problem. This was an enlightening topic, indeed. ***
> For this topic, we went through every entry post, and that is every post with the #hl-exclusive & #hl-w219e3 tag. And with the number of wonderful posts out there, it was quite difficult to make a selection. But eventually, we did just that. And so, the posts that will be featured not just for their exceptional content, but also for their level of engagement with other authors, will be listed below. ![hl_footer.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcnAnsqHA4KMYRqnS9QzWMpQUxM71wRhKabXz7paozHKJ/hl_footer.png)

Featured Contents


[NOT ALL LIES ARE BAD: A FUNNY COLLEGE STORY](https://peakd.com/hive-153850/@bhattg/not-all-lies-are-bad) by @bhattg
*For this author, he told us that we all tell lies. With some lies, there are really no repercussions, but for others, they end up changing the course of our lives. This author tries his best to tell the truth as often as he can. But then, when it feels important and needed, he tells a white lie. But not usually for his benefit.*
[WHEN THE TRUTH IS A CRUEL OPTION](https://peakd.com/hive-153850/@michupa/when-the-truth-is-a) by @michupa
*For this author, he told us that regardless of how strong and intense our values are, the well-being of the people we’re in charge of is more important than our ethics, and we just might have to lie to them to protect it. A white lie should be told only to protect the interests of the person being lied to, never for deception.”
[THE UNCOMFORTABLE TRUTH ABOUT WHITE LIES](https://peakd.com/hive-153850/@yechee/the-uncomfortable-truth-about-white) by @yechee
*This author told us that sometimes, she tells white lies to protect the feelings of the people around her. And she has also learned to stop beating herself up for it because she usually does them out of necessity. In the end, white lies shouldn’t be considered a big deal.*

These posts were selected because of their special attention to detail and how they followed the topic. There were a lot of good ones out there, but we just could not pick them all. But then, we have some honorable mentions listed below:

Honorable Mention

[A WHITE LIE OR LIE OF HYPORITE?](https://peakd.com/hive-153850/@intishar/a-white-lie-or-lie) by @intishar [THE COMPLICATED SIDE OF WHITE LIES](https://peakd.com/hive-153850/@zoe01/the-complicated-side-of-white) by @zoe01 [LITTLE LIE](https://peakd.com/hive-153850/@kilvnrex/little-lie-2qc) by @kilvnrex These are posts that were also found to be quite exceptional. ---- ---- ![hl_footer.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcnAnsqHA4KMYRqnS9QzWMpQUxM71wRhKabXz7paozHKJ/hl_footer.png)
AND NOW, WE MOVE ON TO THE NEW TOPIC!
***

Week 220 - Edition 01 Topic

**THE SCHOOL YOU GO TO**

links.title: Why Educational Institutes Matters to Me?
links.body:
Hello **Hive Learners Community!** Welcome to my blog. After about six months, I'm back to my journey as a content creator. I missed all the Hive Family a lot but it was tough time that has passed. It was all I was suffering from last couple of days. Now let us back to the topic about **School or Collage** and Memories. Educational institutes are sacred places where foundations of great leaders are laid. They not only make memories but also share the beautiful charms of their lives.

![1000605071.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aslamrer/242YADLAZwLmi7N72uyQAjTZemiuA2r6nZSvcNQpyhcDYXXXdrheJC7nNfAREUBS2NX5R.jpg)
> Some moments I ever like
 

---
# <center>School of Thoughts Regarding School or College Experiences</center>
---


![1000609242.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aslamrer/242Y7yexA57XxsHF6NMxyTc2wQ5RpGhoz3fZcyF5VPnHoXfMv5LFpDmH5uWC6Vpa2xdYP.jpg)
> Flower can't retain its beauty always 

We can't deny these facts where we get education, play a wonderful role in our life. Some people have good experience about their schools while some have worst. Good exposure to school life indeed will make a good memory and there will be no one who want to delete it from their past. Similarly, a bad memory will be hurdle that everyone wanted to go in their past for improvement and changes. 


![1000601253.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aslamrer/EoErwFYyXpLMTGzAa1pjJ2wKXnFn6KEuT3Vu9uUGYUW2uKnnoQ8pU9tW6ZWcwoxmTjf.jpg)
> Childhood is always beautiful in school time

Where I was getting my school education was one of the best training hub for the kids. They have not only books but also toys to familiarise with sports and games. It was the golden period in my life. Whenever I remember about those golden days, I found myself lucky and pleasurable. Would that I were rich to buy those moments again. However, it is life where we have memories only. 

Similarly my nephew has bad memories regarding his school. She always blamed that she has destroyed his childhood due to toxic environment of school. Ma'am was totally aggressive and always had scolded her for mistakes. She always complained about these bad experiences in school and always prayed to God, \

. I always advised her what has been passed is now memories and hence we should think about our future. 1st We must make our present better then we can enjoy life. 


![1000602854.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aslamrer/23zGm5dAT8KUCysBkt17Cpstgse7PEdGNvLv8MyPi3SEGSpQZQfAj4TyVVY8QpHsimX8w.png)
> Childhood version of my nephew 

Anyway, each school of thought regarding past memories about educational institutes is good. People who had bad experiences would try to delete this past or substitute it with better environment. While people who have good experience will never delete or replace memories about their educational institutes. Hence, we have to accept, they are not the educational institutes that were bad or good actually they were the people that made educational institutes good or bad. 

---
# <center>Final Thoughts</center>
---

It is not essential everytime our life will entertain us with beautiful moments. Night can't be permanent, similarly day can't be permanent. They both change in their pace to make our life beautiful. Either we have good or bad memories about our school or colleges or we have met to good or bad colleagues or fellows, we have to learn from our past and move on.

![1000593820.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aslamrer/Eoc9rPwG86fEGhCybWBpKHauw1ZsXq9x14zcjtjV95mM1AbEaQxLSUjLZemVeTigF5i.jpg)
> Company of School Friends 

I always like to learn what mistakes I have done in my school days and like to save my life in the future. Nothing is permanent in our life, hence we should try to make our present beautiful without worrying about past or future. Everyone remembers about school or college days and there are many things that needs to be back but we can't. 

This post is my entry for HL Weekly Featured Content **The School you go to**. I hope, you have enjoyed my post. Thanks!

/> Emergency Medical Services: The Foundation of Rapid and Life-Saving Healthcare Introduction Emergency Medical Services (EMS) play a vital role in modern healthcare systems by providing immediate medical care to individuals suffering from sudden illness, injury, or life-threatening conditions. EMS serves as the critical link between the scene of an emergency and definitive hospital care. The primary goal of EMS is to preserve life, prevent further injury, promote recovery, and ensure safe transportation of patients to appropriate healthcare facilities. EMS professionals work in highly demanding environments where quick decision-making, clinical expertise, effective communication, and teamwork are essential. Whether responding to road traffic accidents, cardiac emergencies, strokes, respiratory distress, or natural disasters, EMS personnel are often the first healthcare providers to interact with patients during their most vulnerable moments. This article explores the importance of Emergency Medical Services, the role of teamwork, patient care principles, emergency management strategies, and an overview of stroke and cardiac arrest management. Understanding Emergency Medical Services Emergency Medical Services encompass a coordinated system of healthcare professionals, communication networks, ambulances, emergency medical technicians (EMTs), paramedics, nurses, physicians, and healthcare facilities working together to provide urgent medical assistance. The EMS system generally includes: 1\. Emergency call reception and dispatch. 2\. Rapid response by trained personnel. 3\. On-scene assessment and stabilization. 4\. Safe patient transportation. 5\. Communication with receiving healthcare facilities. 6\. Continuity of care upon hospital arrival. The effectiveness of EMS depends on timely intervention. In many emergencies, especially cardiac arrest and stroke, every minute can significantly affect patient outcomes. Therefore, EMS professionals must be prepared to act efficiently under pressure. Importance of Teamwork in Emergency Medical Services Teamwork is one of the most essential components of successful emergency medical care. Emergency situations often involve multiple healthcare professionals working together in dynamic and stressful environments. Effective teamwork improves patient safety, enhances communication, reduces errors, and increases the efficiency of care delivery. Key Elements of Teamwork in EMS 1. Communication Clear and concise communication ensures that all team members understand the patient’s condition, treatment plan, and responsibilities. Accurate information exchange prevents misunderstandings and supports coordinated patient care. 1. Leadership A designated team leader helps organize tasks, make clinical decisions, and maintain overall control of the situation. Strong leadership promotes confidence and efficiency during emergencies. 1. Role Allocation Each team member should understand their specific responsibilities. One provider may manage the airway, another may administer medications, while another monitors vital signs and documents interventions. 1. Mutual Support EMS professionals rely on one another for assistance, feedback, and problem-solving. Supporting fellow team members enhances overall performance and patient outcomes. 1. Situational Awareness Team members must continuously monitor the environment, patient status, and available resources. Situational awareness allows teams to anticipate complications and adapt to changing circumstances. Effective teamwork not only improves operational efficiency but also contributes significantly to patient survival and recovery. Patient Care in Emergency Medical Services Patient care is the cornerstone of EMS practice. Every patient deserves compassionate, respectful, and evidence-based care regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, socioeconomic status, or medical condition. Principles of Quality Patient Care Rapid Assessment EMS providers must quickly identify life-threatening conditions while maintaining a systematic approach to patient evaluation. The primary assessment focuses on: • Airway • Breathing • Circulation • Disability (neurological status) • Exposure and environmental control Compassion and Empathy Patients experiencing emergencies often feel frightened, confused, or distressed. Demonstrating empathy and professionalism helps reduce anxiety and fosters trust. Patient Safety Ensuring patient safety involves proper lifting techniques, infection control practices, medication verification, and continuous monitoring throughout transport. Pain Management Pain is a common symptom in emergency situations. EMS providers should assess pain levels and provide appropriate interventions when indicated. Documentation Accurate documentation ensures continuity of care and provides a legal record of patient assessment, treatment, and response. Patient Advocacy EMS personnel serve as advocates for patients by ensuring their needs, concerns, and preferences are communicated to receiving healthcare providers. High-quality patient care extends beyond medical interventions and includes emotional support, dignity, and respect for every individual. Emergency Management in EMS Emergency management refers to the organized approach used to prepare for, respond to, mitigate, and recover from emergencies and disasters. EMS agencies play a critical role in all phases of emergency management. 1. Preparedness Preparedness involves planning, training, and resource allocation before emergencies occur. Examples include: • Disaster drills • Staff education • Equipment maintenance • Emergency response planning • Community awareness programs Preparedness ensures that EMS teams can respond effectively when emergencies arise. 1. Response The response phase begins immediately after an emergency occurs. Key response activities include: • Dispatching resources • Patient assessment • Emergency treatment • Rescue operations • Transportation to healthcare facilities Rapid and coordinated response minimizes morbidity and mortality. 1. Mitigation Mitigation focuses on reducing the impact of future emergencies. Examples include: • Public health initiatives • Injury prevention programs • Road safety campaigns • Community CPR training These measures help reduce emergency incidents and improve community resilience. 1. Recovery Recovery involves restoring normal operations after an emergency or disaster. Activities may include: • Patient rehabilitation • Community support services • Equipment replacement • Staff debriefing and mental health support A comprehensive emergency management strategy strengthens healthcare systems and improves patient outcomes. Stroke Management: A Brief Overview Stroke is a medical emergency that occurs when blood flow to part of the brain is interrupted or when a blood vessel in the brain ruptures. Brain cells begin to die within minutes of oxygen deprivation, making rapid treatment essential. Common Signs and Symptoms of Stroke The FAST assessment tool is widely used: F – Face Drooping One side of the face appears uneven or droops. A – Arm Weakness One arm becomes weak or numb. S – Speech Difficulty Speech may be slurred or difficult to understand. T – Time to Call Emergency Services Immediate medical attention is required. Additional symptoms may include: • Sudden confusion • Vision changes • Loss of balance • Severe headache • Difficulty walking EMS Management of Stroke EMS providers focus on: 1\. Rapid recognition of stroke symptoms. 2\. Determining symptom onset time. 3\. Assessing airway, breathing, and circulation. 4\. Monitoring blood glucose levels. 5\. Providing oxygen when necessary. 6\. Establishing intravenous access if indicated. 7\. Prompt transport to a stroke-capable hospital. 8\. Pre-notification of the receiving facility. Early recognition and rapid transport significantly improve the chances of successful treatment and recovery. Challenges Faced by EMS Professionals EMS providers encounter numerous challenges in their daily practice, including: • High-stress situations • Long working hours • Exposure to traumatic events • Limited resources • Environmental hazards • Emotional and psychological strain Despite these challenges, EMS professionals remain committed to delivering high-quality emergency care and protecting public health. The Future of Emergency Medical Services Advances in technology continue to transform EMS practice. Modern developments include: • Telemedicine support • Portable diagnostic devices • Advanced cardiac monitoring systems • Electronic patient care records • GPS-enabled dispatch systems • Artificial intelligence-assisted decision support These innovations enhance response times, improve diagnostic accuracy, and support better patient outcomes. Furthermore, ongoing education and evidence-based practice ensure that EMS providers remain prepared for emerging healthcare challenges. Conclusion Emergency Medical Services are an indispensable component of healthcare systems worldwide. EMS professionals provide immediate assessment, treatment, stabilization, and transportation for patients experiencing medical emergencies. The success of EMS operations relies heavily on teamwork, effective communication, strong leadership, and patient-centered care. High-quality patient care remains the primary mission of EMS, requiring compassion, professionalism, and clinical excellence. Emergency management principles guide preparedness, response, mitigation, and recovery efforts, ensuring communities remain resilient during crises. Stroke and cardiac arrest are among the most time-sensitive emergencies encountered by EMS providers. Rapid recognition, early intervention, and coordinated care can dramatically improve survival and recovery outcomes. As healthcare continues to evolve, Emergency Medical Services will remain at the forefront of emergency care, serving as a lifeline for patients in critical need and contributing significantly to the health and safety of communities worldwide.

links.title: Reflection of greenery on the canvas of calm water |Reflection Hunters Contest ~ Round 274
links.body:
Hello Hive Community and Reflection Hunters friends around the world! Hope everyone is healthy.

'Reflection Hunters' is a great contest on this platform, which gives us a chance to see the ordinary scenes around us with a different eye. After hearing the idea of ​​this contest, I decided to participate and in today's round (274), I have appeared with my entry.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVoTTgsjvJE7bnrnq9Qfs1sL7YYaMajKFzHMn4UKGnnDz/20260602_174859.jpg)

(This picture is my original entry)

​I went out this afternoon mainly for this contest to hunt for some beautiful reflections. My eyes are always looking for the perfect reflection of nature. When I walked in the afternoon and stood next to a quiet water reservoir in the village, the weather was absolutely strange. There was no movement in the air, no leaves were moving, no waves or tremors on the water. It felt like someone had laid a huge natural mirror on the ground. And this was exactly the scene I was looking for.
​You can see in my main entry photo, rows of betel nut trees standing on the other side of the water and some banana trees in front of them. In this stillness of nature, the reflection of the trees on the still water was like a mirror. The long stems of the betel nut trees on the water and the color of the green leaves were so clear that it seemed that another green forest was standing upside down just below the water. Not only the trees, but also the light gray sky behind it seemed to have taken its place on the water. It is always very peaceful to see this perfect parallel form of nature.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmU9yJvJd6QNoSKhK2sVGu1soJntN6JhEcXRVJjcpCA3p6/20260602_174955.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaLCZnhiNSbEieQwrzE18n92kNR5TaAGWSu5456hsWVs8/20260602_175139.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcvvAYXtUt1zvqp4JBzenWT1C94vyKHHU16eZaC5FW5S3/20260602_174851.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNrTDVPub1REHVWdD7pTiEwXTNUf34FaheEjkG3wjujJS/20260602_175000.jpg)

​I took several photos from different angles and moods for the contest, because the reflections were captured differently from each angle. Those who know my work know that I usually prefer to do macro photography. My main interest is to highlight the details of small insects or flowers at close range. Most of the time, my eyes search for small subjects on the ground or behind leaves. But today, for the purpose of the contest, this huge canvas of nature was presented to me in such a way that I could not help but take pictures of the landscape and reflection. Today, I was looking at the huge mirror of nature, leaving the world of small insects.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSS1ZV6R5cUJfpJNL12hfEqr2e8db35WuLtzHCDPSZUa1/20260602_175051.jpg)

The pictures were taken with my smartphone. The true form of nature is so beautiful that I did not feel the need for any special heavy editing. I also took some black and white photos from different angles to test, but I chose this colorful natural picture as the main entry, because the true colors of nature seem the most beautiful to me.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaKcX9tq22vgycfLR5X8YNzAzbccmPzWbHSc3Jaop2yNj/20260602_175009.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmc8W78kaPJ8tJ7YD7pXHA8xZhsNutsWMXdDNtB1nrG8Aq/20260602_174949.jpg)

The reflection of the greenery on this still water of the pond was a truly peaceful moment for me. I am really happy to participate in this contest using the tag SMARP (Show Me A Reflection Picture).

Many thanks to Olga (@olgavita) and Melinda (@melinda010100) for organizing such a wonderful contest. Everyone stay well, stay close to nature!


(All posts are written in Bengali and translated into English using Google Translate.)

links.title: Does The School You Attend Really Matter? My Answer As A Student And Teacher Is Yes.
links.body:
I can't say, or I can't be so sure, but I believe we will all have our various opinions on this amazing topic. But for me, it is a big yes, the school we go to does matter.



Right from creche, to kindergarten, to nursery, pre nursery, primary, secondary and up to the tertiary level. It all matters. As a student that I once was and as a teacher that I am at the moment, I've seen and understood things better, and I can tell you for a fact that schools go beyond teaching just subjects, they shape values and attitudes, and even relationships because we meet various people all coming from different backgrounds.


![1000718621.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marsdave/23xVM1nY3TXzWNcVxoPTottsozt9nmPkfqg1M8d7vKGoyPecmM18KuyuR6ZvBFo2MdVGF.jpg)



Also, the school I'm teaching in is one that has no staff of their own, they depend mainly on we corpers, so imagine the kind of experience the students will be having, when they don't have a permanent teacher, you can t compare that school to one that has stable and permanent teachers. 



But then, I will love to focus mainly on higher institutions, because that is where we get to make major decisions and focus on a certain career or course to go for....this is not to say that other levels in education are not important.



First off, I agree that two student can be in different schools and be taught the same thing, but the way it is being taught, the environment of learning, the facilities, equipments and all that is supposed to aid and facilitate learning can or will definitely be different.




If for instance a person is aiming at learning a technical course, one that he or she will have access to equipments, machines and the most practical part of things, you will agree with me that. A university and a polytechnic can help with such courses, but you will also agree with me that it will be best for such a person to opt for a polytechnic because polytechnics are known for their practicals, and not just focusing on theories. Opting for a university is not bad, I'm just saying which one focuses on handling such equipments, learning hand on skills, doing practicals and all of that, the other mean more towards research and theories. 




The sad part of everything is just the bias that most people have towards other schools. We have people who look down on college of education students, some look down on those who attended nursing schools, some on those of us that attended a polytechnic. They believe the university is superior and that no other schools can impact knowledge like a university will. I actually don't agree with that and never will. Every institution serves its own purpose, some of us who went to a polytechnic did have scores and grades that would have made us gain admission into a university. 

![1000718723.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marsdave/23xenLLFYPvWHwkA5tQYEuHaEFiNsyXDhkTGm8tAD95yeYHKEYFLQxSmLow3gkfzgWrfS.jpg)



We just need to understand certain things. College of educations produce teachers which we won't stop needing, nursing schools as well produces nurses that we will always need, technical schools as well produces technicians that will always be needed and same goes to a university too.. . I'm just saying that every institution has and serves its own purpose.


So, depending on ones future career, the school you go to or choose to go to is important. As much as the school we go to matter, what we the students do as well matters, if we are indeed making the best use of the opportunity and what's made available for us. Because the most important thing is to be focused on learning and growing.







🌹

**Images are mine.**

**Thanks a lot for taking your time to read through, kindly do well to stop by my blog @marsdave for more exclusive and amazing content.**

❣️❣️❣️

links.title: Choose Action
links.body:
>

I have been pretty active so far today, since I haven't been sitting as much as normal, but I still have a ways to go to be *active enough.* The Oura ring tracks my movement and most days I am sedentary (not including sleep) between 7-10 houra a day. That is quite a lot, however I don't think it tells the whole story, since I usually only sleep around 5-6 hours a night, whereas most are 7-8. The evenings are the worst for my activity of course, since I sit down and write until well past midnight most evenings, barely moving. The days though, I am pretty active, though I could get some more steps in. 


---


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tarazkp/23vhnqkDQPPzYUeeY4wv5KRuryVyMkCewJc63kh2pGqb3zQwvkPmuDg2q54DHtEEeVqua.png)


---

Looking at some of the general trends though, I am doing pretty well at meeting daily goals (which seems to mostly calculate based on steps, but I add in my gym workouts there, where I am currently averaging 5.5 a week for the last six months, which is well above my year average of 4.2. I must have been pretty lazy last year!

---

<div class=\

ticked up into the *Strong* range for the first time, with the last four months seeing quite a shift as for the year prior, I have spent most of the time in the *Adequate* range, which is largely because I don't recover enough at night when sleeping, or during the day. This is likely also affected by my workout frequency, but it is working for me at this point of life. \n\nAs a kid I was athletic, but I can't remember a time in my adult life where I didn't have aches or pains in my body. I think I have become accustomed to feeling uncomfortable to the point that it is my normal and when I feel a little better, it feels great. But I suspect that if the \

person could experience the feelings of my body for a day, they wouldn't enjoy it a lot. But, I am in better condition than many others, albeit comparing *how we feel* is impossible and quite futile. Perhaps one day with AI, AR and some nerve stimulation, we could experience \

accurately. > Though like all tech, it would mostly be used for porn. Tracking everything is pretty useless *unless* it is changing behaviours, and I think since I got the ring a little more than a year ago, I have changed many parts of my daily activity to walk a little more, go to the gym a little more, eat a little better, but also take time to rest when I have the chance. It has been a relatively passive reminder (I don't get many notifications from it) to stay active and perhaps more importantly, shows when I am *inactive.* I reckon a lot of people overestimate how much they do and underestimate how sedentary they actually are. It is the same with screen time spent, where those who actually use a tracker and check it, tend to use their phone less. Most of life is about getting more, but with the screen time trackers, it is about keeping the number as small as possible. I monitor my daughter's phone usage and she is under thirty minutes a day most days, and 80% of that is listening to an audiobook or singing karaoke. Her phone is usually on silent, and has no notifications. > My own usage is far, far worse. But I have only just started tracking the screen time on my phone and also seeing where that time goes. Now, my goal is to cut out the unnecessary, non-value-adding activity and push that time to something more useful that I really enjoy. Or rest more. As said, tracking is useless information unless it is going to be used to change behaviour, and I think quite a few people get attracted to checking the numbers, but not using those numbers to make new choices. If we don't make new choices, the path we are on remains the same, and if we are heading downhill, our decline will get faster. Do you track something? links.title: Why fulfillment is the most overlooked part of business
links.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSbpUVQ4Tdk3sgCBXng9UDhQeGUjpcVKjQnrLoda1F89q/img_7845.png)

WHY FULFILLMENT IS THE MOST OVERLOOKED PART OF BUSINESS
========================================================

Disclosure: This post contains affiliate links. If you purchase through my links, I may earn a commission at no extra cost to you.


Everyone talks about getting customers. Almost nobody talks about what happens after.

In microfinance, I get to see what happens to businesses over time. The ones that survive -- and more importantly, the ones that grow -- aren't always the ones with the best marketing. They're the ones that deliver.

Consistently. And then some.


WHAT FULFILLMENT ACTUALLY LOOKS LIKE
------------------------------------

Fulfillment isn't just doing what you said you'd do. It's a few things:

1. Overdelivering on the promise. If someone expects a ten and you give them a twelve, they talk. That's how word-of-mouth works -- not through referral programs, but through people being genuinely impressed.

2. Making the experience easy. Every point of friction between you and your customer is a reason for them to hesitate next time. The easier you are to work with, the more likely they come back.

3. Building systems that don't depend on you. If your business falls apart when you take a week off, you don't have a business. You have a job.


THE COMPOUNDING EFFECT
----------------------

Here's what most people miss: fulfillment compounds.

One happy customer tells a few people. Those people each tell a few more. Meanwhile, you're not burning money on ads to replace customers who left because you underdelivered.

The entrepreneurs who reach a point where they're not constantly chasing new business -- they all have this in common. They deliver. Reliably. And they've built systems to keep delivering as they grow.


IT'S PART OF THE SYSTEM
------------------------

The Make More Offers Challenge covers fulfillment as one of its four modules. Most business programs stop at \

Myron Golden's framework goes further -- it's about building something that grows because customers stick around and bring others.

That's the difference between a business that makes a few sales and one that actually scales.

If you want to build something sustainable:

links.title: Lucky Spin! Facing 'Al The Mountain' in Splinterlands’ Rare Pit Fight Challenge
links.body:
<center>  

## Hello all [Hive](https://leofinance.io/@leoglossary/leoglossary-what-is-hive) People & @splinterlands lovers,
 
 ![hive blockchain](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRTaRy3deTwfStEUXSsH9A6hVpvXGDpH8VpjDfvs1SCc4/image.png)

[Made with Canva](https://www.canva.com/projects)
  
  
![blockchain gaming](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRR8wiGFHrW1gYMewjrihY4P86FiomRy8DQemK4MzbFSC/untitled_design.png)

In my previous post I talked about the new section added by @splinterlands team i.e. Lux's Favor or you may say a  free wheel spin. It rewards people for login daily on site irrespective of paying the game, on other side it encourage the players to login daily on site. Players get the chance to win rewards like Spark token (which are newly added token in Splinterlnds ecosystem), Frontier energy (to play more frontier mode battles), skin/items and a rarest reward which is **Pit Fight Challenge**. Do not forget that maintaining the streak in wheel spin is also rewarding as you will get extra bonuses. In the below screenshot you can clearly see that their are total 24 slots on wheel and only one slot for Pit Fight Challenge, which means 4.17% percentage winning chance.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTWosZAe69V66A6ZyfxBFLaYxyR6i8BfzsvhoXW7yExA5/image.png)

Recently I got luck and get a chance to participate in Pit Fight Challenge. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRERGzWGvniwuRfbzAut3mis7KjsHkdi5KTmRBUQwiKJN/image.png)

I was super excites as I was seeing this first time and also not seen any post on same, I guess its very rare to get that is the reason people do not get chance to post about same.  Lets see what we get inside a Pit Fight Challenge. 

Along with Pit Challenge received sparks also (check the above screenshot). I was not able to find any tab where I can check the Spark history. If anyone know please let me know in the comment section and do not forget to login daily to try your luck with free spin.

![blockchain gaming](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRR8wiGFHrW1gYMewjrihY4P86FiomRy8DQemK4MzbFSC/untitled_design.png)

## Pit Fight Challenge 

Once you get the chance of Pit Challenge you have to complete the fight in defined time so it comes with two day expiry and clock shows the time remaining to participate. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXJvXfu1hLUgpgWoNGZhKyDHux8tnoCEAzfUK48Pw5yb9/image.png)

In the above screenshot, you can see a timer highlighter in rectangle 1. I decided to participate immediately as I was too much curios to know more about same. Their are three modes available to play which varies from Easy to Hard, the rewards are also based on the option players choose to battle. The Spark token rewards varies form 250 to 1000 Sparks, the higher rewards are 4x then the lower rewards. I decide to go with easy mode as I was playing for the firsts time.


![blockchain gaming](https://images.ecency.com/DQmRR8wiGFHrW1gYMewjrihY4P86FiomRy8DQemK4MzbFSC/untitled_design.png)

**Pit Fight Challenge** is like Boss fighting, team battle against the Boss. It was 99 mama battle and the **AL THE MOUNTAIN**  with two speed, 4 Melee attack, 5 shield, 42 health was ready for fight (along with two abilities). 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVCPSEGxnRmKeKwFNvDTqYaRvzFDzkWTA5NmnDYJtoDQX/image.png)

I choose the Water team against the **AL THE MOUNTAIN** as water team is one of the strongest team in Foundation series. Below is the screenshot shows my team lineup.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdTEtBG67WL9ysDLTRpcCSbvgLcshX4hD1djEuJKbr4TS/image.png)

After the end of round 1, the **AL THE MOUNTAIN**  lost the 13 health and 5 shield.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmc5tjXrZzZa25tGbkd8PfgSzAL4yEp8xVbKPf1mqvjZee/image.png)

After the end of round 2 **AL THE MOUNTAIN**  lost 13 more health and my first line up cards was also getting exhausted. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXjarefr79MsM2ZkEeFuUaD63WHXfre7MRwU4ofnbWg1S/image.png)

At the end of round 3 **AL THE MOUNTAIN**  was left with 3 healt only and unfortunately I also lost my fist card. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQc71zNoG7N2RJ2xkvYioW9pTj9moYpwMzLHHU3KG92jL/image.png)

The battle was ended in round 4 it self as **AL THE MOUNTAIN**  lost all the health and I was still holding my five cards. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVcNSg8M1W7QC3DbpCniMTqFwvb3jGfW7qW5kToXQJqfj/image.png)

As a reward received the 250 Sparks. Next time when I will get the chance will try the hard mode.

Following three Legendary Cards (form Neutral, Death and Water splinter) pulled form previous season loot chests. Kulu Matermind looks awesome and Drybone Raider looks dangerous. Waiting for Gold Foil Legendary.

Ojalá se sume el país entero a esta iniciativa. 

Recuerdo que cuando construí mi casa en lo que algunos aún llamaban el pueblo (barrio de Sabilar), era normal que el carro amaneciera cubierto de rocío, pero con los años este fenómeno desapareció. La ciudad siguió creciendo y la carretera se convirtió en avenida y las tierras de cultivo en urbanizaciones de casas y edificios donde, con tristeza, a nadie se le ocurrió dejar o sembrar un árbol. 
Vi con dolor cómo se talaron sin piedad mangos, guayacanes y tamarindos o almendrones. Cualquiera que con sus raíces levantara una acera fue víctima del hacha y la sierra.
Ahora se fueron las nubes; las vi pasar de largo con mucha prisa y ahora no hay canto ni llanto que las haga parar a dar sombra a tanta ingratitud.

> I hope the entire country joins this initiative.
I remember when I built my house in what some still called the village (the Sabilar neighborhood), it was normal for the car to be covered in dew in the morning, but over the years this phenomenon disappeared. The city continued to grow, and the road became an avenue, and the farmland became housing developments with houses and buildings where, sadly, no one thought to leave or plant a tree.
I watched with sorrow as mango, guayacán, and tamarind or almond trees were mercilessly cut down. Any tree whose roots supported a sidewalk fell victim to the axe and the saw.
Now the clouds are gone; I saw them rush past, and now there is no song or weeping that can make them stop to shade such ingratitude.
