title.title: Artificial intelligence is taking control.
title.body:
Artificial intelligence is taking control.


https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmXre731xE2gSAjwiFKxXTJvDAWj463JPHYaCYVXa9HWwR/image.png
>Souce

> What would the world be like if satellites not only observed the planet, but also interpreted what they see, made decisions and defined priorities and the need to wait for human commands. Space surveillance has always worked as a gigantic network of eyes spread throughout Earth's orbit, but now China wants to transform those eyes into something much more sophisticated, an artificial brain.


Chinese aerospace researchers recently revealed the Air Target Agent System, an architecture based on large language models, the same technological principles behind the conversational artificial intelligences that we know today, the difference is that in this case it is no longer answering questions, it is analyzing images captured from space and coordinating complex monitoring operations in real time.


The developers themselves describe the system as a combination between a central brain and an army of specialized tools. Instead of relying solely on conventional image recognition algorithms, the main model acts as an intelligent coordinator, distributing tasks to secondary agents capable of analyzing different types of data simultaneously. This completely changes the speed of decision making.


Traditionally, satellite images need to go through various stages of interpretation before reaching a conclusion. First capture, then processing, then human analysis and finally decision making, the new system seeks to drastically shorten that path. Artificial intelligence interprets the context of the scene, identifies patterns, prioritizes information and can even reorganize its own strategies in the face of unexpected situations.


During the tests disclosed by the researchers, the system demonstrated the ability to handle operational failures, reorganize tasks and continue executing its mission without direct human intervention, this means faster, more continuous and potentially much more efficient surveillance. But it is precisely there where an increasingly intense global discussion arises. As artificial intelligence takes on strategic roles, concerns also grow about how far that autonomy should go.


In recent years, defense, ethics and technology specialists have warned that automated systems are no longer simple support tools and are becoming central elements in the decision-making chain. According to information associated with the Chinese Academy of Sciences, the next steps include expanding testing and validating the technology in more complex and larger-scale scenarios. The goal is to further increase the operational capacity of the system, reducing dependence on human operators. And this places us before an issue that goes far beyond technology. We are entering an era in which satellites not only observe the planet, but begin to interpret events, define priorities and act as extensions of artificial intelligences distributed throughout space.


We know that these machines can already see us from Earth orbit, but how much power are we willing to give to systems that learn to observe the world on their own? My friends, when artificial eyes in space gain a brain, surveillance stops being just observation and becomes understanding and this may be one of the most profound transformations of the age of artificial intelligence. And so, in your opinion, autonomous space surveillance systems make the world safer, controllable or more unpredictable.
>Souce\n\nPosted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@bntcamelo/-artificial-intelligence-is-taking-control-7ho)

**Nerd By Northwest #369 – “A Dungeon Story”**

<a href=\
>
> --- Ah, the critical fail roll... the time for Dungeon Masters to shine! Any novice DM can fall back on a \
or \

ruling on a critical fail roll of '1'. But a good DM will use the opportunity to exercise their devious creativity and make things interesting. And a _great_ DM will come up with something special enough that players will wax nostalgic on the moment YEARS later.\n\nAs to the movie reference, if you're from the US or Canada you know the movie extremely well. Heck, I bet there are polar bears on ice floes in the far North who've seen it. But for those of you from elsewhere, \

is a family comedy film set somewhere around the late 1930's or 1940 about a young boy and his family in Indiana during Christmastime. Every Christmas season there are channels on TV and cable that show the movie all day... it's that popular there. And the scene this comic strip calls back to is easily one of the most memorable.

But for the rest of you deprived souls, you can find that memorable scene here: 
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mc6pk2FRhbA

One particular challenge of this strip was making the stuck tongue plainly obvious to the reader. I zoomed it in as much as I felt I could get away with, and made the tip of the tongue a little redder and the part of the iron bar it was stuck to a bit lighter in color. I'm not completely satisfied with it, but it's good enough for government work.

So how do _you_ think Nolan will get his tongue unstuck? No answer is too wrong! 😁

title.title: Asking for help is facing uncertainty and taking a step forward
title.body:
Why do people find it difficult to ask for help?
 It is because sometimes “help” comes with insults, uncertainties and silence feels as a safe thing to do but not completely wise.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcTv1dJa5do83TKpVftp1jwxw5i4PKCAH6EKrXtMGWdpn/1780412720264.jpg)

There has been times, I asked for help that  it became a ridicule. Some offered to help with buckets of insults and demeaning remarks. 
As a firstborn child who has been on the giving end, I always tell myself that I will find a way round it. 
Which is one of the reasons I really appreciate every help I get whether in word, kind or cash gifts a lot because it's not something that happens all the time to me.

No one is weak or lazy for needing help.
 Sometimes it is also been human to protect yourself from further ridicule and shame.
 
While seeking for help endeavor it doesn't become a routine, else you lost your sense of dignity and worth. 
Some might look at you with contempt and dismeanour especially those in position or privileged to help.

There are also people who notices that you are stuck and they offer help even before you get to ask. These kinds are rare but they exist. Sometimes, you should have a circle of friends you can count on or who can come together for you.

In my case, they always assume with great confidence that I'm doing so well. I remember a season I was so broken financially and mentally, my back was against the wall.
I reached out to someone who had enough to spare either for a loan but the man's statement was like \
but I needed money for support. \nI had to explained the situation carefully to him and the next thing \

. 

 **Even if you cannot help, be kind with your choice of words**

I felt sad about it but someone i did not expect to help was the one who bailed me out that day. 

Guess who called me again three months ago to seek help, I could have reminded him of that time but I did not but I simply asked him to pay for the service to be rendered.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdZNaNv7XgqRN7ZuCe1uUCfjDPbmaMjD5vnmDeATHjfoK/1780412786723.jpg)

Sometimes when you ask for help from others. They are might be quick to assume you are lazy or unproductive. Maybe if you worked or did extra, you would not be seeking help.
Life just happens that people lose their jobs, get sick and spend all their savings.

I often tell people that life can test you to an extent that your finances alone can't handle the problem or situation.

It takes a lot of courage and effort for me to ask for help because I'm always anxious about what the person's reaction might be.

And I do not hate people because they didn't help out. I always have in mind that  \

They have their reasons too, they could be struggling with pain or something you don't know. 
I was hurt by his response of rice but we are still in touch.  Also I have not asked him for help anymore but he has sent several gifts across to my kids on their birthdays.
He tried to apologize three years later, I told him that we have passed that stage.

title.title: My opinion about the movie \
//  Mi opinión sobre la película \
title.body:
<div class=text-justify>





![1000257522.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mariolisrnaranjo/23y8zUKgnkC4Kd7QQwBe8CGhQiwo2skx8JeP2Qbi7ZQqJSiFXDosbzrubPbN7eYMNXghR.jpg)



<Center>[Sources](https://www.imdb.com/es/title/tt0785007/mediaindex/?ref_=mv_close)</Center>




Hello, #hive friends, and especially to the Movies&TvShows community. As always, I hope you and your family and friends are doing well. Today I’m stopping by to tell you about a 2008 film titled “Over Her Dead Body,” directed and written by Jeff Lowell. It’s a lighthearted romantic comedy that combines ghosts, postmortem jealousy, and the classic story of moving on after a loss. Starring Eva Longoria, Paul Rudd, and Lake Bell, the film aims to be fun, unpretentious entertainment, though it doesn’t always manage to shine with the spark its premise promises.




![1000257523.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mariolisrnaranjo/23wCFiyx4fUoR9D1bNq26rGaPs4BKXQMruYSP9GE3QybWdFXgCEGJa7ehY6J267C6jcxL.jpg)

<Center>[Sources](https://www.imdb.com/es/title/tt0785007/mediaindex/?ref_=mv_close)</Center>


The story begins abruptly and in a tragicomic way, as Kate—played by Eva Longoria—a bride obsessed with the perfect details of her wedding, dies in an absurd manner when a giant ice sculpture falls on her. Her fiancé, Henry—played by Paul Rudd—a kind and somewhat clumsy veterinarian, is devastated. A year later, his sister Chloe, played by Lindsay Sloane, convinces him to visit a psychic, Ashley, played by Lake Bell, so she can supposedly contact Kate and give him permission to move on with his life. What starts as a farce gets complicated when Kate’s real ghost appears, furious and determined to sabotage any romance between her ex and the psychic.



![1000257527.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mariolisrnaranjo/23tvioZ8gtUyCMqtaSJB7ep9zsqLPRvBXdavbvanfZvGazpBL6jvnUVoxNpznshDSKU7j.jpg)


<Center>[Sources](https://www.imdb.com/es/title/tt0785007/mediaindex/?ref_=mv_close)</Center>


The film plays with the physical humor and absurd situations typical of the jealous ghost subgenre, but with a much more American and contemporary tone. Eva Longoria clearly has a blast in the role of the vengeful ghost, as she screams, manipulates objects, and gets up to all sorts of supernatural mischief—which is entertaining in small doses, though it sometimes veers into over-the-top territory. Paul Rudd, as always, brings his natural charisma and comedic timing, making the good-natured widower trying to heal believable. Lake Bell is probably the best part of the film, as her Ashley is eccentric, vulnerable, and charming, and the chemistry between her and Rudd is genuine and warm.



![1000257524.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mariolisrnaranjo/23uFK1oBm6j7mLCSK4nD6g2vXxHLU5qwvDnmA31zYevV5uHd5EhGQkH4LKnFPVKUNzc3z.jpg)



<Center>[Sources](https://www.imdb.com/es/title/tt0785007/mediaindex/?ref_=mv_close)</Center>


Where the film falters is in its screenplay. Many jokes feel predictable, and the development of the central relationship moves at a forced pace. The subplot involving Ashley’s best friend, Jason Biggs—who harbors a secret—adds little and feels like filler. Lowell’s direction is functional, but lacking any notable visual personality; the film looks good, with bright cinematography typical of romantic comedies of the era, but it doesn’t stand out. However, despite its flaws, it works as an escapist comedy. It has genuinely funny moments, primarily in the interactions between Kate and Ashley, which are the highlights.




![1000257526.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mariolisrnaranjo/23tvkxWeVVJ99zWxwxGW4icFM4yeGGtv9omsTpXSygTeYMpg14TtqjjDKWBZzT6ZtHPrP.jpg)


<Center>[Sources](https://www.imdb.com/es/title/tt0785007/mediaindex/?ref_=mv_close)</Center>


The film delivers a positive message about letting go of the past and opening your heart to love again, and it also features a cast that fully embraces the absurdity. It’s not a masterpiece, nor does it claim to be. It’s simply the kind of movie you pop in on a Sunday afternoon, expecting some easy laughs and a predictable—yet satisfying—ending. So, in short, friends, if you’re looking for a lighthearted supernatural romantic comedy with good actors and no grand ambitions, this one is perfect, since it doesn’t reinvent the genre but more than fulfills its goal of providing a pleasant time. Without further ado, I bid you farewell, and I’ll see you next time. Blessings galore.




![1000257525.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mariolisrnaranjo/243M2nPhuQjHeCL1djeRs8EdgEvHbDMPRYeYNRatMGZBvJE5mpAd1FBPAmx3WGhGcjmnx.jpg)

<Center>[Sources](https://www.imdb.com/es/title/tt0785007/mediaindex/?ref_=mv_close)</Center>




<div class=\

> The sources for the images used in this post have been provided. Texts translated into English by [DeepL Translate](https://www.deepl.com/mobile-apps/?utm_source=android&utm_medium=app&utm_campaign=share-with-friends). ‎
‎VERSIÓN EN ESPAÑOL (click aquí!)

Hola amigos de #hive y en especial a la comunidad de Movies&TvShows, como siempre espero que se encuentren bien al igual que sus familiares y amigos. En el día de hoy paso por acá para hablarles de una película titulada \
o conocida en el inglés como \

del los años 2008, la misma está dirigida y escrita por Jeff Lowell y es una comedia romántica ligera, que combina fantasmas, celos postmortem y además la clásica historia de seguir adelante después de una pérdida. Protagonizada por Eva Longoria, Paul Rudd y Lake Bell, la cinta busca ser un entretenimiento divertido y sin pretensiones, aunque no siempre logra brillar con la chispa que promete su premisa.





La historia comienza de forma abrupta y tragicómica, ya que Kate papel que desempeña Eva Longoria, que es una novia obsesionada con los detalles perfectos de su boda, muere de manera absurda cuando una escultura de hielo gigante cae sobre ella. Su prometido, Henry papel que desempeña Paul Rudd, un veterinario amable y algo torpe, queda devastado. Un año después, su hermana Chloe papel interpretado por Lindsay Sloane, lo convence de visitar a una médium, Ashley papel que realiza Lake Bell, para que supuestamente contacte a Kate y le dé permiso para seguir con su vida. Lo que empieza como una farsa, se complica cuando el fantasma real de Kate aparece, furiosa y decidida a sabotear cualquier romance entre su ex y la médium.





La película juega con el humor físico y las situaciones absurdas típicas del subgénero de fantasmas celosos, pero con un tono mucho más estadounidense y contemporáneo. Eva Longoria se divierte claramente en el rol de fantasma vengativo, ya que grita, manipula objetos y hace todo tipo de travesuras sobrenaturales que resulta divertida en pequeñas dosis, aunque a veces cae en la exageración. Paul Rudd, como siempre, aporta su carisma natural y timing cómico, haciendo creíble al viudo bonachón que intenta sanar. Lake Bell es probablemente lo mejor de la cinta, ya que su Ashley es excéntrica, vulnerable y encantadora, y la química entre ella y Rudd es genuina y cálida.






Donde la película flaquea es en su guion. Muchas bromas se sienten predecibles y el desarrollo de la relación central avanza con rapidez forzada. La relación con el mejor amigo de Ashley Jason Biggs, que esconde un secreto, añade poco y parece relleno. La dirección de Lowell es funcional, pero sin personalidad visual destacable, la película se ve bien, ya que posee una fotografía luminosa, típica de las comedias románticas de la época, pero no destaca. Sin embargo, a pesar de sus defectos, cumple como comedia escapista. La misma tiene momentos genuinamente graciosos y fundamentalmente en las interacciones entre Kate y Ashley, que son lo más destacado.





La cinta nos muestra un mensaje positivo sobre dejar ir el pasado y aceptar el amor de nuevo, y además cuenta con un elenco que se entrega al disparate. No es una obra maestra ni pretende serlo. Es simplemente el tipo de película que uno pone un domingo por la tarde esperando risas fáciles y un final previsible, pero satisfactorio, así que en resumen, amigos, si buscas una comedia romántica sobrenatural ligera con buenos actores y sin grandes ambiciones, esta entrega es la ideal, ya que no reinventa el género, pero cumple con creces su objetivo de pasar un rato agradable. Yo sin más me despido de ustedes y nos vemos hasta la próxima peli. Bendiciones miles.

title.title: [Esp-Eng] Exploring and Breathing in Buenos Aires-Argentina 2026
title.body: \n
alt=\

>

<hr>

<div class=\

> This year, for my birthday, Ru and I decided to take a quick one-week trip to Buenos Aires, one of my favorite cities. The mix of old and modern architecture makes you feel like you’re in Europe; in my opinion, the architecture is very similar to that of France. Plus, the friendliness of the people is a real bonus—they make you feel right at home.

> Este año por mi cumpleaños Ru y yo decidimos hacer un viaje express de una semana por Buenos Aires, una de mis ciudades favoritas. La mezcla de arquitectura antigua y moderna hacen que te sientas como en europa, la arquitectura es muy parecida a la de Francia en mi opinión. Además, la amabilidad de la gente es un plus, hacen que te sientas en confianza.
alt=\

>

<hr>

<div class=\

> We traveled right in the middle of March; the weather was perfect because it wasn’t too hot yet. Coincidentally, it was a holiday that week, and the city was a bit empty, so there wasn’t much traffic. At first, we had a sort of itinerary, but due to time and distance, we later decided to buy tickets for a 24-hour tour on the Buenos Aires City Bus.

> Viajamos exactamente a mediados de marzo, el clima estaba perfecto porque no hacía ya tanto calor, casualmente era feriado esa semana y la ciudad estaba un poco vacía, así que no había mucho tráfico. Al principio, teníamos una especie de itinerario, pero por el tiempo y la distancia decidimos luego comprar boletos para hacer un tour de 24 horas en el Buenos Aires City Bus.
alt=\

>




<hr>

<div class=\

> The first neighborhood we visited was La Boca; there was a game that day, so it was packed with fans everywhere. Honestly, words can’t do justice to the excitement you feel in the streets seeing so many people gathered for the same reason: to watch Boca Juniors play. We didn’t have tickets to the game, but we took a walk around the area, visited the famous Caminito, and then went to buy some souvenirs. I took the opportunity to buy my Boca jersey, because yes, I’m a Xeneize too.

> El primer barrio que visitamos fue La Boca, ese día había partido y pues estaba lleno de hinchas por todos lados. Honestamente, me quedaría corta describiendo la emoción que se siente en las calles de ver a tanta gente reunida por un mismo motivo, ver jugar a Boca Juniors. No teníamos entrada para el juego, pero nos dimos una vuelta por los alrededores, visitamos el tan famoso Caminito y luego fuimos a comprar algunos souvenires. Yo aproveché para comprar mi camiseta de Boca, porque sí, también soy Xeneize.
alt=\
>
alt=\
>
alt=\
>
alt=\

>

<hr>

<div class=\

> From there, we walked to Puerto Madero; the atmosphere there is different—just as festive and full of tourists, but at the same time more relaxed. One of the places where we absolutely wanted to take a photo was the Puente de la Mujer, but it was almost impossible that day—it was packed with people. Still, we had a great time because we were soaking up Buenos Aires.

> De ahí, nos fuimos caminando hasta Puerto Madero, ahí el ambiente es diferente, igual de festivo y lleno de turistas pero a la vez más tranquilo. Uno de los lugares donde si o si queríamos tomar una foto era en el puente de la mujer pero, casi imposible ese día, estaba abarrotado de gente. Igual, la pasamos genial porque estábamos respirando Buenos Aires.
alt=\
>
alt=\
>
alt=\
>
alt=\
>
alt=\
>
alt=\
>
alt=\

>

<hr>

<div class=\

> The next day, we took a stroll through downtown; we wanted to check out Galerías Pacífico and then head to the Obelisk. We just walked around a bit, took our respective photos, and then headed to the Casa Rosada. Since it was a national holiday, there were many cultural events taking place in the surrounding area, so the building’s facade was closed off.

> Al siguiente día, nos dimos una vuelta por el centro, queríamos conocer galerías pacífico y de ahí irnos hacia el obelisco. Sólo dimos unas vueltas, tomamos nuestras respectivas fotos y luego fuimos hacia la casa rosada. Cómo era feriado nacional, había en los alrededores muchos actos culturales así que la fachada del lugar estaba cerrada.
alt=\
>
alt=\
>
alt=\

>

<hr>

<div class=\

> That same day, we came across a Buenos Aires City Bus stop, and well, at first I wasn’t too sure about these buses, but it was a good decision to buy the 24-hour tour. About $38–$39 per ticket, converted to Argentine pesos—it all depends on the bank’s exchange rate. This service, while it might be a bit pricey for some tourists, is an excellent option because you can visit the city’s various tourist attractions and landmarks. This particular company has several stops, and the buses usually arrive on time at each station. We took the 24-hour tour because we were also planning to travel to Uruguay. If you can’t complete the tour on the same day, you can finish it the next day before the time of purchase; you just need to go to the stop closest to your destination and take one of their red buses. Plus, they explain the history of each place in Spanish and English; you can listen through headphones they give you once you board for the first time.

> Ese mismo día, nos encontramos con una estación de Buenos Aires City Bus, y bueno, al principio como que no le tenía mucha fe a estos buses, pero fue una buena decisión comprar el tour de 24 horas. Unos 38-39 dólares por cada boleto, al cambio de moneda a pesos argentinos, todo depende de la tasa del banco. Este servicio, aunque pueda resultar un poco costoso para algunos turistas, es una excelente opción porque puedes recorrer los diferentes puntos turísticos y emblemáticos de la ciudad, esta empresa en particular cuenta con varias paradas y los buses suelen llegar a tiempo a cada estación. Nosotros, hicimos el tour durante 24 horas porque también íbamos a viajar a Uruguay, si no puedes hacer el recorrido el mismo día, puedes terminar al día siguiente antes de la hora de compra, solo debes ir hacia la parada más cercana a tu destino y tomar alguno de sus buses que son color rojo. Además, te van explicando la historia de cada lugar en español y en inglés, puedes escuchar a través de unos auriculares que te dan una vez que subes por primera vez.
alt=\

>

<hr>

<div class=\

> There, I took the opportunity to return to La Bombonera at a more leisurely pace, and we went into the Museo de la Pasión Boquense. Each ticket cost $24. There, you can see all the trophies, learn more about the team’s history, and see the field. If you’re a soccer fan, you’ll love this tour.

> Ahí aproveché para volver a la bombonera con más calma y entramos al museo de la Pasión Boquense, cada entrada costó 24 dólares, ahí puedes ver todos los trofeos, conocer más de la historia del equipo y ver la cancha, si eres fanático del fútbol, este recorrido te encantará.
alt=\
>
alt=\

>

<hr>

<div class=\

> Afterward, we visited the Japanese Garden and the Ecopark, two places where you can relax by walking among the trees and enjoying the scenery. Admission to the Japanese Garden costs money; it’s cheaper if you’re an Argentine resident or citizen. Since we were foreign tourists, we paid about $17 per ticket. The place is small, but it’s worth visiting because the grounds are very well maintained, and it feels like being in a little piece of Japan right in the heart of Buenos Aires. From there, we headed to the Ecopark. Both places are relatively close, so we walked there. That day, they asked for ID at the entrance; we had copies of our passports on our phones, and that was enough to get in for free. Honestly, I’m not really into visiting these kinds of places because I love animals, but I prefer seeing them in their natural habitat. Luckily, the animals I saw were practically free to roam around the park. It feels very peaceful inside because of all the trees and vegetation, plus it’s very cool and quiet—ideal for visiting with kids.

> Después, estuvimos visitando el parque japonés y el ecoparque, dos lugares donde puedes relajarte caminando entre los árboles y disfrutar del paisaje. Por su parte, la entrada al parque japonés tiene un costo, si eres residente o ciudadano argentino es más barato, nosotros por ser turistas extranjeros pagamos unos 17 dólares por cada entrada. Es pequeño el lugar, pero vale la pena visitar, porque las instalaciones están muy bien cuidadas y es como estar en un pedacito de Japón dentro de Buenos Aires. De ahí, nos fuimos hasta el ecoparque, ambos lugares están relativamente cerca, así que nos fuimos caminando, ese día en la entrada nos pidieron identificación, teníamos una copia de los pasaportes en el teléfono y ya con eso entras gratis. Sinceramente, no soy visitar este tipo de lugares porque me encantan los animales, pero verlos en su habitad natural pero, por suerte los animales que vi, están prácticamente libres caminando por el lugar, se siente mucha paz aquí adentro por la cantidad de árboles y vegetación, además de ser muy fresco y tranquilo, ideal para ir con niños.
alt=\
>
alt=\
>
alt=\
>
alt=\
>
alt=\
>
alt=\
>
alt=\
>
alt=\

>

<hr>

<div class=\

> Finally, we made an almost mandatory stop in Chinatown. Unlike others I’ve visited, this one feels safer despite being crowded—another place worth visiting if you’re traveling to Buenos Aires. Here you can see the city’s Asian contrast, plus you have plenty of options for eating and buying souvenirs. Without a doubt, Buenos Aires is one of my favorite places because there’s always something to do. This city has something for everyone, and it seems like it never sleeps. Of course, we’ll be back to the City of Fury.

> Por último, hicimos una parada casi necesaria en el barrio chino, a diferencia de otros que he visitado este a pesar de estar lleno de gente se siente más seguro, otro lugar que vale la pena visitar si viajas a Buenos Aires, aquí puedes ver el contraste asiático de la ciudad, además de que tienes muchas opciones para comer y comprar algún recuerdo. Sin duda, Buenos Aires, es de mis lugares favoritos porque siempre hay algo por hacer, esta ciudad está hecha para todos los gustos, además de que pareciera nunca dormir, por supuesto que volveremos a la ciudad de la furia.

title.title: Gardening successes
title.body:
This has been my favourite season for many years. It's a lot of work, but I slowly see how my garden is changing and I have even started harvesting already. From now on, it's a lettuce day everyday 😊 

Last year, I didn't do anything with my elderflower as I had a couple of bottles with syrup from the year before, but this year I managed to make almost 7 litres which I poured in small bottles and will share them with our neighbours, friends and family. I love changing our produce into something delicious when I finally find time to do that. The process of making elderflower syrup takes time, but it is so worth it. Half of the bottles are infused with rosemary which gives the syrup a little bit bitter taste that will be perfect for cocktails and the other half is pure. 

![1.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EoK7jeKFi6eDFuz69FQFfLr7rEmJANTphHJDAGAnRZ8HWmS6QseXnnwmpf9ooCP1ceh.jpg)
-----
When I look at my bush at the moment I feel like I should still do something with all those flowers. You might say that I should let them be and enjoy the berries later, but the birds wouldn't let me. They pick all of them and the bush is bare by the time the berries should be ripe. It's either harvesting the flowers or nothing.  

![1a.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EqazhjXkbuFirTwwaQvMqSSPXG6VnXv4Cx8kSFRfFK22dkaM9ALCQDUe3HH1YSDD7Qf.jpg)
----
My mom mentioned that I could try to make fermented elderflower lemonade which I found a great idea. I have some experience in fermenting, but it's always a gamble for me - is it going to be fermented or will I make vinegar again? I prepared the lemonade 4 days ago. I stir it twice a day and taste it every time. It's actually very good. I give it one more day and then we will enjoy it. 

![2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EpCAwuD58AqRvw3KtRLhVJwzuMJoSur8tRmHtaN2hEQx1dSVTJh96pVT4K78AFzARFv.jpg)
----
This is the place where the lemonade is spending days. In the evening, I bring it inside to slow down the fermentation and to protect it from the cats that roam our garden at night. 

I wonder what else I can make with those delicious flowers...

![3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/Ep3gep7xEag3yVwrR9VNNnUbjZwYSpmaLnAPVbQgBFLvu4o2kNNBTmxYAcHEJQ95hQT.jpg)
-----
Years ago, I learned to harvest lettuce by taking only the outer leaves and live the heart untouched so that it can produce more leaves. This practice works so well for us, and every time we have tender young leaves instead of big lettuce heads. This was our very first harvest from last week. The plants took off and we simply can't eat them all, so I will be preparing lettuce bouquets for our neighbours soon.

![4.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EpA41tJLeGaGUDPE9XCY7iJYbAumtWAQGvC4F4VwfjKKFoYcjaaHDUtwBNeopZBNo6Y.jpg)
-----
Radishes are coming too. Honestly, I love them, but I prefer the green part. This makes amazing pesto. I take radish and carrot greens, some garlic, any nuts that I have at hand, lemon, salt, pepper, nutritional yeast, olive oil and ice cubes, blend it all together and enjoy it over pasta topped with grilled cherry tomatoes. So good! 

![5.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EpEJJP8Hfyb6gkfJbwLFctMqorqt74G6ybBnyDybPtubEDCKD8PVJ1wKQERZcb1Psfd.jpg)
----
I have never had luck with beans. Every time, I planted them, the slugs would eat as soon as they germinated and that killed them. This is the first year when I have seen success! There are a few of them that slugs destroyed, but I will put some more beans in those spot to close the gaps. 

![6.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EoiWCQ1jukUCSmEpRGgThMt414Vkmn27N7ZVcZaTA1UY8aYNGFpxwSjaYLNZzgkyhRS.jpg)
----
I planted tons of beans as I didn't expect many to come out and now I wonder what I will do with all those beans? 

![7.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EoiW9ZVurLWYt94USKPg1da35HEXxasGmGqjbaj8XAnTLARhbeumHpgmULfJrCoVJAL.jpg)
----
This year, I didn't manage to start tomatoes from the seeds, but my neighbours were so kind to give me 12 plants. This is the perfect amount for my greenhouse. I planted them last week and so far they are looking great. 

![8.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EogQFwFFvLSdd4wwn15JH4FFNiABY12veF1TukKjDHXQchCcTie7aUsu3DyezXhggNG.jpg)
----
Peppers are super strong this year. I have 24 of them and a couple of chillies. These varieties look the same and when I was planting them I got distracted by a podcast and now I have no idea which are regular peppers and which are chillies. Well, that will be a surprise later on.  

![9.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EpT56vAAHvcsmgWs8ziReQxVn4XysdTcFU7yDVYBWwf2HFhnvD2YHFLoGHTGW7Mv3J9.jpg)
----
Cucumbers and basil are growing well too. If it's going to be a good cucumber year then I will have enough to feed the entire street. 

![10.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EoGypRzYkdgyGY3ReSjyZ5iEgeCFZXLVmk16YxhfkyUPxoosGkTay1yyEcUQF3xisAx.jpg)
---
More cucumbers... But this is the pickling variety. I never make pickles, but we love those tiny cucumbers. If it's a good year, I would expect around 200 cucumbers out of these 6 plants - based on my prior experience with this variety. 

![11.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EoAbE8fdVCfvwDZqpvHxAuV1F8JizR7ZPUpwXj1mLZmfVv2qzJr7xtWneewR9e5Jjij.jpg)
----
I also have 2 green and 2 yellow zucchinis. They are very prolific, so this might even be too much...

![12.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EogPD7Nk7B7r5KK5rdmmf8K5zVZWNfqXYKoupoBL8uH7vDkWsa9CwXJ3xnjUuh9cRV2.jpg)
----
Not everything goes as planned though. I have planted so many dill seeds that actually germinated, but got burned by sun. This is the only survivor.

![13.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/Eo4CUXgtQKPsUnQNxxTNG8i6Z3BgaSgKKFwQpdJbFnJm22jfTe9EwQZGJA55nMq6Mpv.jpg)
---
And now to my flower collection...

I can't stop admiring my Love in a mist flowers. I have three shades of blue, but I would also love to have the white ones. I have seen them in my neighbour garden, so I will take some seeds to plant for next year and then my collection will be complete. 

![14.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/Eopssp4YKEhXALZAo8wV4Nw8hZwh5CZP3ftw2V8MbRVVAVE7b7r5Ygn3D4wwRqX2jrp.jpg)

![15.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EoCiaZt9gz2hMFXkZGiNJawsNPskSiU2Ruz5XNceWTcGBHmEoN2KDEY9kWzpFAxUczR.jpg)
----
They are so precious!

![16.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EoK5RBiSLCETVwHMtapXsNYjq26zbCSTdu11baHHshjXPrm7sibPY6xTPBtmbbbiWkV.jpg)
----
This has been a very good year for roses. I'm still learning how to prune them, and it looks like I'm getting better at it as there are so many of them. All of my roses are fragrant and smell so good. 

![17.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EpEJL7DNyJ5iiAgrMXS4jtQDG5eYoNP7eJMZ7LY2VJ5tK4qxY7AAx4texu96HzSsDgm.jpg)

![18.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EoptvsxuuVGF6FrhcMpMrnSe72GndWmpqaFVfHXJzD34nWd4GtnVrfknpu1qBK25GMV.jpg)

![18a.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EoK7L9FXLoRYRokvRwfGcEe2h1WbxQseqxa1ePVgVuF2jGH3QWsbSPG8uh7kStrP7hi.jpg)

![19.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EoiUoEBHnEqAUGAW4SBKPw3XoRsJW36Y1js9x7NeKUBbBFDRaG4W43VqsK8wy7tCH2Q.jpg)

![20.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EopryJadg9wqkhL2Rc6FJPPDLQQGZbngvtoHMSCKVfAKAaTp2Fb4Ju1hmnebwddaPb3.jpg)

![21.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/Eq38a3FUCSoUKVvrpe2XGT9qG72qVGgQ795VciyfB3BHrDoWXsGLcakrDBn8iPetLHW.jpg)

![22.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EoiTEbsE873toPm5k2QaYKhgevb4nv6R2JJf2UmocWXJDrhoyqvyDkWWcDB2193UZNY.jpg)

![23.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EoeESXt8gFMLMwbddYpe4DtAe9ZHRwRMP67tA7tE3pvnYFPkVeJz9tWL4G3c7mPgqsk.jpg)

![24.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EogMRFdw7NE9wMxMENKYHdpbriurSxLVyogZnn2H3oFCAuyzAbhEEDXqk3k3R1dXVLB.jpg)
----
Peonies have been beautiful too. They're almost done, so I will soon remove the stalks that flowered and leave the leaves for the plant to get some energy for next year. I have never been into planting flowers, and it makes me so happy when I see these successes because it means that I'm getting better at it. 

![25.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EoGwtN7DWpPGmpTw4aEBsodQMMN1v6MLYThUkjiGsB7UwDffXknKeZPMB2x8v1T4JJc.jpg)


![26.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/Eokce7MVuW6hSmXmLc2PvvwJt6gCKvb2meg64YZVBEuGgU1pWg6Nop78ayVbkmcQqVH.jpg)

![27.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/Ep5nBLR5z9eF33ijtLH8XCapVaEj3MPtcea8G1xTZhSCjBtHLLkEAipQFYfcp3iwCd6.jpg)
----
Lady's mantle is that plant that I would recommend to everyone. You simply can't kill it and the more you neglect it the stronger it gets. How convenient! 

![28.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EoK4w3T9CBG4kkT2Nxp4w1hfuuMX3U4LQKyrN4GEaYe5aGFeRzv9KqJh4HTmPVNkcUc.jpg)
---
Heuchera would be number 2. I haven't done anything with this plant for years and it still comes back with beautiful purple foliage. 

![29.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EoK5KRF9hoCvQfk381hwiK9YmNqiLdDjMYMQ5waZKw8RBvn9NMM2sAptyxB7iGd3Jxf.jpg)
----
It looks like there will be many calendulas this year. This plant appears all over the garden and I love it as it repels pests and attracts beneficial insects. 

![30.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EoeDU5QEiFR3EupSzmAkVghP92925NGpASfwfbeLg2RVzUT7DQoRqfCKFJ5V8Qj9ZMk.jpg)
----
Snails are always welcome in my garden as they eat slugs eggs. This one seems to have had an accident and I hope it wasn't me who stepped on it. 

![31.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/Eou9kMaLLkbHh5FkTSfe7ARwwZv9ohawWtMAxsiJyjYf6MeTiuPAtqgw1ejeYAMFZME.jpg)
----
When those roses and rosemary grow a bit more we won't be able to see our garden house anymore 😊

![32.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/delishtreats/EpLfUXSu7RJmkdBxrpoLdhq7itmtFvQzvi9uJDvL8KfB2WvtU1hUQBiwDnMoHgbKUcg.jpg)
----
Sharing here motivates me to take photos of my garden which I tend to forget. I love looking back at those photos and see huge difference that happen in such a short period of time - the magic of Hive. 

Thank you for reading and until next time...

title.title: Anxiety and Depression
title.body: alt=\

/>

It is truly heartbreaking to know that so many people struggle with anxiety, depression, and everything that life can throw at them. In today's fast-paced world, countless individuals are silentlystruggling with issues that aren't always visibleto others. Many people may appear successfuland happy on the outside, but inside, they might be overwhelmed by feelings of stress, fear, and exhaustion.

Anxiety and depression are common issues that plague people of all ages. Anxiety can cause an individual to worry about what is coming next, fear failing, or simply be nervous in everyday situations. Depression can lead to feelings of sadness, emptiness, and loss of interest in activities one once enjoyed. These issues can lead to troubles with friendships, relationships, work performance, schooling, and overall quality of life.

What makes many of these struggles so painful is the fact that life keeps moving forward. People still have responsibilities that need attending to. Students need to stay on track in school and get their work done, parents need to raise children and support their families, and workers have to do their best at their jobs. Simultaneously, problems like debt, family drama, health issues, and social pressures create a huge burden. The struggle of coping with anxiety or depression and still attending to life can feel absolutely exhausting.

Many people are afraid to reach out to others because of a fear of being judged or not being understood. They may feel like they have to solve all of their own problems or that if they ask for help, they are weak. This unfortunately leads to a much higher chance of having these feelings get worse. It is crucial that one remember that mental health is a real issue, not something that you do wrong. Getting help from a friend, family member, therapist or doctor is a sign of strength.

We, as people in society, need to be more aware and more empathetic toward people who are struggling. Someone or a helping hand can make a world of difference in a person's life. You can never truly know what someone else is fighting against so always approach others with understanding.

Even though problems such as anxiety and depression make it feel as though they do not, there is hope. You will most likely be able to recover or learn ways to manage with the help of therapy, friends, healthy habits, or doctors. Recovery will probably take some time but it is still possible.

title.title: On the Beach.
title.body:
Every game has a story, but some moments deserve to be frozen in time. Alpha Gamer here, bringing you today's visual journey.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZjSFqT7vuVdXioqTnKPE1BcykRg2oJnPAQvxWQYcVtD8/image.png)

I am incredibly glad to be back in this beautifully haunting world. Seeing Lou again, now as a living, incredibly cute baby, instantly brought back all the emotional weight of the first game and made me realize just how much I missed this universe.

When I first stepped into the original Death Stranding, I was completely blown away by its unique atmosphere and cinematic storytelling. It quickly became a game I deeply loved, and ever since completing that journey, I have been eagerly waiting for this next installment.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQmsKs3CoaVE3iWnU3ohMYtCMavVjVV4cRftCX5UgyPh6/screenshot_1_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmY8aQzmJmHdqF16M1PWUmBsVVox7PxKDyPegGZ3s19AWF/screenshot_2_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmV4cxxan7g4HFGdTN3CFmsxXQvhECx7nh55yWEZRsgHdR/screenshot_3_.png)

The opening of this new installment absolutely amazed me, especially when I saw the incredibly detailed landscapes that I immediately felt eager to frame up using the in-game photo mode.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmREEzKDETRRb4MS1G1iVAuT7RSuMpUvvpU32VgUjAZUDE/screenshot_4_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPEwX8YiHHyP8Ajwxjr6WzcuGcyM13QvuziwiPhpgnySR/screenshot_5_.png)

The scene transitioned to show Sam taking in the vast desert views, but the quiet moment was interrupted when a tiny hand reached out and started touching his face.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbyXTi2CYMgjmNrdVeJguEiJTVp8FsuFvgmW3KXDJZtTQ/screenshot_6_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZEgt1UyfzHuqG7ijkCXGutnBdV44uhiiXBpqyG49CJvq/screenshot_7_.png)

As Sam stood up, it became clear that this was no longer a Bridge Baby kept inside a pod, it was a real child named Lou, who had served as Sam's constant companion throughout the events of the first game.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmatAibLBufvNLsL4kgbjYqAYBZQp6sqfHTg5kqrEfGczk/screenshot_8_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbKgfamnm7Mky3Ha8JF1URDdNvR1qfcvE7hbd4e89NyPS/screenshot_9_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUZ9SVWBHdqVRpysHBZBSkLwCZVz6R7FtT2csAax8eqEr/screenshot_10_.png)

Once the cinematic sequence concluded, I opened the photo mode and was thrilled to find that the system had been significantly updated compared to previous entries, even though it still retained that familiar vibe I enjoyed.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTHsZEiqU2hZckNSyng6HFj3uokMYwjHb1zaasB6YZknY/screenshot_11_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNpPmLkZKcMU85sNN9JaKvL3zdrDiHnis7AKsgBhTuotY/screenshot_12_.png)

I began tweaking the settings to see exactly what was possible, discovering that I could change not only the body poses of the characters but also their specific facial expressions, including making the kid look directly into the camera lens.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPuCy6e9jGq2Ebks9PjJDwbntuiBD3tZY7k5DkTTyh8mj/screenshot_13_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSKJWrHm4JLZ39W3kvYqtYBwn2uYVdU1LpdznxrMJoSWQ/screenshot_14_.png)

After spending a good amount of time capturing various shots in the photo mode, I finally started moving ahead across the terrain as I was meant to reach home.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmP4w6R2DVioQo6WoRrhRAahXhNmChd63nVB6Jsron5jg9/screenshot_15_.png)

I paused for a moment to highlight the scanner, an object that brought back a flood of memories because it had also been such a vital companion to Sam during his earlier travels.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfJNUjQAeKBndvdPoZeRn2hrCDFCQJwninapwwJmowDx6/screenshot_16_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTRraStDNxVzTKzLKgnbpoeFi2JtkvoV2QpSaQDC1idpP/screenshot_17_.png)

While I was walking and running across the difficult terrains, the game suggested an aerial view that looked remarkably cool, almost as if a drone were flying alongside me as I moved through the environment.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPaQpddVRk5jgQUfUiCuFJ4c925XFVUKtCdu1Efee1c4K/screenshot_18_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeW2QEChSzGSmnMRZm42PzWSiTTeKWwJs9vjKy2NiKSHq/screenshot_19_.png)

I noticed several real birds flying through the sky, which added a sense of life to the area, along with a prominent rainbow that left me wondering if it was a natural phenomenon or one of the haunted varieties.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPuF5z3NcUnpHEpX8cFRdakotPrQvcM6TNpvu5tgd9yyT/screenshot_20_.png)

As I continued my run toward home, a sudden earthquake began to shake the ground and caused the surrounding hills to start crashing down, forcing me to come to a complete stop.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmenssoWYMfASLFHjMgEZUUiHgVUsYhZox6gE8Y1f98dxi/screenshot_21_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcCH3B1nMnvAZZF199P8Nzx4nF41LmdaaG5ytRSLEfboJ/screenshot_22_.png)

The child started crying loudly because he was so frightened by the tremors, so I had to stop everything to soothe him, taking several minutes to comfort him until his tears finally turned into laughter.

-- -- --

Which shot was your favorite from today's set? Let me know in the comments. Until the next frame drops, keep exploring. Alpha Gamer, out.

> 📸 ** Every image in this gallery is an original screenshot captured during my live gameplay. Please credit if sharing.**

title.title: Uzun Hava Mix
title.body:
by Siberiann on Paul Lindstrom 
View my bio on Blurt.media: https://blurt.media/c/paulindstrom [![Uzun Hava Mix](https://blurt.media/lazy-static/previews/2be33c79-ef27-4101-b79f-14e1a5a0559c.jpg)](https://blurt.media/w/79KTJepAuwtqxMbAN2rM4x) 
 
 El aire en las estepas no pide permiso para extenderse, y esa misma libertad es la que define al Uzun Hava. No se trata simplemente de una canción larga, como podría sugerir una traducción literal del turco, sino de una filosofía sonora donde el tiempo se disuelve. Los músicos que han dedicado su vida a este estilo saben que la partitura es apenas un mapa aproximado; el territorio real se construye con el aliento, con la vibración de la garganta y con esa capacidad casi sobrenatural de sostener una nota hasta que pierde su significado lingüístico para convertirse en pura emoción.

Este género, arraigado profundamente en la tradición folclórica de Anatolia y las regiones túrquicas de Asia Central, nació lejos de los estudios de grabación y los metrónomos rígidos. Surgió entre pastores, nómadas y comunidades rurales que utilizaban la voz no solo para narrar historias de amor o pérdida, sino para dialogar con el paisaje. La estructura melismática, esas cascadas de notas que giran alrededor de una sílaba, imitan el viento silbando entre las montañas o el llanto contenido. No hay compases estrictos que marquen el paso; el ritmo lo dicta la respiración del intérprete y la intensidad del sentimiento que se desea transmitir.

A diferencia del Kırık Hava, su contraparte rítmica y bailable, el Uzun Hava exige una paciencia extrema tanto del ejecutante como del oyente. Es una música que requiere ser escuchada con el cuerpo entero, permitiendo que las microtonalidades, esos intervalos menores que un semitono occidental, resuenen en el pecho. Los grandes maestros de este estilo, figuras legendarias cuyas voces se han transmitido de generación en generación, entendían que la técnica vocal era secundaria frente a la autenticidad del dolor o la alegría expresada. Un fallo técnico podía perdonarse, pero la falta de alma era imperdonable.

Hoy, cuando un intérprete se enfrenta a un micrófono para cantar un Uzun Hava, no está solo reproduciendo una tradición antigua; está participando en un ritual vivo. La audiencia, ya sea en una plaza de pueblo o en una sala de conciertos moderna, queda suspendida en ese espacio intemporal donde la melodía se estira hasta el infinito. No hay prisa por llegar a un clímax estructurado ni por resolver la tensión armónica de manera convencional. La belleza reside precisamente en esa espera, en la tensión sostenida que conecta al presente con siglos de historia oral, recordando que, antes de que existieran las palabras escritas, ya existía el canto para llenar el silencio.

La resonancia del Uzun Hava ha trascendido las cuerdas vocales para impregnar otras formas de expresión artística, actuando como un hilo conductor invisible que une disciplinas aparentemente distantes. En la literatura turca contemporánea, autores como Orhan Pamuk o Elif Shafak han utilizado la estructura narrativa de este género musical como metáfora de la memoria colectiva. Sus prosas a menudo emulan esa cualidad melismática, donde una sola idea o emoción se desdobla en párrafos extensos, llenos de digresiones poéticas que giran alrededor de un núcleo doloroso o nostálgico, imitando la manera en que una sílaba se estira y se quiebra en la garganta de un intérprete tradicional. La escritura deja de ser lineal para volverse circular y contemplativa, invitando al lector a detenerse en el detalle sensorial antes de avanzar en la trama.

El cine, por su parte, ha encontrado en el Uzun Hava una herramienta poderosa para definir el paisaje sonoro de la identidad anatolia. Directores como Nuri Bilge Ceylan no utilizan estas melodías simplemente como banda sonora de fondo, sino como un personaje silencioso que dicta el ritmo de la edición. Las tomas largas, esas secuencias donde la cámara observa el horizonte o el rostro inmóvil de un actor durante minutos interminables, están sincronizadas con la respiración amplia de estos cantos. La tensión visual se mantiene no mediante acción, sino mediante la acumulación atmosférica, reflejando la misma paciencia extrema que exige la escucha de una pieza vocal tradicional. El silencio entre las notas se convierte en espacio cinematográfico, llenando la pantalla de una presencia tangible.

Incluso la moda ha bebido de esta fuente, aunque de manera más sutil y simbólica. Diseñadores que buscan reconectar con las raíces estéticas de Asia Central han incorporado la fluidez y la asimetría del Uzun Hava en sus colecciones. Las telas caen con una gravedad estudiada, evocando la caída libre de una melodía que no conoce barreras rítmicas rígidas. Los cortes irregulares y las capas superpuestas recuerdan a las improvisaciones vocales, donde cada pliegue del tejido responde a una lógica orgánica más que geométrica. No se trata de vestir con trajes folclóricos literales, sino de capturar la esencia de esa libertad ancestral, traduciendo la audacia tonal en siluetas que desafían la estructura convencional del cuerpo.

En el ámbito musical, la influencia es quizás la más directa y transformadora. Géneros como el rock psicodélico anatolio de los años setenta, liderado por bandas como BaBa ZuLa o artistas anteriores como Erkin Koray, tomaron la escala modal del Uzun Hava y la electrificaron. La guitarra eléctrica comenzó a imitar los microtonos de la voz humana, utilizando efectos de delay y reverb para crear ese sentido de espacio infinito. Más recientemente, productores de música electrónica y ambient han sampleado grabaciones de campo de cantantes rurales, integrando esos lamentos ancestrales en beats minimalistas. Esta fusión no diluye la tradición, sino que la proyecta hacia nuevos oyentes globales, demostrando que la necesidad humana de expresar el dolor y la belleza a través de la prolongación del sonido es universal y atemporal. La frontera entre lo antiguo y lo moderno se difumina, permitiendo que el espíritu del Uzun Hava siga respirando en contextos completamente nuevos.

El Uzun Hava se erige como un monumento invisible en la arquitectura cultural de Turquía y las regiones túrquicas, funcionando mucho más allá de una simple categoría etnomusicológica. Es un pilar fundamental de la identidad colectiva, un espacio sagrado donde la historia oral se preserva no a través de documentos escritos, sino mediante la transmisión viva de la emoción. Este género actúa como un archivo sonoro de la resistencia humana, conservando las memorias de desplazamientos, amores truncados y la conexión profunda con la tierra que definieron la vida de generaciones enteras. En un mundo cada vez más acelerado y digitalizado, el Uzun Hava representa un acto de rebeldía silenciosa, una afirmación de que hay valores que no pueden ser comprimidos ni acelerados sin perder su esencia.

Su estatus como hito cultural se consolida en su capacidad para unir comunidades dispersas. Para la diáspora turca y las poblaciones túrquicas alrededor del mundo, escuchar o interpretar estas melodías es un ritual de pertenencia. No importa cuán lejos se esté de las estepas de Anatolia o de las montañas del Cáucaso; la estructura modal y la estética vocal evocan inmediatamente un sentido de hogar. Esta música sirve como un ancla emocional, permitiendo a los individuos negociar su identidad entre la modernidad global y sus raíces locales. La práctica del Uzun Hava se convierte así en un ejercicio de memoria activa, donde cada interpretación es una reafirmación de la continuidad cultural frente a la homogeneización global.

Además, este género ha desafiado las jerarquías tradicionales entre la cultura \
y la \

. Aunque nació en los campos y entre las clases trabajadoras, su complejidad técnica y profundidad filosófica han obligado a instituciones académicas y salas de concierto de élite a reconocerlo como una forma de arte sofisticada. Esta validación no ha venido sin tensiones, ya que existe un debate constante sobre la autenticidad versus la institucionalización. Sin embargo, el hecho de que el Uzun Hava haya logrado traversar estas fronteras sociales demuestra su robustez intrínseca. No necesita de la aprobación externa para existir, pero su aceptación en círculos intelectuales ha amplificado su voz, permitiendo que su mensaje de libertad interior llegue a oídos que antes lo habrían ignorado.

La preservación del Uzun Hava también ha impulsado movimientos de revitalización lingüística y poética. Las letras de estas canciones, a menudo compuestas por poetas anónimos o trovadores locales, contienen un vocabulario y unas estructuras gramaticales que reflejan dialectos regionales en peligro de extinción. Al cantar, los intérpretes mantienen vivas formas de expresión que de otro modo podrían desaparecer bajo la presión de lenguas dominantes. Así, la música se convierte en un vehículo de conservación lingüística, asegurando que las nuances del pensamiento regional sigan teniendo un espacio de resonancia. Cada melisma, cada giro vocal, lleva consigo el peso de una lengua que se niega a ser silenciada.

Este legado cultural no es estático, sino que se renueva con cada generación que decide apropiarse de él. Los jóvenes músicos que hoy experimentan con el Uzun Hava no lo ven como una reliquia de museo, sino como un lenguaje vivo capaz de dialogar con el presente. Esta vitalidad continua asegura que el género no quede congelado en el tiempo, sino que evolucione manteniendo su núcleo espiritual intacto. El Uzun Hava permanece como un testigo eterno de la capacidad humana para transformar el sufrimiento y la alegría en belleza duradera, recordando constantemente que la verdadera riqueza cultural no reside en la posesión de objetos, sino en la profundidad de la experiencia compartida a través del sonido.

Es todo por hoy.

Disfruten del mix que les comparto, esta vez, sin voz, solo instrumental.

>
Muy buenos días respetable audiencia, para este post les obsequio una música tradicional del estado lara de la República Bolivariana de Venezuela, donde se concentran las más importantes , tales como: el tamunangue,el golpe tocuyano, la zaragoza, san pascual bailón, canturías y bambas.
La palabra suite, significa varias piezas integradas en una misma tonalidad. Eso quise reflejar cuando reuno a las tradiciones en la tonalidad de Sol Mayor.

La composición es de mi autoría y grabada por ODILA.

>Good morning, esteemed audience. For this post, I present to you traditional music from the state of Lara in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, home to some of the most important musical traditions, such as the Tamunangue, the Golpe Tocuyano, the Zaragoza, San Pascual Bailón, Canturías, and Bambas.

>The word \

refers to several pieces arranged in the same key. That is what I intended to reflect when I brought these traditions together in the key of G major. The composition is my own and was recorded by ODILA.

Hola amigos de LIKETU! Aquí les muestro unas fotos de como me definí mi cabello por primera vez. La técnica que utilice fue la de rizo a rizo. Es decir, me seccioné el cabello (tiene que estar muy húmedo) y le aplique crema para peinar, la que utilice es de Alice especialmente para rizos. Me dividí el cabello y comencé a rizarme el cabello mechón por mechón con el dedo. Es decir, agarraba el mechón y lo enrrollaba en mi dedo hasta arriba y luego lo soltaba. Y así hacia con cada mechón de cabello. Al finalizar hice scronch con mis manos y una cera que me regaló mi novio que tiene olor a piña para que se mantuviera. Y pues así quedó ☺️🥰

✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨✨

Hi, LIKETU friends! Here are some photos of how I defined my hair for the first time. The technique I used was strand-by-strand. That is, I sectioned my hair (it has to be very damp) and applied styling cream—I used Alice’s, which is specifically for curls. I divided my hair and started curling it strand by strand with my finger. Basically, I’d grab a strand, wrap it all the way up around my finger, and then let it go. I did this with every strand of hair. When I was done, I scrunched it with my hands and used a pineapple-scented wax my boyfriend gave me to help it hold its shape. And here’s how it turned out ☺️🥰

## Signal Scout Report
**Creator:** Cybersecurity HS

Escanear una red wifi con nmap es sencillo y un procedimiento vital en ciberseguridad,porque la principal ventaja es que nos muestra todos los dispositivos que estan conectados en nuestra red. Esto nos va a permitir saber cuales son los dispositivos que estan usando nuestra red sin nuestro permiso.

El comando nos permite ademas ver cuales son los puertos que tiene abiertos nuestro sistema, permitiendo asi conocer las vulnerabilidades que tenemos. 

Ademas es una herramienta gratuita que pocas veces se usa para redes wifi, ya que su finalidad es otra en el pentesting, generalmente enfocada en detectar los puertos abiertos, que podemos usar para analizar la respuestas de los paquetes y asi medir comportamientos anormales.

Es de codigo abierto, gratuita y muy interesante y simple de usar. 

Hoy en dia hasta las versiones de windows con powershell creo que permiten usarla.

title.title: Getting to FOUR rides in a week!
title.body:
<center>
![temp1.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nozem01/245HerdFxoE7CeknMHJywot5gE2LLWjV7wPsMof28n8QiuaYPjfniLhsbeDMBM2XNe3DZ.jpg)
</center>

Hey everyone, I hope your miles has been safe and puncture free for the last week (and weeks to come as well!) It's a Sunday morning at the time of making this post, which is a bit ahead of schedule since the new Cycling Chit Chat will probably launch later today or tomorrow, depending is there's electricity in Cuba at the moment and whether @nanixxx isn't busy delivery dresses and hairpins around the city and beyond. 😃

I wish the packets here were delivered by cyclists as well but they use vans, driving WAY too fast in residential area's... 😒

First, I want to ask the Hive Cycling Community a question about the way I will go forward with [my cycling YouTube Channel](https://www.youtube.com/@MTBtheDutchWay) since my roots are here and will always be, I'm up to 24 subscribers so it's growing steadily but even if no one would watch, I enjoy editing the video's so it's fine either way BUT I'm asking myself a question in the last two weeks, I posted this in my YouTube Community as well;

The issue I have with making English content is, because it's not my native language my speaking isn't as  spontaneously because I'm translating in my head what I want to tell to you, typing and speaking are two very different things so my question is:

### Would it be better to talk in my own language (Dutch) and use good subtitles?

The con for this will be obviously that some viewers don't like to read subtitles and swipe away, the pro is it's a lot more natural and the speaking will show more personality and doesn't look as scripted.

<center>
![MTB Banner 5.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nozem01/23swsB5Ru5F1r3aaFmZzK2DegWTDyuR5XUAgawWt7CLvcwXF76qFZ74gZKQy7v3Y8TdB1.png)
</center>

# Cycling is addictive 

<center>
![02.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nozem01/243zZHvurQP1XZmwFJbx5rvB1NQgWzrrpcWfAhe2qm23EZkc7XZ7T8dx8BhZ9TkqQn349.jpg)
</center>

Fair warning for everyone thinking about starting with cycling, it truly is addictive but maybe this goes for all sports because our body produces chemicals during exercise that make us feel good and when I can't sport, I get grumpy 😅 and I want MORE! 

The grumpy part I found out when I was sick for a week, sitting on the couch all day preserving energy is not my thing, of course on the other hand because I have a wife and kids, I have to be careful not to overdo it as well. 🙂

Since last Thursday, Google Health (the Fitbit app no longer exists) is finally giving me better recovery scores again and as of today, it's all okay 😃
It's crazy to see how good a tech gadget is at this, because it was already signaling I was getting sick the day before I felt anything because my resting heart rate was going up.

<center>
![WhatsApp Image 2026-05-31 at 08.11.25.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nozem01/23t74Zk65b5EtScj5JoemseMhgkbUZ1RUZJmacszCBszC9RD2E9SYCw4DSp4hmXCD6dhj.jpeg)
</center>

<center>
![MTB Banner 4.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nozem01/23swsB5m6hjPyTdTdGdySaQY6xPsWBd9e7bHaUrdRZ7UrBY5dtKt9T4toi3vDvVr26JNR.png)
</center>

# Dropping another rider

It occasionally happens when I'm out on my mountainbike I'm closing in on someone on a road bike, which is cool because in most cases they're a lot faster than me, but in many cases when I get closer it's either a woman on the roadbike or a 65+ old man... 😅

On MyWhoosh however, the playing ground is even, we're all on fast bikes! Yesterday morning at 8:30am I was on the indoor trainer to ride my last stage for this months event to earn a really nice Giant Aero bike, it was only a 24km ride with about 200 meters of elevation in it, so it should't take more than 1 hour to complete.

This was planned to be just an in between endurance building ride and meant to be 100% in zone 2, but then another Dutch cyclist, Zino tagged along and we were just peacefully riding together, taking the lead in turns so the other could draft until about 7km before the finish the last climb started with parts between 10% and 14% and the funny thing was, we both had the same idea to drop the other in this climb 😁 
OK.. s you want to play huh, game on! So I switched to zone 4 and after a couple of minutes of heavy breathing I was able to drop him after I got out of the saddle on a really steep part and the seconds between us started to grow.

It's kinda strange on MyWhoosh that even you're not in visual range of another rider you can see in the list on the right how many watts/kg they're doing, so when we were both in the descent I stayed in zone 4 for a while to mess with his head not to get any ideas of catching up 😁 and when we were on flat terrain again his power dropped from 3 watts per kilo to only 1.5 watts per kilo so I could get a breather as well and I finished with a 1 minute 15 seconds lead on him, that felt good! 

<center>
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nozem01/23tGTG4V8VtcT77Je3m5YyCMJbipbSqg94nsg5wD5CAfsRCBdFBQtPY1VMsxBayS3B82n.png)
</center>

But I was thinking about the women and old men on the road bikes, and the name Zino can be any gender too but the cool thing, cycling online is you can see the profiles of other riders!

<center>
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nozem01/23tRqtSibaVyo36mxLXuwdqv8jjhaHJsoSK8rgE1aK4jFHjHKot3MeNRMypxmUrBrojY8.png)
</center>

It turned out to be a man 6 to 10 years younger than me, with a higher FTP but he's a kinda big dude with 185cm and 92kg compared to my 173cm and 69kg, on climbs that's a HUGE difference 😄 but I actually felt excited, winning my first ever 1 vs. 1 mini race even though it was a virtual one.

<center>
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nozem01/23uEoNu3fGbffihHQG517uCGPGfjQpAfXm8wavoTpnTqzHzw4vmzz5iGXKy8KbmC76NG5.png)
</center>

<center>
![MTB Banner 3.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nozem01/23swsB5Rj2bY9qyPxNf72wNLujSSg8KGBUnabrDpNwFbpnA48m4w41qXy59ieRzrvCMfF.png)
</center>

# Four rides

Because of the MyWhoosh I event I missed when I was sick I now had to catch up with before the event ends this weekend, I'm already at three rides and today I'll be going to the trail with my daughter doing about 40km, getting this weeks total up to 160km

<center>
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nozem01/23tSyukanrLdViDSkPS6xKRtXb4WgDYmA6dkLEwdtqwhc7HJHQHhsxkpm72UYudsyjVz8.png)
</center>

Although I've been sick, I'm still over 300km ahead of reaching my 4000km yearly goal.

<center>
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nozem01/23tcNnfbkSCvedXDWfthUu4RCNAgxrfV9Fn8oSJ32HusZBfmXLSGdtLTUMvRwNEqG9GPr.png)
</center>

Last week I replaced the chains for both mountainbikes, and switched to drip on wax now the summer has started so hopefully the new chain doesn't wear as fast as the old one did, it also helps this is a more expensive KMC chain, instead of the cheapest available Shimano that was recommended to match my Shimano Deore Groupset. 

<center>
![MTB Banner 2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nozem01/23swsB5Rj2bY9wtqkTLsNfFvjcM8c7BrVDwNkLsEAjotUAXUL6B2rCZyZWyZd2xpY9hbM.png)
</center>

# Sharing some pretty pictures

I shot this video while experimenting with the camera mounted to my handlebars but it gives crappy footage to use in a video so I scrapped the idea of using the footage to make a video and after getting some nice stills from it the video will just be deleted, not before sharing the pictures here in my posts because the stills DO look nice.

<center>
![03.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nozem01/241EvLYL9TpeJKVAqB868ABJbVCb5LwPdphYAMWWAV6Z5gRcBqunX2VNyGxh5Tm8bxxBW.jpg)
</center>

<center>
![04.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nozem01/23sU8jiARLYCe55BuciYyxtDTwrEudTGMHdusGKPhdY1TqbosBWmRnsmPGuLa89mLGmS1.jpg)
</center>

<center>
![05.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nozem01/23uaH35Wm8c9djRVj5rbDo8hfPWdU77fJAPfRBHYycyFdRspynFvkii2rMffjDbCN98oA.jpg)
</center>

<center>
![06.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nozem01/245wFDvzzG5MqroTb7pqeW8TnC42JmK1jMCEho7JdnHChu4A16v9CZ4tx2GDxRmo9tGqs.jpg)
</center>

<center>
![07.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nozem01/23xVKNKwVAK9GNDJdwVDvAMsEp4N42b6XBjqhxYu4hAc6UH4gtMWv5owHrx83BkyCwDCd.jpg)
</center>

1000+ words again so I'll leave it at this and add the Cycling Chit Chat part later! 😊

<center>
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nozem01/23yU4ZjQjRXQ6vRpfKA1NY3mniDpV43QbtisVaAFtKZD2N6mq3Pa1a5Y4djNZYtG4Dqum.png)
</center>

![untitled.gif](https://media.tenor.com/wcpJDl4mPyUAAAAC/mike-wazowski-monsters-inc.gif)

It must be the heat in Cuba and the hours and hours in the gym 😇

So, we're back with some cool questions again, respect for always thinking of cool new questions every week!

### When did you first notice real improvement after starting to ride your bike?

I think the most awesome thing about starting a new sport, especially untrained in general is the amazing progress you make in the first weeks, probably between three weeks and three months the progress is the most, it's great to see and it's easy to keep going, and this blends in great with the second question and I was thinking about exactly this while driving, what cycling brought me in my first year and what changed...

### What made you fall so deeply in love with cycling that you even decided to wear bib shorts and a jersey?

Never say never, I think this saying is known all around the world in many different variations and languages, I remember when I bought my mountainbike, I told my wife I would not get too crazy in to cycling and I told myself, I bought a mountainbike so I would be different than all these crazy looking slightly too fat men in lycra on their road bikes, shouting, misbehaving and in general, thinking the entire road in theirs, I think this is how non-cyclists see cyclists in my country, it's not a good reputation at all and something that's been build over years and years unfortunately.

In the summer I always had a pair of running shorts over my bib shorts, or my long running pants but when winter came, and I wanted to continue cycling I needed something that wouldn't soak up all rain and I found out the most practical way was.... thermal bibs!
6 months later and there I was, cycling as a true MAMIL (I learned this abbreviation from our fearless leader Moose) and a year later, getting all in on cycling and even having longer term plans to own a road bike as well, I think it's fair to say I didn't held up to what I told myself OR what I told my wife... 😏

So, it's not the love of cycling that made me wear lycra, it's just the most practical way. What made me fall in love with cycling is probably a post on it's own 😆

* Getting in way better shape then I was even in my twenties
* Adventure and being outside
* Getting to places I've never been before, even really close to home
* Staying fit and healthy
* It's not as impact-full on the body as running, so I can hopefully keep doing this until I'm really old 
* Getting all nerdy about training stats and the science behind it all

And really the only thing what I didn't like about cycling...

![untitled.gif](https://media.tenor.com/_l1qMl3GBG0AAAAC/its-outrageously-expensive-expensive.gif)

Well, it's time to wrap it up and time to eat dinner, and after that I'll be doing another hour of training in the virtual world of MyWhoosh, but for some people out there this is not counted as cycling... 😁

title.title: The things and hurdles learning to ✅ an unplanned bucket list
title.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSw114ZSMr3G1uFkhHHcqVnR6EXGZptMhWu2MJiScVCig/book_cover_marketing.jpg)
<sup>_Photo is embedded into photofunia's template_</sup>

Oh wow, I didn't realise that [**_photofunia_**](https://photofunia.com/) is still running strong after for more than a decade!

---

### I'm digressing 😂
Maybe I am hitting my _Jubilee year_ soon!

---

What a journey of 12 days... an unplanned _side trail_ that my Almighty has redirected me while I am still drafting and re-visiting _@the3rdcord of the wire_ since its inception more than a month ago.

#### Publishing a book was never in my bucket list. 

But over 2 decades ago, my older brother an I once wanted to become _story publishers_ for others to have a digital platform where people can just come and share their story.

##### Well, that went to the shelves when my brother got married, and I went on in a roller-coaster ride of relationship, faith, and life hurdles to cross

## Until ... now(?)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbTFdpFG6m8TKrjqj37SdeEU7tvR65VLP825SAXCNMQox/image.png)

I have always wondered how easy would one be able to write a book and be published because often time I kept seeing podcast interviews that usually ties to an author; but publishing this book isn't really about fame, but about something that many people like me, who have been living and \

in Malaysia (with many _roller-coaster_ rides) usually do not want to speak out loud... and if it does, it often comes with frustration.

#### And I truly hope, I heard His voice correctly

To see things in a different way, and to be grateful in the midst of turmoil and frustration.

---

Moreover, to arrive to this stage requires a steep learning curve for 12 days.

1. Learning how to write backbones of a book.
2. Learning book cover design.
3. Learning to use different tools including AI to generate illustrations.
4. Steep learning of grammar faults; when Malaysian English is not truly acceptable to international audience.
5. Learning how to generate epub books as fast as possible.
6. Learning the consequences of **falling into Amazon's new writer's marketing TRAP**
7. Learning the **_VERY STEEP_** tax from the US—even if you are not a citizen there. And how low priced e-books will eventually earn me **nothing** except a few cents per copy.
8. Learning to mentally prepared how to file income tax, even as little as $50 USD when it happens. (Probably for a really long time)
9. Learning that Amazon Kindle is VERY hostile to users who do not have Amazon sub site running there—ie. Malaysia.

And all these are just technical—excluding the emotional journey writing this book.

I can't say this is a bad book to write, just something that requires realisation in order to have internal healing.

---

That being said, if anyone here actually resides in non \

country and would love to help me to test if the pre-order kindle version works, I will reimburse you the profit I will get (which I have no idea how much it is yet) back into your HIVE account in HBD—straight into savings. 

I need a pool of people to help me test whether it truly works.... Especially people in US and outside US (like Europe, Canada, or Australia perhaps...)

If you do happen to help me pre-order it successfully, do snap-shot and post in the comments here, so that I will be able to keep track when it officially launches. There is a tiny bit of (politically correct) typo that I probably need to update, but I guess that's just an err for the locals.

Hit me up at the comments if you are game to help me out—and my launch date should be on June 4th, 2026 UTC (?) with an \

price for about 60 days. --- I am currently unable to multi-platform launch because I was trapped in their marketing gimmick... I hope I can disable it in 36 hours time haha... # Until Then Stay healthy, stay curious and learn new things, and stay happy! ![](https://images.ecency.com/p/GLhDmHx9sqz2PfsVn8wmBCwMuAjSEj5N9rRH9KxQYTWLtELcDRXZtVdjbN2AibXohZTX8B3xfvGWjtzGDkgEE8a3iAFobu3fDp84Hi8Teia5j7Q3QebpP3iBXwoiux2rDd2ALKGSdmxF5xfCp25jXZswvbNo7FF6cpm5iNH3qcPafYq7u8UDsRd3ecUXNMvoQFNKnGh94Zn7LkEVgKFEa8t35DvqrEGAx66S1mDshn5.webp?format=webp&mode=fit) ![](https://images.hive.blog/768x0/https://cdn.liketu.com/media/littlenewthings/images/clqq5wgah0097g1sz2uqqc3u5_littlenewthings-buymeacoffee/clqq5wgah0097g1sz2uqqc3u5_littlenewthings-buymeacoffee.webp) If you would like to give some encouragement outside HIVE with some fiat backing, please feel free to visit: https://www.buymeacoffee.com/littlenewthings You can also support me in HIVE

</liketuimages>

昨天的雨下得太大了，早上醒来，还在想，今天会不会又下太雨了，还好，睛空万里，天气真好呀，雨后更让人感觉舒服。

到了办公室，就是忙，今天忙得有点呼吸不过来，有三个同事去越南，出机票就是好久，而且那个订票系统既然出问题了，而且更气人的是，我试了订好久没有订上，最后得出的结论是，网上的票只给大陆人订，香港人的票既然没有了。订那几张票，把我搞得伤心累累，也不知是怎么回事，这几天又是特别的忙起来。

去越南也多，美国来这边也多，光订酒店，订车，都让人呼吸不过来啊，我在想，这美国人来这边，机票的钱那贵，也来这么多，这公司能挣几个钱呀。一个字，忙，马上端午节来了，香港老板又要我安排饭局。

问了几个老板，结果都说要出差，看来，这个时间真的不是个好时候，我早上去公司也没吃饭，也自己煮了两上鸡蛋，吃了一包麦片，没有想到，真的饱肚子，搞得中午只想去吃粉了，选了一碗伴粉，没有想到，真的很好吃，食堂那个档口，我也没有去过。 

明天欢欢学校开家长会，这次挺好的，开会时间是晚上，这样，我就不用请假了，下了班可以直接过去，只是明天晚上英语课不能参加， 给光头说了一下，他既然说，你请假的话那这周就取消了，呵呵，搞得我不好意思，我不参加，既然取消？看来我的面子真大，不过，也好，我们也可以好好的休息。

---
