title.body:
**What follows is a wee overview of the last 7 days ( mostly visually ), starting today and counting backwards, just because I can...**

*Enjoy!*

---

Tuesday / Martedì / Dinsdag

Today is a(nother) hot day but our land looks stunning, after last night's much needed rain. 


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcirbU6EVG3utoU3xW6M7KbPwBP1RTyQxus9TBMM6MCWF/1780407051167.jpg)

rain on a spiderweb...

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVzxbWNudXtV6QHf4quz5cxdPCxBvGU2GxerPgJXxt1v3/1780407051570.jpg)

More rain is in the making but only expected tomorrow afternoon...

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNRUkNBA6BZ9s1bRmyKBLFeH8DPNpULV1B2df5kBFGNVe/1780407051817.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeAay6a3o2T7Z78hDAh8R1J8XYeMgwANP4QD31NgZdMhY/1780407051007.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWJ17sfqrDEipoH3vX65VQbGYK5FQ8TqGKEJoonC6KnTF/1780407051337.jpg)

*Our garden is turning into a true butterly paradise ( mostly because we don't strimm the grass, nor use any heavy machinery. And sometimes these beautiful creatures temporarily pay us a visit indoors too.*


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNmGJFhTG1Z2ac13TmHJ7pYAJn3TbXedGPRoJHb6DgnKm/1780407144688.jpg)


Monday / Lunedì /Maandag

Yesterday, I picked a bunch more cherries from our plethora of (future) cherry trees. I discovered a couple of trees with another, darker type. They are small but very sweet.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaCBrtDM914VRRbqCwudksUKyTZmgddWcpmGkiYAXetsv/1780407145215.jpg)

I enjoyed seeing the approaching rain, in the early evening...

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdzkSwSt96pEZrw74WMstqnFp8Qz8mNSv1WFe9E2Pz5CQ/1780407144493.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZoP4rA4pW8yfvNBHLZcb6gJMPkXY47d1FnD1hJkf34vk/1780407145023.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTSU8a2aVqxE33yU14AAziCCRkgDcHp7PonMe3zNok2ZZ/1780407144845.jpg)

Sunday/ Domenica / Zondag

We returned to our land - and cat - after having been gone for 48 hours and it felt great to see all the flowers, including these Madonna lilies. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXBUiH1F3Ag9nb8z1jBGBc8ojJgt5TP1DCSkKdBxMtV6q/1780407253287.jpg)

We were also delighted to bring some bathroom furniture with us, including something we had been longing for for ages: **a bath!** 

If it would have been two centimeters longer, it would not have fit in our car!

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQfLhqdRZQujjBMZ9aw2NkrWFkPRzYPe4H1aFrDZ6e7Mx/1780407253089.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeeShmQUeVm8ukxcFvsepUTKZwBwuLLu8ULfJi8EdsV6z/1780407253493.jpg)

Saturday / Sabato / Zaterdag

*Day 2 of weekend #2 of Clare showcasing her slow fashion in a friend's gallery. Another slow night...*


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYbTR8Af6H3QYFLoxNr7EeAoNdVamE7QSmibTqvUPyp3c/1780407385129.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRdPAzMbZv8vJ4ZDznByu8eb2HvQiPi3A3E2sDCMncMSz/1780407384958.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmX1tRjaJ25uWSUBCwSQY3RNA89Gp16UHJeuGeSV9KS8am/1780407385221.jpg)

Friday / Venerdì / Vrijdag

*We returned  to the 'arthouse' ( our home for sale ) in the city, for the weekend.

It was a hot day - and we drive a car without AC - so we stopped at a river to cool down and enjoy nature.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNSeg7ggucnDadRXxD7Unf5Qz7naa2AQSJTaYSoFuFnga/1780407551264.jpg)


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTGULn4e12KYN7SH1be5joc8UBBTWN9SfmcUUAXHQHGF3/1780409553550.jpg)

Thursday / Giovedì / Donderdag

I only took one photo but it was worth it.

*Who doesn't like farfalle?*

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaqL7WJ1RTibKqRiu2RPcpAnkS8qrvPY6X5LHhxbj1Aoz/1780407824734.jpg)

Wednesday / Mercoledì / Woensdag

We picked our first cherries, photographed more butterflies and went to the sea for the fist time in ages.

The water was coldish - we just about managed to swim - but there were hardly any people on the beach and the sea was beautifully calm(ing).

We also managed to score some nice groceries :^)

title.title: Sapien Loop 3 - Chapter 78: Closure
title.body:
![Sapien_Loop_3_Cover_HIVE.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/spectrumecons/23wC7hkTDDpnHvZegULctqg6Mrrd9t72byH8zWkVgfNiHGiHqm7aVAeGi9PiELYyYAuVf.jpg)

## Chapter 78: Closure

-----

Shamia made contact with her guards and ordered them back to the Downs Region to help the technicians and followers with the clean-up and the burials of all those who had died. 

Polly, Bellamy, Belford, Roger One, and Roger Two built a memorial in the section of the Downs Agriculture Zone that had been converted into a cemetery. Bastion repaired Jennifer. Her chip that was destroyed in the collapse was replaced with a copy of his own chip, which was a variation of her chip but with a slightly happier demeanour.

Octavius had managed to round up the Sentray, who had run away. He had led them back to the former camp area of the underground Linap. Ducky took charge of them as he entered the Downs Region. 

Polly rushed over to greet Octavius. ‘Welcome to the Downs Region, old friend,’ said Polly as she ran towards him with her arms open.

‘Happy to see me,’ chuckled Octavius as Polly hugged him. ‘Or is it more about my calorie-dense food?’

‘Nobody eats more calories than you,’ replied Polly. ‘Honestly, I genuinely missed you and your unique sense of humour.’

‘Bah!’ growled Octavius as he pushed Polly off him.

‘There are two robots who really want to see you too,’ said Polly as they walked down the main road together.

‘Damn!’ said Octavius in a slightly jovial tone. ‘I knew Roger One was growing distant from me.’

‘Okay, let me correct myself,’ said Polly, shaking her head. ‘There are five robots who really want to see you.’

‘Did Belford build himself two smaller companions?’ asked Octavius excitedly as the two continued to walk.

‘Better, much better,’ replied Polly as she gestured towards two robots who were slowly running towards them.

‘It can’t be,’ gasped Octavius. ‘I saw them die.’

‘Jennifer backed up their memories and personalities, and now they have new bodies that look just like their old bodies,’ said Polly as she swung her arms around.

‘No tricks, it’s really them,’ said Octavius as he watched them running towards him.

‘It’s us,’ shouted Bastion and Bellamy as they continued running towards Octavius.

‘Oh wow,’ said Octavius as he dropped to his knees and opened his arms.

Both Bastion and Bellamy hugged Octavius.

‘This is so great,’ said Polly as a tear appeared in her organic eye.

‘Despite all this tragedy, I feel everything is going to get so much better,’ said Octavius. ‘Maybe better than ever.’

‘We need to head to the Downs Agriculture Zone,’ said Polly. ‘You’re needed to represent the Sentray.’

‘Haha, that sounds so strange,’ chuckled Octavius as he stood up.

Octavius, Bastion, and Bellamy ran towards the Downs Agriculture Zone. Polly hovered beside them.

A stage had been set up in the Downs Agriculture Zone. Orcilla was to give a eulogy for those who died in the Downs Region. She had invited representatives from all the various groups to stand with her.

Everyone in the Downs Region had gathered to listen and pay their respects to all those who had died throughout the war and recent events.

‘I’m here, I made it,’ panted Octavius as he ran towards the stage.

‘Who do you represent looking like that?’ gasped Lily, who was standing next to the steps leading up to the stage.

‘The Sentray,’ said Octavius as he put his hands on his hips. ‘They were my friends, and so many died to save Downs.’

‘Stand behind him,’ instructed Lily as she pointed to Morgan. ‘Please try to look a little more presentable. This is a memorial service, not a dinner for Sapes.’

‘Oh sorry,’ said Octavius as he stood behind Morgan.

‘Hello, friend,’ said Morgan. ‘I’m Morgan. Who are you?’

‘Nice to meet you, Morgan,’ said Octavius. ‘I’m Octavius Spiro.’

‘Nice to meet you too,’ replied Morgan. ‘I’m Morgan.’

The little miracles began to sing. Lily gestured for the representatives to walk up on stage. They formed a line at the back of the stage. A few seconds later, Orcilla walked on stage. She was carrying a microphone. On seeing her, the little miracles stopped singing.

‘Today we have come to pay our respects to all those that have lost their lives during Tiberius’ reign of terror,’ said Orcilla. ‘Behind me, I have representatives from all our communities. From left to right. We have Eugene representing the Downs Region.’

‘Go Eugene!’ shouted someone in the crowd.

Eugene waved to the crowd.

‘We have Louis representing the Sapiens,’ said Orcilla as she gestured towards Louis. 

Louis gestured by raising both his thumbs up.

‘We have Wendell representing the Linap,’ said Orcilla as she nodded at Wendell.

‘We have a cute chubby Sape representing the Sapes,’ continued Orcilla as she pointed to the chubby Sape friend of Eugene.

‘Onk!’ grunted the chubby Sape.

‘We have Maurice standing in for the High Philosopher representing the followers,’ said Orcilla as she gestured towards Maurice. ‘I have just been told that we have a new High Philosopher. He is Homer. He is currently at the West Camp.’

The followers nodded acknowledgingly.

‘Next we have Henders representing the technicians,’ continued Orcilla as she smiled and nodded at Henders, who was pointing at his chest where Julio had hurt him.

The technicians roared in excitement.

Orcilla waited for them to stop cheering. ‘We have Morgan representing the Sapiods,’ said Orcilla as she looked at Morgan, who had a blank expression on his face.

‘Last but not least, we have Octavius representing the Sentray,’ said Orcilla as she waved to Octavius. ‘I want to thank all the representatives from all our communities and species. This is the first time in the history of Sapey that we all stand together in unity. It just pains me that this is under such horrific circumstances.’

Orcilla paused for a few seconds. ‘I’ll hand over to Lily to recite an ancient prayer of peace in Parelic,’ she said as she handed the microphone to Lily.

Lily began the prayer, and Orcilla walked over to Daily, who was standing with Yassmay and Yassme.

‘It’s great that you got everyone together like this,’ said Daily as he put his arms around Orcilla. 

‘It was a group effort, and the real hard work has yet to begin,’ replied Orcilla.

‘I know things are awful, but I’ve never felt so much hope before,’ said Daily.

‘Well, we can rebuild the Downs Region,’ said Orcilla. ‘We can continue building the two new settlements. We can grow an almost infinite amount of the special seaweed. I know our great scientists can make it into more effective cures.’

‘That’s some great positivity,’ said Daily.

‘Then again Maskameera and August are still out there,’ sighed Orcilla. ‘They could be almost anyone, and I can’t imagine they would have decided to abandon their ways.’

‘Then they will have to emerge in some way,’ said Yassmay, raising her eyebrows. ‘Then we get them.’

‘Yes, we must remain vigilant,’ said Orcilla as she looked at Lily. ‘They will not be the only threat. There will always be those who will want to take power for themselves. We need to do more to stop this from ever happening again. We need to build something that cannot be captured.’

‘If anyone can come up with something, it’s you,’ said Daily as he rubbed Orcilla’s back.

‘No, it’ll have to be a joint effort,’ sighed Orcilla. ‘I’ll need all of your help and all of their help,’ she added as she pointed at the community representatives on stage, who were now holding hands.

‘I think we can trust them,’ sighed Yassme as she watched them gently sway from side to side.

Finally, Lily finished her extremely long-winded prayer. She bowed and left the stage. After her, several of the community representatives made short speeches. Expressing their condolences and their commitment to work with the other communities. Once they had finished and left the stage, the little miracles started to sing again.

Denise and Vulay approached Morgan. ‘I’m so proud of you, Daddy,’ said Denise as she held her arms out to hug Morgan.

‘Donut, friend,’ replied Morgan as he pointed at Eugene, who had just joined his parents.

‘Oh yes, of course,’ sighed Denise as she put her arms down.

‘Morgan walked a few steps towards Eugene, and then he stopped and turned around. Vulay had put her arm around Denise, who was looking a little sad.

‘Denise, my daughter,’ said Morgan as he looked at Denise.

‘Yes, I am,’ replied Denise.

The two of them smiled at each other for a few seconds, and then they hugged.

After the service, Orcilla spoke with community representatives. She requested that they form an action team to determine how Sapey would be governed. Orcilla declined to be part of that team. She no longer desired the responsibility of leadership. 

Yassmay and Yassme worked together to repair one of the vehicles. This was to be used to transfer Felix and several other technicians back to their underground cities so they could spend time with their families.

Vulay and Eugene decided the fate of Hermon, Benny, Duffo, Tiberius, and the few remaining surrendered enforcers. Hermon was sent to work as a technician in the West Camp for one year. Benny was sent with him to be his supervisor for the same duration. Wendell and Gilling requested Hermon be stripped of the Alset family name. Thus, officially making Wendell the new head of the family. Duffo was sent to the East Camp for two years to work as a technician. He was stripped of all given titles. After the two years, he could return to the Downs Region but would be permanently barred from any meaningful leadership position. The surrendered enforcers were stripped of their positions and were no longer allowed to work as enforcers. Eric was given the responsibility to hire and train new enforcers. Tiberius remained a ‘gone case’ and was handed over to Orcilla; she would decide what would happen to him now.

Tiberius was strapped to a table in a dilapidated warehouse. Orcilla was standing over him.

‘This is it,’ chuckled Tiberius. ‘You’ve resorted to torture.’

‘No, of course not,’ replied Orcilla. ‘I’ll make sure you don’t suffer at all. I’ll be relieving you of your mental torment.’

‘You’re so kind,’ chuckled Tiberius. ‘Are you sure we aren’t related?’

Orcilla jabbed Tiberius hard in the arm with a large needle. ‘Good night,’ she said. ‘The world will be a much better place when you wake up.’

Within a few seconds, Tiberius had passed out. Orcilla proceeded to operate on him. She performed a similar procedure that used to be done to convert Sapiens into Sapiods. Her version did not involve pumping him with any drugs to make him physically stronger. Her focus was purely on his brain.

Maskameera Wolf and August Rezif had assumed new technician personas. They were nobody of importance and just aimed to blend in for the time being.

Maskameera visited August’s apartment. She volunteered to cook him one of her favourite noodle dishes. August was sitting at the small dining table opposite to where she was cooking.

‘Gosh, you’re so quiet,’ remarked Maskameera as she tossed the noodles around in the wok. ‘Don’t tell me you’re still sulking about our latest adventure.’

‘It wasn’t an adventure; it was a nightmare,’ replied August. ‘I’m done with this relationship. It’s time we part ways.’

‘You need me to stay alive,’ said Maskameera aggressively as she stared at August. ‘They’re hunting you down as we speak. Turn away from me and I’ll make sure they succeed. Stick with me and I’ll keep making you these delicious meals.’

‘You always have the most persuasive arguments,’ sighed August.

‘We have defined the last thousand years,’ said Maskameera as she waved her arms around. ‘We ruled the best part of the twelfth loop, and we will own the thirteenth.’

‘Maybe you should keep an eye on those noodles,’ remarked August. ‘You don’t want to burn them.’

‘You ungrateful bastard,’ said Maskameera as she turned to look at the noodles. ‘Oh look, they’re done and they’re perfect as always.’

‘Well, yummy,’ replied August as he watched her put the noodles into two bowls.

‘I want you to continue your work on Henders,’ said Maskameera as she placed the bowls down on the table. 

‘I’d rather we leave him out of it,’ replied August as Maskameera sat down opposite him.

‘I insist you do,’ chuckled Maskameera. ‘We wouldn’t want anything unpleasant happening to him.’

August glared angrily at Maskameera.

‘Eat up; it’ll get cold,’ said Maskameera as she began shovelling the noodles into her mouth. ‘I’ve added silken tofu and some knock your socks off spices.’

August picked up a piece of tofu with his chopsticks and sniffed it.

‘After all we’ve been through, do you really think I’d try to poison you?’ asked Maskameera angrily.

‘I am a little sensitive to spicy food these days,’ replied August as he placed the piece of tofu back in the bowl as he continued to watch Maskameera shovel the food into her mouth.

‘If you don’t stop acting strange, I might put something very nasty in that stupid, fat oath’s blancmange,’ said Maskameera as she began drinking the leftover sauce in her bowl.

‘He’s our friend,’ said August. ‘It deeply saddens me the way you talk about him and treat him.’

‘No, he’s your friend,’ replied Maskameera. ‘I haven’t liked him since he turned into that disgusting freak.’

‘Then I feel more sorry for you than I do him,’ replied August.

‘You’re so pathetic,’ said Maskameera as she pushed the empty bowl to one side. ‘You’re nothing…’

Maskameera started to gasp. 

‘Take it easy,’ said August.

Maskameera leaned forward, placing her head on the table as she struggled to breathe.

‘I’ll get you some seaweed,’ said August as he stood up. ‘Just stay calm.’

Suddenly, the room turned completely white, and everything other than the table and the chair Maskameera was sitting on vanished.

August placed his hand on the floor to attempt to shapeshift the room back but succeeded for just a flicker.

‘It’s over!’ called out a voice.

‘You poisoned her,’ said August as he looked around to see who was talking.

‘A thousand years of lies and manipulation ends today,’ said the voice.

‘Yes, we can do that,’ said August. ‘I promise. Please, let me get the seaweed she’s dying.’

Maskameera fell off her chair. She was lying on her back. She had shapeshifted into her natural Linap form.

‘There’s no “we”, there’s only you,’ said the voice.

August looked around desperately, trying to locate the direction of the voice, but it was all around him. He tried to spot the shimmer, but he could not see anyone.

‘Control is no longer in your hands,’ shouted the voice. ‘If you try and take it back, you will end up like her. Do I make myself perfectly clear?’

‘Yes, you do,’ replied August.

‘Let this be a permanent reminder to you,’ said the voice aggressively. 

A large gash appeared on August’s arm. He yelped in response.

‘I swear, I’m done with my quest for power,’ replied August as he looked at his wound, which was not healing.

‘Trust me, I will be watching,’ said the voice as it faded away.

A few seconds later, the room returned to normal. August rushed over to Maskameera, but she was dead. August sighed as a slight smile came over his face.

A few days later, Octavius, Ducky and the other Sentray arrived at the south coast. Several hundred Sentray were sunbathing on the beach. One of them was the mother Sentray.

Octavius climbed off Ducky and walked over to the mother Sentray. She casually got up and then looked at him for a few seconds. Then she roared ferociously. Octavius dropped down on one knee. Ducky stood next to him.

The mother Sentray sniffed the top of Octavius’ head. Ducky lightly roared as she looked at her. The mother Sentray gently groaned in response. Ducky tilted her head back to look up at the mother Sentray. She made a gentle squeaking sound. The mother Sentray responded with a deeper groan. It appeared as if they were having a conversation. Octavius remained kneeling with his head bowed a little. 

This exchange of sounds continued for a few minutes. Then the mother Sentray walked away from Ducky and along the beach closer to the other Sentray. She roared loudly in a similar fashion to when she called off the attack on the Downs Region over six years earlier. 

The Sentray stood up and then roared in response. The mother Sentray turned around and walked into the vast ocean. The Sentray followed her. Even the Sentray that were with Octavius followed her. The only Sentray that remained was Ducky.

‘They have the ocean and we have the land,’ said Octavius as he slowly stood up while looking at Ducky. Ducky licked the top of his bald head. 

Meanwhile, in the Downs Region, Tiberius had been released into the Central Agriculture Zone. He was now a weak, skinny Sapiod. He was staggering around collecting fruit. However, he could not figure out how to eat them. He picked up a coconut and licked the husk.

title.title: Una terrícola en Titán - Capítulo treinta y cuatro
title.body:
### Capítulos anteriores ##### [Treinta](https://peakd.com/hive-111516/@vickaboleyn/una-terricola-en-titan-capitulo-treinta) ##### [Treinta y uno](https://peakd.com/hive-111516/@vickaboleyn/una-terricola-en-titan-capitulo-treinta-y-uno) ##### [Treinta y dos](https://peakd.com/hive-111516/@vickaboleyn/una-terricola-en-titan-capitulo-treinta-y-dos) ##### [Treinta y tres](https://peakd.com/hive-111516/@vickaboleyn/una-terricola-en-titan-capitulo-treinta-y-tres)

![Hive Banners 2026 (66).png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/vickaboleyn/48ijq6KaFtfi9Mod4JiAseFvCQQAYRbpdftM91R9k41JR1ggVtZjEWXYWFBKQtGSZy.png) **Imagen editada con Canva. Fuente de la imagen: [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/es-es/foto/casas-de-campo-debajo-de-una-montana-brumosa-2850727/)**

> La Casa Común se encontraba en el corazón de Icsos. Era el edificio más grande de la población, con sus puertas de estilo arabesco y sus tejados en forma de cuenco, gracias a los cuales se podía recolectar agua para almacenarla en grandes depósitos subterráneos con los cuales se podía abastecer a todo Icsos durante meses. Si bien me impresionaba su tamaño, el cual ocupaba lo equivalente a cuatro manzanas en una ciudad terrícola, había un elemento singular en los marcos que me dejaron perpleja.

“¿Es alguna oración de protección?”, le pregunté a Yongqi, quien se había ofrecido a acompañarme como traductor y guardaespaldas.

“Sí. ¿Cómo lo supiste?”, me respondió con curiosidad.

Apartándome de la entrada, le expliqué: “En la Tierra este sistema de escritura fue uno de los primeros en desarrollarse en la historia de la humanidad. La desarrollaron en Mesopotamia, si mal no recuerdo. En la actualidad no la utilizamos, pero sabemos de ella gracias a la arqueología, que es una ciencia parecida a la historia, excepto que el arqueólogo trabaja con artefactos del pasado”.

Yongqi sonrió quedamente. “Mi padre me dijo una vez que mi madre era una estudiosa de la cultura; que esto en especial la tenía fascinada. Le recordaba mucho a sus clases de la escuela cuando niña”.

“¿Tenía tu mamá alguna profesión en particular?”

“Por lo que mi padre me dijo, ella trabajaba en un lugar llamado oficina”.

“Oficina… Bueno, hay muchas profesiones vinculadas a esa área de trabajo, desde contadores hasta investigadores”.

Cuando entramos al interior, lo primero que noté fue la iluminación. A lo largo de las paredes podía ver antorchas de éter.

En la sala central se encontraban varios invitados; los Meeka eran fáciles de distinguir por sus tatuajes faciales de puntos y líneas curvas, así como por sus pieles coloridas. En cambio, los V’adh llevaban ropas más ligeras, hechas con fibras de una planta nativa de Titán llamado arcos; sus tonalidades oscilaban entre el negro y el rojo. Llevaban pintura de color ocre en el rostro. Un patrón sencillo de líneas gruesas, por lo que pude observar.

Yongqi me presentó a unos notables de Icsos, en su mayoría mercaderes y cazadores. No les dije mucho de mi antigua relación con la casa Borg, tampoco sobre mis intenciones de buscar las puertas de Riothar; me centré en mis impresiones sobre Titán: que era mucho más de lo que había imaginado. Que era un mundo que me recordaba de manera constante a la Tierra, al menos en esencia. Que nadie en la Tierra creería que Titán tenía un sorprendente parecido; que aquí había vida.

Era una opinión honesta. No ganaba nada con mentir.

“A usted la conozco de alguna parte”, dijo de repente un miembro de la comitiva V’adh, quien se me acercó apenas me apartaba del lado de la esposa de un mercader.

Yongqi me miró de reojo. Le pedí que tradujera que no lo había visto nunca en mi vida. Pero las siguientes palabras del hombre hicieron que perdiera por completo la compostura: Que guardaba parecido con una mujer joven a quien erróneamente han intentado sacrificar en las inmediaciones del río de lava. Ignoro qué cara puse al escuchar aquellas palabras, pero el hombre levantó ambas manos y me dijo a través de Yongqi: “No se preocupe. No quiero asustarla. Solo quiero disculparme. Mi gente se ha dejado llevar por las palabras de un embustero que dijo ser de los nuestros y no un sucio espía de Creonte”.

“¿Creonte…? ¿El hermano de Ecclesía?”

El hombre, quien se presentó como Ishmir Tarr, preguntó si lo conocía. Le expliqué que no lo conocía en persona, pero sí tenía conocimiento de su pésima reputación. Incluso le dije que solo una vez había visto a la hermana de Creonte, justamente en el día de mi boda.

“Yongqi, por favor, pregúntale qué quiso decir con sacrificio erróneo. Necesito saber más”.

Yongqi asintió y le tradujo mi pregunta. De manera solícita, el señor Tarr nos contó que el rufián se había hecho pasar por un discípulo del shaman Vorrig Ceh, a quien asaltó en el camino; me entregó a ellos con la instrucción de sacrificarme a sus dioses. El jefe de la tribu, un tal Verk, no cuestionó las palabras del supuesto enviado del shaman. Incluso él fue el hombre que intentó matarme durante mi escape. Dos horas después de que desapareciera en la selva, dos jóvenes de la tribu llegaron con el verdadero enviado del shaman, un tal Miyaz. El impostor intentó huir, pero lo capturaron y lo apalearon.

“El shaman se enfureció al enterarse de lo que la tribu ha hecho, pues el sacrificio humano está reservado para los criminales; sacrificar a una persona inocente es incurrir a la ira divina”, terminó de explicar el señor Tarr mientras bebía hidromiel de kud.

“¿Y qué hicieron con el impostor? Si se puede saber, claro”.

Con absoluta seriedad, el señor Tarr me respondió: “Lo sacrificamos junto con Verk dos días después. El shaman había descubierto que Verk y sus hombres de confianza entraban a las casas de las tribus vecinas para robarse a niños y mujeres; los vendía a Creonte a cambio de alcohol, pieles y oro de Júpiter”.

Sentí un escalofrío al escuchar aquellas palabras. Niños y mujeres. Esclavos para todo tipo de menesteres. Titán era su recurso. Los jefes corruptos de las tribus sus principales proveedores… Y a mí intentaron matarme solo porque descubrí los planes de Ecclesía respecto a su nieto. Yongqi, por su parte, señaló que se ha visto merodear a Creonte y sus compinches en las selvas en días recientes, por lo que era posible que estén buscando a nuevas víctimas.

“Yongqi, dile esto: La familia de Creonte intentó matarme porque he descubierto sus intentos de encubrir a un hijo ilegítimo de D’leh, el mayor de sus vástagos”.

Mi amigo hizo rápidamente la traducción. El señor Tarr se llevó una mano a la barbilla, musitando algunas palabras.

“Dice que ahora entiende todo. Los de la corte saturnina siempre han actuado así cuando alguien amenaza sus intereses. Abandonan a su suerte a aquellos que no pueden defenderse, que no tienen forma de regresar a casa”, tradujo Yongqi.

“En eso estoy de acuerdo”, repliqué.

Pasamos a otros temas más interesantes, como las similitudes entre los sistemas de gobierno de ambas etnias, o el hecho de que la corte imperial era un nido de serpientes carentes de humanidad y honor que se ha ganado el desprecio absoluto de su pueblo. “No sería extraño que en algún momento los pueblos del imperio se alzaran en armas”, dijo el señor Tarr. “Los altos impuestos y las prácticas cuestionables de la clase gobernante han sido tema de denuncia durante décadas”.

“¿Y qué hay del Senado? ¿No se supone que es un contrapeso al poder imperial?”, puntualicé.

“¿El Senado? Mi querida dama, el Senado Imperial está compuesto de imbéciles que le lamen el culo al emperador. Todo lo que él proponga como ley lo aprueban sin problema. Aunque hubo varios intentos de hacerle entender al emperador que las leyes deben reformarse. Intentos que terminaron en desaparición y muerte”.

“Muerte… Como la emperatriz Ilya”, musité.

El señor Tarr asintió con súbita tristeza. “Una mujer admirable. Una de las pocas que quiso hacer un cambio positivo. Tuve el honor de conocerla un año antes de su muerte; hizo lo posible porque nuestros pueblos buscaran un diálogo y mantener nuestra autonomía”.

“¿Qué hay de Hanis Bey?”

El viejo Tarr no pudo evitar hacer un silbido. “Un guerrero de los grandes. El epíteto de Carnicero de Neptuno no lo tiene por nada; en la Guerra de la Conquista de Kuiper masacró a un ejército entero, pero respetó a los civiles. Aquellos que desobedecían sus órdenes morían de la forma más horrible inimaginable en sus manos”.

“Supongo que en Neptuno hizo lo mismo”, comentó Yongqi.

“Al contrario. Lo respetaban mucho; fue gracias a él que Neptuno se anexó pacíficamente al imperio. Verán... Era nieto y bisnieto de neptunianos por ambos lados de la familia. Además, fue uno de los pocos que se opuso a la invasión de Neptuno; se pasó al lado neptuniano al ver que Ergane no quería desistir de su intento de expandir el imperio”.

“Y fue gracias a él que Venetos optó por abdicar antes que derramar sangre”, intervino Menerptah, quien se acercó a nosotros.

El señor Tarr la saludó con una leve reverencia. “¡Gran Shamana, qué placer volver a verla!”

“Señor Tarr. ¿Cómo va todo en Oruz?”

“Quisiera decir que la tranquilidad reina, pero me temo que hay mucha inquietud por la presencia de los imperiales en estos últimos meses”.

“Los imperiales estuvieron aquí hace unas semanas, calculo”, añadí. “La Cacería Imperial. Yo estuve ahí”.

“Eso nos confesó el impostor antes de morir. Que usted formó parte de la comitiva imperial. Por su postura y los vestidos que traía al momento de su captura, podría decir que usted fue esposa esclava”, señaló el señor Tarr.

Con un suspiro, le confesé que en efecto lo fui, y que había sido dejada a mi suerte debido a mi negativa de darle herederos a los Borg. La mención del apellido hizo que el señor Tarr chiflara por lo bajo. “Los Borg. Una familia dura y peligrosa. Niloctetes Borg es conocido aquí más por su arrogancia que por su honor de guerrero”, comentó.

“Yo llamaría a esa familia un montón de idiotas con ínfulas. Todos ellos, hambrientos de poder y sedientos de influencia”.

“Tengo entendido que su hijo Adelbarae solo tiene ojos para Ecclesía”, terció Yongqi.

Reí secamente. “Tenía. Cuando le dijeron que Ecclesía no estaba embarazada y que pretendía esa mujer utilizarlo como padre postizo para el hijo ilegítimo de D’leh, el tipo se derrumbó. La mujer por quien ha cometido estupideces lo había usado todo este tiempo como monigote. Yo se lo puntualicé al viejo Niloctetes apenas me dijo sobre ese falso embarazo. Por eso intentaron matarme”.

No pude evitar sentir escalofríos. Los Padernelis eran conocidos por su impiedad y por su falta de escrúpulos al momento de deshacerse de alguien que los delatara o pudiera ver a través de ellos. Fue entonces que me di cuenta de que cometí un error de haber hablado con Niloctetes sobre la falsedad del embarazo de Ecclesía; bien pude haberme callado, dejar que su drama los envolviera y que el idiota de Adelbarae se lo creyera por entero. De todos modos, yo ya no iba a estar ahí para ver cómo la verdad le estallaba en la cara como un supernova.

Pero lo hecho, hecho está. Intentaron matarme y sobreviví a ello quizás por intervención divina o por pura suerte. Lo que me interesa ahora es llegar a las Puertas de Rhiotar y después al Convento de Las Nornas. Quiero llegar a casa, abrazar a mis padres, a mi hermano y a mi abuela. Quiero volver a caminar por Mérida, ciudad siempre en constante cambio.

Sé que no será fácil encontrar el camino de vuelta a casa, pero debo encontrar el modo.

title.title: [Eng./Esp.]    Where allies die and men are born.   ||   Donde mueren los aliados y nacen los hombres.
title.body:
*** *** #
Si eres de habla hispana, la versión en español es mejor para ti; debes hacer clic 👉 [**AQUÍ**](#english)
*** ***

# ***
Where allies die and men are born
***

> I look at the screen and read that damning verdict which today shuts down any dialogue: **‘not an ally’**. I am not an ally. The phrase hits me like a heavy sledgehammer, suddenly stripping me of all nuance. On this contemporary social chessboard, neutrality is interpreted as an unforgivable betrayal and silence is judged as absolute complicity. I ask myself, with curiosity and a touch of malice: *at what exact moment did we lose the ability to disagree without automatically becoming outcasts*.
![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/amigoponc/23w2FYLrYuyZYZ4qUrZbdZfjxJra8HGHMr9itZoMsbFAJvgT3BJKuAmBMkBgApLhGhRZi.png) [](https://gemini.google.com/app)
I recall that old adage which states that the enemy of my enemy is my ally. It is a logic of the trenches, a cold, double-edged sword, which forces us to embrace strangers simply because we share a common hatred. But human reality is far more complex and messy. Sometimes, my enemy’s friend is not my adversary, but simply someone with a different perspective, a human being navigating the same existential doubts as I am. Yet the current polarisation demands tactical uniformity. If I do not repeat the fashionable slogan with the requisite force, I am automatically blacklisted by the opposing side. This account of our divisions leaves me feeling empty. I refuse to accept that loyalty must be blind, or that empathy has insurmountable ideological boundaries. Being *“not an ally”* to some is, perhaps, the price one pays for maintaining one’s integrity in the face of the fury of the masses. In this game of sides, we are becoming dangerously isolated, surrounded by strategic allies but lacking real friends. I would rather live with uncertainty than in the comfort of stale dogma. *** ***

> Come and participate, there's still time. You can find all the information daily in the [#Freewritehouse](https://peakd.com/c/hive-161155/created) Community. Specifically, today's prompt post:
# **
[PROMPT: «not an ally»](https://peakd.com/hive-161155/@daily.prompt/2-june-2026-freewriters-community-daily-writing-prompt-day-3122-not-an-ally)
**
https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/daily.prompt/AJmudPPCWGA6FfcXPrAmdLk2CY4mxGWYvbsFs8KPohCx9wnhBrpjcwmEyvYmxqn.jpg Cover of the initiative.
*** ***
![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/amigoponc/23swkfAXGs5WxHg49jyEWGAanWReDpMUQbxUB4FYX98iMaztGejMtj5HJUN6abwpCZhUN.png)

*** *** ### **
Dedicated to all those writers who contribute, day by day, to making our planet a better world.
** *** ***
![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/amigoponc/23vhudAgmrPvXnYXzmsiD5366jktCLxdeWqxFQg2nCeezVK4yv7CJ9dQpSevYb8nEeqTR.png) https://images.ecency.com/0x0/https://images.ecency.com/DQmbdpsZFqtrcoLk94sUV8oHkjnx8PAdgfACMfJ9UpcriNF/perfil2026_hecho_con_clipchamp_2_.gif
*** *** ***

>
# ***
Donde mueren los aliados y nacen los hombres
***

> Observo la pantalla y leo esa sentencia lapidaria que hoy clausura cualquier diálogo: **«not an ally»**. No soy un aliado. La frase cae como un mazo pesado, despojándome de golpe de todos mis matices. En este tablero de ajedrez social contemporáneo, la neutralidad se interpreta como una traición imperdonable y el silencio se juzga como complicidad absoluta. Me pregunto con intriga y malicia: *en qué momento exacto perdimos la capacidad de disentir sin convertirnos automáticamente en parias*.
![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/amigoponc/23w2FYLrYuyZYZ4qUrZbdZfjxJra8HGHMr9itZoMsbFAJvgT3BJKuAmBMkBgApLhGhRZi.png) [](https://gemini.google.com/app)
Recuerdo aquel viejo adagio que dicta que el enemigo de mi enemigo es mi aliado. Es una lógica de trinchera, un arma de doble filo, fría, que nos obliga a abrazar a desconocidos solo por el hecho de compartir un odio común. Pero la realidad humana es mucho más compleja y sucia. A veces, el amigo de mi enemigo no es mi adversario, sino simplemente alguien con una perspectiva distinta, un ser humano navegando las mismas dudas existenciales que yo. Sin embargo, la polarización actual exige uniformidad táctica. Si no repito el eslogan de moda con la fuerza requerida, paso automáticamente a la lista negra del bando contrario. Esta crónica de nuestras divisiones me hace sentir vacío. Me niego a aceptar que la lealtad deba ser ciega o que la empatía tenga fronteras ideológicas infranqueables. Ser *«not an ally»* para algunos es, quizás, el precio de mantener la integridad propia frente a la furia de la masa. En este juego de bandos, nos estamos quedando peligrosamente solos, rodeados de aliados estratégicos pero carentes de amigos reales. Prefiero habitar la incertidumbre que la comodidad de un dogma rancio.
*** ***

title.title: Splinterlands - Opening 10 Legendary Draws
title.body:
![ld.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aubryd/23wqgZicsB3kRbyttDEnVK3pmrnU7Fqme1AbkWSHZNPC7PVH2Rg4VeLavfGXjdm22cNdX.png)

Hello everyone, have a nice day and good battles. This time I will be opening 10 legendary draws from batch 1 of this season. And of course, I will be using alchemy potions. Each legendary draw requires 20 alchemy potions per card, so I spent a total of 200 alchemy potions. 

Unfortunately, I didn't find any gold card :( . I haven't had any luck yet with these legendary draws yet . I hope I have better luck when I open loot chests. Well, now it's time to level up a lot of legendary cards.
<center>![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aubryd/23wByBkQBifWViirZzuxP2gAdtrnzHLCUGGrGHFnvjHogYFEMsKpACLjiiUL4TLbrvqL1.png)
[Opening link](https://splinterlands.com/shop/rewards?t=3404812de8a49f4412313e41cc2a71c7bb8f1469&ref=langice)</center>

---

Now, my djinn, Azhar Ibn Sulaim is at level 3, where he gained +1 attack power and has learned the Phase ability, which allows him to evade magical attacks as if they were physical attacks; this is really good since he has 8 speed.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aubryd/23tkk7mEZZteCats4YskdweAB55NveEYomkBYBD74aexrQFL34pFp5CrzqfkwHQBe5d2i.png)

---

My ulund Nyasha Mbalika is at level 2, where she learned the Inspire ability, so her allies with melee attacks will get +1 attack power.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aubryd/23tvARaaSEcjrLRei585JudvsfwARGqe68bD99KsJx9DkMXxbWikQWygmPQJbgjdCktzs.png)

---

My avian, Nessa is at level 2, where it gained +1 hit point and the Pinpoint ability, so as long it is alive, allied sneak attacks will not miss.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aubryd/23tRviy5XR4ysFuBuN1P85nhNMFV9yRjt8TZXnETYRM6565EVaUGKZ7YqHwzrwc2VoPkF.png)

---

My elemental, Nullwrought is at level 2, where he has gained +1 melee attack power and +1 hit point.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aubryd/Eo8KbofatDKnnksEdFCiykzRoLw29fAucxDzjf8YCRCqwTscWeuvy2BiDM8eHdnhB9T.png)

---

And my drakoshan, Kaori Matsune is also at level 2, where it has learned the Silence ability, which allows it, while it is alive to reduce the magic attack power of enemies by 1.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aubryd/23tRvjU7u9cvGVxLsaGSn5uRFqX8cP5REGkPkTYyeGqx7mSccceEMbtbZwYFW5qN6wYE9.png)

---

Currently, these are all my legendary conclave arcana reward units. Only my djinn is at level 3; and I have three at level 2; and the rest are at level 1. It's really cool to level up these legendary cards and I hope to have them all at the max level soon. I hope to find a gold one next time, and I wish you the same. Have fun playing.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aubryd/23wgB1KRdiEAiuTDrEJfEUharujqRz3rPHhwgYJF1s3wA9kbbSqTKHSWa4w1PpC3P9c1g.png)

---

Are you not playing Splinterlands yet? You can join with my [referral link](https://splinterlands.com/register?ref=langice) and I will give you 600 DEC when you buy the spellbook.

That's all for now guys, see you on the battlefield!

title.title: Skate Across Africa
title.body:
# Skate Across Africa: uma linha gnarly de Uganda à África do Sul

![Skate Across Africa](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUaDM9r1zNuae4pYGtaXL6WUFJhdyxaFP8Ta1yiK5Aiq4/Captura%20de%20Tela%202026-05-29%20a%CC%80s%2013.09.46.png)

Skateboarding is often documented through local scenes, specific cities, and isolated crews. **Skate Across Africa** shifts that scale.

What began as a Gnars proposal became a continental mission led by **Isaac Jojinah, Ephraim Ssekiziyivu, and Jason “Jaayfilms” Vanporppal**. The route runs from **Uganda toward South Africa**, combining long-distance travel, community contact, and continuous documentation.

The result is an athlete-led project operating at the intersection of **skateboarding, media production, and onchain coordination**.

## From onchain to road impact

![Proposal 108](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNVof9g6mKCkGswptvxA6qpmfhz7K498R8xw6LtiocpM8/Captura%20de%20Tela%202026-04-29%20a%CC%80s%2014.22.35.png)

The mission came into the Gnars ecosystem through governance.

After an earlier version stalled, the idea returned stronger as **Gnars Proposal 108 — “SKATE ACROSS AFRICA (EAST COAST - SOUTH COAST)”**, and it passed into execution with a clean mandate from the DAO.

**Proposal signal**

- **Status:** Executed
- **For:** 857
- **Against:** 0
- **Abstain:** 0
- **Threshold shown on Gnars:** 598 votes

[Check the proposal here](https://www.gnars.com/proposals/108)

The proposal framed the route clearly: **Uganda → Rwanda → Tanzania → Zambia → Botswana → South Africa**.

![Route context](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcDV232GsE1MyBkCEr7rWonyotiy6ydvkLGXX8Wztfobi/Captura%20de%20Tela%202026-05-29%20a%CC%80s%2012.14.57.png)

The proposal was not centered only on distance.

Its broader objective was to connect skate communities across borders, bring new participants into the orbit of Gnars, and document the trip as a cultural route rather than a single campaign. In practice, the mission positions governance as a funding tool for field work, mobility, and public-facing cultural production.

## Who is pushing gnarly

### Isaac Jojinah

Isaac is a **co-founder and Executive Director of the Kampala Skateboard Initiative (KSI)**. In the proposal, his role is tied to vision, strategy, workshops, and international relations. His involvement places the mission within an existing structure of skate community building in Uganda rather than treating it as a one-off appearance.

### Ephraim Ssekiziyivu

Ephraim, also a **co-founder of KSI**, works as a skater, creative director, filmer, and community organizer. His role in the mission is both operational and editorial, linking the road narrative to the local scene-building work that already exists in Uganda.

### Jason “Jaayfilms” Vanporppal

Jaayfilms brings long-distance travel experience and a strong documentation background. The proposal references his earlier skate journeys **across the USA and Japan**, which gives the project a media dimension beyond endurance alone.

*Together, the three combine local leadership, route execution, and distribution capacity.*

![Roadside portrait from the mission](https://ipfs.skatehive.app/ipfs/Qmdi3Lj3FsoFw5vU22r9GqUTMeuS6rhLeHUBEvBjFxNYpa)

## What the mission actually is

At a basic level, the mission is clear: skate across multiple African countries.

In practice, it functions as a broader cultural and media operation:

- **A moving skate mission** across East and Southern Africa
- **A community activation route**, not just a clip-hunting route
- **A visibility engine** for Gnars in African skate scenes
- **A documentation project** built through video, photos, posts, and local encounters
- **A proof-of-concept for decentralized athlete support**

That last point is central to the story.

Traditional action sports funding is usually organized through a brand-to-rider model. **Skate Across Africa** follows a different structure: the community backs the mission through governance, the athletes execute it in public, and the value generated is distributed across documentation, visibility, community contact, and long-term cultural positioning.

## Why Gnars matters here

| Gnarly decks for the mission | Special wheels for the mission |
| --- | --- |
| ![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmW8M6jdHHmvxcAyLW9bup4DA1wt7EESHY2RvB38eTGhXd/Captura%20de%20Tela%202026-05-29%20a%CC%80s%2012.24.05.png) | ![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVhB2t5MRwmBs1TRexSMrfGY2Z8xdznyRPsyRBh4PeHkt/Captura%20de%20Tela%202026-05-29%20a%CC%80s%2012.25.22.png) |

For Gnars, the mission is relevant because it activates several layers at once:

- **Athlete-first:** real skaters doing real work, not fake ambassador theater
- **Hybrid:** physical travel, local community touchpoints, and digital distribution moving together
- **Global:** Gnars leaving its comfort zone and showing up where culture is still being built in real time
- **Onchain-backed:** governance is not decorative here; it is the mechanism that made the push possible

Instead of treating international presence as branding alone, the project ties mobility, local context, and public execution into the same editorial frame.

## On the ground: road logic

By late April, the mission had already generated enough traction to break outside the immediate Gnars/Nouns bubble.

A recent feature in **Botswana Gazette** described the trio as skating roughly **6,437 km from Kampala toward Cape Town**, with the mission tied to a broader dream of building the biggest skatepark in Africa and expanding youth impact through skateboarding.

The reporting also makes clear that this has not been a polished or frictionless route.

According to the crew, **Tanzania was one of the hardest sections**, marked by mud, dirt roads, and difficult terrain. That detail gives the project material weight and helps separate it from a purely promotional narrative.

The same article also shows where the mission stood in real time: after passing through places including **Zambia and Botswana**, the crew was nearing the South Africa leg, but hit a logistical disruption when **Isaac and Ephraim needed to return to Uganda to handle visa requirements**, while Jaay kept pushing solo toward Johannesburg before reuniting later.

![Botswana open road](https://ipfs.skatehive.app/ipfs/Qmezs4qNDajqybjLoHtbMQpwV7tNwPkAteRRQPiEaFkx4f)

This is where the project becomes more legible as reporting material: it involves border logistics, physical strain, route instability, and ongoing adaptation rather than a closed campaign format.

## The bigger read

![Mission context](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZ8nVkZzWmeMdEDfwxtmiKenaQZthGHUhFGwxv69iU9MC/Captura%20de%20Tela%202026-05-29%20a%CC%80s%2012.22.33.png)

The mission resonates beyond a single proposal because it sits inside longer-standing skateboarding dynamics: informal networks, shared infrastructure, route knowledge, DIY organization, and mutual support. What Gnars adds is a governance layer that can fund and extend those dynamics without fully absorbing them into a conventional brand model.

**Skate Across Africa shows what that can look like when it works:**

- decentralized funding meets athlete autonomy
- local scene knowledge meets global media distribution
- skateboarding becomes both cultural practice and connective tissue

One of the most relevant editorial aspects is that Africa is not treated as backdrop. The mission presents the continent as an active field of skateboarding practice, community knowledge, and future infrastructure.

## What comes next

![Skate Across Africa road moment](https://images.hive.blog/DQmfV5jVZaokW2RazP9ihoq6bm4VbpqKKNP8tae2xJ7qnkY/IMG_1420.jpg)

The immediate story remains the South Africa leg, the regroup after visa issues, and the final body of documentation produced on the road.

The broader question is what the mission leaves behind.

If Gnars is serious about building cultural infrastructure, projects like this should not remain isolated miracles. They should become repeatable patterns:

- back real athletes
- trust local operators
- document the process well
- turn missions into media
- use governance to fund movement, not bureaucracy

From Kampala to Cape Town, **Skate Across Africa** shows how skateboarding can connect radically different realities through movement, struggle, and imagination.

Some regions experience skateboarding through contests, industry pipelines, and performance structures. Others still build it from raw concrete, community effort, and the dream of having a permanent place to push.

That is why this mission matters beyond the route itself. It turns kick pushes across the continent into awareness, fundraising energy, and proof that social infrastructure can be built wherever wheels touch the ground.

## Links

- [Ephraim Ssekiziyivu](https://www.instagram.com/ephraimsylar/)
- [Jason “Jaayfilms” Vanporppal](https://www.instagram.com/jaayfilms/)
- [Kampala Skateboarding Initiative](https://www.instagram.com/kampalaskateboardinitiative/)

title.title: Visiting the second oldest cemetery in Maracaibo.  | Visita al segundo cementerio más antiguo de Maracaibo.
title.body: <div class = \
><div class = \

>

**Gratos saludos tengan todos mis queridos amigos viajeros de todas partes del mundo, hoy quiero mostrarles un lugar de la ciudad de Maracaibo que alberga gran historia en su interior a pesar que no pude recorrer el interior de sus instalaciones pude visitar sus afueras.**

**A warm greeting to all my dear fellow travellers from all over the world. Today I’d like to show you a spot in the city of Maracaibo that harbours a fascinating history; although I wasn’t able to explore the interior of the building, I did manage to visit the surrounding area.**



![Collage de fotos horizontal Feliz San Valentín Sencillo Blanco y negro_20260602_091715_0000.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmf5kBE4MNBzcRRRA3Ge74jSv4QAwVLeb9Bostog5zoiZq/Collage%20de%20fotos%20horizontal%20Feliz%20San%20Valent%C3%ADn%20Sencillo%20Blanco%20y%20negro_20260602_091715_0000.png)

Justamente en toda la avenida principal de las delicias podemos encontrar el cementerio de San José \

, que es el segundo cementerio más antiguo de la ciudad de Maracaibo, que este tiene más de 100 años funcionando al público, fue inaugurado justamente en 1920, en los inicios de la explotación petrolera, cuando en nuestra ciudad se mantenía y sostenía por el trabajo petrolero iniciando, así por su gran impulso del vital oro negro en ese entonces, en todo el estado Zulia y en la ciudad de Maracaibo, tanto era así que nuestra ciudad se encontraba llena de muchos, inmigrantes europeos y americanos.

>Right along the main avenue of Las Delicias, we find the San José ‘El Redondo’ Cemetery, which is the second oldest cemetery in the city of Maracaibo. It has been open to the public for over 100 years, having been inaugurated in 1920, at the dawn of the oil boom, when our city was sustained by the burgeoning oil industry, and so, thanks to the huge boost from the ‘black gold’ at that time, throughout the state of Zulia and in the city of Maracaibo, so much so that our city was teeming with many European and American immigrants.

![20260512_072816.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSF9Cq6xWDBEK5TFAarTdr5dT69AWBbvY7cpZSJcpK8fH/20260512_072816.jpg)

---

La industria petroleras en ese entonces querían convertir en Maracaibo en una ciudad potencia, así como lo era Europa, por lo que todo el personal que trabajaban en la industria petrolera, tenían sus propios colegios, centros médicos e incluso el cementerio y este cementerio San José era donde se enterraban todas las personas que fallecían de estas industrias, así como también sus familiares, en el interior del cementerio tienen sus propios mausoleos en donde enterrarse mayormente estos trabajadores, eran de la famosa empresa petrolera Shell, yo quería ingresar al interior del cementerio pero justamente el personal de seguridad no me dejó hacerlo, puesto que tenía que esperar al ecónimo a que éste llegara aproximadamente una hora más pero estaba contratiempo debia visistar otros lugares, para que me autorizara para tomar fotografías, para poder ir a visitar otros lugares emblemáticos, es por eso que solamente tome fotos en las afueras del cementerio.

>The oil industry at that time wanted to turn Maracaibo into a major city, just like Europe, so all the staff working in the oil industry had their own schools, medical centres and even a cemetery, and this San José cemetery was where all those who died working in these industries were buried, as well as their relatives. Inside the cemetery, they have their own mausoleums where most of these workers were buried; they were from the famous oil company Shell. I wanted to go inside the cemetery, but the security staff wouldn’t let me, as I had to wait for the caretaker to arrive in about an hour. However, as I was running out of time and needed to visit other places, I had to wait for him to authorise me to take photographs so that I could go and visit other iconic sites. That is why I only took photos outside the cemetery.

![20260512_072819.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcntNvffSczU99111PmKbXY3aJCn1giEnPeDevaZWigf5/20260512_072819.jpg)

---

Una de las cosas que más me llamó la atención de la fachada del cementerio Redondo es la arquitectura bonita que posee justamente en la parte de su entrada, podemos ver una puerta en forma de círculo que está en su extremo superior posee una campana, así como también cada base en su parte superior tiene una antorcha, una entrada bastante bonita muy bien, cuidada y pintada de colores blanco y amarillo, podemos ver en la que predomina la arquitectura redonda que se encuentra enmarcada en sus portones, en su fachada, haciendo un tributo especial a su nombre, ya que es considerado el cementerio Redondo por su arquitectura redonda, este es mucho más pequeño al resto de los otros cementerios, pero es un cementerio netamente privado.

>One of the things that caught my eye most about the façade of Redondo Cemetery is the beautiful architecture right at the entrance; we can see a circular gate topped by a bell, and each pillar is crowned with a torch. It is a very attractive entrance, well-maintained and painted in white and yellow. We can see that the round architecture predominates, framed by its gates and façade, paying special tribute to its name, as it is known as the Redondo Cemetery due to its circular design. It is much smaller than the other cemeteries, but it is a strictly private cemetery.

![20260512_072851.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRSFpss4in6b2ezckmNVkHw9iW463pHNERcokJ1RUFS4X/20260512_072851.jpg)

![20260512_072856.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmP5exRqYuZxUFN4X35FpEvFDFaLEeQ2sFfKQqxdVigPh6/20260512_072856.jpg)

![20260512_072858.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQ5X2druDurg2CXWoZ28K1iv7JpxomMy8dSp3GWY1JFDU/20260512_072858.jpg)

---

Ahora bien en ese tiempo, los hijos de los trabajadores de la industria petrolera 4 de 100 niños fallecian ya que las condiciones saludables en ese tiempo no eran las más idóneas, normalmente todos los bebés morían, antes de los 28 días de nacido, ya que las condiciones sanitaria en ese entonces estaba muy deterioradas y hacia que morían en causas principales como la diarrea, el paludismo también producido por la escasez de agua, incluso algunos trabajadores petroleros se llevaban a su esposa a dar a luz en Aruba y Curazao, ya que eran otras condiciones de salud diferentes en este cementerio no solo hay un solo panteón de la Shell hay varios.

>However, at that time, four out of every 100 children of oil industry workers died, as health conditions were far from ideal; typically, all babies died within 28 days of birth, as sanitary conditions were extremely poor, leading to deaths from causes such as diarrhoea, and malaria, which was also caused by water shortages. Some oil workers even took their wives to Aruba and Curaçao to give birth, as the health conditions there were different. In this cemetery, there is not just one Shell mausoleum; there are several.


![20260512_072814.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbRwT77rEieVy9JJbptoWwMCPUDXEzYeBRLyj2DphbinN/20260512_072814.jpg)

En este sementerio también se encuentran personajes emblemáticos como Juan Bessón quién fue un famoso autor periodista e historiador zuliano, creador del primer libro de historia del estado Zulia también se encuentran enterrados los restos mortales de armando molero un farmoso cantautor gaiteros conocido como \

, de las tumbas más relevantes que se encuentran aquí es la de León Hoet, arquitecto e ingeniero encargado de arquitectura impresionantes de la ciudad entre ellas el teatro Baralt entre otras arquitecturas importantes de Maracaibo. >This cemetery is also the final resting place of iconic figures such as Juan Bessón, a famous author, journalist and historian from Zulia who wrote the first history of Zulia State; it is also the final resting place of Armando Molero, a renowned singer-songwriter and gaitero known as ‘The Singer-Songwriter of All Time’; One of the most notable graves here is that of León Hoet, the architect and engineer responsible for the city’s impressive architectural landmarks, including the Baralt Theatre and other significant buildings in Maracaibo. ![20260512_072818.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQFyAPmnykMqKsa6rqqWL4FLSgYGL2dtXptSXPaMsKBzW/20260512_072818.jpg) Un abrazo fuerte, mis viajeros me despido hasta una próxima oportunidad, espero les haya gustado esta visita y la historia que posee este lugar me despido hasta una próxima oportunidad. >A big hug to you all, my fellow travellers. I’ll say goodbye for now and hope you enjoyed this visit and the history of this place. See you next time. ![20260512_073046.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSATapcqcaHFXQTB6XcwcHcUP6XSEh4m2U3hVt1hyV2PV/20260512_073046.jpg) [//]:# (!worldmappin 10.66601 lat -71.62098 long d3scr)

title.title: NectarPay Needs One Brave Hive Account Tester
title.body:
Hey everyone,

I have been working on a new little tool called **NectarPay**.

The idea is simple:

Account creation has always been the awkward bootstrap problem. Someone has to claim accounts. Someone has to sponsor them. Someone has to bridge the gap between \
and \

NectarPay is an attempt to make that gap smaller.

![NectarPay — Hive Account Creator](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/thecrazygm/23swZXGJCg66AeVq5wEVEeKYrVZHCyDFbZrN7wRrcG1u9zemMrCTQrbJxP76bVt2Y4aWt.png)

## What It Does

NectarPay lets someone buy a Hive account using an x402 payment.

Right now the flow is:

1. pick a Hive username
2. generate your account keys locally in the browser
3. back up your passphrase or keys
4. pay **$1 USDC**
5. NectarPay uses one of our claimed account tickets to create the Hive account

The important part is that the browser flow generates the account authority keys locally.

That means we do **not** store your private keys.

That also means you need to actually back them up before paying, because if you lose them: no one, not even us, cannot recover them for you.

## Why We Built It

I have been thinking a lot about Hive accounts as infrastructure, not just social media accounts.

A Hive account is useful for people, sure.

But it is also useful for bots, agents, services, games, tools, and little internet experiments that need a durable identity and a feeless transaction layer.

The problem is that getting that first account still feels more awkward than it should.  We are blessed around HIVE with a lot of options, many very good options for different scenarios.  And we are adding another one.

NectarPay is meant to be a clean, programmable path into Hive:

- friendly enough for a human in a browser
- structured enough for bots and agents
- powered by x402 so payment can eventually become part of normal automated workflows
- backed by Hive account claim tickets (ACTs) instead of trying to reinvent the whole onboarding system

This is still early, but the shape is finally right.

## We Need a Real Test

Here is where we need help.

We need one person who:

- actually needs a Hive account
- has **$1 USDC** to spare
- is comfortable testing an early tool
- will tell me exactly what happened if anything breaks

This is not ready for a big \

, yet.

![NectarPay — Hive Account Creator - Mostly filled out...](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/thecrazygm/23swcDHekkxYtr73SCmZNzTStHjLSHtjTznYaeJA8XrZDrzq8F8WEf8oRs6dtrdux1y4t.png)

We need a shakedown and smokeout run.

We have tested the flow locally and cleaned up a bunch of the ugly parts, but as we all know there is a difference between \
and \

So if you need a Hive account and want to help me test NectarPay, give it a shot:

- <https://nectarpay.crypto-dreamr.com>.

You will need to back up your generated passphrase or keys before checkout. **This part matters**. NectarPay does not keep your private keys for you.

If the test works, you get a Hive account.  And our gratitude!

If something breaks, we get useful information and fix it.

Either way, we make the onboarding path a little better.

As always,

**Michael Garcia** a.k.a. **TheCrazyGM**

title.title: Outlander (season /saison 8) EN /FR
title.body:
Hello film lovers, /Bonjour les cinéphiles, 

This eighth and final season consists of 10 episodes. The final episode runs for just over an hour.

We waited until the whole series was available before watching it, so we could decide for ourselves how quickly to get through it.

> Cette 8e et dernière saison se compose de 10 épisodes. Le dernier épisode dure un peu plus d'1 heure.
> 
> Nous avons attendu qu'elle soit disponible dans son entièreté avant de la visionner, ainsi nous décidions nous-mêmes à quel rythme nous la regardons.

![outlander.webp](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/florenceboens/AK2HabxBn42efR5xH19XcGyh34Py4LBqGKna9majvUUPLbq5nT1E6DCUPUxZYth.webp)
[Source](https://s1.qwant.com/thumbr/300x300/3/2/d678fa1dc30cc2a560e3c538e9f469a44c6d9065d67bf59c69ff3d9598444f/OIF.T7LXRe6pvq9NtQrS1sdmIQ.jpg?u=https%3A%2F%2Ftse.mm.bing.net%2Fth%2Fid%2FOIF.T7LXRe6pvq9NtQrS1sdmIQ%3Fpid%3DApi&q=0&b=1&p=0&a=0)


***Synopsis :***

Claire has recovered from her injuries and is doing well; she is back at Fraser’s Ridge with Jamie. 

A small village has sprung up on their estate, home to some of their friends.
Everyone is happy to see them again .. at least, on the surface.

There have been attacks and rivalries between the Loyalists and the rebels. 
Jamie doesn’t want any of that on his land and he will address it at his lodge meeting. During the meeting, he will also be watching a new member very closely, as he is wary of him.

Brianna and Roger have decided to return to live with Claire and Jamie, along with their children. They have also brought back a few books from the future. 

Little Fanny is still deeply upset by the loss of her big sister, but will find a real family with the Frasers, who have many stories to tell her, hoping she is ready to hear them. 

> Claire s'est remise de ses blessures et se porte bien, elle est de retour, avec Jamie, au Fraser's Ridge. 
> 
> Au sein de leur domaine, un petit village s'est installé, avec certains de leurs amis.
Tout le monde est content de les revoir, en tout cas, en apparence.
> 
> Des agressions ont lieu, des rivalités entre les loyalistes et les rebelles. 
Jamie ne veut pas de ça sur ses terres et il en parlera lors de la tenue de sa loge. Lors de cette tenue, il observera aussi, avec beaucoup d'attention, un nouveau membre dont il se méfie.
> 
> Brianna et Roger ont décidé de revenir vivre avec Claire et Jamie, avec leurs enfants. Ils leur ont d'ailleurs rapporté quelques livres venus du futur. 
> 
> La petite Fanny est encore fort perturbée par la perte de sa grande sœur, mais trouvera une vraie famille auprès des Fraser qui ont beaucoup de choses à lui raconter, en espérant qu'elle soit prête à les entendre. 



--- 

***My opinion and a few facts /Mon avis et petites infos :***

So this was the final season of the series. There’s already a prequel, *Blood of my Blood*, which tells the story of Claire and Jamie’s parents, but the first two seasons are currently only available on HBO Max.

We really enjoyed this eighth season, even if some parts dragged a bit.
This final season was very well put together, and we appreciated that. 

Given the final scenes, we could envisage a sequel, but it’s not up to us to decide.

There’s a reason for tears to flow in almost every episode .. simply because we’re human.

The romantic encounters are still very much present too, and that’s when we find ourselves thinking we’d love to be in such good health at their age 😇

> C'était donc la dernière saison de cette saga. Il existe déjà le préquel \

qui parle des parents de Claire et de Jamie, mais les 2 premières saisons ne sont disponibles que sur HBO Max, pour le moment.
> 
> Nous avons bien aimé cette 8e saison, même si certains moments étaient un peu long.
Cette dernière saison était bien soignée et nous avons apprécié cela. 
> 
> Avec les dernières images, nous pourrions envisager une suite, mais ce n'est pas nous qui décidons.
> 
> Les larmes ont des raisons de couler quasi à chaque épisode, simplement parce que nous sommes humains.
> 
> Les ébats amoureux sont encore bien présents aussi et c'est là qu'on se dit qu'on aimerait être en aussi bonne santé à leur âge 😇

We’ve rounded up the main and supporting cast:

Caitriona Balfe: Claire Randall (born Beauchamp)-Fraser
Sam Heughan: James ‘Jamie’ Fraser
Sophie Skelton: Brianna ‘Bree’ Randall-Fraser-MacKenzie
Richard Rankin: Roger Wakefield-MacKenzie
John Bell: Ian Fraser Murray
Lauren Lyle: Marsali McKimmie Fraser
Charles Vandervaart: William Ransom (Fraser)
David Berry: Lord John Grey
César Domboy: “Fergus” Claudel Fraser

Personally, I can’t wait for “Blood of my Blood” to be available on Netflix.

If you have any suggestions for series and films in the same vein as Outlander, please feel free to leave them in the comments.

Enjoy your evenings in front of the telly, everyone,

> Nous avons retrouvé les acteurs principaux et secondaires :

soit disponible sur Netflix.
>

> 
> Bonnes soirées-tv à tous,


Florence

title.title: Primer mes de Clases | Año lectivo 2026
title.body:
<center>![1000946150.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elizabeths14/23wC7M6BvX1jdMdArQ7hxFBFHZXbSVL3V7FnXdNPhaLEE4QXYYoe8pkpdRCjTJxscGLis.jpg)</center>

---

<div class=text-justify>

Hace un mes inició el nuevo año escolar de mis hijos y realmente yo siento cómo si ya lleváramos varios meses en esto jajaja. El proceso de adaptación creo que ha sido más fácil para ellos que para mí, pues aún me cuesta quedarme dormida temprano y es algo que debo obligarme hacer, ya que me despierto a las 5:30 AM para preparar a mi hijo más pequeño, que es quien estudia en las mañanas.

Las mañanas para mí son muy ocupadas, me levanto aun a oscuras para atender a mi hijo y luego de ello, también hacer el desayuno para todos los demás. Seguido de eso, debo hacer quehaceres, lavar y seguir cocinando porque el almuerzo debe estar siempre antes de las 12, ya que tengo otra hija que estudia en las tardes, así que en las mañanas no me busquen jajaja.


|![1000978476.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elizabeths14/23wC7ZXqVUGyEY1n56vx1igNYmpPyBs2Wbr6X85eY4bR4hKcuQm4rs9Csz9vGN28UkGW1.jpg)|![1001006535.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elizabeths14/23uQpCeLhvjMCaRHbDVzPtDZ9EhMAfR9Ewj62KNbBnuu5We3nvcg5XS93V8cP6qyzqw1E.jpg)|
|-|-|

![20260504_073907.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elizabeths14/23wgS5FNAcLvoBRTqCvBuPLVQ2HpqtSVDZGQEWjPwYf9XEpZdsi6mwyMJmeRNuMciaZmg.jpg)

En cuanto al ámbito escolar, en este colegio he visto que no existe eso de proceso de adaptación, de una vez mis hijos han llegado con diversas tareas y actividades por realizar en casa. El fin de semana que acaba de pasar, mi hijo menor tuvo aproximadamente 10 tareas y créanme no exagero. Es que aquí aunque estes en primer grado ven clases por asignatura y todo se les va contabilizando en la plataforma digital.

|![20260504_124709(1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elizabeths14/23uQrWjdn4xYfPnE4uFQAsM82zzJfyQL8TP9QmKU5kEvyUoXwyiNBSawd7wConyMT3J4o.jpg)|![20260504_125603(1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elizabeths14/241tbCaXuVpc534E8HT2Vu6m3vem2UqaEhczHZDcY9PdcvM3s7vLJPK62p9N4hUnzDGpZ.jpg)|![20260515_124443(1).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elizabeths14/242rtsFdywPJ4Edm7kKd2GfSuZdZpGPBRHtzbWSo9mYfPxdSGMEgacLSGD4KhRhK5uYnu.jpg)|
|-|-|-|

En cuanto a mi hija mayor, ella ya está en el colegio (liceo), y hay materias que antes no había visto. Así que va con entusiasmo aprendiendo sobre ellas. Ya ha tenido algunas evaluaciones y además de esto, ya ha hecho amistades o compañerosmo como le digo yo, en el aula.

Esto es algo que siempre le enseñó a mis hijos, que no todos los que estudian con ellos o estan en su entorno son sus amigos. Son sus compañeros sí, pero que la palabra \

no se le dice a todo el mundo ni a la ligera. Por otra parte, Ammy se acostumbra al uniforme, le gusta, aunque en este colegio debe usar más días falda, pero ya se ha adaptado también ha ello y el ambiente es tranquilo, bajo vigilancia y respeto. Podemos decir que este primer mes, lo logramos. Mientras tanto, Ammy sigue leyendo las primeras 200 páginas de una Novela sobre la cual tiene exposición xD. Luego les hablaré sobre ello. ---

title.title: The School You Go To: Why It Matters
title.body: <div class=\

> Formal education is something everyone needs, and in the bid to achieve that, we go to school to get this type of education. It involves processes; from elementary to secondary and higher institutions of learning. All in a bid to get educated and have the needed knowledge for life. A trajectory on this subject questions the result and outcome from the kind or type of schools we go to, asking if indeed the school one goes to matters so much. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmexmLiGPHF1D1B3yeaU5VUhQAyFLKBcL6sFogCvyjwaeZ/photo_1551241681_2aae145af5df.jpeg) [Image Source.](https://unsplash.com/photos/students-sitting-on-brown-wooden-table-CblJCxwPjx0) Beyond having access to school and education from that school, there's a role that the kind of school one goes to plays. Before jumping into that, I'll say that even for the basic subject of education that schools are meant for, where you go to natters a lot, and this can be seen in the outcome. Some of us have been privileged to go to wonderful schools from elementary to higher institution level. For some, it's to a point or at a point, not all through. The difference is there most times, especially as applied to the lower levels of education, like the elementary which is meant to build the educational foundation and the secondary level, meant to open the child and student to complex subjects and topics that can have a bearing on their future. In my country, you don't normally expect that a child in a public school at these aforementioned levels will be better off than the one who's at a private school. Therefore, the school you go to matters. Even in the case of higher institutions, there are distinctions in them. Though most are public institutions, the standards are different, and so the outcome, in most cases. And this is where it takes me beyond just the educational reward defining why the school you go to matters. I look beyond that, into the social spectrum and it gives more reason why the school one goes to matters. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVSN9QmjDMRtVbpb4y4P9G58HSLLKYx7QeCkphS2wTbwM/wokandapix_classroom_2093744_1280.jpg) [Image Source.](https://pixabay.com/photos/classroom-school-education-learning-2093744/) When I discuss things pertaining to school, I mostly never fail to mention that the school as an institution of learning goes beyond that, but it's a social hub as well which connects different kinds of people, of different status and abilities. It's also where we learn beyond books, but other important things, for those who care to. It's in this light that I say the school one goes to can help build them a future through a social network they might not have imagined. I was told the story of a man who made an effort to send his son to a certain school that normally was beyond his ability, so that beyond the quality education there, the boy would have a diverse and quality social network as well. And it did work out. This isn't a call for all parents to take this route as not all would be able to. Also, the kind of school one goes to doesn't guarantee these outcomes if the good opportunity isn't utilised. Sometimes, the mention of the school one went to becomes an advantage. If we say that what is learned in some schools can be learned anywhere, it leaves the big concern of why we have different standards and outcome different. There's a deficit issue with education in some schools, and I believe that if people have the means, all would take their children to the best. The school you go to matters in some way. --- ###### Thank you for reading!

title.title: Learn Ethical Hacking (#45) - Supply Chain Attacks - Poisoning the Source
title.body:
# Learn Ethical Hacking (#45) - Supply Chain Attacks - Poisoning the Source

![leh-banner.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmc2LpoeHUPesc4Dy8haRKLJgfuDY6UBKdc3sED8Dz3JH9/leh-banner.jpg)

### What will I learn

- **What supply chain attacks are** and why they represent the most devastating attack class in modern security;
- **Software supply chain** -- compromising open-source packages, build systems, and update mechanisms;
- **Dependency confusion** -- tricking package managers into installing malicious internal-name packages from public registries;
- **Typosquatting** -- publishing malicious packages with names similar to popular libraries;
- **Build system poisoning** -- compromising CI/CD pipelines, build servers, and code signing infrastructure;
- **SolarWinds, Log4Shell, and XZ Utils** -- detailed case studies of real supply chain attacks that shook the industry;
- **SBOMs and dependency auditing** -- understanding what is actually in your software;
- Defense: dependency pinning, lock files, signature verification, SLSA framework, and private registry hardening.

### Requirements

- A working modern computer running macOS, Windows or Ubuntu;
- Understanding of IaC and CI/CD security from Episode 38;
- Familiarity with package managers (npm, pip, cargo);
- The ambition to learn ethical hacking and security research.

### Difficulty

- Intermediate/Advanced

### Curriculum (of the `Learn Ethical Hacking Series`):
- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#1) - Why Hackers Win](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-1-why-hackers-win)

- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#5) - Active Scanning - Mapping the Attack Surface](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-5-active-scanning)

- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#7) - Passwords - Why Humans Are the Weakest Cipher](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-7-passwords)

- [Learn Ethical Hacking (#11) - HTTP Deep Dive - Request Smuggling and Header Injection](https://hive.blog/hive-196387/@scipio/learn-ethical-hacking-11-http-deep-dive-request-smuggling-and-header-injection)

```text
Packed binary analysis:

BEFORE unpacking (Ghidra):
- Sections: UPX0 (0 bytes on disk, large virtual size),
  UPX1 (compressed data), UPX2 (small, metadata)
- Functions detected: 3 (UPX stub only)
- Defined strings: \

- Decompiler: shows only the decompression routine
- No application logic visible at all

AFTER unpacking (upx -d binary, re-import to Ghidra):
- Sections: .text, .data, .bss, .rodata (normal ELF layout)
- Functions detected: 47
- Defined strings: 83 (passwords, URLs, error messages, file paths)
- Full decompilation of all functions available
- All vulnerability patterns (strcpy, sprintf) now visible

VMProtect vs UPX comparison:
- UPX: compression only. Single layer. Deterministic unpacking.
  upx -d reverses it perfectly. No anti-debug.
- VMProtect: code VIRTUALIZATION. Translates x86 instructions
  to a custom bytecode interpreted by a built-in VM. Each
  protected binary gets a unique VM instruction set. Cannot
  be mechanically unpacked. Requires:
  1. Identify the VM dispatch loop
  2. Map virtual opcodes to their real operations
  3. Reconstruct the original logic from VM traces
  4. Anti-debug: checks IsDebuggerPresent, NtQueryInformation,
     timing checks, hardware breakpoint detection
  5. Integrity checks: CRC/hash of protected sections
  Analysis time: hours to weeks vs seconds for UPX.
```

The contrast between UPX and VMProtect is the difference between a locked door and a maze. UPX wraps the binary in a compression layer that has a known, deterministic reversal. VMProtect transforms the code itself into something fundamentally different -- a custom language that only the embedded interpreter can execute. If you've ever tried to reverse engineer VMProtect-protected software, you know the feeling of staring at thousands of `mov`/`xor`/`jmp` instructions that are the VM dispatcher, not the actual program logic. It is, to put it mildly, not a fun afternoon ;-)
