title.title: The ‘Horseshoe theory’ and Restore Britain.
title.body:
![horseshoe-theory-political-left-and-right.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mrfahrenheit211/Ep1bhMvHXKzSvMuN48ryGZp8bePJQRg5RFX8TQhoumgpN3RMoGyvFKJupbJndCfUgNn.jpg)



As many regular readers will know, too many decades ago I used to be a man of the Left.  I supported nationalisation, comprehensive public services, workers rights, freedom of speech all the things that used to be associated with the traditional Left.  I still have sympathy for some traditional left wing views such as support for freedom of speech and the state supplying those services that are difficult to supply in any other way.

However although I spent some time on the peripheries of the Far Left and the Revolutionary Left I both intellectually and politically rejected those ideological currents because something felt a bit ‘off’ about them.  The proponents of revolutionary leftist views could never really properly answer my questions about what happens after the ‘revolution’.  How would the revolutionaries ensure that the lights were kept on, that the people were fed, that services and transportation worked or how to run the agencies of the state such as healthcare?  They were quite keen on hanging the political and admin classes from the lampposts of Whitehall and Victoria Street, but less keen on how to manage things to ensure that ordinary people didn’t starve, freeze, become victims of crime or die from preventable diseases.  These particular types of revolutionary Lefties were a mix of the misguided, those who like to LARP as Lenin and the truly dangerous.

If you challenged their views the misguided and those LARPers who had read a bit of Marx and thought they knew it all would come out with a mixture of stock arguments told to them by other members of their particular Leftist party or engaged in a tirade of insults including ‘fascist’, ‘class traitor’ and so on and so on.  That sort of stuff becomes water off of a duck’s back after a while, empty words nothing more.  However the more dangerous ones, like so many others who are in leading positions in cults, would freeze out, sometimes with some aggression, those who showed signs of critical thinking about Leftism.  They would scream, shout, denounce, insult the alleged ‘heretic’ along with the their family, background or any other aspect of the ‘heretic’s’ person.  They didn’t use the stock Leftist phrases like the misguided and the LARPers did, they would go out of their way to destroy a person to protect their particular political cause.

One of the things that I took away from my observation of the revolutionary Left was that they took the view that the means, no matter how awful or how destructive, justified the ends.  They’d hurt, insult, exclude, threaten, demean and do whatever they could for ‘The Cause’.

Of course being human such egregious and cult like behaviour is not confined to the Far Left or the Revolutionary Left.  Like a great horseshoe of politics the extremists of the Left tend to look or feel a lot like the extremists of the Right and the behaviour of the cults of the Left are mirrored in the cults of the Right.

I’m seeing lots of really troubling cult like behaviour from some of the more voluble supporters of the Restore Party.  Watching them talk to others who are not fully on board with the worship of Rupert Lowe MP is unsettling to say the least.  They are attacking anybody no matter their age, sex, race, religion or political allegiances past or present.  These pile-ons by Restore supporters or people who claim to be Restore supporters are pretty nasty and all too often play the man or woman and not the ideological ball.  Of course I need to say that not all Restore supporters are like too many of those that I’ve seen, some are reasonable, will debate points, will not engage in thought terminating insults, but there’s too many of the other sort for my liking.  

I’ve caught some of them on my social media timelines and they are monomaniacal about Restore and Lowe to what looks to me to be an unhealthy degree.  I brush these off or discuss that issue at hand with them from my point of view and sometimes they make like the Leninist LARPers of my earlier life and just shout ‘traitor’ at you or something similar.  Sadly some of these Restore cultists go far beyond that and don’t just target with extreme nastiness those of us who have been around the political block a few times and can go ‘Meh!’ but people who are quite young and may be forming Right orientated views despite the pressure of most of the society around them being moulded by the left wing thought being pushed in schools and colleges and the mainstream media.  They are already walking a somewhat difficult and transgressive road because they have chosen to think for themselves and not parrot the Left’s empty palliative phrases.  These people don’t need to be called ‘slags’ or ‘sub human cucks’ or be accused unjustly of giving succour to ‘Islamic rape gangs’.  I’m of the view that nobody who is starting a political journey on the Right should be treated like that and I’m also old enough to believe that someone who is a 19 year old woman should especially not be treated like that.

Below is an example of a 19 year old female user of X who supports the Reform Party being utterly monstered by various supporters of Restore.  Now fair play to this young lady, she’s not cowering away from the slings and arrows of outrageous arseholes, but coming back at them quite hard, respect to that, politics is somewhat of a contact sport of an intellectual and tribal kind sometimes. However the point is that this should not be happening.  We who are on the Right and Centre Right should not be behaving like radical Leftists and calling people names because they may not accept your or my particular flavour of Rightism or disagree with aspects of it.  This sort of behaviour reminds me of the regimented, no dissent, no viewpoint diversity that could be found in the Socialist Workers Party.

Some of the stuff that this young lady has received is not just nasty or cult like some of it looks to me to be based in misogyny.  It was stuff that denigrated her right to hold the views she holds and stuff that treated her as an adjunct to a man.  I can be ferocious in print when talking about politics but there’s no way on Earth would I go as low as some of those who have talked to the young lady in question.

Here’s the examples of the stuff I’ve seen on this lady’s timeline. I have redacted not just the name and handle of the young lady herself but also her Restore supporting interlocutors.  This is to a) not create a pile on for this young lady and b) to give those who are dishing it out privacy to reflect on the reasons why they are behaving like arseholes and maybe act differently in the future.


![R5R.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mrfahrenheit211/23uFrsyiKtvjE3GpQc5BbYpFd9jRoP6cMj8LispMnRRf2GDGJMYE21UaVVdQdoV4w68UF.jpg)


I wonder if this Restore cultist would say the same to an adult male?  Is ‘sub human cuck’ his everyday choice of words in normal life?

Or this:

![R4R.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mrfahrenheit211/23w3AVJmiDUxT6BqxfhCe5kSwZ9TVgkwqQjACg1mb1ZqXJHbLnCYdEMLLXhifahs8bqrB.jpg)



Or this: 


![R3R.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mrfahrenheit211/23xLJ4ocHfvScR6XhUBDgNGWMcWPkw5Drmp9JUjWghNEPng3eSej2BhRkVyxSZuUH1GLT.jpg)



![R2R.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mrfahrenheit211/23viREg7QwFjmh6kBvhaVgxoRpyLnZQpfCQ77FR9cMXN67gmu5qk2Mkba5vJCHrZhE3dj.jpg)



Or even this: 


![R1R.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mrfahrenheit211/23w3CvfJ42hGoC4QmAQu1vyiFtfaLgkqwVhqRXBwNBHW38Rk5dpyMo7FSPw833jqZd6Ra.jpg)





What you have read above is just a little of what this young lady was getting.  She’s not a brainwashed Lefty she sounds to me like a sensible nationalist from what little I have read from her timeline.

What we are seeing in the form of those attacking this young woman for disagreeing with Restore or its policies or the behaviour of some of its personalities is little different from the cult like in group protective behaviour as you would find in one of the lefty ‘lost cause’ organisations such as the Stalin Society or The Cuba Solidarity Campaign.  From what I’m seeing of the more extreme of the Restore supporters is that too many of them are monomaniacal obsessives who cannot have their cult leader or their cause debated or even mildly criticised before the insults, the misogyny and other crap falls from their mouths and their keyboards. Are these honestly the sort of people that you would want running a nation?  I’m not sure I’d trust them to run a parish council.

There’s no need for the sort of crap that the Lowe cultists dished out to this woman.  It’s not debate it’s gobshite-ery nothing more and nothing less and we need much better than that to help to solve the massive problems Britain is in at the moment.  If nothing else this episode of Rupert’s cult members going wild has inspired me to go and purchase an even longer bargepole in order to not touch the Restore Britain party.

Fair play to the lady for not backing down and coming back at the members of Rupert’s Restore cult but it shouldn’t have been necessary for her to do so.  The Restorers could have debated her without all the bullshit, name calling and threats, but some of them it seems cannot bring themselves to do that.  Still, at least it’s another reason for me to not vote for Restore.

The tech world is buzzing, especially the semiconductor sector. If you are watching Microchip Technology (MCHP), you probably noticed the price action has been exciting lately. There are two big news stories that everyone is talking about today, June 2, 2026.

​First, global investors have their eyes on COMPUTEX 2026 in Taipei. This tech expo is the main stage for giant companies to show off their latest innovations. Nvidia's dominance in data center architecture is making competitors think hard, and this is keeping the sentiment in the chip sector quite active.

​Second, for MCHP specifically, there is a presentation today at the **Bank of America Global Technology Conference.** The market is waiting for details on their Data Center Solutions business, which is projected to grow by 65%. If management provides a positive outlook, MCHP could become a favorite for many investors.

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmcA59jHsfRPdNL7VLDFH8civuqQBWh3jaNrFRhQG5J1ri/1000011629.jpg 


**​Analyzing Financial Health**
​After checking the news, let us look at how healthy MCHP is through its fundamental data. Looking at the profitability ratios, there is an interesting trend. The Gross Margin and Operating Margin have been improving and rising consistently from late 2025 to early 2026.

​This is a positive sign, showing that the company is becoming more efficient. Also, the Current Ratio is stable above 2.0, which proves that the company’s short term liquidity is in good shape.

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmVHXBLAUGe6VTCz2TboAKYL6eUWFpcqoGYxEqyo42tJQx/1000011571.png 



**​Dividends and Chart Direction**
​Speaking of profits, investors are happy to see that MCHP keeps a consistent dividend policy. With the current payout ratio, the company is trying to keep its commitment to shareholders. You can see the payment schedule details below.

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmRY3dZLrPTQkoSB4h3gHtopdaoFrdEwMTNGmVEDZJkecY/1000011572.png 



​Finally, looking at the technical side, the price is currently in a critical area. For those using the Smart Money Concepts approach, the Fibonacci levels shown in this chart are essential for finding high probability zones. The price has been testing the levels between the 61.80% and 78.60% retracement zones, which often act as a Discount area where institutional buyers look to enter the market. Watching these specific levels is crucial, if the price finds support and holds above these Fibonacci zones, it could signal a strong reversal or the start of a new bullish leg. Conversely, a clean break below these levels might indicate further weakness.

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmUKgmofnPJuw6dHMaz8Yt4NwuX5EdW7xT8vNtkomrhe47/1000011628.jpg 


**​My Take?**
​In my view, MCHP shows great potential when looking at the recent improvement in its operating margins. Even though the semiconductor sector is currently dominated by the AI hype at COMPUTEX, MCHP has its own niche in data center solutions. From a technical perspective, I am waiting for price confirmation in the marked areas to see if there will be a rejection or a breakout. Stay disciplined with your trading plan and do not forget risk management, as volatility in chip stocks is quite high right now.

title.title: Casa Batlló - Have You Been Here?
title.body: <div class=\

>\n\nToday I want to tell you about my visit to Barcelona and more specifically about the wonderful Casa Batlló. This is one of the masterpieces of the genius of architecture - Antonio Gaudi. In his beloved Barcelona, ​​brilliant buildings were built, the fruit of his fantasies. His hatred of straight lines and the traditional produces magnificent and inspiring wonders. A walk along the elegant \

boulevard cannot help but lead every passerby to one of Gaudí's jewels - Casa Batlló. Just one look is enough for hundreds of interpretations to arise for the architect's bold imagination. Multicolored shards of pottery and broken pieces of stained-glass windows glisten in the sunlight. Mosaic chimneys jut out from the top and compliment the scaly ceramic skin and a graceful tower that ends triumphantly with a cross. Each floor, each detail, each play of light, is an explosion of creative freedom. ![Ca (12).jfif](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZSTHptYozGfXvpjGFJBJDL3yR4RrArkaU2aEhVraBHjB/Ca%20(12).jfif) In front of the large windows are six fine columns that seem to simulate the bones of a limb. The undulating roof, covered in mosaic, resembles the scaly spine of a huge dragon. Balconies are like the massive jaws of sea creatures escaping from the sea. Balconies also look like skull masks. The inside of the building is also extremely beautiful. Magnificent stained glass windows, colorful tiles, exquisite details. Pastel tones and marine motifs are carried over to the interior of Casa Batlló. The attic of the House is considered one of the most unusual spaces. It was previously a service area for the tenants of the various apartments in the building, which included laundry and storage rooms. ![Ca (11).jfif](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWnvQYBq8jJLZ99pnMz1vRsCV69TutvWZxeQZLeJtDM6U/Ca%20(11).jfif) The interior of Casa Batlló is a marvel of design. Gaudí collaborated with the best craftsmen of the time, working with wrought iron, wood, stained glass, ceramic tiles and stone ornaments, among others. When you walk around the house, its details never cease to amaze. The doors leading to the various apartments are labeled with modernist letters. The windows on each landing distort the tiles of the light well, turning them into beautiful waves of water. The handles and railings are ergonomically shaped... It is a true work of art in which the artist was involved in every single aspect: design, color, shape, space and light. ![Ca (10).jfif](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaJ26RugEXWj7EpFT27M7KmtVcGB7UufqWbHFM9rGjY9C/Ca%20(10).jfif) The building was originally built in 1877 by Emilio Sala Cortés - one of Gaudí's professors of architecture. At that time, there was still no electric lighting in Barcelona. Casa Batllo then consisted of eight dwellings divided over four floors. In 1903, the property was bought by the wealthy textile industrialist Joseph Batillo, who owned several factories in Barcelona. Gaudi reconstructed and renovated the magnate's original house between 1904 and 1906. Although the owner allowed Antoni Gaudi to completely demolish the building and rebuild it according to his design, Gaudi did not do so. The architect completely changes the facade we admire today. ![Ca (9).jfif](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTDhuR3xeSf4Rz57AELXoQnVLSBZh1xRP9cQamDkJGvKA/Ca%20(9).jfif) The building is extremely functional, as according to modern architects, Gaudí's creation foreshadows the architectural trends of the late 20th century. In the 1950s, Casa Batlló was no longer owned by the Batlló family. After being taken over by various companies and individuals in the 1990s, the building is in the hands of its current owners, the Bernat family, who have completely restored the house. In 1995, the family opened the house to the public and presented this architectural a gem of the world. Currently, Casa Batlló is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and an emblem of Barcelona. The building is among the top-rated cultural and tourist attractions in the city, which is visited by 1 million people each year. ![Ca (8).jfif](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbmmjvv2XCjUwWZxYxCuRKvb6JnG22eq7q7jwMN2wanMN/Ca%20(8).jfif) ![Ca (7).jfif](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdM9YSot1o5WAHkKYncnxcR2dhyBEDUdS21JjRhFo9a2B/Ca%20(7).jfif) Gaudí himself never explained his work and worked on the facade from the outside, without concrete plans, something that is characteristic of his work. His work is filled with symbols, fantastic images of an inscrutable story that everyone must complete with their own imagination. Casa Batlló became one of the most beautiful and extravagant buildings in Barcelona. Stone, glass and colored ceramics are interwoven to create a glow that light turns into movement. The building does not have a single sharp corner. Everything is wavy and rounded. ![Ca (6).jfif](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQvHKBafyTuSeEqsNXvYEMC8AhbGdBydeySNhSazpVPQq/Ca%20(6).jfif) ![Ca (5).jfif](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXwm3Vv7ogoDc1ng1C3njf7DcTV5korZYNmsRFgTcRA7K/Ca%20(5).jfif) This abundance will never cease to amaze you, but the most surprising thing is that it is always based on functionality. Beauty and functionality come together in every corner of the building, from the entrance hall to the roof terrace. ![Ca (4).jfif](https://images.hive.blog/DQmd2kMeH4hKHFPBmdVVFjYWyLegBv4TBeYbU2TujXtVbkM/Ca%20(4).jfif) The roof terrace is dominated by what is popularly known as the dragon's back, which characterizes the facade and which was represented by Gaudí with different colored tiles. However, the main focal point of the roof terrace is the 4 curved and polychrome chimneys designed to prevent back draft. Here I saw again the beauty and functionality that are brought together in the most beautiful and emblematic house of Catalan modernism. ![Ca (3).jfif](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWQLt8nvecJvk9xvvRzsC44wRyTKoVfVt29hBr6Ye2Zsp/Ca%20(3).jfif) And here it is time for a little contemporary modernism. In order not to spoil the surprise, I will only open the curtain and advise you at the end of my tour of Casa Batllo, not to miss the visual experience, the work of the artist Refik Anadol. ![Ca (2).jfif](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPNg86z622sszRcXD5DNnQszMoWz3RdKWAoSPwVhmbZRr/Ca%20(2).jfif) How to talk about light in an enclosed space with almost no openings for natural light? Here, too, a solution to the problem has been found, through aluminum chain curtains, which through their precise materiality capture the light, like fishing nets, presenting it in all its different forms: sparkles, silhouettes, shadows... In this way, avoiding the use of any other materials and with these curtains the staircase is illuminated. The different shades of aluminum are arranged like this, starting from brighter on the roof and slowly darkening to black as they reach the depths of the former coal cellar in the basement. ![Ca (1).jfif](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbus6SP37Sv1BsMj9CYW7AHPVdgz6u5ybyWpke8o5i8mT/Ca%20(1).jfif) The staircase is a tribute to Gaudi's work, while presenting it in a more contemporary architecture that does not seek to compete with the historical work. I recommend everyone who has the opportunity to visit this place. You will definitely be impressed. Whether you're an architecture buff or just looking for a good time, Casa Batlló offers something for everyone. My visit to this house was like a journey back in time when the city was in the process of transformation and growth. Casa Batlló is an example of sustainability and adaptability as it has been renovated and preserved over the years so that it can continue to delight and inspire visitors. It also has various amenities to ensure visitors feel comfortable during their visit. The building is handicap accessible and offers an audio guide in several languages ​​to help visitors understand the building's history and significance. Casa Batlló also has a gift shop where tourists can purchase souvenirs and mementos of their visit. Visit ticket prices: Adults: 35 € Children up to 12 years: free Children between 13 and 17 years: 19 € Students: 29 € Pensioners: 32 € [//]:# (!worldmappin 41.39170 lat 2.16492 long d3scr)

title.title: Alone With the Moon          ...Part 1            .... Strange Occurence
title.body:
*Why do people have to be this lonely? What's the point of it all? Millions of people in this world, all of them yearning, looking to others to satisfy them, yet isolating themselves. Why? Was the earth put here just to nourish human loneliness? ― Haruki Murakami*


![Desperately Seeking Someone.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmavG7dSBfoLxMxRJmN4eK8BUhbxMPWKYuda6CeFL37WPM/Desperately%20Seeking%20Someone.png)
*Lily's View of Me*


There was a time when single and successful seemed glamorous. But no one warned me of empty nights when I’d want to flee to the Moon and hide in its valleys. Outwardly, I’m living the good life as Markus Cole, chief acquisitions editor for Faber and Collins. But inside, I’m a desert—arid and desolate. I work hard at keeping up appearances, but it’s tiresome shoring up a façade. I manage to fool most people, but not Lily, my seven-year-old niece—she sees right through me—like today, while I visit Beatrice, my sister.

“Uncle Monkey!” Lily squeals with delight when she sees me. “I missed you.” I sweep her up in my arms and crush her in a bear hug. “I missed you too, Princess.” She glances around to see if we’re alone, and then whispers, “I made you a picture, Uncle Monkey.” “You did—can I see it?” She nods gravely and takes me by the hand into her pink and purple bedchamber—a rare privilege extended by princesses.

On a small table by the window is a crayon drawing of two mountains. There’s a stick figure on the top of each peak, separated by a big blue sea. “That’s really pretty, Lily. But what does it mean?” “It’s about a man who sees a beautiful princess through a spyglass and falls in love with her – but they can’t be together, so he turns to stone.” “That’s a sad story, Princess. What made you think of that?” “You did, Uncle Monkey. You’re the man in the picture.” “I am—really? Then, who’s the girl?” “She’s the girl you never meet.” “That is sad,” I tell her.

She puts her arms around me and kisses me. “Maybe you’ll meet her someday.” I squeeze her tight and kiss her head, inhaling the scent of wild berry shampoo. Maybe I will meet a princess someday, but if I were a betting man I’d predict Lily would grow up with just an uncle, and not an aunt. And chances are, I’ll turn to stone.

The following morning, I’m back at work, forcing myself to shake off the lethargy of the weekend. Monday mornings are always brutal—I dread my inbox almost as much as going through my mail. The monotony of the usual routine is broken somewhat by the presence of a new editor and proofreader—a Muslim woman named Mariyan. We’re introduced over coffee and she seems pleasant enough— her slight English accent speaks of British schooling. But still, it’s uncomfortable—she wears the hijab—well, sort of. Actually, it’s a black woolen headscarf draped loosely over her hair. She’s a westernized Muslim, I suppose, but still manages to give a sense of living in her own private, screened-off world – dressing modestly, while appearing very feminine and elegant.

The communication between us is very stiff and formal. After my depressing weekend, the last thing I need is to feel at sixes and sevens adjusting to something unfamiliar at work. By the end of the day, I’m stressed and exhausted, and can’t wait to go home and relax with a glass of wine before the fire. At least, that’s the plan—but, at home, the restlessness continues.

I go for a walk in the rain, hiding beneath a huge black umbrella. I want to be sheltered from the elements and shut in with my thoughts. But the murky streets hiss like static and I can’t concentrate. I picture myself as a cowled monk with aspergillum walking lonely corridors, cloistered from the world. I end up back in my front room shivering by the fire and trying to get warm.

That night I have a strange dream. I dream of Mariyan. I see her in a garden behind a leafy trellis, quietly reading. I can’t quite see her face—just the oval of her cheek protruding from her dark headscarf. She reminds me of the Moon veiled in clouds. I creep forward to see if I can catch a glimpse of her. I use a privet hedge as a shield and then tiptoe up to her garden wall and peer over. Her chair is empty. Disappointment crushes me.

Suddenly, there’s a slight rustling behind me. I turn and find myself staring into her huge sad eyes. “”Hello, Markus,” she whispers. “Were you looking for me?” I wake up confused and bewildered. Is this the beginning of some personal crisis or have I been alone so long that I'm desperate to make contact with anyone?

To be continued…

title.title: Learn Creative Coding (#82) - Mapping Data to Visual Properties
title.body: The radial asks \
The grid asks \

Same data, three questions, three anwers. The mapping is the question.

## What's coming

We can map data to any visual property now -- position, size, color, opacity, shape, rotation, and combinations of them all. We know when to use linear vs non-linear mappings, how to encode multiple dimensions simultaneously, and when to break the rules for artistic effect. The vocabulary is in place.

But we've been working with generic datasets -- arrays of numbers, fake cities, simulated sleep logs. Geographic data is a special category with its own challenges and opportunities. Coordinates, projections, boundaries, regions -- mapping the actual shape of the earth onto a flat canvas involves its own set of creative decisions. That's next on the horizon.

## 't Komt erop neer...

- The `map()` function converts a value from one range to another: `map(value, inMin, inMax, outMin, outMax)`. This is the fundamental tool for connecting data space to visual space. Write a clamped version for layout-sensitive properties (position, size) and use the unclamped version for properties where overflow is harmless (color hue, opacity)
- Position is the strongest visual channel -- humans read spatial location before anything else. Map your most important data dimension to position. X from one variable, Y from another creates an instant scatter plot without any chart framing
- When mapping data to circle size, map to AREA not radius. `radius = Math.sqrt(area / Math.PI)`. If you map directly to radius, a 2x value looks 4x as large because area scales with r squared. Area-proportional sizing keeps visual proportions honest
- Color is three channels: hue for categories (different types = different colors), lightness for quantity (dark = low, bright = high), saturation for emphasis/confidence. Don't use rainbow colormaps for quantitative data -- hue doesn't have a natural ordering. Use single-hue gradients or diverging palettes instead
- Opacity creates density maps for free. Thousands of semi-transparent elements accumulate where they overlap, revealing cluster structure without explicit density calculation. Also useful as a direct importance weighting -- more important data = more opaque
- Shape (circle, square, triangle) encodes categories but is a weaker channel than color or position. Effective for small datasets where each element is individually visible. Falls apart above ~100 points. Use it as a secondary encoding, not primary
- Rotation is underused. Angled lines and arrows convey direction naturally -- wind, trend, flow. Switching from circles to oriented elements adds dynamism and an extra data dimension that most people overlook
- 3-4 simultaneous mappings is the practical maximum. Position for the most important dimension, color for the second, size or opacity for the third. Beyond four, channels interfere and the viewer can't separate them. Not every data column needs a visual encoding -- leave things out
- Non-linear mapping (logarithmic, square root, easing curves) fixes skewed distributions. When data spans orders of magnitude, linear mapping crushes small values. Log scaling or an easeOut curve spreads out the low range so you can actually see detail there
- Data visualization rules (proportional axes, no rainbow maps, no 3D effects) exist for clarity. Data art can break them intentionally for emotional or aesthetic effect. But know the rules first -- accidental rule-breaking is a bug, intentional rule-breaking is a creative choice

Sallukes! Thanks for reading.

X

title.title: Walking the second section of the Coastal Path in Kristiansand, Norway
title.body: <center>![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQuEZKRcEtdCi6retr7Ve8CgKFwLtdGGLej48GvUt8KWP/01.jpg)</center>\n\n<div class=\

>Last year I walked the first part of The Coastal Path / «Kyststien» in Kristiansand, Norway. This coastal trail are devided into stages, so that you can do one part and continue later. What I know, is that the currently trail consists of 9 stages, with a total of 126 kilometers. The whole route is marked with signs making it easy to follow. I started with the first stage (orange on the map). It is close to where I live, making it was an easy afternoon walk. My plan was to do the whole trail last fall. Due to being abroad for several months, and a winter with lots of snow, I decided to wait until spring. Last week I completed the second stage.
https://i.ecency.com/DQmfBdgZtVCCeM3RG2TpAdjb4cdNQQh3uKQtzi87vTpHEyD/02.jpg The second (dark blue) part On the map you can see the second part,which is marked in blue. My map might not be updated, as the trail is supposed to extend further on both sides of the city.
https://i.ecency.com/DQmWEh4zNiFRPYxBrWeq5Z4f12jyw7LjQrbfJACxoSx2Tg8/03.jpg https://i.ecency.com/DQme1XGJcRNnUssNybR4f2TSCbqt1rpBZxvTkVHSsTg2QYA/04.jpg The first stage ends at the bridge connecting two areas of Kristiansand. It is my starting point today. As you might be able to see on the map, the trail follows the promenade along the city's edge towards the sea. Except for the island of Odderøya, I will be walking in the city.
https://i.ecency.com/DQmYcuVSpJTh4HiuudUnoyUmKHLFpQJKwqqX4rx6RiihF6p/05.jpg This is where the river meets the sea https://i.ecency.com/DQmcBHWxmBYrw1syyznzDS7fziN2BPXmLVrNiAq6jp8tQx5/06.jpg https://i.ecency.com/DQmTPzAwHCM9TmhMobL6H749F7K88tmWN62uqy1CutYBmYC/07.jpg https://i.ecency.com/DQmPxkSNXstH7qWZuvZpVCdDTCChwaNvkX6nr9SNkgWy8FR/08.jpg After crossing the bridge, I am in the city center of Kristiansand. The trail follows the river Otra to the point called Tangen, located in the corner of our quardrate shaped city center. At the time Kristiansand was founded in 1641, by King Christian IV, Tangen was just sand. This is where Otra meets the sea. Since the foundation, there has been fortifications and cannon positions, shipbuilding, gunboats during the Napoleonic War (1807-14). Now the whole area is residential area.
https://i.ecency.com/DQmdAm9RYJ6GkdaWVqTfqWV3Jr7Ji6oQ5nUVnEwHjp7NUPn/09.jpg «Bystranda» / beach \

was probably part of the sandy point called Tangen. Definitly a popular beach for the residendents living here. It is not summer yet, so it's quite empty.
https://i.ecency.com/DQmcJzLdHp8VBn8vsYBMtD3Y9SomwW4YNFJZJDsM3xVqzwW/10.jpg https://i.ecency.com/DQmej6S5QmjTeU6c3Q3HSkVcir2hvDtyQynDoi7MSBaKV3q/11.jpg The guest harbor Since Kristansand is a coastal city, there are lots of natural harbours and anchorages, including the guestharbour. By walking along the promenade from Tangen to Odderøya, I pass all the harbours for small boats, including the fortress, parkareas and restaurants.
https://i.ecency.com/DQmfBbk8evzPACHec9YkiVhD3deXLYCQnLyitk97YVvDr6T/12.jpg https://i.ecency.com/DQme8fAK6YHzrJ2QHBEpdFP63mRku5WAvJh8QbY9vQNscsC/13.jpg https://i.ecency.com/DQmd86ubRpGmQSXcMCuLTgh62fi5KqJS8zGZk6jtRak3uhc/14.jpg Christiansholm Fortress was built by king Christian IV. The fortress was part of his defense plan for Kristiansand, built between 1658 and 1672. Usually open during the summer to the public. But many events takes place here during the year.
https://i.ecency.com/DQmZfBfL3k2nMbwrZtgsD4hd15M3XJAspzxgGyd47PVDNxS/15.jpg https://i.ecency.com/DQmYt4wz3ZRZjyRTbEFMiswpc3bcY4Sbbf9rYywtFFDwKRC/16.jpg https://i.ecency.com/DQmdpjx4g1FcFdkDwvX3EnAMKspVrJoJZNBmepBqd814p9r/17.jpg https://i.ecency.com/DQmWZQJVt53UzzJMSi2c14pvEPiP4TxNXeAeNxGPtELK6DL/18.jpg I continue along the beach promenade. Here I see an artist making a sculpture in sand.
https://i.ecency.com/DQmNtSocDVT9By6HawmhXV5o43hRTbe3SfDmYGDg69KEG8P/19.jpg https://i.ecency.com/DQmUmThNCxWGMkyanAmm7MRoUDLdi35b5kZqyyUMutdJU6T/20.jpg Odderøya Museumshavn is my next stop. I pass it because the trail follows the northern side of the Odderøya Island. The museum is not completed yet. But you can see an exhibiton of boats from diferent era's. throughout the summer it's possible to rent a boat here. The plan is an aquarium, but I am not sure when.
https://i.ecency.com/DQmVMMZFRWyY567XPXCZGF5mKhHUWwo6xLPXJP1aoNnntrj/21.jpg https://i.ecency.com/DQmYuiTTsPBHdyURJyS66cGWdGnbBWg13Zu7ae4P67PxnU3/22.jpg https://i.ecency.com/DQmdgBcWqCXTHoWAUiakToi4a6MqHL3hEvgstPGJmHobepP/23.jpg https://i.ecency.com/DQmQMhJptm8zHmkdeCaKreqaReCWYoQvrdRHC7wAfeGwbCH/24.jpg The island, called Odderøya is connected to the mainland with a bridge. Now I step away from the city and follow the route along the coast. The island was closed to the public for many years, because of being a military zone. This lasted from 1667 until late 1990s. The island is now a recreational area, but traces of military activity of some great wars like the Napoleonic Wars and WWII are still evident.
https://i.ecency.com/DQmTb4NSwKZQUqYyqe6aNbE8u4FFF795CuhPnyLKsYqWVC6/25.jpg First time I saw a deer on the island https://i.ecency.com/DQmfANWLBweQ7aJW4p3LgyZXdt4nbVWkiWSgNjCqmkfZJgw/26.jpg Along the trail, there are maps and information boards telling part of the history of the island. When the military closed down in 1992, the area became accesable and developed as a place where artists could establish themself. The history goes back to the 1796 when Kristiansand decided to erect a quarantine station on the island. Many ships that arrived brought Cholera along. To prevent spreding a quarantine station was established in 1804 and was operative until 1914.There is also a cholera burial ground on the island.
https://i.ecency.com/DQmWJSqjiHqrkxo9nzrE54hTBJzf9MAwv5qg4G2iKxvLgVK/27.jpg https://i.ecency.com/DQmThALskXFA48FY35y2GGkhfxkH5kxkXttYJbzaq4DLPZF/28.jpg https://i.ecency.com/DQmbMdfd8qMgFroSrFFz6ghu1ziRio7bUTQRkD2V87h3kpc/29.jpg Then I come to the the southern most point. It is a good place to take a rest and enjoy the views. The old cannons dates back to the 1690s. As I continue, I saw the two ferries from \

meet.
https://i.ecency.com/DQmZ72H63sTWgpKRXhomUae78jdEmWkQ3XKcZd8y2926vpK/30.jpg https://i.ecency.com/DQmaqMwizYkYXszrSaANu3UFxFeuVDANqApDevkue6y7R8e/31.jpg This is \

. In 2024 the old silos from 1935 was transformed into an art museum. At the time it was built, it was containing grains. After some years it was assumed that it was no longer nessesary to prepere for famine. The silos were left to stand here, until it was picked to house the private art collectiong belongen to Nicolai Tangen. It has already been noticed around the world. In 2025 it came on the New York Times list of 52 places to visit 2025. It has won an architectual prize among others. The building with the orange roof is placed next to Kunstsilo is our theatre called Kilden.
https://i.ecency.com/DQmcZ5nBVHN6P6K8b6Z4cLbWMJnc3jLakec3i7sTE3UGsNv/32.jpg Popular restarant area https://i.ecency.com/DQmT5mnuZRJ5Wd1uWqioNyGPE7Y4GF3Qb9X5MLar3161mJU/33.jpg Container port https://i.ecency.com/DQmauEDYBv3epGAwS7wEJ7jeHejgkWeHAkULdqoMTbz1d6x/34.jpg Trainstation https://i.ecency.com/DQmbcWgCaSCWWtxsz4HgTm7qrWmr3Xhv3DAHRYoNU3oW1QV/35.jpg The new policestation Kristiansand is a port city with a strategic location, often called \

. Since the city's establishment in the 17th century, Kristiansand has been an important port city. It has hosted the Tall Ship Race several times. Most recently in 2025. I walk past the Fish Bazaar, the container port and the cruise boat quay. Then on to the ferry terminal, the bus station and the train station. All are located next to each other. The policestation was built last year and localted opposite the old trainstation.
https://i.ecency.com/DQmaTm7SUeb9Epvhgwf8p7XxTTpxGoLtvwPFx7ydnJW1HvT/36.jpg When I reach the bridge I am at the end. When I continue, it will be out of town. First part of the trail: https://ecency.com/hive-163772/@digi-me/a-small-section-of-the


Please do follow if you want to keep up with my next travel story. Any upvotes or reblogs are hugely appreciated!

Latest travel story, check out:

>Beautiful Dravidian style temple with an amazing location on the island of Mauritius


U.J

> Zentralisierte Geheimdienst-Software verliert auf lange Sicht immer gegen die fortschreitende Demokratisierung von Rechenleistung und Wissen.

Ich interpretiere den Satz so: Eine kleine Gruppe kann auf Dauer nicht exklusiv über Wissen, Werkzeuge und Rechenleistung verfügen, wenn diese Ressourcen für immer mehr Menschen zugänglich werden.

Geheimdienste verlieren nicht zwangsläufig. Sie verschieben nur ihre Vorteile. Ein Geheimdienst hat heute vielleicht keinen exklusiven Zugang mehr zu bestimmten Analysewerkzeugen, aber er kann auf Datenbestände zugreifen, die Privatpersonen nie sehen werden. Ich glaube sogar, dass die Demokratisierung von Rechenleistung Geheimdiensten teilweise hilft. Denn je mehr digitale Spuren Milliarden Menschen hinterlassen, desto mehr Daten entstehen überhaupt erst zur Analyse.

Zentralisierte Organisationen verlieren langfristig ihre Informationsmonopole, aber nicht zwangsläufig ihre Handlungsvorteile. Das trifft meiner Meinung nach den Kern besser.

title.body:
![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZfUChwrC1R8T3Tb4SLxpuDkLxUjNuPJaH7RHTZpaMMKZ/PXL_20240608_175047556.webp)

---------------------------

The stage is officially set for the Division I Softball finals.  After a four pack of stunning games last night he favorites were taken out and we now have an all Texas championship game.  I'll write more about that tomorrow though.  Today, it's all about Division II.  While the highly televised and publicized stuff was happening over the weekend, there were still a lot of D2 things happening.  

Starting on Thursday when  Saint Leo beat St. Thomas Aquinas 4 to 2, Missouri Southern State beat Glenville State 5 to 3, Cal State San Marcos handed West Texas A & M their first loss 5 to 4, and finally, McKendree squeaked past North Georgia 1 to 0.

That set things up for a couple of winners bracket games on Friday where Saint Leo knocked Cal State San Marco down to the losers bracket 5 to 3, as well as McKendree doing the same to Missouri Southern State 3 to 2.

 Unlike the D1 tournament, this set up a quad of games for Saturday down in the losers bracket.  First we had West Texas A & M knocking Saint Thomas Aquinas out of the tournament with a 10 to 2 throttling.  It was followed up by a 5 to 0 shut out of North Georgia over Glenville State.  

In the later games, Missouri Southern State took West Texas A & M into extra innings, but fell short in the 9th losing 6 to 3 and finding themselves out of the tournament.   After that, Cal State San Marcos had an easy 7 to 1 victory over North Georgia allowing them to move on and sending the ladies from Georgia back home.

Finally, on Sunday we had the games that determine the two teams that would face each other in the finals.  Saint Leon continued their dominance with a 10 inning thriller against West Texas A & M that saw Saint Leo winning 5 to 4 and cementing their spot in the finals.  

Then we had an interesting game or two between McKendree and Cal State San Marcos.  It looks like there might have been a weather delay or something, but ultimately McKendree came out on top 4 to 3.  

This sets things up for a best of three series starting  today with McKendree facing Saint Leo.  I have a feeling Saint Leo is going to come out on top, but don't quote me on that!

They will likely play again tomorrow, then if a game three is required it will happen either tomorrow after the first game or on Thursday.  I'm not exactly sure what the schedule looks like.

title.title: Which Indian Bridal Styles Are Trending This Season?
title.body:
A significant shift in Indian bridal style is occurring as tradition and modern individualism come together. The modern bride desires a costume that is both photogenic and expressive of her individuality while also allowing her to move around freely. The options are more varied than ever, ranging from royal blues and pastel pinks to structured corsets and flowing ruffles. Exploring genuine [Indian Dresses UK](https://shiffonz.com/) collections provides the ideal fusion of classic craftsmanship and contemporary practicality for brides in the United Kingdom who are looking to adopt these worldwide trends. Eight of the most thrilling bridal trends dominating the 2026 season are covered in this guide. 

## Beyond Red: The Emergence of Daring Blues 

The abandonment of the colour red's dominance is the most notable change. Brides are selecting delicate lavenders, emerald greens, and regal blues with assurance. Especially, blue is having a big moment, providing a regal, refreshing option that looks great against gold jewellery in pictures. Lehengas with elaborate silverwork in ice blue and deep sapphire are being displayed by designers. The goal of this action is to express oneself and demonstrate that a bride may be just as conventional in a striking blue dress as in a classic crimson one. 

## Romantic Daytime Weddings Using Pastels 

Destination and daytime weddings are often characterised by soft, romantic colours. Champagne, mint green, and blush pink are some of the colours that give off a light and dreamy vibe. The Pantone colour for 2026, Cloud Dancer, a serene white/ivory, lets exquisite artistry shine without interruption. These subdued tones make a great backdrop for fine pearl or sequin embroidery, which produces a refined, romantic aesthetic. 

## The Return of the Corset 

One of the trends that will define 2026 is the corset choli, which is praised for its ability to shape the body while simultaneously giving it a modern twist. With elaborate embroidery and structured panels, designers are reinventing the corset and turning it into the focal point of the attire. The fitted bodice of this dress is beautifully contrasted by a flowing lehenga skirt, resulting in a strong and elegant shape. Its ideal fusion of traditional and contemporary haute couture is especially well-liked for sangeet and reception evenings. 

## Fluffles for Fun Play 

Ruffles are the way to go for brides who like excitement and fun. They give classic bridal attire a softer touch, giving it amazing movement and romance. Ruffles give a garment a dynamic and eye-catching appearance in photographs, whether they are layered on a dupatta or fall down the sleeves. Designers observe that ruffles give sculptural softness without being overpowering. With dancing as the focal point, this trend is ideal for the mehendi, as it moves the emphasis from intricate ornamentation to happy design. 

## Sarees and saree dresses that are pre-draped 

The saree is being redesigned for today's bride. Particularly popular among UK brides who value tradition and convenience are saree gowns and pre-draped sarees. These designs get rid of pins and intricate draping by including zippers and pre-stitched pleats. The saree gown, which has a classic pallu, maintains its position throughout the evening while providing the elegance of a Western evening gown. With this, brides are free to move around without fear of their sari falling off. 

## Royal headwear and flowery fantasies 

In pre-wedding celebrations, floral jewellery has gone beyond the haldi ceremony and brought a new, romantic vibe. Floral capes and sophisticated hair ornaments are now worn by brides. Royal headgear is making a powerful statement during the main ceremony. Rather than a maang tikka, brides choose statement matha pattis that frame the face like a sculpture and architectural silver floral vines. This trend extends beyond cost to impact, enabling striking, crown-like self-expression. 

## Use of lightweight materials and simple embellishment 

The days of the 20 kg lehenga are gone. The modern bride places a high value on comfort, which has increased light materials such as organza, crepe, and silk mixes. These fabrics provide a beautiful, lightweight drape. The emphasis has changed to simple elegance via excellent tailoring and distinctive necklines. This minimalist approach demonstrates that real luxury is found in exquisite design rather than weight, allowing the bride's inherent beauty to shine through. 

## Extreme artistry 

Maximalism is making a deliberate comeback, celebrating rich cultural history in a stunning contrast. Treating them like architecture, brides adopt striking, multilayered polki jewellery and stacked bangles. Lehengas include zari and mirror work as part of their high-density embroidery. This method incorporates antique items while supporting colour and craft. This strong, luxurious style gives a commanding presence that is grounded in history but also styled with a modern, assured eye, making it ideal for a winter wedding or reception. 

## Conclusion 

Freedom characterises the 2026 nuptial scene. There are no restrictions on the type of attire you select for your sangeet, whether it's a royal blue corset lehenga, a pastel pre-draped saree, or a ruffled outfit. All of the major trends from light materials to elaborate jewellery are intended to boost the bride's radiance and self-assurance. In the end, the best trend to follow is your own intuition, which will help you create a bridal style that is as unique and memorable as your love story.

title.title: A Vat Of Wine
title.body:
![1000137363.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kemmyb/23ynHqtstphUfLJAaKBY94KgXySFn5XEhiWqrdpiDtqZM58dLVDodzxiQPAH7mYgwHh3Y.png)![divider curl .webp](https://img.blurt.world/blurtimage/kemmyb/a75ed810b8aaff74d2505ddf85186840400c52a1.webp)


Forty arrives with much joy and ceremony and a few strands of grey
Perched on the fence post, the same moon stares down like it has forgotten my name
Friends and kin ask ‘what are you waiting for?’

The feeling like an unbroken cord without a beginning tethers me to this road
To a familiar presence whose footsteps are hidden just beyond my reach 
And whose thoughts make my heart rhyme like a medley of unforgettable songs

It began in another life, in an unkempt garden stitched with reeds and ivy around its edges and walls
An undying love bloomed among thorns and briers
And he promised with all the certainty of tides that he would find me again

A macabre time when egos ran high and men raised deadly weapons against one another
At a decade and half, he found me and we defied war and all the cruel odds against us
I relished my surrender to a love so sweet and consuming like wild fire

The garden blooms again awaiting his arrival but his promise blurs over four decades
Trees I once knew as saplings now cast shadows to shelter my grief
His place at my table sits empty for a man who never arrives

Sometimes I imagine him lost to quell my beating heart and fluttering butterflies in my stomach
Years of waiting have poured themselves into me
And filled me like *a vat of wine* becoming darker and richer

No longer the girl who first began waiting 
The gentle breeze brushes against my skin and I feel his invisible pull again across lifetimes
What if somewhere he pauses under the same moon feeling the ache of my absence?

But I'll wait and when he comes, I'll know
For a bird must make its landing after circling the high skies for half a lifetime 
By the sudden relief as the waiting leaves my body,
I will know.

title.title: Mi experiencia como fotógrafa en una actividad de parejas en la iglesia a la que asisto.
title.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXuEjBpGwPcWWnx1MBnR3LhXz2KJpyxEJS5rvxVGaCnJU/1780403339598.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaM225BqpQGLFaKdRFQFrpBuPF4L5nS7opA9qsvcsFzkn/1780400231822.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYfYiXVNjVRq6zuvnBH8oZFFQhLKZcYuCwdTvuLA52JLr/1780400231947.jpg)


Hace días estuve compartiendo con mis hermanos de la iglesia, pero en esta oportunidad fué para capturar cada uno de esos momentos con mi teléfono y fue una experiencia muy bonita para mí. 
Siempre le doy gracias a Dios por esa iniciativa de que las parejas en la iglesia puedan tener ese tiempo de conversar, aprender, aclarar dudas y compartir un tiempo de calidad.  Les cuento que la actividad comenzó a las 7 de la noche el martes pasado y aunque terminó a las 9 pm, realmente fueron dos horas muy gratas y dónde hasta yo pude aprender mientras tomaba las fotos. Jajaja 

<center>━━━━━━ • ✿ • ━━━━━━</center>

Una vez al mes se reunen estas parejas y se trata temas muy variados, en esta oportunidad el tema fue sobre la convivencia en el matrimonio. Entre chistes, anécdotas, risas, preguntas y un ambiente bastante relajado transcurrio la noche en donde las parejas tenían esa cita no solo para aprender, sino también para salir de la rutina que a veces agobia y resta tiempo a las demás obligaciones, ó mejor dicho, a otros asuntos que también son importantes y que hay que abordar en una oportunidad u otra. 

Qué bueno que ese día la luz se fue temprano y no justo esa noche, porque de igual forma la actividad se hubiese tenido que llevar a cabo, aunque sea entre linternas del teléfono. Les confieso que trato de estar atenta a todo lo más que puedo, porque considero que es una oportunidad para yo también poderme ir familiarizando con esos temas, aún cuando todavía no me haya casado ni tenga pareja. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWghNarzXu7D6fsGPwhKg55wmzA1zSMYwMEopFkm447Jy/1780401283448.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfCvT1eh4ACDRaLbeJAYfTAsNhfCjG3qvXwCDy31huehN/1780401443319.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTdWAec77ascFcf3iWWm1u3AwfC1fJBidwiyanemWyWYK/1780402041285.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNN1wXugEuEPuJwcrRezsn271qGMgPoS1QQFfXDUayRdn/1780402041454.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeFQ4paHKeWnJ6sB7Jo5rv2apMhSZSQpKnamQzTXm5gRB/1780402041625.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTdWAec77ascFcf3iWWm1u3AwfC1fJBidwiyanemWyWYK/1780402135818.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZTR9TSfXbEAi3bvAC2HpiYTB3PEDMjS1tbKFh4ZQNnf7/1780402135951.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNN1wXugEuEPuJwcrRezsn271qGMgPoS1QQFfXDUayRdn/1780402136088.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZTjJcCzjTmPLckV7FYTy49WgfzLWma9WsyehhmP5fMMX/1780402136220.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbU28UPaoUba3bkQ827Gy7XfBjBHXHz59ekdrRG91u2oC/1780402136353.jpg)

Y por allá estaba: muy tranquila y contenta en una mesa que me colocaron justo detrás de ellos, y aproveché de tomarme una selfie para no perder la oportunidad, y mientras avanzaba la charla me levantaba de la silla de vez en cuando para ir tomando las fotos desde diferentes ángulos de la iglesia. 

Aunque también iba de vez en cuando  a la cocina a ver cómo iba todo por allá... y sí! es emocionante ver como todo va quedando muy chévere para la ocasión, creo que esa es mi parte favorita, 🤭 el refrigerio final... Es que todo olía muy rico y se veía bien. Les cuento que me fuí sin cenar para al momento de comer no estar tan llena y poder disfrutar cada pasapalo con más entusiasmo y poder saborear todo muy bien. A veces podemos llegar a pensar que tomar fotos es algo que cualquiera puede hacer, y realmente puede ser que sea así, pero de igual forma, siempre le doy gracias a Dios porque formo parte de este ministerio y me gusta mucho ver la alegría de mis hermanos.

<center>━━━━━━ • ✿ • ━━━━━━</center>

No solamente al momento de comer, sino también de contar sus anécdotas y motivar a los demás, es que a veces cuando cuentan su historia ó hacen preguntas sobre cualquier inquietud, todos los demás sé sienten identificados y luego se animan también a preguntar y a contar también sus vivencias y es muy bonito poder escuchar como ha cambiado su manera de ver las cosas gracias a Dios y a esas personas que con amor se dedican a poder enseñar a través de su testimonio y experiencias de muchos años. 

<center>━━━━━━ • ✿ • ━━━━━━</center>

 Considero que se da una conversación dónde cada uno aporta algo diferente, pero igual de motivador y reflexivo dónde todos aprendemos, me incluyo, a pesar de que solo estoy como oyente.
Un punto importante de la charla que me puso a reflexionar fue el momento cuando dijeron que en medio de la tolerancia está entender que somos diferentes y aprendemos a convivir de ese modo. 

<center>━━━━━━ • ✿ • ━━━━━━</center>

De verdad que me pareció muy interesante porque a veces podemos llegar a pensar que esa persona que está a nuestro al rededor es un clon de uno mismo, que no solo actúa, habla, sino que también piensa igual que nosotros, y no es verdad, creemos muchas veces que elegimos un igual donde todo será paz y amor hasta que nos encontramos con la realidad de que cada uno es un ser independiente en todos los aspectos y que está en uno poder tolerar esas diferencias para estar en armonía. 

Claro! También tocaron el tema que todo se basa en mutuos acuerdos y que respetamos a la otra persona para estimular la convivencia y el respeto mutuo y que siempre hay que establecer límites para evitar el desgaste en la relación. Así que son palabras sabias en las cuales me puse a meditar porque pienso que realmente me servirán más adelante y yo misma tendré que poner en práctica. 

<center>━━━━━━ • ✿ • ━━━━━━</center>

Me despido por hoy dandoles gracias a Dios por la oportunidad que tuve de tener un equipo maravilloso que trabaja con mucho amor y dedicación. 
Por aquí dejaré unas fotos que tomé en la cocna justo cuando mi hermana Gloris no podía encender el horno y le tuvo que decir a uno de los hombres que también forma parte de los que apoyan en la cocina que la ayudara.
Así que siempre deberíamos incluir a un hombre en el equipo porque siempre hay cosas que ellos también nos pueden colaborar en ese momento, son una ayuda valiosa. Hay personas que son de gran bendición en nuestras vidas. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRcTGQGpqouP9o5EDrvtaJ9JQudtMjjZEvw6mUWiCQyY8/1780403164018.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQVSQoGuUhkNP8Ry7o2QxMtdNU11obNQyhUwTVCcAfvgr/1780403164193.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPJw7CxU7J5PEh2ZTQUTwJFBm3brcUfM1yx1srkPLqL2V/1780403164351.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdpspTEZ6wTm1Dw18nGUEcZnzjuoj1GaYvkGSUrMK3oiv/1780403164462.jpg)

Espero que tengan un hermoso y productivo día. 
Me despido con mucho cariño y gratitud hasta una próxima oportunidad. 
Muchas gracias por todo! 

Todas las fotos son tomadas con mi teléfono Tecno Spark 30 pro.

When I saw \
and \

, my first thought was: Can AI cook my jollof rice in 2036?



   1. Cooking Jobs That Will DISAPPEAR
Factory food. Machine-cut vegetables. One-click noodles. 
If your job is just \

, robots will take it by 2030. 
McDonald’s already has robot fryers in some countries. 

     2. Cooking Jobs That Will SURVIVE 10 Years + More
But my kind of cooking? It will never die. Why? 3 reasons:
1. Taste is Human: AI can give recipe, but it can’t taste if salt is too much. Only tongue can judge. Every customer wants \
not \

.
2. Emotion in Food: When someone is sad, they don’t want robot food. They want food cooked with care. Food is love, not just calories.
3. Culture + Custom: weddings need special soup. India festivals need special sweets. AI doesn’t know my grandmother’s secret ingredient.

   My Plan to Stay Relevant Till 2036
I won’t wait for robots to replace me. I’m making my cooking \

with 3 moves:

          1. Skill up: Learning baking + cake decoration + small chops. More skills = more money. 
       2. Personal touch: Customers pay extra for \

. They want to see my face, not a machine.
      3. Teach others: I’m teaching 2 young girls in my area how to cook. Skills + people = job security.

      4. The Truth About AI and Cooking
AI can write 100 recipes in 1 minute. But can it smell when the stew is burning? 
Can it adjust pepper because the customer is pregnant? 
Can it cook with prayer? No.

AI will help me find new recipes online. But the fire, the stirring, the tasting - that’s still my job.

Creo que si los moderadores de las diferentes iniciativas valoraran la interacción de las publicaciones (claro, manteniendo la calidad del artículo) y a partir de allí se seleccionara, por ejemplo, el ganador de determinado concurso; veríamos un cambio en la manera de recompensar.

Today I would like to share a few black and white photos from a recent visit to an amusement park. I hope this worked out the way I intended.... The park (The Efteling in The Netherlands) is famous for the theming of its attractions and its attention to details. But judge for yourself. ## This is my entry for the #monomad challenge by @monochromes

This hounted house is one of the newest attractions in the park. You wouldn't say it's new when you see the state of it, do you? ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23vsFsL9Uqad8QsPkjGGRnJPWdfGbAkTAMn2UZHRmf34ZSwDSVmXGuKdNnnUyLXszNRfe.png) https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23t7AuzRFTHLEwfpB7DaBzAdTUkSh57P7LBnvKjxuANMGth2QU5jt1w1wyPpDNgJWpwt8.png This looks like a flying crown, but it's actually called the Pagode; a circular platform in Asian style that goes op and gives you a perfect view over the park and the environment. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23wWvt55kCdFuEVSgNAZ8ujnMt9dU2Q9ypbet1e1pqa54biWbkP3JkgiaRuuJBd1yfF4Z.png) https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23t7AuzRFTHLEwfpB7DaBzAdTUkSh57P7LBnvKjxuANMGth2QU5jt1w1wyPpDNgJWpwt8.png This is the kings castle. ![20260523_150827.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23uFY5b9nong6ft99TspQNgMb6TUUvSeMaXFKSSFMHtorHsScvKMzQVTe6AF8QGTqMWS4.jpg) https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/23t7AuzRFTHLEwfpB7DaBzAdTUkSh57P7LBnvKjxuANMGth2QU5jt1w1wyPpDNgJWpwt8.png This last one was actually my favorite ride; a rollercoaster with a horizontal drop. body.title: How to Style Men's Polo Scrub Tops Professionally?
body.body:
There is no longer a need for medical personnel to compromise between comfort and professionalism. The polo scrub top is a game-changer that has been brought about by the smart-casual revolution. It strikes a balance between practical need and professional appearance by combining a structured collar with breathable material. Just donning the top is not enough, though. The way you wear your [Mens Polo Scrub Top](https://skrubz.com/collections/men-collar-scrub-top) speaks volumes to patients and coworkers. This manual offers crucial styling tricks to help you feel confident, at ease, and look your best during your shift. 

## Give the ideal fit top priority

If the fit is off, the most costly scrub top seems unprofessional. Don't make the typical error of purchasing a size that is too big. A polo that is too large might bunch up the material and make you seem unkempt. In contrast, a too-tight top limits mobility. A customised fit that skims the body without being too tight is what you should look for. Your shoulder bone should line up with the shoulder seams. The hem should be just below your belt line. A good fit denotes attention to detail and guarantees that you can complete clinical duties without the cloth interfering or rubbing uncomfortably across your back. 

## Learn how to handle the collar

The collar is the most important aspect of a polo scrub, and the way you handle it defines your appearance. An untidy appearance is given by a crumpled, floppy collar. Keep the collar standing crisply after washing by ironing it or using a [fabric steamer](https://www.waivio.com/). Fold the top down neatly with a sharp crease when wearing it without a jacket. Instead of inexpensive polos with collars that roll inward, buy high-quality knitted collars that retain their form all day. Your face is framed by a crisp, clean collar that pulls the eye upward, giving the impression of authority and vigilance, which are qualities patients seek. 

## Select Dark or Neutral Solid Colours 

Maintain a subdued colour scheme for everyday professional styling. Wine red, charcoal grey, navy blue, black, or deep teal are all wonderful options. These hues conceal stains more effectively than white or pastel colours, and they work well with any scrub pant colour. Stay away from excessive logos, intricate designs, or high-contrast colour blocking. A men's polo scrub top with a strong, dark hue projects professionalism and competence. It also functions as a neutral foundation, highlighting your name badge or stethoscope as the focal point of your attire. Reserve vibrant colours for everyday attire. 

## Use a jacket or vest to layer strategically

Unpredictable temperatures are common in hospitals. The ideal foundation for layering is a polo scrub shirt. Add a tight fleece gilet or soft-shell jacket in a complementary hue to complete the look. Make sure the layer isn't thick; it should zip up without tugging on the chest. When wearing a white coat, leave the polo unbuttoned at the top to expose the collar, but keep the rest of the buttons fastened. Under your polo, avoid wearing a hoodie since it appears cumbersome. A simple long-sleeved thermal in a neutral colour, on the other hand, provides warmth while preserving a neat, layered look.

##  Know the Rule for Untucked vs.  Tucked In 

Whether or not you should tuck in your polo scrub is determined by the workplace culture. Tucking in is the more professional choice for the majority of medical facilities. It gives a polished silhouette, defines your waistline, and keeps fabric from snagging on machinery. Untucked can work if the polo has a short, straight hem and your position is in a laid-back environment, as long as there is no diaper impact around the hips. Make sure the hem doesn't drop below your crotch line when untucked. If you're not sure, put it inside. The neat lines of a tuck with a little military fold give off an air of discipline. 

## Conclusion 

When styling a men's polo scrub top professionally, one must pay attention to fit, collar design, colour selection, and upkeep. You can transform your everyday attire from simple workwear to a symbol of clinical excellence by adhering to these eight principles, which include choosing dark solids, perfecting the tuck, layering strategically, and taking care of the fabric. In a matter of seconds, patients conclude. Before uttering a single word, a healthcare professional who is well-groomed exudes confidence. Spend time on your appearance; it's a direct investment in your professional pride and in gaining the trust of your patients. The ideal appearance is always achievable.

---

body.title: How Mind-Body Practices Are Changing the Way We Heal
body.body:
A subtle revolution is occurring in the way people view their health. Many people are shifting away from solely symptom-based treatment and seeking out approaches that focus on the whole person including mind, body and spirit. This isn’t an outcome of discontent alone, but is rooted in research that demonstrates the profound connection between emotional health and physical well-being. The ****[holistic healing approach Philadelphia](https://www.kessudaholistichealing.com/) practitioners Wellness coaches, practitioners, and integrative medicine experts have witnessed this shift firsthand as the demand from clients for more comprehensive treatment is increasing across the country.



![Meditation Teacher Philadelphia.png](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/e9d40103cfd472808ef21bcdb43e09b0e0d003d932df8de2539ce6689d3dd6e5)



**What Holistic Healing Actually Means — and Why It Matters**

The phrase “holistic” is often misunderstood or used in a loose sense, however its meaning is clear that it treats the entire person instead of focusing on only one organ, one symptoms, or a single diagnosis. An holistic approach evaluates physical health in conjunction with emotional, mental and even spiritual aspects of one’s life. The practitioners who adhere to this paradigm believe that stress from emotional issues may be manifested as chronic discomfort, digestive issues fatigue, fatigue, or an inability to fight off illness. Studies published in peer reviewed journals confirms the notion that cortisol levels, inflammation and the nervous system’s dysfunction are closely linked to the emotional and mental state. This is not alternative thinking anymore — it is being validated by mainstream medicine through fields like psychoneuroimmunology, which studies how the brain, immune system, and behavior interact. Understanding the relationship between these two will be the very first thing towards creating an improved model of your personal health.

**The Practices That Are Making a Real Difference**

Many therapies can be considered holistic which is why the best methods include combining various modalities instead of simply relying on one technique. Breathwork, for instance, is receiving a lot of attention because of its ability to regulate the nervous system’s autonomic part and reduce the body’s stress response, without the need for medication. Somatic therapy, which is focused on the relationship with the body as well as emotional experiences has demonstrated measurable outcomes for those suffering from anxiety, trauma, or post-traumatic stress. 

Acupuncture, which has been a part of the tradition of Chinese medicine, is currently being researched in clinical settings to study its effects on fertility, pain management and mood control. Meditation and yoga-related stress reduction (MBSR) have a solid scientific basis supporting them, specifically in reducing the symptoms of depression as well as improving health and quality of life for people dealing with chronic illnesses. What is what makes whole-body healing Philadelphia services so beneficial in a city environment is their ability to deal with the stressors compounded with a fast-paced, high-pressure lifestyle which means that the body is rarely given an opportunity to fully recover from the demands.

**Building a Personal Healing Framework That Lasts**

The biggest change that a person could make is switching from a model of health that is reactive to a proactive health model. Reactive health involves seeking assistance only when something is wrong. Proactive health is the continuous maintenance of the conditions that allow the mind and body perform at optimum levels. This means a healthy sleep and nutrition awareness, as well as movement techniques, tools for emotional processing and connecting with the communityeach of which has demonstrated impacts on the long-term health of a person. This also involves becoming an active person in your own health care. Inquiring questions, investigating various options and working with professionals who are willing to get to know your complete background rather than only your present complaint will produce greater outcomes. Most effective recovery paths are not always linear and usually involve the use of a combination of integrative and conventional methods which work in tandem. 

If someone is dealing with an illness that is chronic or recovering from burnout or just trying to be more at ease it is not always one-size-fits-all. The choice of [holistic healing Philadelphia](https://www.kessudaholistichealing.com/) as a component of a larger wellness plan will help create the conditions to ensure a lasting, long-lasting recovery, not just temporary relief. The body has an incredible ability to heal itself provided it has the right conditions, constant assistance, and the trust of being considered as a whole than as a collection of distinct components. This understanding, more than any single treatment or method is the most important factor in effective health improvement.

---

body.title: Getting old, gloomy or gold!!
body.body: /> The gloomy sunset reminds me of old age. The darkness symbolizes the dark side of human life.

/> When I am watching my mom going through dementia. She is 73, but the way her health is declining is so bitterly painful for all of us, especially for my daughter, who is the apple of an eye of her grandmother!! I have five sisters, and each of us is responding to this issue in her own unique way!! We have always seen her very strong from the time we opened our eyes. Perhaps that's the reason we feel very sad when we find her getting more vulnerable and helpless as the days are passing by!! I think we all are helpless in front of nature. Nature is very powerful. It transforms a cute baby into a youthful teenager and then from a passionate young man to a decent gentleman, and then finally slowly and gradually, the process of decline begins. Sometimes, I ponder deeply on the phenomenon of old age. Yes, it's a bitter truth, but we all have to experience this episode of our lives. Are we brave enough to face this bitter truth of life? I pray from the depth of my heart that may God give me an easy exit from life, not after experiencing a lot of pain and misery. My ideal old age is a very healthy and fit one in which we get a lot of spare time to spend with our grandchildren and old friends , indulging into wonderful hobbies and recreation!! We all have our own unique vision of an ideal old age. Lets see what nature has in store for us at this phase of life!! All my sisters want to contribute to the caring of elderly mom. We all work as a teem and also a lot of individual efforts going on to help mom cope with her condition. One of my sisters is dealing with medical issues. The doctors visits, medicine setting, and consulting the doctor in case of any complaints. Me, being a stay at home mom, having a grown-up daughter , sharing the same house with my parents, giving her company and support most of the time. I have two sisters living nearby. The youngest sister helps part-time to care for her, and the other one helps during emergencies.

/>\n\nLast but not least , my dad also takes a great part in supporting my mom!! How amazing to see my dad being very fit at the age of 75 and also helping mom by giving her company and arranging her medicines!!

body.title: 🇲🇦  Reseña: «El Perfume de las Flores de Noche» (ESP/ENG)
body.body:
> Saludos cordiales, queridos amigos de @hivebookclub. Me reencuentro con ustedes a través de #ecency para compartir una nueva reseña. Hoy te propongo hablar de una escritora franco marroquí: Leila Slimani (Marruecos , 1981) y de este libro que se ha versionado al español con el título: «El perfume de las flores de noche». ***
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmabdVAfmBUb1Vq1WSL4uXmXpcenzawUZ8M6umkKTYM8jg/1780363062976.png)
***

> Hay una fotografía que no está encuadernada en este libro, pero que lo atraviesa como un fantasma. Un hombre sentado en el suelo de un estudio ajeno. Los dedos embarrados de bermellón. El rostro vuelto hacia el objetivo con una felicidad que parece prestada. Pinta hombres que llevan cascos de buzo en la cabeza. Ese hombre es el padre de Leila Slimani. Estuvo en la cárcel. Después de la cárcel, sus cielos se rasgaron con tormentas negras. Y ella, la hija, nunca habló con él de arte. Esa herida no cicatriza. Solo se cultiva, como una bacteria en un frasco de laboratorio. Slimani comete la imprudencia de aceptar una noche en el museo Punta della Dogana de Venecia. La primera norma de quien escribe novelas —nos advierte— es saber decir no hasta que el teléfono enmudezca y el correo solo escupa publicidad. Decir no para que te llamen misántropa, arrogante, solitaria. Y sin embargo, va porque la contradicción es el único territorio fértil del escritor. Encerrarse no es huir del mundo, sino mirarlo desde el hueco de la cerradura. Venecia, ciudad obscenamente contada, donde todo parece dicho, se convierte entonces en el decorado perfecto para una desobediencia de esta autora inquietante: la de hablar desde el silencio. Escribir, para Slimani, no es renunciar a la felicidad cotidiana. No intentar consolarse. Cultivar las propias penas como los investigadores cultivan bacterias. Hay una honestidad feroz en su actitud, porque desnuda el oficio de su última gran mentira: la literatura no salva. La literatura permite sobrevivir, pero no promete ningún paraíso. Ella lo dice sin retórica: «habría sobrevivido sin ser escritora, pero no estoy segura de que hubiera sido feliz». ***
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQSwmxBZ2nDkLzBu89vWsDrkiiccs7Bj5YLpeR7yTXAgX/1780363169136.png)
***

> El libro es breve, pero las digresiones son su verdadera arquitectura. Slimani pasa del arte contemporáneo a los cuadros naífs de la pintora Chaibia. De los monstruos con cabeza de pájaro de Abbess Ladi —que poblaron sus pesadillas infantiles— a los cielos negros de su padre. Habla del colonialismo sin nombrarlo. De la vergüenza de no pertenecer a nada. De vivir en un no-lugar, entre Oriente y Occidente, como las aguas de Venecia navegan entre la belleza y la destrucción. No hay en ella la voz de quien reivindica una identidad estable. Hay, por el contrario, la confesión de una derrota necesaria: cuanto más escribe, más excomulgada se siente. Más extranjera. Y esa es la paradoja que sostiene el libro. Slimani quiso que la escritura fuera una empresa de reparación. Reparar la injusticia de su padre. Las infamias contra su pueblo y su sexo. Quiso que las palabras le procuraran una identidad firme, lejos de la mirada de los otros. La isla no es un refugio, es una atalaya. No se escribe para huir de los demás, sino para contemplarlos mejor. Para satisfacer esa pasión —tan incómoda, tan poco confesable— que se siente por los otros. ***
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYuPr3P9RkDQunvBjCr63Lpgrx2To4gHNjUERPkangaMU/1780363206674.png)
***

> El pasado, dice la autora en estas páginas, no está muerto. La literatura no entiende de fronteras temporales. Por eso el padre aparece en estas páginas y por eso los muertos vuelven como esas preguntas que no supimos formular en vida. Escribimos para exhumar secretos y dar vida a los fantasmas. Aceptamos que la identidad estable era una ilusión, y que uno se inventa cada vez que escribe, lejos de la mirada de los otros, pero también a través de ella. Quiero creer que en Hive Book Club , como en Venecia, la belleza se hunde mientras nosotros, testarudos, seguimos diciendo que no. Seguimos escribiendo. Leyendo. ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdvc788wxsBSQHY3z21o3wSTU7hqRnyYc2JFEn2pEYSev/1752848220077.png) La traducción al inglés en Google Translation La edición visual en servicios gratuitos de Banner Maker. **© Marabuzal, 2026. Contenido original. Todos los derechos reservados.** ![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVDUKVA6YugQdRrhGACmnps8ddBkV8W6UwGEo9DwaNQxF/1768408479017.jpg)

>

Warm greetings, dear friends of @hivebookclub. I'm reconnecting with you through #ecency to share a new review.

Today I'd like to talk about a French-Moroccan writer: Leila Slimani (Morocco, 1981) and this book, which has been translated into Spanish as \

> There is a photograph not bound in this book, but which haunts it like a ghost. A man sits on the floor of someone else's studio. His fingers smeared with vermilion. His face turned toward the lens with a happiness that seems borrowed. He paints men wearing diving helmets. That man is Leila Slimani's father. He was in prison. After prison, his skies were torn open by black storms. And she, his daughter, never spoke to him about art. That wound doesn't heal. It only festers, like a bacterium in a laboratory flask. Slimani makes the imprudent decision to spend a night at the Punta della Dogana museum in Venice. The first rule for anyone who writes novels—she warns us—is to know how to say no until the phone goes silent and the mail is nothing but junk mail. To say no so that they call you a misanthrope, arrogant, a loner. And yet, she goes because contradiction is the writer's only fertile ground. To shut oneself away is not to flee the world, but to observe it through the keyhole. Venice, a city obscenely described, where everything seems to have been said, then becomes the perfect backdrop for this unsettling author's act of disobedience: to speak from silence. ***
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQSwmxBZ2nDkLzBu89vWsDrkiiccs7Bj5YLpeR7yTXAgX/1780363169136.png)
***

> The book is brief, but its digressions are its true architecture. Slimani moves from contemporary art to the naive paintings of Chaibia. From the bird-headed monsters of Abbess Ladi—which populated her childhood nightmares—to her father's black skies. She speaks of colonialism without naming it. Of the shame of belonging nowhere. Of living in a no-place, between East and West, like the waters of Venice sailing between beauty and destruction. There is no voice in her that claims a stable identity. On the contrary, there is the confession of a necessary defeat: the more she writes, the more excommunicated she feels. The more foreign. And that is the paradox that sustains the book. Slimani wanted writing to be an act of reparation. To repair the injustice of his father. The infamies against his people and his sex. He wanted words to provide him with a firm identity, far from the gaze of others. The island is not a refuge, it is a watchtower. One does not write to flee from others, but to observe them more closely. To satisfy that passion—so uncomfortable, so difficult to confess—that one feels for others. ***
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYuPr3P9RkDQunvBjCr63Lpgrx2To4gHNjUERPkangaMU/1780363206674.png)
***

> The past, the author says in these pages, is not dead. Literature knows no temporal boundaries. That is why the father appears in these pages, and why the dead return like those questions we couldn't formulate in life. We write to exhume secrets and give life to ghosts. We accept that a stable identity was an illusion, and that one invents oneself each time one writes, far from the gaze of others, but also through it. I want to believe that in Hive Book Club, as in Venice, beauty sinks while we, stubbornly, continue to say no. We continue writing.
