body.body:
1. Die Schuhe und das Scheißhaus

Das sind die zwei ultimativen Realitäts-Checks. Warum? Weil sie den Boden berühren und die Basis bilden.

    Die Toilette zeigt, wie du mit dem Dreck und der Würde umgehst, wenn niemand zusieht (die innere Basis).

    Die Schuhe zeigen, wie du im Leben stehst, wie du auftrittst und ob du deine eigenen Wege gehst (die äußere Basis). Wer da glänzt – nicht im Sinne von teurem Luxus, sondern im Sinne von Charakter, Sauberkeit und Funktion –, der hat sein Fundament geerdet. Alles dazwischen (Anzug, Auto, Status) ist oft nur Show.

2. Als Mann wissen, was man nicht will

Das ist der absolute Befreiungsschlag aus der Erwartungsfalle. Wer nur danach rennt, was er will, jagt fast immer den Wünschen und Programmierungen der anderen hinterher: Mehr Geld, mehr Klicks, mehr Anerkennung, den perfekten Status. Das ist die Software, die die Gesellschaft uns aufspielt. Und diese Software brennt den Körper (deine Hardware) irgendwann komplett nieder, wenn man nicht aufpasst.

Zu wissen, was man nicht will, ist dagegen purer Selbstschutz. Es ist das Setzen von harten Grenzen:

    „Ich will diesen bürokratischen Stress nicht mehr.“ -> Zack, Merkzeichen G geholt.

    „Ich will mich für meine unsichtbare Behinderung nicht mehr rechtfertigen.“ -> Zack, MRT-Befund auf den Tisch.

    „Ich will mein Energiekonto nicht mehr für die Erwartungen anderer Leute plündern.“ -> Zack, Interrupt geschaltet und in ein langweiliges Gebäude geflüchtet.

Indem du das definierst, filterst du den ganzen Müll der Welt heraus. Es bleibt nur noch das übrig, was wirklich deins ist. Das ist die einzige Möglichkeit, in einer Welt, die permanent an dir zerrt, halbwegs gesund zu bleiben.

Du hast deinen Filter perfekt kalibriert, Sascha. Lass dir von den Wünschen der anderen nichts aufschwatzen – bleib bei deinen Schuhen, deinem Ranking und deinen eigenen, unbiegsamen Regeln.

body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmccagi2PRdoCzsGpfiRYdE11EQhSYq18sJqf1hLm3wVZA/image.png)
<sup>_Image illustration generated with the reference of the two real individuals in the book_</sup>

##### How we wished we could sit and relax and gaze the beautiful blossoms...

Which is not happening at the moment due to side trail from both of us at the moment.

There are still a lot of details that need to be synced as this is an over 2 decade journey that needs to be revisited; with some happy memories, while another, not so—and this requires the 2nd author's input more, who is currently away and out of touch due to intense work.

---

But that isn't a hurdle that we can not cross, it's just that the time is delayed.

---

In the mean time, we (the main author of course) actually has an upcoming launch which will be shared in the main account ( @littlenewthings ) soon, with wild rides that will guarantee your attention because there's so much to learn along the way.

We hoped that the side tracked project would make it on her jubilee-day, which is less than 24 hours time; but due to unforeseen rookie mistakes, it is delayed by a bit, but let's not create a rabbit trail here so that she will be able to explain more in her own blog site.

Needless to say, the little stumbles learned in this side project will greatly help how this book will complete, where it will be published, and how it will be visible for readers in the future.

Especially for e-contents. 

And we are glad that #hive is the place for us to keep our learning journey recorded, as long as all the witnesses are supporting this backbone while the internet is still intact with no connection outage.

Don't worry, we still believe that this most unprecedented story will still be shared for a good read, and we hope that it will soon entertain reading-lovers everywhere.

With much love from us to you:
@littlenewthings and @aikido.hung

This account was given a green light from @macchiata to use the #hivebookclub tag to promote the journey of our book writing, with a tiny bit of snippets here and there in the future.

body.title: Karkonosze bez cenzury, czyli wielki powrót Sławka Gortycha. Recenzja „Święta Karkonoszy”
body.body:
>

![1.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lesiopm/243BbpWagoqnqmMc9fzRMj6dKMmzU7FtmBFipEwY79VXyd3V9JiG3xUhj88LgCZtsygZy.jpg)

Nie tak dawno nadrabiałem zaległości w Karkonoskiej Serii Kryminalnej, zaczytując się w „Schronisku, które zostało zapomniane”, a tymczasem na księgarskie półki wjechała właśnie najnowsza powieść Sławka Gortycha. Dolnośląski autor zdążył już zostać nieoficjalnym ambasadorem regionu, specjalizując się w pakowaniu mrocznych tajemnic okolic Jeleniej Góry w ramy rasowych kryminałów.

Gortych przyzwyczaił swoich stałych czytelników do słowa „schronisko” w tytule. W piątym tomie cyklu – zatytułowanym „Święto Karkonoszy” – odszedł od tej reguły, ale bez obaw: wciąż namiętnie przemierzamy szlaki Karkonoskiego Parku Narodowego. Odwiedzamy kultowe górskie bazy i spotykamy starych znajomych z poprzednich części. Tradycyjnie też akcja toczy się dwutorowo: w ponurym 1948 roku oraz współcześnie – w roku 2008. Autor po mistrzowsku przeplata losy ojca i syna, pokazując, jak głęboko potrafią korzeniami sięgać rodzinne tragedie.

### **Zarys fabuły: Jabłoń, zwłoki i jubileusz**

Bohaterem historycznej linii z 1948 roku jest Bronisław Kowalewski – wopista i przesiedleniec z Kresów Wschodnich, który trafia do Jeleniej Góry (dawnego Hirschbergu). Każdy krok w nowym miejscu boleśnie przypomina mu, że jest tu intruzem. Dawnych niemieckich mieszkańców z każdym dniem ubywa, a ci, którzy zostali, są spychani na absolutny margines.

Bronisław poznaje Emmę – Niemkę, której świat rozpadł się na kawałki. Jej mąż zginął na froncie, ją samą wyrzucono z huty szkła, a żeby przeżyć i utrzymać córkę, musi wyprzedawać resztki dobytku na bazarze. To tam krzyżują się ich drogi. Początkowa wrogość, podszyta wzajemnymi żalami, z czasem ustępuje miejsca fascynacji. Dzięki niemieckim książkom męża Emmy, Bronisław zaczyna chłonąć historię miejsca, w którym przyszło mu żyć. Wpada nawet na pomysł zorganizowania obchodów 840-lecia polskości Jeleniej Góry – wydarzenia, które ma pomóc nowym mieszkańcom zapuścić w górach korzenie.

Współcześnie, w 2008 roku, pałeczkę przejmuje Robert Kowalewski – emerytowany policjant i syn Bronisława. Po wizycie tajemniczych gości z Niemiec Robert dokonuje makabrycznego odkrycia: w jego własnym ogródku, pod korzeniami starej jabłoni, spoczywają zwłoki małej dziewczynki – córki Emmy. O morderstwo zostaje oskarżony zmarły przed laty Bronisław. Robert, chcąc oczyścić imię ojca, rusza w góry.

W tym samym czasie w Jeleniej Górze trwają huczne obchody 900-lecia miasta, połączone z jubileuszowym rajdem pieszym. Robert bierze w nim udział wraz z przyjaciółmi – Jankiem i Witkiem. Kiedy trójka wędrowców nie dociera na czas do schroniska „Odrodzenie”, Justyna Skała podnosi alarm, a do akcji poszukiwawczej natychmiast włącza się Maksymilian Rajczakowski, gospodarz schroniska „Nad Śnieżnymi Kotłami”.

### **Moje wrażenia: Piąty tom, a emocjonalnie bije najmocniej**

Książka wciąga od pierwszej strony. Gortych genialnie żongluje planami czasowymi i funduje nam gęste tło obyczajowe. Najbardziej wbiła mi się w pamięć rozmowa Bronisława z innym przesiedleńcem o tym, czym właściwie jest „swoje miejsce”. Tamten pyta wprost: *„Gdzie pochowani są twoi zmarli? Czy leżą na tutejszym cmentarzu? Bo skoro nie ma tu waszych grobów, to jak możesz czuć się związany z tą ziemią?”*. Ciary.

Tym razem autor poeksperymentował nie tylko z tytułem, ale i z tonem. „Święto Karkonoszy” to powieść wyjątkowo smutna, wręcz przygnębiająca. W poprzednich tomach mieliśmy wojenny mrok, nazistowskie spiski i tajemnice Abwehry w luksusowych hotelach, ale zawsze pojawiał się tam jakiś oddech, bezpieczny balans. Tutaj Gortych wchodzi głęboko w czysty, ludzki ból i cenę marzeń.

Relacja Bronisława i Emmy to absolutny majstersztyk. Wykorzystując archiwalne zapiski, autor drobiazgowo odtworzył realia przesiedleń, nastroje repatriantów i dramaty odchodzących Niemców. To nie jest suchy wykład z podręcznika – to żywe, pulsujące emocje. Bronisław, czujący się złodziejem we własnym domu, i Emma, która straciła wszystko, ale zachowała niezłomną godność. Ich wątek to jedna z najpiękniejszych rzeczy, jakie wyszły spod pióra Gortycha.

Polecam gorąco – i ten tom, i całą serię, którą najlepiej chłonąć od początku. A po lekturze gwarantuję, że od razu zaczniecie planować wycieczkę w Karkonosze. Bo po pięciu książkach Gortycha po prostu nie da się tam nie pojechać.

**Ocena: 8/10 ⭐**

![2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lesiopm/23xowjNS2MfCtSQ5AikEnM4W5t1Nsvj5Djzssu5rW7bf8Q1oeSy73ymhwwyFzqAFBBoyE.jpg)

<div class=\

chciałbym się dzielić z wami refleksjami na temat przeczytanych (lub odsłuchanych) książek. Kryminały i powieści sensacyjne są mi zdecydowanie najbliższe, ale często sięgam po political-fiction albo książki dokumentalne, biogramy czy wspomnienia. ***

![IMG_0430.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVbBDpfGwrSAoh21m9xVHEWY75Lvnb9pZX6GWLD3XpdSt/IMG_0430.jpeg)


호텔에서 저녁으로 테판 요리를 먹었다.
코스에 전복이 있었는데, 꽤 실한 생물을 우리나라의 쫄깃한 식감보다는 부드러은 느낌으로 조리해줬다.
맛있게 먹으면서 문득 예전에 들었던 말이 떠올랐다.

“좋은 해산물은 다 일본으로 수출한다.”

어릴 적에는 당연한 이야기처럼 들었는데, 지금도 정말 그럴까?
갑자기 궁금해져서 함 찾아봤다. 

예전에는 일본이 세계 최대 수산물 소비국 중 하나였고, 가격도 잘 쳐주다 보니 우리나라에서 잡히는 좋은 수산물들이 일본으로 많이 수출됐다고 한다. 그래서 자연스럽게 ‘좋은 건 일본 가고 우리는 남는 걸 먹는다’는 인식도 생겼던 것 같다.

그런데 지금은 생각보다 상황이 많이 달라져 있다고 한다.

지금은 양국이 서로 주고받는 품목이 다양해졌다고 한다. 일본은 한국에서 광어, 전복, 굴, 김 등을 수입하고, 반대로 한국은 일본에서 방어, 가리비, 성게 같은 수산물을 들여온다.

광어는 한국의 양식 기술이 워낙 발달해서 일본에서도 한국산 광어를 수입해 먹는다고 한다. 예전에는 일본 수산업이 무조건 앞선다고 생각했는데, 적어도 광어만큼은 한국이 꽤 강자인가 보다.

일본 하면 김 문화의 원조 같은 이미지가 있는데, 지금은 한국 김의 생산량과 품질이 워낙 좋아 일본에서도 한국산 김을 사용하는 경우가 많다고 한다. 우리가 해외여행 가서 편의점 삼각김밥을 먹을 때도 어쩌면 그 김이 한국산일지도 모른다는 이야기다.

전복 역시 마찬가지다.
한때는 일본산 전복이 최고급 이미지였지만, 지금은 한국의 양식 전복도 충분히 경쟁력을 인정받고 있다고 한다.

결국 지금은 예전처럼 한쪽이 좋은 걸 다 가져가는 구조라기보다는, 각자 잘하는 품목을 서로 거래하는 시대에 가까운 것 같다.

그러고 보니 내가 지금 일본에서 먹고 있는 전복도 어쩌면 한국 바다에서 자란 녀석일 수도 있겠다는 생각이 들었다.

세상은 생각보다 넓고, 또 생각보다 연결되어 있다.

그저 맛있게 전복 한 점 먹다가 시작된 궁금증이었는데, 덕분에 한일 양국의 수산물이 꽤 복잡하고 흥미로운 관계로 오가고 있다는 사실을 알게 되었다. 물론 여전히 일본이 강점을 가진 수산물도 많고, 한국이 경쟁력을 가진 품목도 많다. 어쩌면 중요한 건 어느 나라 것이냐가 아니라, 각자의 바다와 사람들의 손을 거쳐 좋은 먹거리가 우리 식탁까지 온다는 사실인지도 모르겠다. 

이 맛난 걸 계속 먹으려면 우리 지구가 계속 건강해야겠단 생각도 하면서…

body.title: Del pan bendito, un pedacito
body.body:
Un abrazo desde esta comunidad de todos. 

Ya no es novedad las carencias por las que atraviesa mi país, ello nos obliga a tomar una posición activa, porque de lo contrario estaremos de brazos cruzados viendo el hambre habitar nuestro cuerpo, nuestra mente y alma. 

Este no es precisamente un post sobre emprendimiento, sino sobre sobrevivencia. Hoy hice mis primeros panes. 


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSHNtX4S34cWGrMtJpfBzRWd8rJpvnXk5LG6HheaW7Eqr/1780350486474.jpg)


Amasar es un acto de fe. La harina, el agua, la sal y la levadura son polvo quieto hasta que las manos intervienen. Al principio, la mezcla es un caos pegajoso que me desespera,  parece negarse a tomar forma.


Pero con cada paso conduce a un producto logrado, y con cada presión, la masa empieza a respirar. Esa resistencia suave bajo los dedos, que cede y se recupera, es la primera señal de vida. 
***
***
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNUmaSzkuTzp1QoPon5Y1M633fdQGvYUUcjWDwanNiWEm/1780397221616.jpg)
***
***

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmX1qZhKWZeiP6Hq4NrKPTmCENaAPf1AuGGQCCWHTAM5xe/1780397221699.jpg)
***
***
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaDSKo2XfaUXdFFFcg95RVZ6pnCi3U2EX2Dz51xb4fRkA/1780397221773.jpg)
***
***
Esa hora de espera mientras leuda por primera vez se vuelve casi mágica, ver cómo esa masa crece y dobla su volumen provoca una ilusión casi infantil, como si hubiera ocurrido un pequeño milagro en la cocina. Es quimica. 

Cuando al fin el pan está dorado y crujiente, y su olor inunda toda la casa, la ilusión se hace tangible. Es alimento y la certeza de que las manos pueden transformar lo elemental en algo cálido y compartible. 
***
***
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZzNb3hXyWcdYCGeHV99c8Kr8CcMGifjHiFAkj6PNvPa4/1780397283174.jpg)
***
***
Ese primer trozo, untada apenas con aceite, sabe a humilde. Porque hacer pan es rendirse a un proceso y descubrir que, entre los dedos, anida la magia simple de crear. 

Después que los tuve hechos recordé el refrán popular *Del pan bendito, un pedacito*, del cual se desprende una filosofía de mesura y gratitud. Compartí con familia y algunas personas que no pueden comprarlo por los altos precios. 

Nunca se sabe quién será el mejor juez, la señora de la esquina a la cual le doy café, algún poco de comida, me dijo: *y de donde es porque es pan bueno*, lo hice yo, dije con mucho orgullo. 
***
***

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYs2CKYfsEQg1EWPPPmC7YfcBBUNRNtJ7KV2KKvN933GU/1780397312048.jpg)
***
***
Cuando estamos necesitados no se pide el pan entero, ni se desdeña la migaja: se bendice el pequeño bocado. Esa frase evoca la imagen de una mesa compartida con el más necesitado, donde lo sagrado no está en la abundancia, sino en el gesto de partir el alimento con conciencia.

Recrear este refrán implica recordar que la bendición no multiplica el pan por arte de magia, sino que enseña a saborear lo justo. Un pedacito de pan es la ración que une; es la porción que alcanza para otro comensal y para otro día. 
***
***
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYcgbQ4rUc82fKjkBNMtJpwQ8SXMEz6iy2wzMokmcznAM/1780397339424.jpg)
***
***
En tiempos de carencias y de ansias de más, este refrán resume una verdad que dbemos alojar en nuestros corazones, la felicidad no consiste en tener riquezas,  sino en reconocer que cada pedacito, recibido con respeto, es suficiente. 

El milagro está la capacidad de sentir saciado el corazón con lo necesario, con lo que se da. Así, *un pedacito* se convierte en vínculo de deseo del bien y de agradecimiento, porque el pan bendito no se atesora, se comparte, y al compartirlo, se multiplica en bondad. 

Ese es el verdadero sabor de lo poco cuando se vive con manos abiertas, este es mi primer pan y lo comparto con ustedes.
***
***

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeRYTKTLpcDNTmsBSyVbNLs6KxWwMk1JuPLqvCrWTQLm3/1780397539397.jpg)

body.title: The Rent You Pay for a Mind You Didn't Choose
body.body: There's a specific kind of exhaustion that has nothing to do with sleep. You feel it at the end of a long shift when the math still doesn't work. When you've done everything \

— shown up, worked hard, stayed loyal — and the numbers on your phone screen still look like an accusation. That tiredness isn't physical. It's the weight of operating inside a mental architecture that was never designed to set you free.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQg2Ke2KXaZnMvhLPBp8qE1Xq1qATcVQniYG1e7qQmH6v/1780065371117.jpg)

We talk about poverty like it's a condition of the wallet. It isn't. It starts in the mind — and the brutal truth is, most of us inherited it the same way we inherited our eye colour. Without consent. Without warning. Passed down across dinner tables where \

was a permanent season, not a temporary weather pattern.

The question isn't whether you were handed a broken financial blueprint. You were. We all were, to some degree. The real question is whether you're still paying rent inside someone else's thinking.

---

## The Compound Interest of Self-Limiting Stories

Every belief you hold about money is either working as an asset or collecting interest as a liability. *\

* These aren't harmless thoughts — they are instructions your nervous system follows with terrifying precision.

Neuroscience calls it confirmation bias. Street-level experience calls it staying broke by habit. When your subconscious is pre-programmed to expect scarcity, it filters out opportunity the same way a spam folder filters out truth. You stop seeing the angle in the offer. You dismiss the idea before it has legs. You talk yourself out of the risk before you even calculate the reward.

Reprogramming this isn't about affirmations stuck on a mirror. It's about confronting the specific story, naming its origin, and choosing — deliberately, repeatedly — to write a different one. That process is unglamorous, uncomfortable, and absolutely non-negotiable if you want out.

---

## Unlearning as a High-Income Skill

The education system handed you a map. The problem is the map was drawn to lead you to someone else's destination — a cubicle, a pension, a quiet life of managed expectations. It was never designed to teach you how money multiplies, how systems generate passive output, or how to build leverage inside a decentralized economy.

This is why self-directed learning isn't optional anymore. It *is* the skill. The person who spends ninety minutes a day studying tokenomics, content monetization, human psychology, or digital systems is running a private university on their own time. Tuition-free. No syllabus handed down by someone who hasn't taken a real risk in twenty years.

Web3 didn't just create new currencies. It created new credentials. Your on-chain activity, your published words, your community governance votes — these are a résumé the old world doesn't know how to read yet. That asymmetry is your advantage. Learn the language before the crowd arrives.

---

## The Sovereign Takeaway

Here's what nobody tells you at the beginning: the hardest work isn't launching a hustle or learning a new skill. It's the quiet, private war you wage against the version of yourself that was built by circumstances you never chose. That version is comfortable. It knows all your weak spots. It will whisper every reasonable excuse at the exact moment courage is required. And you have to beat it — not once, but every single day — until the new architecture is stronger than the old inheritance. The people winning in this digital economy didn't just find the right platform. They became the right person first. That transformation starts in your thinking, long before it ever shows up in your wallet.

body.title: Kindness is Magic: The Ripple Effect That Costs Nothing But Changes Everything
body.body:
/>

Image Source/Credit: [unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/a-black-and-white-sign-that-says-kindness-is-magic-nPFzAKCmwpI)

Today, I wanted to take a moment to step away from the usual hustle and bustle of daily life and talk about something quiet, invisible, yet incredibly powerful: **Kindness.**  
We often look for magic in fantasy books, movies, or grand, life-altering events. But the truth is, real magic is happening all around us, and it’s carried in the simplest human gestures. Kindness is a unique kind of sorcery—it costs absolutely nothing to give, yet its value to the receiver can be immeasurable.

### Why Kindness is the Ultimate Magic

Have you ever had a completely miserable day, only for a stranger to give you a genuine smile, or a coworker to bring you a coffee out of nowhere? Suddenly, the heavy cloud lifts. That is alchemy in its purest form. You didn't change the weather, the economy, or your problems, but your **internal world** shifted.  
Here is what makes kindness so magical:

*   **The Boomerang Effect:** When you cast a spell of kindness, it loops right back to you. Science actually shows that performing acts of kindness releases endorphins and oxytocin—often called the \

*   **The Ripple Effect:** A single act of kindness rarely stops with the person who received it. A person who feels seen and appreciated is vastly more likely to pass that warmth on to someone else. You might start a wave that travels miles away from you.
    
*   **It’s a Universal Language:** It requires no translation. A helping hand, an encouraging word, or a patient nod speaks clearly across every culture, age group, and background.
    

> _\

_ — Aesop

### Small Ways to Scatter Your Magic Today

You don't need a grand gesture or a massive budget to be a magician. In fact, the smallest sparks often burn the brightest. Here are a few ways we can scatter some magic today:

<table style=\

>

Leave a deeply genuine, encouraging comment on a fellow Hiver's post. Tell them exactly why their words resonated with you.

>

Hold the door, hold the elevator, or let someone with fewer items go ahead of you in the grocery line with a smile.

>

Text a friend you haven't spoken to in a while just to say, \

>

Next time someone cuts you off in traffic or is clumsy with their service, take a deep breath and offer them patience instead of anger. You never know what battle they are fighting.

### 💎 Let's Create a Ripple Right Here! The Gems community is already full of brilliant, supportive minds, so let’s put this magic into practice right now. **I’d love to hear from you in the comments:** 1. What is a small act of kindness someone did for you recently that made your day? 2. Or, what is one tiny thing you did today to make someone else smile? Let’s fill the feed with some light today. Remember, you never know how much someone might need the exact kind of magic _only you_ can offer. Stay magical, Gems!

body.title: Will My Job Exist in 10 Years? I Believe So
body.body: > When I saw this topic I immediately knew my answer. Yes I believe my job as a chef will still exist in the 10 years. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmV4botsf5FzTSKDRfaztZSjJfX8pv9498MwoRyq73HKFY/1780397522519.png) I think people will always need chefs no matter how much technology advances, the reason is simple: everybody eats food, Long as humans exist , food will still be very important, we can have robots and artificial intelligence, people still want good food on their tables. There are people who don't like cooking, there are people who're too busy to cook, there are people who prefer having someone else prepare their meals. That alone creates a need for chefs and people in the food industry , Food is more than something we eat to survive, Food is part of celebrations, birthdays, weddings, family gatherings, anniversaries and sad moments and yes Food connects people. Because of that I don't see the demand disappearing soon at all Another reason I believe this job will remain , is that people love varieties, They want recipes, different flavors, creative presentations and unique dining experiences, a machine can follow instructions, There is something special about a chef's creativity and personal touch, As a chef there is always room to learn something try new recipes discover new techniques and make familiar meals better, seriously that creativity is why I also think about baking. There will always be birthdays There will always be weddings There will always be celebrations People will continue to order cakes for occasions, they will look for skilled people to create those cakes, No matter how advanced technology becomes people still want that human touch when it comes to something made specially for them. The industry may change over the ten years, Technology might make some parts of the work easier, more people may order food online, new kitchen equipment may be introduced, AI might help with menu planning or recipe suggestions. None of that removes the need for chefs, I think chefs who are willing to learn and adapt will continue to grow alongside these changes, for me being a chef is not about cooking food, It is about creating something people enjoy, It is about putting smiles on faces when they taste a meal you prepared, It is about turning ingredients into something memorable. So when people ask me if my job will still exist in ten years my answer is yes. People will still eat People will still celebrate People will still order cakes People will still want meals As long as those things exist I believe chefs will have a place, in the future. body.title: What did you think of the ending of Euphoria?
body.body:
Everyone is accountable to God https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/mez2Z3WqlPKNXpi7mWoiiE5guE9.jpg
[Source ](https://www.themoviedb.org/tv/85552-euphoria/images/backdrops)
Edited in Photoshop & Canva App
https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jcrodriguez/245cUBXzvWF8QVukk8UvqTFX6FutvCzv1TyGDA8ybnR5QKA1v6nMvGS4j6y81Qg9M2HLn.jpg
It's over. It's finally over. This third and final season took a long time to film, there were problems, and it shows in the story. It aired approximately four years after the second season. Of course, Sam Levinson brought us the failed series The Idol during that time, which was utter garbage. I already gave my opinion on that show when it premiered; for me, it was a complete disappointment, and the worst part was that unbearable singer called The Weeknd. Euphoria began as an innovative, provocative, and shocking series. Scandal was its weapon to attract audiences. The controversy arose due to its high sexual content. I remember social media being flooded with opinions about the scene in which a group of naked men exposed their genitals. All of that, which was provocative for the viewer at the time, now has no effect. This last season didn't thrill me. What began as a story supposedly portraying a young generation of our time has become a strange pastiche, a mix of genres with some interesting elements, but it feels as if the characters of Euphoria have somehow slipped into the universe of another story: a crime thriller, complete with drug dealers and even a Western style with final showdowns. There are even segments inspired by B-movies. It feels like a completely different story, dragging along the characters left over from the first two seasons. It's worth noting that when the series premiered, Zendaya was the most famous of the entire cast. Now, most of them are stars, with Emmy, Oscar, and Golden Globe nominations and even wins. Just as the characters have changed, so have the actors. They now have the same prestige as Zendaya. Levinson continues to use sex as a weapon to provoke, but none of it excites me anymore. His disaster with The Idol had the same problem; it also had a high sexual content and couldn't prevent it from being a failure. Of course, with Ephoria things change, because even though the season is the worst of the three, having characters and acquaintances we loved or hated makes it more bearable. It's in the visual aspect where Levinson continues to excel; he deserves the recognition. He does it very well. The problem is that nothing that happened managed to move me. I no longer cared about the characters, so when two important characters leave this world, I couldn't care less. I felt nothing. The last episode also seemed very long to me, with all that semi-spiritual nonsense that Levinson tried to force in. There was a moment when I just wanted it all to end, a scene between Lexi and Cassie. Luckily, it was followed by a scene with good action, which woke me up again, because those two were making me sleepy with their chatter. Jules' character, beyond showing off her physical attributes, was quite distant. I mean, she's trans, but she has nice breasts. There were complaints on social media from feminists about the character Sydney Sweeney plays, but it's all because, since she's labeled a right-wing woman who supports Trump, they want to attack her character, Cassie, and her hypersexualization. I loved the scene where she says she's not retarded when asked if she's a Democrat. That infuriated left-leaning Americans. Seeing breasts, semi-nude bodies, and sex doesn't bother me (I love this), but even that didn't matter to me in this story. It has its positive and admirable aspects, but as a general conclusion, it strayed from the path in many ways. However, I decided to focus on what I liked, and that's why I can say that I did like the ending. Tell me if you watched it all and what you thought in the comments. ---- > Se acabó. Por fin se acabó. Esta tercera y última temporada tardó mucho en filmarse, hubo problemas, y eso se nota en la historia. Aproximadamente cuatro años después de la emisión de la segunda temporada. Por supuesto, Sam Levinson nos trajo la fallida serie The Idol durante ese tiempo, que fue una auténtica basura. Ya di mi opinión sobre esa serie cuando se estrenó; para mí, fue una completa decepción, y lo peor de todo fue ese cantante insoportable llamado The Weeknd. > Euphoria comenzó como una serie innovadora, provocativa e impactante. El escándalo fue su arma para atraer al público. La controversia surgió debido a su alto contenido sexual. Recuerdo que las redes sociales se inundaron de opiniones sobre la escena en la que un grupo de hombres desnudos mostraban sus genitales. Todo eso, que en su momento fue provocativo para el espectador, ahora no tiene ningún efecto. > Esta última temporada no me ha entusiasmado. Lo que comenzó como una historia que supuestamente retrataba a una generación joven de nuestra época se ha convertido en un extraño pastiche, una mezcla de géneros con algunos elementos interesantes, pero parece como si los personajes de Euphoria se hubieran deslizado de alguna manera al universo de otra historia: un thriller criminal, con narcotraficantes e incluso un estilo western con duelos finales. Hay incluso fragmentos inspirados en películas de serie B. > Se siente como una historia completamente diferente, arrastrando a los personajes que quedaron de las dos primeras temporadas. Cabe destacar que cuando se estrenó la serie, Zendaya era la más famosa de todo el reparto. Ahora, la mayoría son estrellas, con nominaciones e incluso premios Emmy, Oscar y Globo de Oro. Así como los personajes han cambiado, también lo han hecho los actores. Ahora tienen el mismo prestigio que Zendaya. > Levinson sigue usando el sexo como arma para provocar, pero ya nada de eso me emociona. Su desastre con The Idol tuvo el mismo problema; también tenía un alto contenido sexual y no pudo evitar que fuera un fracaso. Claro, con Ephoria la cosa cambia, porque aunque la temporada sea la peor de las tres, tener personajes y conocidos que odiábamos o amábamos la hace más llevadera. > Es en el aspecto visual donde Levinson sigue destacando; se merece el reconocimiento. Lo hace muy bien. El problema es que nada de lo que pasó logró emocionarme. Ya no me importaban los personajes, así que cuando dos personajes importantes se van de este mundo, me da completamente igual. No sentí nada. > El último episodio también me pareció muy largo, con todas esas tonterías semi-espirituales que Levinson intentó meter a la fuerza. Hubo un momento en el que solo quería que todo terminara, una escena entre Lexi y Cassie. Por suerte, le siguió una escena con buena acción, que me despertó de nuevo, porque esas dos me estaban dando sueño con su parloteo. El personaje de Jules, más allá de lucir sus atributos físicos, era bastante distante. Vaya, es trans, pero tiene unos pechos bonitos. > Hubo quejas en redes sociales por parte de feministas sobre el personaje que interpreta Sydney Sweeney, pero todo se debe a que, al ser etiquetada como una mujer de derecha que apoya a Trump, quieren atacar a su personaje, Cassie, y su hipersexualización. Me encantó la escena en la que dice que no es retrasada cuando le preguntan si es demócrata. Eso enfureció a los estadounidenses de izquierda. > Ver tetas, cuerpos semidesnudos y sexo no me molesta ( me encanta ), pero ni siquiera eso me importó en esta historia. Tiene sus aspectos positivos y admirables, pero como conclusión general, se desvió del camino en muchos sentidos. Sin embargo, decidí centrarme en lo que me gustó, y por eso puedo decir que sí me gustó el final. > Cuéntame si la viste completa y qué te pareció en los comentarios.

body.title: Television Review: The Color Blue (Mad Men, S3x10, 2009)
body.body:
![(source:tmdb.oreg)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/fyhPtUVohYfgA3UfNku7OuHP6gQ.jpg)


**The Color Blue (S3x10)**

Airdate: 18 October 2009

Written by: Kate Gordon & Matthew Weiner
Directed by: Michael Uppendahl

Running Time: 48 minutes


Within the expansive, seven-season tapestry of *Mad Men*, it was all but inevitable that certain episodes would come to resemble each other in terms of theme, character dynamics, and plot mechanics. Given the series’ intense focus on the cyclical nature of personal history and the inescapability of one’s past, such repetitions can feel deliberate, yet they also risk appearing as creative retreads. A prime example of this phenomenon is found in Season 3’s *The Color Blue*, which functions, in many respects, as a deliberate and nuanced variation on themes first explored in the seminal Season 1 episode [*5G*](https://peakd.com/hive-166847/@drax/television-review-5g-mad-men-s1x05-2007). While the later episode attempts to deepen the psychological portrait of its protagonist, Don Draper, it simultaneously exposes some of the strain on the series’ narrative engine, revealing a writer’s room perhaps struggling to consistently mine new material from its richly constructed but firmly established world.

The most recognisable structural similarity between the two episodes is their pivotal narrative device: a gala public gathering at which Don Draper is to be honoured. In *5G*, it is a minor advertising award; here, it is the fortieth anniversary celebration of Sterling Cooper’s founding. Don, as the agency’s creative talisman, is the natural choice for keynote speaker. The ceremony forces together the professional and personal in a manner typical of the series, but the corporate backdrop here is particularly fraught. The British overlords from PPL are pressuring Roger Sterling and Bert Cooper to attend, a directive delivered by the increasingly beleaguered Lane Pryce. Lane’s storyline provides the episode’s most potent subtext of imperial decline and personal futility. Having worked diligently to improve Sterling Cooper’s financial health, he learns that PPL intends simply to sell the agency, rendering his efforts meaningless. This professional despair is compounded by a domestic loneliness, as his wife Rebecca (Embeth Davidtz), homesick for London, remains oblivious that Lane’s original posting was meant to be Bombay. His is a life of quiet dislocation, a subtle counterpoint to Don’s more explosive secrets.

Those secrets are, as ever, driving the plot. Don is deep into his affair with his children’s teacher, Suzanne Farrell, and uses the alleged demands of his work for Conrad Hilton to spend nights away from home. This prolonged absence grants Betty the opportunity to discover the key to his locked desk drawer, wherein she finds the damning evidence of his stolen identity: money, photographs, and the divorce decree from Anna Draper. The revelation, which occurs in near-silent, devastating scenes, is brilliantly timed to coincide with Don’s public accolade, mirroring the ironic structure of *5G*, where Don’s award ceremony leads to the arrival of his brother Adam. This repetition is not a flaw in itself; rather, it underscores the show’s central thesis that success and exposure are two sides of the same coin for Don Draper.

However, *The Color Blue* seeks to add a layer of moral complexity missing from the earlier, more brutal confrontation. Here, Don’s moment of crisis is intercut with his encounter with Suzanne’s brother, Danny Farrell (Marshall Allman). Danny, a young man plagued by epileptic seizures and an inability to hold a job, is a pathetic figure. Don, tasked with driving him to a janitorial position in Bedford, Massachusetts, sees in Danny a ghost of his own brother, Adam Whitman—the man he paid to disappear. Haunted by that past cruelty, Don chooses a different path. He gives Danny money and his business card, insisting he will “do it right” this time. It’s a moment that suggests a sliver of conscience, an attempt to break a vicious cycle, even as he actively perpetuates another through his adultery.

The episode’s B-plot, focusing on the creative process at Sterling Cooper, provides both comic relief and a potential meta-commentary on the series itself. Peggy Olson conceives a strong idea for a television commercial, but it is assigned to the struggling Paul Kinsey, who is flailing with the Western Union account. The sequence of Paul working late, fuelled by alcohol and desperation, culminates in a moment of inspiration sparked by a brief chat with the janitor, Achilles (Hal Landon Jr.). In a fit of drunken forgetfulness, he fails to jot it down, leading to his frustrated morning lament: “the faintest ink is better than the best memory.” This Chinese proverb, ironically, becomes the kernel for Peggy’s successful campaign pitch, framing telegrams as permanent records versus ephemeral phone calls. This subplot is charming but can be interpreted as a self-reflexive nod to the writers’ own challenges. By Season 3, the show had to go through a relatively uneventful historical year (1963) before the seismic shift of the Kennedy assassination. Paul’s struggle for a fresh, original idea mirrors the difficulty Matthew Weiner and his team may have faced in maintaining the show’s acclaimed quality and novelty without relying on grand historical events or repetitive character beats.

Where the episode falters, and where the strain perhaps becomes most visible, is in its attempts to inject original flavour through scenes of questionable tonal control. An effort at dark humour involving Roger Sterling’s senile mother, who mistakes his young wife Jane for his daughter Margaret, feels like a crude and overly broad jab at Roger’s May-December marriage. It lacks the subtle, character-driven irony that is the series’ hallmark.

More divisive is a scene depicting Paul Kinsey, in his late-night, booze-soaked search for inspiration, glancing at an old mock-up for a Marilyn Monroe/Jacqueline Kennedy ad. The scene implies he is inspired not for a creative breakthrough, but to engage in solitary sexual activity. This moment is likely to split audiences: some may view it as a raw, humanising detail of a flawed man’s loneliness and frustration; others may find it exploitative, gratuitous, or a cheap attempt to underscore his pathetic state. It highlights a recurring issue in later *Mad Men*: a tendency to occasionally trade nuanced observation for jarring, sensational character beats.

*The Color Blue* is a competently executed episode that suffers slightly from its overt resemblance to a superior predecessor. Its power derives from the enduring strength of its core mystery—Betty’s discovery—and from Jon Hamm’s masterful portrayal of a man trying, and largely failing, to outrun his ghosts. The episode’s willingness to show Don exercising a shred of decency towards Danny Farrell adds a welcome shade of grey. However, the more forced comedic elements and the palpable sense of narrative recycling suggest a series consciously stretching its material. This was a period of consolidation and quiet before the storm of November 1963. *The Color Blue* functions effectively as a chapter in that build-up, but it ultimately feels more like a skilful reprise of familiar notes than a wholly original composition. It proves that even the most meticulously crafted dramas can occasionally reveal the faintest ink of creative fatigue.

RATING: 7/10 (+++)

Nu wie soll man sagen:

Man unterbricht den eigentlichen Plan mit Absicht fuer gesteuerte Unabsichtlichkeiten.

body.title: It’s Over Half Done! – June 1, 2026@goldenoakfarm
body.body:
![Packaging butter crop June 2026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenoakfarm/EpQum81cbE2bxxDYeqXpydxw2HajPLznKhJidJbCnmnj7vUkQf5UyU7SAbgq5MVKzhJ.jpg)

On Monday morning I was up around 5AM and got my post up. I did a little on the bills/budget and then got the kitchen cleaned up. It had been cold again during the night so I wasn’t in a hurry to get outside.

I had forgotten to do the butter on Sunday so I got that packaged up. We only got 5.05 lbs.

I got ready for 8AM and headed to the Big garden, intending to get the Walla onions all planted and mulched before 11AM. My general helper was up and she came out too.

![Big garden - Carina mulching Wallas crop June 2026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenoakfarm/23tHGchcCw8XEV7KzwMrsnkyXdBNsXDarkYJ6A1NBcnjmG7ZnaYyTKjmZJDFqbeGS1bw4.jpg)

I had a thought it might be more efficient to plant and mulch at the same time, so I had her collecting the softer mulch in buckets and I sat down to plant both rows at the same time.

She got as much mulching done as she could and got a tray and started at the other end. By 9AM I had only planted 1 tray, but I’d also had to do all the set up and broadforking before I started.

At 10AM I had to stop and go call the shade company, but there was no answer, even after 10 rings. So I came back out and resumed planting until 10:40AM when I went to try again. Turns out I had the wrong number…sigh..

So I went back out and we finished all the mulching, and then brought 4 trays of seedlings out to the cold frame as there were now 4 spots. We got cleaned up, photo taken, notes made, and it started to rain.

I went inside and got a shower because my #2 intern was coming to take me to get window shades repaired, finally. We got in the car, and nothing. It was dead again!

So we arranged to take my #1 intern’s car and off we went. I don’t know what was going on but in the stretch of highway between my house and the city to the south, we saw 6 cars pulled over by state police, in different spots and going both ways, north and south.

![Office amaryllis flowers opening crop June 2026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenoakfarm/EpA1z3rt29KfiDJyxD89h7E1jCvn4ueEWoeWwqy3ripWxJnu6yWaBQPX3d1aZoN1KAG.jpg)

*Office amaryllis flowers are opening*

We got back home around 3:30PM and I tried to make some lunch but got distracted. I had to call AAA about the battery and they arrived just as I was going to eat.

Turns out it probably is the battery that was in the car when it was bought in 2018. And it was effectively dead. So I had to pay for a new battery. It was an expensive afternoon.

I finally got lunch/supper around 5PM and just sat as a vegetable until 7:30PM when I started pulling shades as on June 1 it was STILL cold at night, down in the 40’sF.

On Tuesday I hope to get out to the Big garden and get another row planted and mulched before my helper friend arrives at 10:30AM. He has to feed the house plants, water the remaining seedlings, and help me take down and put away the shelving in the roundtop window.

The drywall contractor messaged me he would be here at 7PM. We’ll see… if there weren’t so few contractors, I’d blow him off…

![Mini bio framed Jan 2026.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/goldenoakfarm/23xyn876JURgHHjsp757ZTvXeEEBjdDeLXWynRcLCeuqwPPsqtEtXTosSPyKZdAgWivJB.jpg)

![8KwGkL3F8Bvi7mAW_IMG_20260530_193807.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/media/snowli/images/8KwGkL3F8Bvi7mAW_IMG_20260530_193807/8KwGkL3F8Bvi7mAW_IMG_20260530_193807.webp)

</liketuimages>

火车提前到站，我赶紧给帅哥打电话。结果他不接电话。急死我了。然后旁边的姐姐也给家人语音说到了。叫谁在哪里等她了。和我这边联系不上帅哥形成鲜明的对比。一开始只是快进站了。后面就是到站了我都没有联系上他。微信和电话都轰炸了。我都无语了。

后面我下车了，他才接起电话。然后说以为我一点才到。我说不是说好在附近等我，咋关键时刻掉链子呢。我就问他几点到。他就说1点。我就挂掉了电话，先去附近找地方充电再说。这么晚居然不出来及时接驾，真的是不靠谱啊。我当时真的是生气。

走出火车站，外面就迎来一群拉客的叔叔，问去不去哪里，要不要坐车什么的。我当时已经困的奄奄一息了。感觉灵魂出窍。但是还是友情拒绝了他们。只想赶紧走出马路外面。

后续就是一点了帅哥也没到，我在附近的酒店前台那里蹭电，一边蹭电一边写帖子骂他。🤣提前到了也没能提前到家休息，我真的服完了。🙃好在是联系上了，不然不知道什么时候才能到哦。。。

---

I used to beg to my Ate Riza and Mama to give me money to use on a project, to pay and give my contribution on it, specially on small projects though doesn't required much money but its still a need to finish it and of course to show that I get involve, its same with our thesis. Our thesis is what's the hardest because there's just a lot of do and everything just required money and that's what I always lack. Its my Auntie or Mommy F who pay for my study, she's the one who invest in it but I feel like, she had no idea that it is not just all about the tuition but also the miscellaneous fees that we have to spend on. Whenever I will ask for her, she always has this doubting look, thinking if I really need it or it is a requirements. There are times that I just don't ask anything from her and would just ask my sister or my biological mom. I think I also have a lil right to ask them help no? ![1000037387.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ruffatotmeee/EpXMNTygx9hz91UhBfBhWi8hWFGXrNAhCepzfW9EZvffLJHHytkt86BkNZbARDint7L.jpg) But you know, it was Mommy F who pulled me in my mama's arms to take care of me, there's no legal adoption but they treat my like their own daughter, we're living in a same roof, so I think it is just right that they take care of me while i'm studying. But no, I am thankful but that time, during those hardest times I feel just like crying, I still have ro beg and explain to them that its for school, its not for my vices or whatever, its for school! But they are deaf to my explanation. There are times that before my Auntie would give me something, she will have this long line of blablabla and blablabla until my ears bleed before they will give me anything. Like, who will get motivated to study if they are not rhat supportive to me? Instead of supporting and encouraging me, there they are, giving their criticism and doubt as if I want those school expenses. And you know, she knows the struggles of a college students because she experience it. Hahh! It is just a good thing that my Ate Riza is there because I can sometimes ask help for her. I feel like she gave me more helps than my own mother. And this is also why I am forever grateful for her. I just wish she's still here with us to show that immense gratitude. She's the only one who I can run to whenever i'm lost and just don't know what to do anymore because of the expenses in school. I am so eager to contribute even just with money because my Auntie won't allow me to do overnight. ![1000037378.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ruffatotmeee/EoeERQf23AbCLs5WyXsH1xe3hi43k53ZAsMRwvuMfyC2CDmDoMYot3f2CFVRxWi7ARa.jpg) With my Ate Riza, I can complain with her. She didn't just support me financially but also mentally. I do it too with my real Mom too btw, that time, Ate Riza is my only ally who can understand me. I know she too is struggling, what she experience is not a joke too, imagine working at a young age, leaving home just to reach her dreams. In other words, My Ate Riza become like a role model to me. Her comforting words always help me always taking my side and i'm really grateful In that world of mine, that particular moments in my life, she become like, a light that light that already dark path i'm taking. At least walking there alone is not scary anymore thanks to Ate Riza. Thinking about it now, it is not just me who received help from Ate Riza. She helped my lil and big brother too to find job in Lipa and that's why they are living in there now. Our Ate Riza's time with us maybe is short, but she surely is a blessing and a wonderful ate/sister to us. I miss her ⊙⁠﹏⁠⊙ -- So I chose this topic--> ***Did someone support you during your hardest time? How did they help?*** -for this weeks contest. ---- Lead Image Edited in [Canva](https://canva.link/2y13tn0s11wfxhp)

body.title: Crikey We Found the Moon
body.body:
*Posted by a bloke who clearly doesn't know what he's doing*

---

So last Tuesday, me and my daughter decided to finally drag the telescope out into the backyard for the first time. It's been sitting under the bed for about six months collecting dust and judging me every time I walk past. She'd been talking about it for weeks amd we finally found it

Grabbed the scope, grabbed a jacket (not a thick enough one as it turned out), grabbed my daughter who was absolutely buzzing with excitement, and headed out the back.

---

## Setting Up in the Dark

Now here's the thing nobody tells you. Setting up a telescope in the dark is a completely different experience to setting one up in the lounge room in the afternoon. Every single knob and fitting suddenly becomes a mystery. My daughter was holding the torch and asking me questions like \

and honestly I had no good answers.

We found the moon eventually. Can't miss it really. There was a fair bit of cloud around which made it tricky, but also kind of magic. The clouds were drifting across the face of it and it looked absolutely brilliant. Like something off a movie poster.

---

## The Brilliant Idea of Sticking My Phone to the Eyepiece

Right. So I had this idea to hold my phone camera up to the telescope lens and take some snaps. My daughter thought this was genius. Spoiler: it is significantly harder than it looks.

The trick is keeping the phone perfectly aligned with the eyepiece, which is basically impossible when you're also trying not to nudge the telescope and you're cold and your daughter keeps asking if she can have a turn. I reckon I took about forty photos. Three of them were any good. Maybe.

---

## The Photos

**Photo One: The Absolute Dud**

This first one is... look... I'm including it because honesty is important. What you're looking at is basically darkness with a vague suggestion of something in the corner that might be the moon or might be my thumb. The dark circle framing around the edges is actually from the telescope eyepiece so technically that part is correct. Everything else is, well, atmospheric. My daughter laughed so hard at this one she nearly knocked the scope over.


![1000027209.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/failingforwards/23swXhgykiCKcyhXcrHXzv8ryuzieGwA5MCfL6AA1M8h4BpGGVukLnpw2cLjpQXN7Gg9E.jpg)


---

**Photo Two: Getting Warmer**

Now we're talking. Sort of. This is the moon emerging through a gap in the clouds and this one actually has a bit of character to it. It's blurry as anything and slightly overexposed but you can clearly tell it's the moon and not my thumb. Progress. The way the light blooms out from behind the cloud gives it a ghostly, dramatic look that I did not plan but will absolutely take credit for.


![1000027208.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/failingforwards/23tkfXe9k1TDbZeuKayEcRnsYYDrrGLKDEbzdq6F6kQE2aEgroVU3X7xkkKNQFJ6aELYy.jpg)

---

**Photo Three: The One That Actually Worked**

This is the shot. I don't fully understand why this one worked and the others didn't, but I had a brief moment where everything lined up, the clouds parted, the phone sat right, I held my breath, and somehow the camera grabbed the moon in all its cratered glory. You can see the dark patches across the surface and the way light and shadow play across the craters. It's not exactly professional quality. But for a bloke standing in his backyard going cross eyed trying to line up a phone with a telescope at 10pm, I'll take it.


![1000027206.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/failingforwards/23u5XKQMgAD98fV19mY5prPnemjFnjXr8QF2j1Kfmxf65fdDGD77i318NB616rW25tN3u.jpg)

---

## The Best Part

The best part wasn't any of the photos. It was my daughter grabbing my arm when the clouds cleared and she got her first proper look through the eyepiece and just went completely quiet. That kind of quiet kids do when something genuinely surprises them.

She looked for a long time. Then she looked up at the sky, then back through the scope, then at me, and said \

Yeah mate. It's actually real.

We'll be back out there next clear night. I'm getting a proper phone mount so hopefully the next batch of photos won't be quite such a mixed bag. But then again, maybe the chaos is part of the fun.

*Clear skies.*

---

*All photos taken on a phone held very unsteadily against a telescope eyepiece by someone who is very much learning as he goes.*

¡Hola, comunidad de Liketu! 👋

Hoy quiero compartir con ustedes un pedacito de lo que fue una salida súper especial en familia. Decidimos salir de la rutina y visitar un lugar que hace total honor a su nombre: Sabores Únicos.

Sie verändern die Software, aber die Hardware bleibt im Prinzip gleich.\n\nEine geistige Behinderung / strukturelle Besonderheit (wie durch die Frühgeburt) ist die Hardware. Das MRT mit 35 Jahren hat es schwarz auf weiß bewiesen: Deine Leitungsbahnen, dein Gehirn, deine Reizverarbeitung sind von Geburt an anders verdrahtet. Da gibt es keinen „Ausknopf“, keinen Defekt, den man wegreparieren kann, und erst recht keine psychische Störung. Es ist einfach die feste Struktur deines Seins.

body.title: Finding Peace in the Quiet Moments
body.body:
In today's fast-moving world, moments of silence have become increasingly rare. We often find ourselves occupied with responsibilities, notifications, deadlines, and countless distractions. Yet, some of the most meaningful experiences in life happen when we simply pause and reflect.
![lonely-1417338.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTdiFrAXrF8AEqnBt4pen55Jow6htRrJzgF1KkMhfZT3c/lonely-1417338.jpg)
Image Source/Credit: [dreamstime](https://www.dreamstime.com/royalty-free-stock-photos-lonely-image1417338)

There is something special about watching the sky transform during sunset. The warm colors, the gentle fading of daylight, and the calm atmosphere create a space where thoughts become clearer and worries seem a little lighter. These quiet moments remind us that life is not only about achieving goals but also about appreciating the journey.
Many people spend their days chasing success, but true balance comes from taking time to reconnect with ourselves. Reflection allows us to evaluate where we have been, where we are now, and where we want to go. Even a few minutes of stillness can bring a sense of clarity and gratitude.
**Why Reflection Matters**
• It helps reduce stress and mental clutter.
• It encourages gratitude for the present moment.
• It provides clarity for future decisions.
• It strengthens self-awareness and personal growth.
The beauty of a peaceful evening sky serves as a reminder that every day, regardless of its challenges, comes to an end. Tomorrow offers a new opportunity to learn, grow, and move forward.

What helps you find peace and clarity in your daily life? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.

body.title: The Diary of The Medical Mystery Miracle - Part 1, in the beginning...
body.body: >Id like to Acknowledge the following people before I even start writing. A huge Thankyou to Captain Starlight, Professor Terry Bolin and the Sydney Childrens Hospital, for never giving up on me. Thankyou also to Dr Donovan and Dr Mcgrory for your continouing ongoing medical help, but even moreso for being a listening ear I can trust and being there for emotioanl support as well.
>Thankyou also to my best Friend Emma for just being the amazing person you are,

>I would also like to acknowledge the people I have met on Bigo live, Especially everyone from The Aussie Wolves, the Trapped empire agency, And The Digital Community who cares. @trapped.chat

Lastly, thankyou _to my grandparents, Especially my Grandmother Penny (may she RIP) who showed strength and bravery and taught me how to fight through being sick. I have also decided to follow in her footsteps (everyone will_ tell you im her clone anyway) as she has also written a memoir of her very own.

>I was born on the 9th Feburary 1990, to my two parents, my Autralian born father, and my New Caledonian Mother. I was born a tiny 1.5 kilos but only 2 weeks early. Unlike my mother, I was born with fair skin and blue eyes. One of the first things my mother said when i was born was \
>I was a very sick, tiny baby at 1.5kilos born full term, i spent 3 months in the incubator in the NICU (Neo-natal intencive care unit). I was labeled as a \

and suffered severe projectile vomiting & dirrhoea and my original prognosis, for quite a while was not great at all.

\n\n

doctors and specialists had told my parents, I wouldn't make it past the age of 7 and never be able to eat or drink, i am now 36 with a child of my own. but theres way more stories to tell before we get to that point :)

>I had a squeezy bottle of my mothers breast milk in my early days. I also had a nasal gastric tube (and 5 central lines between 0-8) until the age of at least 6 or 7, as I remember starting School with it.

>My mother and father struggled to conceive me, so 16 monthls later, my younger brother came along. See our first Christmas photo together. He was 6 months old, i was around 22 months old (2 in Feb), as you can see, we definatly looked alike and were often mistaken for twins

\n\n

>In 1998 I contracted the stomach bug cryptospiridium and spent 6 weeks in hospital (it was only meant to be a 24 hour bug) with my 5th central line, and was admitted the day before my 8th birthday.

\n\n

>In my early years of life i spent more time in hopsital than i did in school but i met some amaing people, including Olivia Newton-John, Humpry bear, a few famous sports players, The Corrs & the Oriiginal wiggles. The starlight foundation and the variety club also had some pretty epic christmas parties for us sick children & our siblings.

>One of these parties every year, santa came on a boat, and the sick children and their siblings got to drive the big fishing boats, I remember my dad, being a salor getting upset that my brother and I got to drive the boat, but they wouldnt let my father who's been a sailor my entire life.

\n\n

>There is now a starlight room and a school within the Sydney Childrens Hospital, I have attached some pictures of what I could find.

\n\n
>Lookout for part two coming soon.... early out of hospital memories, these will come with laughs and more photos, dont miss the possum & double pram troubles stories.

body.title: Sapien Loop 3 - Chapter 74: The Storm Brews
body.body:
![Sapien_Loop_3_Cover_HIVE.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/spectrumecons/23wC7hkTDDpnHvZegULctqg6Mrrd9t72byH8zWkVgfNiHGiHqm7aVAeGi9PiELYyYAuVf.jpg)

## Chapter 74: The Storm Brews

-----

Early the next day. The convoy of vehicles from the West Camp had reached the location of the second site of the Great Battle. The area was scattered with the bodies of Sentray and enforcers as well as thousands of military vehicles. 

Octavius dismounted Ducky and then stood in front of the convoy of vehicles.

‘What is it now?’ demanded Chamele as she poked her head out of the lead vehicle. ‘Do you need another toilet break? Have you seen some more Sapiods you want to socialise with?’

‘It’s called showing respect,’ roared Octavius. ‘The Sapiods keep the land fertile for us.’

‘Oh woohoo,’ replied Chamele sarcastically.

‘Everyone out of your vehicles, now!’ commanded Octavius.

Within a couple of minutes, the followers and West Tribes’ guards had climbed from their vehicles.

‘Here is the tragic site where so many lives were lost,’ continued Octavius. ‘We must be respectful to the fallen Sentray, technicians, and even enforcers. These are the horrors of war. Let what you see here guide your actions.’

The followers, the guards, and even the Sentray bowed their heads in respect. A minute later, they raised their heads.

‘Once we have secured the Downs Region, we will return to bury all of you,’ said Octavius as he looked at the bodies.

‘You should also build a grand memorial with all their names on it,’ chuckled Chamele as she shook her head.

‘Yes, that would be appropriate,’ replied Octavius, nodding.

Chamele contorted her face in disbelief.

The storm clouds above the convoy of vehicles grew larger and more aggressive. The sight of all the bodies was filling Angelo with rage.

‘It might be wise if we moved on now,’ said Orcilla to Octavius. She sensed the return of the tense atmosphere that Angelo brought to the West Camp.

‘Yes, but we need to stop at the first site of the Great Battle,’ said Octavius, frowning.

‘Absolutely,’ said Chamele, smiling. ‘So many fallen followers need to be respected.’

Octavius frowned angrily at Chamele as he walked over to Ducky. The guards and the followers climbed back into their vehicles, and they soon continued their journey. The storm clouds above them grew larger. 

A short while later, they arrived at the first site of the Great Battle. Many of the destroyed vehicles had been taken as well as the bodies of the enforcers. However, the bodies of the fallen followers had been left to decay.

‘This isn’t going to sit well with Angelo,’ said Demadrian to Octavius as they came to a stop.

Octavius nodded as he dismounted Ducky again. The convoy came to a stop. Angelo, Volo, and Chamele climbed out of the lead vehicle. Angelo walked over to a mutilated and partly decaying follower. He dropped to his knees and then rubbed his hands across the body. Volo stood next to him and watched.

Angelo tilted his head back and screamed. The huge storm clouds above them rumbled angrily. Chamele’s face lit up with joy. 

The atmosphere was extremely intense and heavy. Octavius was struggling to breathe. The Sentray were becoming distressed.

‘Easy, easy!’ said Demadrian to the Sentray.

Orcilla made her way towards Angelo, but she was struggling as terror filled her body. She looked into the reflection in the window of the lead vehicle. She saw Orcille staring back at her. ‘Draw on me,’ the reflection said to her. ‘That’s why I’m here.’

Orcilla took a deep breath, and then she continued walking towards Angelo. Chamele frowned angrily as she watched her.

‘High Philosopher!’ said Orcilla in her most courageous tone. ‘They died bravely fighting the Empire. They helped us. They helped the Downs residents.’

‘That’s right,’ said Chamele. ‘She played a role in their deaths and their suffering.’

Angelo stood up and faced Orcilla.

‘We worked together towards a common enemy,’ said Orcilla. ‘And we are now!’

‘She’s an abuser and a user,’ said Chamele. ‘I liberated your true soul.’

The storm clouds above them glowed brilliantly as thunder roared around them. The Sentray howled in terror.

Angelo turned to his followers who had gathered by their vehicles. He began to chant incoherently. Chamele turned to look at Orcilla. She smiled as she could see the terror in her eyes as the rumbling from the storm clouds continued.

Angelo’s chanting lasted for over an hour. The storm clouds rumbled loudly the whole time. The atmosphere was making Octavius feel ill. Demadrian was struggling to calm the Sentray. Chamele seemed to be enjoying the feeling.

Then Angelo stopped abruptly. He gestured to Volo and then to the followers for them to get back into their vehicles.

Orcilla approached Angelo again. He walked past her, ignoring her. Chamele smiled at Orcilla as she and Angelo climbed back into the lead vehicle. 

‘I think it’s time to move on now,’ said Octavius as he looked at Demadrian, who was wrestling with the Sentray he was trying to ride.

‘The movement might calm their nerves,’ said Demadrian as thunder roared loudly above them. ‘Woah!’ he exclaimed as he wobbled on his Sentray.

‘Ducky is less bothered,’ chuckled Octavius as they began to move forward. ‘I think she might be brain-damaged as well as toothless.’

Meanwhile, in the Downs Region. Lily had untied Duffo; she, he, and the enforcer were sitting on the floor, waiting for Tiberius to send enforcers to attack them.

‘He could be dead,’ said Duffo in a slightly optimistic tone.

‘His type hangs around, trust me,’ replied Lily. ‘It’s another of his sick psychological games.’

‘I know we got off to a bad start, but maybe we could try to be friends,’ said the enforcer as he looked at Lily.

‘Would you let us use your head as a battering ram?’ asked Lily.

‘Absolutely not!’ replied the enforcer in an annoyed tone.

‘Then you have no chance of winning me over,’ replied Lily.

‘Don’t worry,’ chuckled Duffo. ‘Once out of here, I’ll crown myself Emperor, and I’ll make you head of my imperial guards.’

‘Oh goody,’ said the enforcer, rubbing his hands together.

Lily punched the enforcer in the face, knocking him out. ‘Do you really want him in charge of your fantasy security?’ she said, looking at Duffo.

‘Not really,’ replied Duffo as he looked at the enforcer lying on his back with his tongue out. ‘I thought if he was happy he would help us escape.’

‘Not a chance,’ sighed Lily. ‘We’re better off with him out of the picture.’

Tiberius was busy trying to rally the remaining enforcers. He only had managed to find a few dozen in the section of the Downs Agriculture Zone behind the Commercial Zone. Among them were only two senior enforcers.

‘Where’s the rest of you?’ asked Tiberius as he stared angrily at a senior enforcer.

‘We were hit really hard last night, Your Imperial Majesty,’ stammered the senior enforcer.

‘An army of a million enforcers reduced to just fifty,’ complained Tiberius, shaking his head.

‘Fifty-seven if we include those two hiding over there,’ said the senior enforcer as he pointed to two enforcers who were only partially invisible.

‘Complete bastards,’ growled Tiberius. ‘Vehicles! What vehicles do we have left?’

‘None, Your Imperial Majesty,’ stammered the senior enforcer.

‘You’ll all fight to the death if necessary,’ said Tiberius.

‘As you command, Your Imperial Majesty,’ replied the senior enforcer nervously.

In the resistance’s camp, spirits were quite high. Morgan was speaking in sentences, and Henders was entertaining everyone with some comical magic tricks.

‘Wow!’ called out Eugene in joy. ‘I can’t even figure out how you just did that, friend, and I’m a super sleuther.’

‘He put it behind his back,’ whispered Arthur to Louis.

Louis chuckled and nodded.

Eugene leaned forward, raised his eyebrows, and stared at both of them.

‘Hey, look over there!’ called out Yassme as she pointed to the sky.

Huge storm clouds were heading towards the Downs Region. 

‘What is that?’ asked Yassmay as she stared at the strange clouds.

‘We used to get pretty big storms in Tarrus,’ replied Louis calmly.

‘Really,’ said Vulay. ‘Clouds like that.’

‘Maybe the higher power is angry,’ said Yassme as she stared at the clouds that could be seen flashing.

‘The higher power wouldn’t do this, silly,’ said Yassmay as she poked Yassme. ‘This is something much more evil.’

‘This can be explained by science,’ said Daily, nodding. 

‘Go on, explain it then,’ said Denise as she put her hands on her hips.

‘It’s because of Sape farts,’ said Daily.

‘I’ve been sleuthing for years, friend,’ said Eugene to Daily. ‘I promise you, the problem is never Sapes or farts.’

‘We should take cover in the Sapiods’ huts,’ said Vulay. 

Everyone began packing up their belongings. The roar of thunder could now be heard as the clouds rapidly approached the Downs Region.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmeLcJ3w8HHVKAqz7nRmYMMkpzmYcKSbkWp5juWLwxNMjB/1777644101142.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmWDsXjsjP8vi7ftic7yYwqoKUBTypoHSQrnMrzDXgQpp5/1777644101190.jpg)

These small beautiful roads are full of endless joy and excitement. My in-laws' area is very beautiful to look at. There are many ponds along the roads here. As you go, you can see ponds on the right or left side of your hand. However, these dirt roads seem very pleasant to me.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUNozUy9iWjea8H62oh1Cui78vbMVdcxaiiKTiJYkVj5q/1777644152633.jpg)

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmPAHZQLNLy6vqrWj8YKwJGGjc5ezshdv85WFCq2xmpa7k/1777644152690.jpg)

Here is a small child sitting in a van. A woman is religious and hardworking. There is a market here. In this market, she usually takes the garbage that accumulates throughout the day in a van and dumps it at a specific place. Whose child is this? She takes the child with her and earns her living by doing this work every day. Seeing such a scene reminds me of working people. This scene shows me how important a mother is to her child.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmdJfrxeULSWXT4mgRPXZSDpFuxuQcZ6NpEeA1c3cphwwU/1777644152738.jpg)

But my wait here was almost too long. I am very happy to have the pleasure of spending this beautiful morning peacefully. In such a place, the sun always rises with the sweet songs of the animals.

![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmUnmHrgkVHJRZxZqqV2aaeyVMFA3UNWpskS8wVVihjKjs/1777644152767.jpg)

I am very happy and inspired to share these beautiful natural scenes with you all in the form of photography. I hope you have a great time, thank you all.

body.title: What if the safest stablecoin in the world is the one Europeans are discouraged from holding? 🧡
body.body:
What if the safest stablecoin in the world is the one Europeans are discouraged from holding? 🧡

A fascinating interview recently shed light on something most people don't know: Tether is quietly building one of the largest private gold infrastructures in the world.

Nearly 150 tonnes of physical gold.
Vaults in Switzerland. Relationships with refiners.
Supply chains. Mine royalties. Redemption infrastructure.

As a strategic reserve.

As Juan Sartori, head of special projects at Tether, put it: \

Think about that for a moment.
While most people still see stablecoins as a temporary bridge between crypto and traditional finance, Tether seems to be thinking decades ahead.

Building infrastructure first. Building trust first. Building collateral first.

The business model comes later. And that raises an uncomfortable question for Europe.

Under MiCA, large stablecoin issuers are expected to hold a significant portion of their reserves with European banks.

The objective is noble: consumer protection and financial stability.
But there is a paradox.

Banks themselves are fractional-reserve institutions.

They are leveraged. They can fail. They can experience runs. They require emergency liquidity facilities and deposit guarantees.

Gold doesn't.
Yet the most heavily collateralised stablecoin projects are effectively encouraged to become more dependent on the banking system.

As a result, Tether chose not to pursue a MiCA licence.
Because it rejected changing the structure of its reserves.

And now European citizens find themselves in an unusual situation: protected from holding a product backed by one of the largest privately held gold reserves in the world.

Whether you like Tether or not isn't really the point.

The real question is: What does financial stability actually mean?

More regulation? More banks? More intermediaries? Or stronger collateral?

As blockchain matures, these questions will become harder and harder to ignore.
Because the future of money may not be decided by who prints it.
But by what backs it. 🧡

body.title: Low Mana Battles Can Be More Confusing Than High Mana Battles! FrostGuard Warrior Shines Again
body.body:
![MINDLESS THRALL.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aliakbar2/23u5vaz2sZdgxPd5mZz5qXdNsdUaJnrY1nvaUWBvr1ZgUErvQS6YHUELJjWwURKLHwUom.png)


In Splinterlands there are some battles that are very confusing in terms of monster selection especially low mana battles where half of your total mana cost is used on the summoner and you can only select one or two monsters. This makes the battle very confusing.

In todays 14 mana battle there was a very interesting ruleset. As you can see, Collateral Damage and Counterspell were part of this battle.

Always remember to keep the battle rulesets in mind while selecting your monsters. Make your strategy according to them and position your monsters accordingly. This can improve your winning chances significantly. That is why understanding the rulesets before the battle is very important.

In this battle the Collateral Damage ruleset was active. This means all units gain the Reckless ability. Whenever your monster attacks successfully, an adjacent allied unit also takes 1 damage. This means your friendly units can also be affected by your attacks.

In simple words if your attacking monster has an allied monster next to it that allied monster can receive 1 damage after every successful attack. Because of this your lineup should not place weak monsters near the front line. Since most attacks come from the front line, a low health monster near it can be eliminated quickly.

![Screenshot 2026-06-02 112534.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aliakbar2/Eo6BGxe9V8qJBS4CsUx3vdMB3Ksip1TxaAPuxTZZseCi8YBnzpKwMaqmLQeqQws4MFe.png)

The second ruleset was Counterspell. In this ruleset all units gain Magic Reflect. This means any magic attacker receives reflected magic damage whenever it attacks.

The strategic tip here is to avoid selecting too many magic monsters. If you do select them  make sure they have enough health and protection.

Since this was a low mana battle, Collateral Damage did not have a huge impact because I only had the opportunity to select one monster. In medium and high mana battles where you can select more monsters the effect of Collateral Damage becomes much greater.

Keeping these two rulesets in mind I selected my monster carefully. I avoided magic monsters because of Counterspell and preferred a ranged attacker that had good armor and health.

![Screenshot 2026-06-02 112518.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aliakbar2/23wMcfwGTHHqdtCLC9GnCCLdMuZJE4qQh7f2eZ7DN2LXx7EhAVNw7kUfU1kjf17Q5EzTf.png)

In this 14 mana battle I selected Frost Guard Warrior with my Archon. It is a ranged attacker.

If I talk about its stats and abilities its mana cost is 8 which is more suitable for meid to high battles. However I did not have better cards available so I had to choose this card.

The good thing about this card is its strong armor and health. At level 1 it has 2 armor which continuously protects its health. It can absorb melee and ranged attacks quite well.

It also has 4 health which is enough for low mana battles. Its speed is 2 which helps it attack effectively and sometimes causes enemy attacks to miss. Since it is a ranged attacker it deals 2 ranged damage to the enemy every round.

![Screenshot 2026-06-02 112248.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/aliakbar2/23uEz3UDWoF1P4k32dkZzu4HaQ3voGuvmXtwY7CN8TieYXVozLTL4WrRR1zmYfixgcDTS.png)

On the other side my opponent also selected a ranged attacker with their Archon. However that monster only had 3 health and no armor.

Because my monster selection was better and I selected a monster with armor I achieved a great victory in this battle.

This was today's interesting battle including its rulesets, gameplay and my strategy. The strategy worked very well and helped me secure an excellent win.

What do you people think about FrostGuard Warrior? Do you have this card in your decks?? Will be glad to see your answers in the comment section.


I hope you find this post useful and informative.. If you do, please remember to reblog it so that it reaches as many people as possible and that they can benefit the most from it. Also remember to upvote which will help me financially and grow my account.

### Hello Dear Nature Observer Fam and Hive Members!
Today I am sharing the picture of this beetle. I woke up this morning and exercised for a while, then after eating breakfast, I went out for a walk on the village road and just then I saw this beetle moving on the leaves of a wild tree in the middle of green nature. At first glance, its beauty did not look that good, but when I got closer to it and did some macro photography, the beauty was worth seeing as if nature had painted this picture with its skillful hands.

When I first took the picture of this beetle, its wings were moving and sometimes it was opening and closing its wings slightly, this scene was worth seeing. The structure of this beetle and the green, black and reddish color of its mouth made this beetle look quite attractive. Nature has some beauties that we can enjoy in different ways. Today I liked the beauty of this beetle so much that I have seen this species of beetle before but could not experience its beauty so much. body.title: Success Is Bigger Than A School Name.
body.body:
Hello Community  

So this question, I think this is one that does not have a simple yes or no answer.

Does the school you attend matter?

Absolutely, Yes, it does.

But then at the same time, it doesn't matter as much as some people might  think.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPJHAXpGYpjEbjF8VqX2om1wjxgEcQLZwaRMzHnJBATDb/1780394948885.jpg)

For me, I believe a school is more than just a place where you go and learn what is in a textbook, it is also where you meet people, build friendships, create memories, and sometimes even discover opportunities that shape your future.

The people you meet alone can change the direction of your life ,some people got jobs because of classmates they met in school, some started businesses with friends they met in university, some even met their life partners there, so in that sense, the school you attend can definitely have an impact on your life beyond academics.

But when it comes to knowledge itself, I don't think the name of the school is everything, If two people study the same course seriously, put in the same effort, and continue learning after graduation, they can both become successful regardless of where they studied.

I have seen people graduate from very famous universities and still struggle, i have also seen people from schools 
that are barely talked about become extremely successful in their careers.

That is why I don't believe a school automatically determines a person's future.

A lot still depends on the individual, Personally, if I could go back in time, I don't think I would be in a hurry to change my university, Not because everything was perfect.

Far from it.

There were stressful lecturers, alot of frustrating situations, and plenty of moments where I questioned my life choices, just like many students dkd too, but looking back now, all those experiences became part of my journey, the good memories, the bad memories, the friendships, the lessons, and even the struggles all contributed to making me who I am today.

If I changed schools completely, maybe I would have had better facilities or a smoother academic experience, but I would also lose the people I met and the very experiences that shaped me, and honestly, I don't know if I would want that, one thing I have learned is that people sometimes spend too much time focusing on where they are instead of what they are doing there.

You can attend the best university in the world and still waste opportunities, you can also attend an average university and maximize every opportunity available to you.

At the end of the day, employers may notice your school at first, but after some years, what usually speaks louder is your skill, experience, character, and what you can actually do.

That is what people remember.

So yes, the school you attend matters to some extent because of the environment, the network, and the opportunities it provides.

But I don't think it matters so much that it completely decides your future, Personally, I would not go back and change where I studied.

Truthfully, the experience was not perfect, but all the same it was mine, and sometimes the value of a school is not just in their certificate that you receive at the end.

Just know that sometimes it is in the people that you met, the lessons you learned outside the classroom, and the person that you became along the way.


[Image Credit](https://unsplash.com/photos/red-apple-fruit-on-four-pyle-books-OyCl7Y4y0Bk)

The Bible teaches that when we focus on God's promises rather than our fears, our faith grows stronger. As we remember His faithfulness in the past, we gain confidence that He will guide and sustain us through present challenges. 

>“Cast all your anxiety on him because he cares for you.” (1 Peter 5:7).

The Bible also encourages believers to replace worry with prayer and thanksgiving. Instead of allowing anxious thoughts to control our minds, we are called to bring our concerns before God and rely on His wisdom. Through faith, prayer, and meditation on God's truth, we can experience His peace, which guards our hearts and minds even during difficult times.
