# Newton's law of universal gravitation

**Source:** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newton%27s_law_of_universal_gravitation

This is a general physical law derived from empirical observations by what Isaac Newton called inductive reasoning.[3] It is a part of classical mechanics and was formulated in Newton's work Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica (Latin for 'Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy' (the Principia)), first published on 5 July 1687.
The equation for universal gravitation thus takes the form:

where F is the gravitational force acting between two objects, m1 and m2 are the masses of the objects, r is the distance between the centers of mass, and G is the gravitational constant, (6.674×10−11 m3⋅kg−1⋅s−2).
The first test of Newton's law of gravitation between masses in the laboratory was the Cavendish experiment conducted by the British scientist Henry Cavendish in 1798.[4] It took place 111 years after the publication of Newton's Principia and approximately 71 years after his death.
Newton's law of gravitation resembles Coulomb's law of electrical forces, which is used to calculate the magnitude of the electrical force arising between two charged bodies. Both are inverse-square laws, where force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance between the bodies. Coulomb's law has charge in place of mass and a different constant.
Newton's law was later superseded by Albert Einstein's theory of general relativity, but the universality of the gravitational constant is intact and the law still continues to be used as an excellent approximation of the effects of gravity in most applications. Relativity is required only when there is a need for extreme accuracy, or when dealing with very strong gravitational fields, such as those found near extremely massive and dense objects, or at small distances (such as Mercury's orbit around the Sun).

Before Newton's law of gravity, there were many theories explaining gravity. Philosophers made observations about things falling down − and developed theories why they do – as early as Aristotle who thought that rocks fall to the ground because seeking the ground was an essential part of their nature.[5]
Around 1600, the scientific method began to take root. René Descartes started over with a more fundamental view, developing ideas of matter and action independent of theology. Galileo Galilei wrote about experimental measurements of falling and rolling objects. Johannes Kepler's  laws of planetary motion summarized Tycho Brahe's astronomical observations.[6]: 132 
Around 1666, Isaac Newton developed the idea that Kepler's laws must also apply to the orbit of the Moon around the Earth and then to all objects on Earth. The analysis required assuming that the gravitation force acted as if all of the mass of the Earth were concentrated at its center, an unproven conjecture at that time. His calculations of the Moon orbit time was within 16% of the known value. By 1680, new values for the diameter of the Earth improved his orbit time to within 1.6%, but more importantly Newton had found a proof of his earlier conjecture.[7]: 201 
In 1687, Newton published his Principia which combined his laws of motion with new mathematical analysis to explain Kepler's empirical results.[6]: 134  Newton's formulation was later condensed into the inverse-square law:where F is the force, m1 and m2 are the masses of the objects interacting, r is the distance between the centers of the masses and G is the gravitational constant 6.674×10−11 m3⋅kg−1⋅s−2.[8] While G is also called Newton's constant, Newton did not use this constant or formula, he only discussed proportionality.[9]: 31  That was sufficient to show that the gravity of the Earth on the Moon is the same as the gravity of the Earth on an apple: Using the values known at the time, Newton was able to verify this form of his law. The value of G was eventually measured by Henry Cavendish in 1797.[9]: 31  
Newton made quantitative analysis based on this formula around 1665, considering the period and distance of the Moon's orbit and considering the timing of objects falling on Earth. Newton did not publish these results at the time because he could not prove that the Earth's gravity acts as if all its mass were concentrated at its center. That proof took him twenty years.[10]: 13  When Newton presented Book 1 of the unpublished text in April 1686 to the Royal Society, Robert Hooke made a claim that Newton had obtained the inverse square law from him, ultimately a frivolous accusation.[7]: 204 

Newton's \

[edit]

![Image 1](https://wikimedia.org/api/rest_v1/media/math/render/svg/48f74b3b4d591ba1996c4d481f74ac3ab7e279d7)

While Newton was able to formulate his law of gravity in his monumental work, he was deeply uncomfortable with the notion of \
that his equations implied. In 1692, in his third letter to Bentley, he wrote: \

[11][12]: 26 
Newton's 1713 General Scholium in the second edition of Principia explains his model of gravity, translated in this case by Samuel Clarke:

I have explained the Phænomena  of the Heavens and the Sea, by the Force of Gravity; but the Cause of Gravity I have not yet assigned. It is a Force arising from some Cause, which reaches to the very Centers of the Sun and Planets, without any diminution of its Force: And it acts, not proportionally to the Surfaces of the Particles it acts upon, as Mechanical Causes use to do; but proportionally to the Quantity of Solid Matter: And its Action reaches every way to immense Distances, decreasing always in a duplicate ratio of the Distances. But the Cause of these Properties of Gravity, I have not yet found deducible from Phænomena: And Hypotheses I make not.[13]: 383  
The last sentence is Newton's famous[13] and highly debated[14] Latin phrase Hypotheses non fingo. In other translations it comes out \

.[15]

In modern language, the law states the following:

Every point mass attracts every single other point mass by a force acting along the line intersecting both points. The force is proportional to the two masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them:[16]

![Image 2](https://wikimedia.org/api/rest_v1/media/math/render/svg/48f74b3b4d591ba1996c4d481f74ac3ab7e279d7)

Diagram of two masses attracting one another

where

F is the force between the objects;
G is the Newtonian constant of gravitation (6.674×10−11 m3⋅kg−1⋅s−2);
m1 is the mass of the first object;
m2 is the mass of the second object;
r is the distance between the centers of the masses.

Error plot showing experimental values for G
Assuming SI units, F is measured in newtons (N), m1 and m2 in kilograms (kg), r in meters (m), and the constant G is 6.67430(15)×10−11 m3⋅kg−1⋅s−2.[8] The value of the constant G was first accurately determined from the results of the Cavendish experiment conducted by the British scientist Henry Cavendish in 1798, although Cavendish did not himself calculate a numerical value for G.[4] This experiment was also the first test of Newton's theory of gravitation between masses in the laboratory. It took place 111 years after the publication of Newton's Principia and 71 years after Newton's death, so none of Newton's calculations could use the value of G; instead he could only calculate a force relative to another force.

![Image 3](https://wikimedia.org/api/rest_v1/media/math/render/svg/93bbd7cf7fec2a08bd5b46dcff08b59de31115a3)

Bodies with spatial extent[edit]
Gravitational field strength within the Earth
Gravity field near the surface of the Earth – an object is shown accelerating toward the surface
If the bodies in question have spatial extent (as opposed to being point masses), then the gravitational force between them is calculated by summing the contributions of the notional point masses that constitute the bodies. In the limit, as the component point masses become \

, this entails integrating the force (in vector form, see below) over the extents of the two bodies.
In this way, it can be shown that an object with a spherically symmetric distribution of mass exerts the same gravitational attraction on external bodies as if all the object's mass were concentrated at a point at its center.[16] (This is not generally true for bodies that are not spherically symmetrical.)
For points inside a spherically symmetric distribution of matter, Newton's shell theorem can be used to find the gravitational force. The theorem tells us how different parts of the mass distribution affect the gravitational force measured at a point located a distance r0 from the center of the mass distribution:[17]

The portion of the mass that is located at radii r < r0 causes the same force at the radius r0 as if all of the mass enclosed within a sphere of radius r0 was concentrated at the center of the mass distribution (as noted above).
The portion of the mass that is located at radii r > r0 exerts no net gravitational force at the radius r0 from the center. That is, the individual gravitational forces exerted on a point at radius r0 by the elements of the mass outside the radius r0 cancel each other.
As a consequence, for example, within a shell of uniform thickness and density there is no net gravitational acceleration anywhere within the hollow sphere.

Gravity field surrounding Earth from a macroscopic perspective
Newton's law of universal gravitation can be written as a vector equation to account for the direction of the gravitational force as well as its magnitude. In this formula, quantities in bold represent vectors.

![Image 4](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0e/NewtonsLawOfUniversalGravitation.svg/500px-NewtonsLawOfUniversalGravitation.svg.png)

G is the gravitational constant,

It can be seen that the vector form of the equation is the same as the scalar form given earlier, except that F is now a vector quantity, and the right hand side is multiplied by the appropriate unit vector. Also, it can be seen that F12 = −F21.

The gravitational field is a vector field that describes the gravitational force that would be applied on an object in any given point in space, per unit mass. It is actually equal to the gravitational acceleration at that point.
It is a generalisation of the vector form, which becomes particularly useful if more than two objects are involved (such as a rocket between the Earth and the Moon). For two objects (e.g. object 2 is a rocket, object 1 the Earth), we simply write r instead of r12 and m instead of m2 and define the gravitational field g(r) as:

so that we can write:

This formulation is dependent on the objects causing the field. The field has the dimension of acceleration; in the SI, its unit is m/s2.
Gravitational fields are also conservative; that is, the work done by gravity from one position to another is path-independent. This has the consequence that there exists a gravitational potential field V(r) such that

![Image 5](https://wikimedia.org/api/rest_v1/media/math/render/svg/8c6ee5510ba3c7d6664775c0e76b53e72468303a)

If m1 is a point mass or the mass of a sphere with homogeneous mass distribution, the force field g(r) outside the sphere is isotropic, i.e., depends only on the distance r from the center of the sphere. In that case

As per Gauss's law, field in a symmetric body can be found by the mathematical equation:

![Image 6](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ed/Gravity_Big_G_Measurements_NIST.png/500px-Gravity_Big_G_Measurements_NIST.png)

Newton's description of gravity is sufficiently accurate for many practical purposes and is therefore widely used. Deviations from it are small when the dimensionless quantities  and  are both much less than one, where  is the gravitational potential,  is the velocity of the objects being studied, and  is the speed of light in vacuum.[19] For example, Newtonian gravity provides an accurate description of the Earth/Sun system, since

where  is the radius of the Earth's orbit around the Sun.
In situations where either dimensionless parameter is large, then general relativity must be used to describe the system. General relativity reduces to Newtonian gravity in the limit of small potential and low velocities, so Newton's law of gravitation is often said to be the low-gravity limit of general relativity.

Observations conflicting with Newton's formula[edit]
Newton's theory does not fully explain the precession of the perihelion of the orbits of the planets, especially that of Mercury, which was detected long after the life of Newton.[20] There is a 43 arcsecond per century discrepancy between the Newtonian calculation, which arises only from the gravitational attractions from the other planets, and the observed precession, made with advanced telescopes during the 19th century.
The predicted angular deflection of light rays by gravity (treated as particles travelling at the expected speed) that is calculated by using Newton's theory is only one-half of the deflection that is observed by astronomers.[citation needed] Calculations using general relativity are in much closer agreement with the astronomical observations.
In spiral galaxies, the orbiting of stars around their centers seems to strongly disobey both Newton's law of universal gravitation and general relativity. Astrophysicists, however, explain this marked phenomenon by assuming the presence of large amounts of dark matter.
Einstein's solution[edit]

The first two conflicts with observations above were explained by Einstein's theory of general relativity, in which gravitation is a manifestation of curved spacetime instead of being due to a force propagated between bodies. In Einstein's theory, energy and momentum distort spacetime in their vicinity, and other particles move in trajectories determined by the geometry of spacetime. This allowed a description of the motions of light and mass that was consistent with all available observations. In general relativity, the gravitational force is a fictitious force resulting from the curvature of spacetime, because the gravitational acceleration of a body in free fall is due to its world line being a geodesic of spacetime.

![Image 7](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/Earth-G-force.png/250px-Earth-G-force.png)

In recent years, quests for non-inverse square terms in the law of gravity have been carried out by neutron interferometry.[21]

The problem of predicting the motion of n objects subject to gravity is known as the n-body problem. The two-body problem has been completely solved, but for more bodies the solution is in general chaotic and can only be obtained numerically. The most-studied case is the three-body problem, for which several solutions for particular cases are known, for example those giving rise to the Lagrange points.[citation needed]

También me queda la incógnita, si te desaparecen, ¿qué pasa con el cuerpo?

title.body:
It's money! Test cricket is only really profitable for the likes of England, Australia and India and particularly profitable when they play each other! 

Equally the cricket boards of those countries can afford to pay their players the big bucks to keep them interested in longer format cricket, no one else can. Most high calibre players will still claim that Test cricket is the pinnacle of the sport but again, money talks so if you can make more money playing in franchise T20 leagues around the world than you can representing your country at Test cricket then that's what you'll do with your relatively short career. 

New Zealand are still a very good side! They beat India in India 3-0 they also won in South Africa. They've just not had the chance to build on that. 

A similar thing is occuring with South Africa who won the Test Championship in June last year. Their last Test match was November 2025 their next Test isn't until October 2026. It's the equivalent of PSG winning the Champions League then spending the next season playing 5-a-side football

title.body: <div class=\

> ![obraz.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeYv4VuBYWKMBw3BUjJdRnP5vagt6QDU1HZaqyeAQiaqq/obraz.png) Poniedziałek. Ponure zdjęcie na okładkę, bo ponuro się zaczęło. Spotkaniem bez sukcesu - klient chce dotację, ale się nie kwalifikuje. A potem jeszcze bardziej z grubej rury, bo szef zaprosił mnie na kaweczkę i oznajmił, że ma środki na wypłatę dla mnie do końca roku, potem - nie wiadomo. Z tej prostej przyczyny, że właśnie: ci klienci, co chcą, to się nie łapią, a na programy, które są, nie mamy klientów. Kryzys daje się odczuć i ogromne grono naszych stałych klientów nie chce słyszeć już o żadnych inwestycjach i dotacjach... A te nieliczne wnioski, które stworzyliśmy w tym roku, jakoś nie przechodzą. Tak więc jeśli nie wydarzy się cud, to od nowego roku będę bez pracy. Niezbyt to pokrzepiające. > Monday. A gloomy cover photo, because it started so gloomy. A meeting without success – the client wants a grant but doesn't qualify. And then even more embarrassing, because the boss invited me for coffee and announced he had the funds to pay me until the end of the year, after that – who knows. For the simple reason that: the clients who want it aren't getting it, and we don't have clients for the programs that are available. The crisis is making itself felt, and a huge number of our regular clients don't want to hear about any more investments or grants... And the few applications we've submitted this year just aren't getting through. So, unless a miracle happens, I'll be out of a job in the new year. Not exactly encouraging. ![obraz.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcKBW5zpDvr6FH4PvBU9TJsGu2Rj8u9GK4mmDepQM7RwX/obraz.png) Potem było bardziej wesoło i kolorowo. Wróciłam z nosem na kwintę, bo jak inaczej, ale odebrałam dzieciaczki i od razu cieplej na serduszku. Po szaleństwach tego intensywnego weekendu nie było mowy o jakichś grubszych atrakcjach na dzień dziecka. Atrakcji było naprawdę wystarczająco przez ostatnie 2 dni. Prezent mieliśmy z @sk1920 przygotowany, ale dajcie spokój - po urodzinkach dzieci mają jeszcze jakieś 8 prezentów do rozpakowania, więc bez jaj. Jak więc obejść dzień dziecka? Wystarczy podążać za dziećmi. Poszliśmy do sklepu po jajka, a dzieci same wpadły na plan: kupimy po soczku i usiądziemy na ławce! I tak oto spędziliśmy dzień dziecka: ławeczka pod blokiem, soczki, których zwykle nie kupuję, bo to sam cukier, ale hej, dziś dzień dziecka, niech mają. I cicha, sielankowa zabawa, tylko my i dzieci, przeuroczy czas. > Then things got more cheerful and colorful. I returned with my nose in the air, because what else could I do? But I picked up the kids and immediately felt a warmer heart. After the madness of that intense weekend, there was no question of any serious activities for Children's Day. There were really enough attractions for the last two days. @sk1920 and I had prepared a gift, but come on – after their birthdays, the kids still have about eight presents to unwrap, so no worries. So how do we celebrate Children's Day? Just follow the kids. We went to the store for eggs, and the kids came up with a plan: we'll buy some juice and sit on a bench! And that's how we spent Children's Day: a bench outside our apartment building, juices, which I usually don't buy because they're all sugar, but hey, it's Children's Day, let them have them. And then a quiet, idyllic party, just us and the kids – a lovely time. ![obraz.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYCp8jLqQW9k3AfkFQ4gkbVnNxHSdShGeHMnXhmoPKQv4/obraz.png) ![obraz.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZ1jyKyruR5LoFzjB36FirZzRvaPcc3JxZ2PjzQdyXNXT/obraz.png) ![obraz.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZTkiXEh3HPkBbQbL3cksVxrdesnbAr2eNjWdy8huPUmv/obraz.png) ![obraz.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWPakzq19cESRagafzA34tucnAA4gcNsq32H4usPTH252/obraz.png) ![obraz.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmY7tvq8baWa7xr3m7Uex7iFuTJd51aPpkJJ14ndzTsZkG/obraz.png) A potem - szybko do domu, z okazji dnia dziecka anulowaliśmy angielski, żeby rozpakować kolejny prezent. Gra La Cucaracha - rewelka. Pokażę kiedyś. > And then – quickly home, for Children's Day, we canceled English to unwrap another gift. The game La Cucaracha – amazing. I'll show it sometime.

>Greetings to everyone in the Lifestyle community. Today I’m stopping by to share with you a new chapter in my life. Another month has come and gone, and with it, the kids’ final month of school. It feels like just yesterday that I started with them. We barely knew each other, but you could tell it was going to be a great year. Nowadays, it’s hard for me to imagine life without my kids; I love them so much, and they’re a group of students who have made tremendous progress this school year. So I hope to enjoy these last few days of school with them and that they’ll then (finally) get their well-deserved vacation.

\n\n

>This week we have the Expo Fair, so I’m pretty excited about what’s coming up. I hope to be able to help the kids with this event, where they’ll have the chance to display, explain, and sell their work. We had classes today, but we didn’t expect the weather to turn out so bad—out of nowhere, a heavy rain started falling that left more than a few of us stuck at home. It happened to me, literally—the door to the building where I live is electric, and the power had gone out. Fortunately, a neighbor was able to help us, so I ran (almost swimming) to school. Luckily, a representative saw me and gave me a ride there.

\n\n>

>Saludos a todos en la comunidad de Lifestyle. El día de hoy me uno por aquí para compartir con ustedes un nuevo día en mi vida. En esta ocasión, otro mes ha llegado y con ello, el último mes de clases de los muchachos. Parece que fue ayer cuando comencé con ellos. Apenas nos conocíamos, pero se notaba que sería un gran año. Hoy en día se me hace difícil verme sin mis muchachitos, los quiero muchísimo y son un grupo de estudiantes que han avanzado grandemente en este año escolar. Así que espero poder disfrutar con ellos estos últimos días de clases y que luego tengan (por fin) sus merecidas vacaciones.

\n\n>

>Esta semana tenemos la Expo Feria, así que estoy bastante entusiasmada con lo que se viene. Deseo poder poder ayudar a los muchachos con este evento, dónde ellos tendrán la oportunidad de exhibir, explicar y vender su trabajo. Hoy teníamos clases, pero no contábamos con que llegara tan mal clima pues de la nada comenzó a caer una fuerte lluvia que dejó a más de uno encerrado en casa. Me pasó, incluso literalmente pues la puerta del edificio donde vivo es electrica y se nos había ido la electricidad. Afortunadamente una vecina pudo ayudarnos y así salí corriendo (casi nadando), al colegio. Por suerte que una representante me vió y me dió la cola hasta allí.

![IMG_4911.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/carminasalazarte/EppMcs9S7WKt4gnu7ztVkpK7id5bEx8KWA1pYYp5k9fPoigXQdSBGqUUBX3LrRLTngE.jpeg) ![IMG_4909.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/carminasalazarte/Ep5ngWuZyqGgBYJbKpBVk4hh69nUvNeWRxE56syShJLdsoSC6rs9fxFgvXtsQ3FGw2p.jpeg) ![IMG_4908.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/carminasalazarte/23wgMycGYzVjUrddUCdJfEYrhftSr2CsQCwW3gNQVE8gccBHk9GQsr3K1pnU4MgRTm9zU.jpeg) ![IMG_4904.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/carminasalazarte/EppLi7m3K8A5HcqQxycesdZ5zsb2RUhsRhJHtkzxhPd7pMSMMyeMXj87C1ZLwHAiZXY.jpeg)

>When I arrived, there were only three of my students there, and I was happy to see them, though at the same time I was worried that they had gotten wet. There have been a lot of viruses going around, and it’s not good for them to be getting sick so often. The kids worked really hard; you can see that in the photos. Then three more students arrived, and we worked as much as we could. We’ve been organizing the projects, averaging out the costs, and receiving all the materials. So soon we’ll have everything set up and we’ll be able to have that long-awaited day. Aside from that, today was a really nice day because I got to talk with them, hear their stories, and even enjoy the rain. Very happy. Without further ado, thank you so much for stopping by.

\n\n>

>Cuando llegue solo habían tres de mis estudiantes y yo fui feliz de verlas aunque al mismo tiempo me preocupo que se fueron mojado. Han habido muchos virus y no es bueno que ellos se esten enfermando tan frecuentemente. Los niños trabajaron arduamente, pueden verlo en las fotografías. Luego llegaron tres estudiantes más y trabajamos cuanto pudimos. Hemos estado organizando las obras, promediando los precios, recibiendo todo los materiales. Así que ya pronto tendremos el montaje y podremos tener ese día tan esperado. Aparte de ello, hoy fue un día muy bonito porque pude conversar con ellos, oir sus historias y hasta disfrutar de la lluvia. Muy feliz. Sin más que decir, muchísimas gracias por pasar por aquí.

![Thank You for stopping by_20251222_235935_0000.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/carminasalazarte/EqQRuBXhDFu9VJKoUi9KYBHi1fizexq9zibK9463CkCj7BCiSq9HsujVhAP8Vem6kgg.png)

title.body:
Con este comentario solo quiero agregar una idea —ya que lo que pienso y opino sobre este tema lo dijeron en todos los comentarios que me precedieron—

¿Hay alguna forma de impulsar o abordar más integralmente proyectos como @topcomment para estimular aún más la interacción? 

He notado en el poquísimo tiempo que llevo en el ecosistema que la propuesta de este proyecto es tan buena que merece —y necesita— delegaciones por montón. Pero debemos reconocer que la inmensa mayoría de usuarios de Hive aprecian más las recompensas y esa es una realidad que hay que aceptar.

No tanto así lo que publicamos por gusto, placer y disfrute. Pero quizás pudiera considerarse diseñar una propuesta que incentive o recompense en mayor medida las interacciones sustanciosas... Porque allí es donde está la esencia de una comunidad. 

Si los votos se consiguen en mayor medida con las publicaciones, pues hay que rediseñar el mapa estructural y buscar maneras, ideas, formas, métodos para redireccionar ese esfuerzo por la interacción. El día que dejen de percibirse recompensas por las publicaciones, muchos dejarán la plataforma. Pero si se estimulan aún más las conexiones, pienso que comenzarán a llover los comentarios progresivamente. 

Es un tema interesante que da pie a un inmenso debate. Y la oportunidad de darle un impulso evolutivo astronómico a la plataforma la tenemos al frente.

content.description:
# HiveSuite 
## Node Sync & Authentication Reload Improvements

### Hive Node Synchronisation Fixes

- fix: sync selected Hive node app-wide and prevent reload redirect issues.
- Fixed screens that were ignoring the selected Hive node configuration.  


- Connected Settings directly with HiveReactKit runtime node system:
  - Live node updates  
  - No page reload required  


- Ensured all screens consistently use the currently selected Hive node.  


### Authentication Reload Stability

- Fixed issue where browser reload redirected authenticated users back to Blogs page.  


- Added authentication hydration delay:
  - Preserves current route during session restoration  


- Improved navigation stability during page refresh and authentication recovery flows.  


- Outcome:
  - More reliable Hive node switching experience  
  - Better session persistence across reloads  
  - Improved navigation continuity for authenticated users  



Node Set From Setting
![Node Set From Setting](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sagarkothari88/23t78tyMnkRCPFFK3zY3QWXyYfNoHnK4BVa32zqLAMHtqHcpNSk7hH3g5SwUy7fNVua6X.png)

Runtime Node Sync
![Runtime Node Sync](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sagarkothari88/23t7BGiv9qro5qSR9qHx1gNxTLuJXmvR2bmDGBWJsgRVzCYcEqHeAHsU36NWYvpiDQch1.png)




---

## Unified Actions Menu & Flagging Flow

### Unified Card Actions System

- feat: unify actions menu, add iOS-only flag flow, fix tip cancel handling.
- Replaced all legacy card actions with unified 3-dot actions menu across the application.  

- Removed duplicate action menus from Snaps feeds.  

- Standardized interaction behavior across all card types.  


### Flag & Report Flow

- Added new Flag/Report functionality:
  - Hides flagged posts instantly  
  - Hides flagged authors instantly  


- Added iOS-only flagging option:
  - Ensures Apple platform compliance requirements  


- Flagged content remains hidden consistently across all supported platforms.  


### Tip Flow Fixes

- Fixed Tip cancel behavior:
  - Prevents false success messages after cancelled transactions  


- Outcome:
  - Cleaner and more consistent interaction patterns  
  - Improved moderation and reporting workflow  
  - Better reliability for transactional UI interactions  


Unified 3-Dot Actions Menu
![Unified 3-Dot Actions Menu - My Friends](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sagarkothari88/23tGa4KTfc65viqqWTnSFsehND18E5zhky2M9y8Qqq6rbeigAXxZXakJQ3kmSwBhxo85v.png)

Unified 3-Dot Actions Menu - Polls
![Unified 3-Dot Actions Menu - Polls](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sagarkothari88/23tGZw8FuPWNHKAZ6oxfgYDfDZJKJLDZ5ujasuS5hQoTDEEmdpZwyR4P3vgWK2uWijJqo.png)

Unified 3-Dot Actions Menu - Videos
![Unified 3-Dot Actions Menu - Videos](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sagarkothari88/23tGeN1MqG3oxxkndnutFs4ZxQ8R2aN5tRzc1FwtszRtTarYcF1gVjcBMGqetDoD6ubPp.png)


Flag & Report Flow
![Flag & Report Flow](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sagarkothari88/23t7AwSq4BMjuPtBCURdMXMa1VgyNcxsrxycfYB2zj3SAX267fLhefM8ocQ5NeHsSCtzR.png)


![Report Content Pop](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sagarkothari88/23swbZkLoWPf4m257L1JgNvXpty8D3ReVEaA8vhBCANWNddevsEDbZ7451f2QRJ6iQus7.png)

![Report Content Summary](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sagarkothari88/23tkfzJn9DJeUGJyjYsi5wNL2FBj8pqFDZ7TQ53BQNJTYUPoo96hwJbyFvi9tfY5zYVkF.png)


---

## Anonymous Analytics & Local Kit Linking

### Local HiveReactKit Integration

- feat: add anonymous analytics for screens and games, and link kit locally.
- Linked HiveReactKit locally into HiveSuite:
  - No package publishing required during development  


- Improved local development workflow and iteration speed.  


### Firebase Analytics Integration

- Added Firebase Analytics with:
  - Fully anonymous tracking  


- No personal user data is collected or transmitted.  


### Navigation & Game Analytics

- Added tracking for:
  - Screen navigation  
  - SPA routing transitions  


- Added analytics support for:
  - Game starts  
  - Game wins/losses  


- Analytics coverage includes:
  - 8 games  
  - Inbox  
  - Blogs  
  - Snaps  
  - Additional core application screens  


- Outcome:
  - Better application usage insights  
  - Improved visibility into feature engagement  
  - Enhanced understanding of user interaction flows without compromising privacy  


Anonymous Analytics Dashboard

![Anonymous Analytics Dashboard](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sagarkothari88/23tGTPqxJqE6aRxMB4Gvt6Z9EXmioAJr3BM6uneoTnx9DFAd7UZT1N1ZmqZL7okmVwPMc.png)



Game & Navigation Tracking

![Game & Navigation Tracking](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/sagarkothari88/23swg53Wm4kasTw8CuaSUzdUqwkcRKYzknMoFy6cS6LTqi6ZeLEsqMaS1EXLysnVn3FFu.png)



---

## Powering the Hive Ecosystem

- Continuously improving HiveSuite infrastructure, moderation systems, and developer workflows  
- Building scalable, privacy-focused, and creator-friendly experiences for the Hive community  
- Contributing towards a more stable, modern, and feature-rich Hive ecosystem  

---

- This post has been refined with the help of AI to improve readability and structure  
- The original development updates and optimized version are both available for reference

body.title: Mi lugar en el mundo cabe en una sonrisa [Esp/Eng]
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbiBrFt4jPBuzSegdMfUqC8RhzMfV2w39823w3wyhUYak/1780379584889.jpg)


***
***
Terminó el Día Internacional de la Infancia, y siento esa mezcla de cansancio profundo y gratitud infinita pues ha sido un día más pensando y trabajando para niños pero también, un día para bendecir en silencio el simple hecho de estar cerca de ellos.

Soy neuróloga pediatra y mi día a día son historias de convulsiones que llegan con la urgencia de un relámpago y diagnósticos que a veces saben a consuelo y otras a rabia contenida. Pero mi amor por la infancia no cabe solo en la consulta, lo rebosa. Esta tarde, al salir, me encontré a los hijos de mi vecina jugando en el pasillo, los vi jugando hasta casi me tumban con su pelota, pero ese incidente me supo a alegría, y eso precisamente tienen de bello los niños, que todo lo que tocan lo vuelven de colores.
***


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNmBzVenpwvkqtjX9GxM1CBGMnzoYi8x2RDhfzvDQrVGZ/1780379585281.jpg)

***


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmci1LaFfrK6o62xSC5WBFfbi9nrT7ydbdDE2AtGgvJ2tR/1780379585523.jpg)


***
Pienso también en los hijos de mis amigos, en cómo Ian, con sus nueve años y su hiperactividad bien gestionada, me corrigió la semana pasada cuando confundí un dinosaurio carnívoro con uno herbívoro, y en cómo me regala esa sonrisa desdentada cada vez que me ve, como si no hubiera nada más importante en el mundo que ese instante.

Ser neuróloga pediatra me ha enseñado la fragilidad de un sistema nervioso que aún se está construyendo, pero ser simplemente \

me ha enseñado algo más sencillo y quizá más urgente: que cada gesto cuenta: un chiste malo, un abrazo que dura un segundo de más, el truco para que se tomen la medicina sin llorar, la paciencia de escuchar por décima vez la misma historia del perro imaginario.
***


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSm6ccrAW9MRvX6Ybz5LZyaxRsXJ9wWhdgwhBTH7UQQ32/1780379585579.jpg)

***



![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRcT1jkm1utA5T5CXEKrB2SqffXJfjBzfhcr42BRoph8B/1780379873336.jpg)

***
Hoy, Día de la Infancia, muchos posts hablan de derechos, de políticas públicas, de estadísticas y promesas, pero yo quiero sumar esta verdad pequeña y enorme: los niños sanan el mundo desde lo minúsculo cuando te piden un vaso de agua y te cambian el día o te señalan una mariquita y te obligan a detenerte.

He llorado con diagnósticos devastadores, he sostenido manos de madres que no encontraban consuelo y he visto la sombra de la enfermedad atravesar salas de juegos, pero también he visto a un niño con parálisis cerebral celebrar mover un dedo como si hubiera escalado el Everest y eso, eso me ha enseñado que la infancia no es solo una etapa sino que es una resistencia, una forma de mirar el mundo que deberíamos proteger con uñas y dientes.
***



![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXKEoKRv4PLeSEx5BLjuvoX2h8AoLqNyxvGCQib1WLsv3/1780379873148.jpg)

***
Se terminó el día, pero la infancia sigue ahí, latiendo en cada casa, en cada escuela, en cada rincón donde un par de zapatos diminutos esté a punto de aprender a correr, y qué privilegio y qué bendición tan desordenada y hermosa es estar cerca de ellos.

<center>❤️</center>
<center>❤️</center>

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeQA2nwFQo3sZ1vuEqgLphQMjgqrarqB5nhtG2BYMxCbV/1780292702295.jpg)

<sub>✨**¡𝑮𝒓𝒂𝒄𝒊𝒂𝒔 𝒑𝒐𝒓 𝒍𝒆𝒆𝒓!** ✨
𝑺𝒊 𝒂ú𝒏 𝒏𝒐 𝒎𝒆 𝒄𝒐𝒏𝒐𝒄𝒆𝒔: 𝒔𝒐𝒚 **𝒏𝒆𝒖𝒓ó𝒍𝒐𝒈𝒂 𝒚 𝒆𝒔𝒄𝒓𝒊𝒕𝒐𝒓𝒂 𝒄𝒖𝒃𝒂𝒏𝒂**, 𝒎𝒂𝒅𝒓𝒆, 𝒎𝒖𝒋𝒆𝒓 𝒚 𝒔𝒐ñ𝒂𝒅𝒐𝒓𝒂 𝒒𝒖𝒆 𝒆𝒏𝒄𝒐𝒏𝒕𝒓ó 𝒆𝒏 𝑯𝒊𝒗𝒆 𝒖𝒏 𝒉𝒆𝒓𝒎𝒐𝒔𝒐 𝒆𝒔𝒑𝒂𝒄𝒊𝒐 𝒑𝒂𝒓𝒂 𝒗𝒐𝒍𝒂𝒓.

![cinti 800x20 - copia.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWKGeMBmj14VqKn8xBrmpFM3RYVcgmAXX6bGnGwuNWEnc/cinti%20800x20%20-%20copia.jpg) 

### <center>ENGLISH VERSION</center>

![cinti 800x20 - copia.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWKGeMBmj14VqKn8xBrmpFM3RYVcgmAXX6bGnGwuNWEnc/cinti%20800x20%20-%20copia.jpg) 


## <center> My place in the world fits inside a smile</center>




![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNaEaRqPb83gosD772UhdCrxn3EXbZiEqVbMwdcgPywNv/1780379585092.jpg)



***
***



The International Day of Childhood has ended, and I feel that mix of deep tiredness and infinite gratitude because it has been another day thinking and working for children but also a day to silently bless the simple fact of being close to them.

I am a pediatric neurologist and my daily life consists of stories of seizures that arrive with the urgency of lightning and diagnoses that sometimes taste like comfort and other times like contained rage. But my love for childhood does not fit only in the office, it overflows. This afternoon, as I was leaving, I came across my neighbor's children playing in the hallway, I saw them playing until they almost knocked me over with their ball, but that incident tasted like joy to me, and that is precisely the beautiful thing about children, that everything they touch turns into colors.
***


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNmBzVenpwvkqtjX9GxM1CBGMnzoYi8x2RDhfzvDQrVGZ/1780379585281.jpg)

***


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmci1LaFfrK6o62xSC5WBFfbi9nrT7ydbdDE2AtGgvJ2tR/1780379585523.jpg)


***
I also think about my friends' children, about how Ian, with his nine years and his well-managed hyperactivity, corrected me last week when I confused a carnivorous dinosaur with a herbivorous one, and about how he gives me that toothless smile every time he sees me, as if nothing else in the world mattered more than that moment.

Being a pediatric neurologist has taught me the fragility of a nervous system that is still being built, but simply being \

has taught me something simpler and perhaps more urgent: that every gesture counts: a bad joke, a hug that lasts one second too long, the trick to get them to take their medicine without crying, the patience to listen for the tenth time to the same story about the imaginary dog.
***


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSm6ccrAW9MRvX6Ybz5LZyaxRsXJ9wWhdgwhBTH7UQQ32/1780379585579.jpg)


***


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRcT1jkm1utA5T5CXEKrB2SqffXJfjBzfhcr42BRoph8B/1780379873336.jpg)


***
Today, on Childhood Day, many posts talk about rights, public policies, statistics and promises, but I want to add this small and enormous truth: children heal the world from the smallest things when they ask you for a glass of water and change your day, or when they point to a ladybug and force you to stop.

I have cried over devastating diagnoses, I have held the hands of mothers who could not find comfort, and I have seen the shadow of illness cross through playrooms, but I have also seen a child with cerebral palsy celebrate moving one finger as if he had climbed Everest, and that, that has taught me that childhood is not just a stage but a resistance, a way of looking at the world that we should protect tooth and nail.
***


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXKEoKRv4PLeSEx5BLjuvoX2h8AoLqNyxvGCQib1WLsv3/1780379873148.jpg)


***
The day is over, but childhood is still there, beating in every home, in every school, in every corner where a pair of tiny shoes is about to learn to run, and what a privilege and what a messy and beautiful blessing it is to be close to them.

<center>❤️</center>
<center>❤️</center>

body.title: The Celtic Soul Rebellion of Dexys Midnight Runners in '82
body.body: ### Hello hello silver bloggers, music lovers and Hello hivers! One of my favourite days because it means a post on Hive will be written by me, and I get to hear other music that Hiveians enjoy. Well for the select band that participate in ttt anyway!

/> We are going back to my Silver Chronicles post of a few weeks ago [My Soundtrack for the 80s my favourite decade](https://peakd.com/hive-106316/@tengolotodo/my-soundtrack-for-the-80s) Quite a self-explanatory title and it is my inspiration for the next few posts on ttt! The year is now 1982 and we are diving into a band that underwent a dramatic and successful reinvention in that year!... ### 3 tunes from 1982 by Dexys Midnight Runners * * * It is Tuesday and that of course means that it's #ttt or #threetunetuesday and so it's time to share some tunes with you! * * * @ablaze started #ttt **262** weeks ago! Go check out what it is all about on his latest post [Ireland's Top 30 Songs of all Time (1, 2, 3) for Three Tune Tuesday - Week 261 - win some HBI](https://peakd.com/hive-193816/@ablaze/ireland-s-top-30-songs-of-all-time-1-2-3-for-three-tune-tuesday-week-261-win-some-hbi) **_Do go support @ablaze as without him we would not have this mental fun musical activity that you can win HSBI from! I am happy to be one of the SIX sponsors and it is kinda fun checking out music from all over this global village of ours!_** He has just released some winners posts, so go support those posts, he gets no support from any whales or even curation trails for these posts that he does. 262 weeks is an incredible amount of time, and I for one love that he runs this, and I appreciate the time and dedication that he puts in, when he could be doing something else. ### Long live #ttt 😁🎼 and #threetunetuesday

/>

### The Band - Dexys Midnight Runners

Few bands underwent a more dramatic and successful reinvention that year than Kevin Rowland’s Dexys Midnight Runners.

After the brassy, northern soul-infused success of their 1980 debut Searching for the Young Soul Rebels, lead singer Rowland completely dismantled and rebuilt the band.

Out went the brass section...  
Out went the slicked-back hair...  
Out went the leather jackets.

In came fiddles...  
In came banjos...  
In came accordion...  
In came a look that was part Gypsy traveller, part vintage dungaree-wearing folk hero.

The result was the masterpiece album **Too-Rye-Ay**, a beautiful collision of classic soul passion and traditional Irish folk music—a genre they proudly dubbed \
Here are three awesome tunes from Dexys during that magical 1982 run.

/> ### Tune 1 - Dexys Midnight Runners - The Celtic Soul Brothers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8LNy52B1V-4 This was the opening track of the **Too-Rye-Ay** album and the lead single that introduced the world to the band's brand new sound. It’s an upbeat, joyous anthem driven by frantic fiddles and Kevin Rowland's unmistakable, passionate vocal delivery. It serves as a statement of intent for the new collective, inviting everyone to join their musical rebellion.

/> ### Tune 2 - Dexys Midnight Runners - Come On Eileen https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6BODDyZRF6A You can’t talk about 1982 without this cracker of an ear worm! > Come on, Eileen, oh I swear (what he means) > At this moment, you mean everything > You in that dress, my thoughts I confess > Verge on dirty, ah, come on, Eileen It knocked off every other hit to become the biggest-selling single of the year in the UK and even conquered the US Billboard charts. From the slow teasing fiddle intro to the famous acceleration section that gets every pub and wedding dancefloor moving to this day, it is a flawless pop masterpiece wrapped in Celtic folk clothing.

/> ### Tune 3 - Dexys Midnight Runners - Jackie Wilson Said (I'm in Heaven When You Smile) https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A1vAQM4W02E A brilliant cover of the classic Van Morrison track and it was released as a single in the autumn of '82. Dexys injected it with an absolute burst of energy, blending the brass they were known for with their new string-heavy sound. Fun fact for UK telly fans ~ when they performed this on Top of the Pops, the BBC graphics department famously got confused and projected a giant picture of darts player Jocky Wilson behind the band instead of soul singer Jackie Wilson! Jocky Wilson was a wee character and hailed from the Scottish town of Kirkcaldy which is where I live, hence the lead image of our newly installed heart on the Esplanade!

/> ### So there you have it 3 songs released in 1982 from Dexys Midnight Runners this week with my [80s Soundtrack post](https://peakd.com/hive-106316/@tengolotodo/my-soundtrack-for-the-80s) as the inspiration! Which was your favourite tune? Or have you never heard of them?

/>

**_Note_**_: The 3 YouTube videos that I have shared are not owned by me, I am simply spreading great music on Hive._

I wish that you all have a brilliant happy fun and terrific Tuesday until we meet again enjoy your tunes 🎶🎵🎶

### Thanks for visiting!

The images and ramblings are from me, with some assistance from gemini on the verbage and the lead image, the mad Scotsman TengoLoTodo unless otherwise stated.

@tengolotodo June 2nd 2026

🦉 The white wagtail (Motacilla alba) > - Motacilla lat .: mōto, mōtare move continuously, -cilla tail (cilla like a tail - only in ornithology, erroneous established name) > - alba (lat.) white
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbHUGUo6WBLT4dN6bVmwjTJiy1bLwPAUj9i8QGwvUXL9B/dsc_5770.jpg)
We're all used to seeing these slender, fleet-footed birds scurrying along sidewalks. However, they also live in the wild. They're most often spotted near rivers and lakes. Apparently, water bodies are essential for the insects these birds feed on.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcWrdgFh5ZNS6xDfWHFCT1Ba2p2DzqMkqbbnd1hmSU1F6/dsc_5850.jpg)
In September (around mid- to late September), you can observe them migrating to warmer climates. I've even observed these birds in company with other birds, such as yellow wagtails (their close relatives) and even some species of sandpipers.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUTyQXo1ESGkJSZjsJ7C9Fq8zVcYJoQomvoJGF4a6JKce/dsc_5766.jpg)

Hello beautiful people in this community. Welcome back and happy new month to us all. It is actually a amazing thing to see that we have entered into the sixth month of the year. It was as if we started the year yesterday and today we

Guys this weekend Week 220:- Episode 01. And we have this topic that says - THE SCHOOL YOU GO TO. I am he type that believe so much in the influence of the environment we find ourselves. There this street in the place I live where people go to every night to drink and smoke. Some of go there to get women of all types to take home for the night. The reason why I brought that story up is because every child that is born and raised there has that lifestyle already unless there is any kind of intervention from God. That environment affect the children so bad that most of them becomes very wild and live a wild lifestyle.


Does the school you go to matter so much? 

From what I said above you will notice that it does matter. The environment f that school. The type of students are will mingle with and the kind of teachers you will see there has a way of shaping your life. There is this saying that says - Show me your friend and I will tell you who you are. Your friends has a great influence on you. A first you may not even like their character or lifestyle, but it will soon rob on you without your knowledge. You will use discover that you are already behaving like them.


 If you can learn the same thing in a different school, does it really matter where you learned it? 

You can't learn this same exact lessons at another school because you won't be meeting the same people there. The environment is different so the lessons and lifestyle will be very different. 

Different environment and different lifestyle. If you check anyone that went to a government school and the child that went to a private school, their lifestyle is very different. What the child will be taught is private and what the other child will be taught in government school is the same lessons but because of the environment and the people involved, the assimilation is different. The understanding is different and also the output from the life will also be different. So you will discover that a child that went to a good private school can sit for waec confidently and write at the end come out with good grade, while the child from government school can not do that. There will always be oxpo for them to pass without that they can't write on their own except for some exceptional students.


If you could go back in time, will you change your university or college and school somewhere else?

Hmmm! If I was given the opportunity to change school I would have gone to a very good private school that will help me become a better person. Maybe I would have gone to kings and queens school. body.title: Джес - антистрес
body.body: От так і склалася доля викинутої кимось молоденької собачки: із бездомної бродяжки вона перетворюється в найулюбленішу собаку сім'ї. І вже всім зрозуміло, що її ніхто нікому не віддасть, хоча у планах було прилаштування собачки в новий дім після стерилізації. Але чим довше Джес у нас, тим більше вимог до потенціальних нових власників. А в нашій сільській місцевості ставити такі вимоги - це означає відрізати надію на прилаштування, бо тут собака не друг сім'ї (на превеликий жаль), а - \

, і т.д., і т.п....
Чесно - я вже мабуть старію, бо переконувати суспільство у жахливості такого ставлення до тварин просто втомилася. 
Он у сусіда пес - зачинений тижнями у вольєрі. Іноді на ніч його відпускають на самовигул. То або собаки порвуть, або кліщів нахапається, або наїсться сміття. 
У родичів песик недавно помер, просидівши все своє життя на метровому ланцюгу. Ще в одних молодих сусідів сучечка сидить на такому ж метровому ланцюгу, її пічкають уколами від тічки, бо приводила по семеро цуценят двічі на рік. Але стерилізувати категорично не йдуть, а про ланцюг зняти  то взагалі нема мови: городи потопче...
Тому тішуся нашому рішенню залишити Джес у нас. І бачу, як розквітає ця колись залякана і нещасна собака. Та що там казати, - мені тепер дуже часто саме вона допомагає в скрутну хвилину триматися на цьому світі.
Ех, всім би бездомним таку долю. А ще краще, щоб їх взагалі не було. Та - я не доживу до такого рівня свідомості українців...😒

body.title: Why Some People Keep Making The Same Mistakes
body.body:
> If you do not know why something happened, then you may not even know how to prevent it from happening again, and you may not be able to solve the problem. Some people often say that mistakes are important part of life. Well, to an extent, this may be true, because they can teach valuable lessons, and help one to grow. However, what is bad is not that you made mistake, but that you keep repeating the same mistake over and again without learning anything from it. A lot of people are stuck in the same cycle for years simply because they fail to learn from their experiences. Here, was shall take a look at why some people keep making the same mistake again and again, so you will know how to avoid it.
![pexels-mart-production-7699422.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaH6PLKP4aofWQVQmiJRi8D25JcMqLk3FVcr4KePQoxVj/pexels-mart-production-7699422.jpg)
Image from [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/man-in-black-sweater-sitting-on-bed-7699422)
There was this guy I knew back then, who would always be short of money before the end of the month. Each time, he would blame his salary, or the economy, or the responsibilities that he have. However, he never truly took time to examine and observe that he spends impulsively on the things that he did not need, and that was part of what eats deep into his pocket. Months after month, the same cycle kept repeating until he finally got to tell himself the truth that he was the source of his own financial problems. It was then that he reviewed his spendings and made a budget. For the first time, he did not run out of money before the end of the month. He realised that his problem was not even lack of money, but misappropriation of money. One reasons that cause people to repeat the same mistake over and again is lack of self-awareness. They never take out time to reflect on the decisions they make, on their habits, on their actions, and even on their choices. When they experience problems or when they make mistakes, they will be too quick to blame other people, or even on the situation itself, without taking time to reflect about their own role in the whole thing. This will make them to miss important lessons that they would have learnt, thereby having the tendency to repeat the same mistake again and again. If someone cannot learn from what has happened, then it might keep happening again. Another reason why some people keep making the same mistake is pride. Pride is one thing that makes it difficult for someone to admit when they are wrong. Instead of taking corrections when they make mistakes, they will either become defensive to justify themselves for their actions, or they trade blames. Or they may even give excuses when things do not work out well, instead of taking corrections. What they fail to understand is that if they fail to acknowledge a mistake and take responsibilities for it, they may not learn from it. Growth starts when someone is humble enough to recognise their weaknesses, and then take responsibilities for their actions. The third reason why some people keep making the same mistake is fear of change. There are times when people would know exactly where they are getting it wrong, but the fear of uncertainty may make them not to change it. Change often requires discipline, commitment, efforts, and risks to be taken. It may also mean that you will change routines, improve your attitude, or make some very daring decisions. Because of the fact that these changes can be uncomfortable, some people may choose to continue with what they are familiar with even when it is already a disadvantage to them. This is what happens when you allow fear to make you not to take steps.
![pexels-norma-mortenson-7301673.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcKVL1zhdHt2NpFNN2NNGMU6t8xLjqhXJRntyjWLBNUUW/pexels-norma-mortenson-7301673.jpg)
Image from [Pexels](https://www.pexels.com/photo/a-man-wearing-a-red-sweater-covering-his-face-with-his-hands-7301673)
Why some people repeat the same mistake is that they tend to focus on what is happening and not on why it is happening. That is, focusing on the symptoms and not on the root cause. For example, a student who keeps failing but keeps blaming the difficult questions, or the exam format, while they did not take note of their poor study habits. Or maybe someone who is struggling financially may be blaming the economy or even the salary, but they may not have taken time to look at the way they spend money and their budget. Until you have addressed the root cause of a problem, the problem may return again. The last reason that we will look at here why some people make the same mistake is that that they ignore advice and corrections. By listening to wise counsel, it will make you to see what the problem is, and make you to see the blind spot that you may not have taken notice of. But the people who reject feedbacks have the tendency of repeating the same mistakes again. You have to learn to be teachable to be able to grow. ***Thanks for reading***
Peace on y'all

body.title: The Disadvantage of Being Far from Big Banks
body.body: > Happy Tuesday Hivers! ## We live in a rural area in Leyte where there are no nearby major banks. The closest banks in our area are only rural banks. Although the next municipality has other banks like BDO and Landbank, most of the bigger banking institutions can only be found in the city. Last Monday, I received my final pay from my employer. It was delayed since it should have been released one month after the effectivity of my resignation, but it only came after six months. Still, I’m grateful that it was finally released. Since my last pay wasn’t that large, I requested that my sibling pick it up since I am in Leyte. After receiving the check, my sibling tried to deposit it into my account, but the bank said it couldn’t be deposited and must be encashed instead. Because of this, I decided to send it to Leyte instead, as traveling to Cebu would cost me a lot. Luckily, the child of my cousin happened to be visiting Leyte, so I was able to send it with them. ## ![IMG_4268.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kellyane/23tvifrNW7kHVdApVfT1nsM4Dj5NQqjy8q2w3f3P6NeQnhjqQ7W2WMAbSDE97DMnS3Rya.jpeg) ## Since the bank where the check was issued is not available near our area, I still needed to travel to Ormoc because in Leyte, there are only two branches located in Ormoc City and Tacloban. Since Ormoc is closer, I decided to go there instead. I also had to spend around ₱300 for fare and travel for about 2.5 hours just to have it encashed. This is one of the disadvantages of living far from the city, banks and malls are not easily accessible. However, living in a rural area also has its own charm, especially the peaceful environment and the nice view every day. In the end, despite the expense and long travel, it was all worth it because I finally received my last pay, which I had been waiting for. ##

>

Thank you for reading and see you on my next blog. Cheers!

Saludos amigo! Un placer. Tanto gusto encontrarme con tu opinión. 

Porque este puntito que tocas aquí lo disfruto como no tienes idea. Creo que aún en Hive no se ha hecho un abordaje integral a la interacción. El que aportemos más comentando que publicando es la clave para que el ecosistema tenga muchísimo mas sentido. No se hasta que punto se puede abordar ese aspecto pero en lo personal creo que es la columna vertebral de la plataforma: los comentarios. 

Allí se conoce a la persona porque en el artículo se conoce la marca, la redacción, la generalidad y el argumento. Pero el pensamiento crítico y la verdadera valoración se encuentras es aquí, comentando. 

Es cierto que los posts son los que hacen que el contenido fluya, pero de algún modo hay que ingeniarse algo para revertir ese chip y enfocarse en la interacción humana, en crear vínculos, en comprometerse con el contenido más que con los votos. 

Hasta ahora la mecánica de Hive apunta indicando que el valor de tu publicación lo determina los votos que obtengas por post. Pero soy de los que piensa que hilos de comentarios con sustancia, calidad, que aporten y generen un ambiente sabroso así como el de este artículo, pueden hacer que generemos más recompensas que los artículos en si.

Soy de los que cree que los comentarios tienen más valor añadido que los ingresos por los votos.

Una realidad explicada suavemente pero con una claridad absoluta, un análisis impecable al final yo lo llamo muchas veces señor tiempo, pero siempre habrá personas que sacrifiquen un poco de él para sentarse a leer y comentar. También el devolver un poco de apoyo a los que toman un momento para leerte y dejar un mensaje debería ser prioritario, tomado muy en cuenta. Yo a veces no entiendo perfectamente un texto así que tengo que volver a empezar. 

Pero sin duda que importante es que te dejen un mensaje, ya los votos gordos déjenselos que los den  las ballenas ja, ja. 

Se que yo le doy rebloguear a muchos y dicen que eso es criticable, pero así yo recuerdo pasar por algún post que me intereso con más calma a lo largo del día. Muchas veces no quiero perderme ninguno. Mantener esta comunicación a veces es agotador y motivante. 

Las bajas económicas desmotivan mucho pero allí radica la diferencia entre el que le pone corazón al escribir, el que se toma su tiempo así tenga que madrugar más, el que se preocupa porque no ha escrito. Tienes razón no se debe confundir a votos o  seguidores con verdaderos lectores, esos que reciben de ti algún mensaje que les hace falta, que se detienen a indicartelo y hasta los que te indican algún fallo. 

Resultaría insultante que ellos pensaran a no esa es una viejita (o) que no tiene más nada que hacer y puede tomarse el tiempo que quiera para contestar. Cuando es al contrario y muy a pesar de que nos mantenemos activos, sabemos que se nos acorta el tiempo pero que vale la pena hacer sonreír al que esta detrás de esta pantalla. 

Al igual que @emiliorios nos dejas un gran tema, ya veremos cuantos se detienen a dejar su parecer. Yo con el viaje no he podido pasar por la comunidad solo por encima y mirando a @issymarie2. Y es que me da hasta pena porque cuando escribo por allá por lo general es grande el voto y se supone que estoy de vacaciones retratando fotográficamente mi andar y manteniendo mi pequeño  apoyo a las niñas estudiosas del profesor @lanzjoseg en la comunidad de topfamily. 

Mis deseos es que tengas más de 50 comentarios y tú lo has retratado perfectamente realista con los datos en la mano. No podía dejar de sentarme un rato antes de salir a mi recorrido y apriete el calor. Un gran abrazo.

body.body:
Por mi parte siempre leo o reviso antes de dar un voto, y digo reviso porque en muchas ocasiones se trata de fotografías y poco texto. Si no comento siempre es porque no tengo nada importante para compartir o porque otro se me adelantó y no creo necesario repetirme con la misma idea. Pero sí he notado eso de que una publicación obtiene varios votos y sin embargo no tiene visualizaciones o tiene sólo una pocas de ellas.
No sé si ese fenómeno comentado sea debido a que no siempre se registran todas las visualizaciones, o más bien se deba a que mucha gente sólo busca votar para obtener alguna ganancia sin haber leído o revisado el contenido.
Tal como expresa el autor es posible sea esto último debido a la misma característica de la plataforma de premiar los primeros votos y no tanto las contribuciomes de otra índole.
Es posible se trate de un efecto avalancha y cuando notan que algo es votado lo consideran de calidad sin haber revisado y a su vez votan en busca de un premio.
Pero como un mismo contenido puede ser valioso e interesante para uno y valer poco para otro con independencia de la calidad de su elaboración, considero que todos debían leer, analizar, o revisar antes de dar su voto, porque además así es como único uno aprende de lo expuesto por el autor del artículo y eso también tiene mucho valor en sí mismo.

body.title: ‎🌱 A Positive Mind Can Change Everything
body.body:
Hi Hive,
‎
‎Over the years, I have noticed something about life as the way we think has so much to do with how we experience it. When my mind is filled with hope and positive thoughts, I tend to handle challenges better. But when I allow negative thoughts to take over, even little problems can feel overwhelming.

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmZfrTQVuGL2SostC9CzzkuYndpUyt224Fi6aBqLVUExNE/IMG_20260531_164413_380.jpg 

‎
‎I was not always aware of this. There was a period in my life when I focused too much on what was going wrong. If one thing didn't work out, I would spend days thinking about it. I worried about the future, compared myself to others, and often felt stuck. Looking back now, I realize that many of those negative thoughts were making my situation feel worse than it actually was.
‎
‎Things started changing when I made a conscious effort to protect my mindset. Instead of dwelling on every setback, I tried to focus on the lessons I could learn from them. Rather than complaining about what I didn't have, I started appreciating the things I already had. It wasn't an overnight transformation, but small by small, I started to feel lighter and more optimistic.
‎
‎One thing I have learned is that taking care of your mind is just as important as taking care of your physical health. We pay attention to what we eat because it affects our bodies, but we should also pay attention to what we feed our minds. The people we spend time with, the content we consume, and the conversations we engage in all have an impact on our thoughts.
‎
‎Of course, positive thinking doesn't mean pretending that life is perfect. We all face difficult or tough moments. There are days when things don't go as planned and situations that as well test our patience. However, having a positive mindset helps us face those moments without completely losing hope.
‎
‎I have seen how a simple change in perspective can make a big difference. When you believe that better days are ahead, you're more likely to keep pushing forward. You become more open to opportunities when you focus on possibilities instead of limitations.
‎
‎For me, one of the best habits I have developed is gratitude. No matter how difficult a day may be, I try to find something to be thankful for. It reminds me that even during tough times, there is still something good worth appreciating.
‎
‎At the end of the day, our thoughts shape our attitude, and our attitude influences our actions. The more positive your thoughts are, the more positive your life can become. Take care of your mind, nurture it with good things, and you may be surprised by how much beauty starts showing up in your life. 🌿✨
‎
‎![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmYaWnApEziAtLL5Zwv3ZNbDjRfSfG6h5njgTrpyasnE6y/1775569275821.png)
‎
‎

body.title: The Cat in the Window [ENG🇬🇧|ESP🇻🇪]
body.body: > Hello everyone. On this occasion, I am presenting several photos of a black cat I found in a window. I was walking down a street that I frequent often in my city when I suddenly noticed him watching me from the window. He was extremely calm, and he stayed that way even as I approached to take a few shots. # Even when I got closer to pet him, he remained still, just observing me. I had never seen this cat around here before, and I was impressed by how large and healthy he looked. It is a very well-kept feline without a doubt. The light from the street allowed me to capture his features and the texture of his fur clearly. # I focused the images on his expression and his direct gaze. The window frame provided a natural boundary for the photos, highlighting the cat as the central element. It was a brief and quiet interaction, but his calm behavior made it easy to document the moment from a short distance. # I decided to share these photos because of the specific presence of this cat in that spot. Black cats often have a very solid visual impact, and this one stood out due to his size and posture. It was an interesting find during a routine walk, and I managed to get the shots before continuing on my way. # I hope you find these captures of this feline interesting. Without anything more to add, I bid farewell. Stay tuned for future posts! Until next time!

> Hola a Todos. En esta oportunidad les presento varias fotos de un gato negro que me encontré en una ventana. Caminaba por una calle que suelo transitar mucho en mi ciudad cuando de pronto lo noté observándome desde la ventana. Estaba sumamente tranquilo, e incluso cuando me acerqué para tomarle fotos, se quedó así, solo mirándome. # Incluso cuando me acerqué a acariciarlo, se mantuvo quieto, simplemente observándome. Jamás había visto a este gato por aquí y me impresionó lo grande y saludable que se veía. Es un felino muy bien cuidado sin lugar a dudas. La luz de la calle me permitió captar sus rasgos y la textura de su pelaje con claridad. # Enfoqué las imágenes en su expresión y su mirada directa. El marco de la ventana sirvió como un límite natural para las fotos, resaltando al gato como el elemento central. Fue una interacción breve y silenciosa, pero su comportamiento calmado facilitó documentar el momento desde una corta distancia. # Decidí compartir estas fotos por la presencia específica de este gato en ese lugar. Los gatos negros suelen tener un impacto visual muy sólido, y este destacaba por su tamaño y su postura. Fue un hallazgo interesante durante una caminata rutinaria y logré las tomas antes de seguir mi camino. # Espero que estas capturas de este felino les resulten interesantes. Sin más que agregar me despido, estén atentos a los próximos post. ¡Hasta la Próxima! ------ ---- |

body.title: Television Review: Wee Small Hours (Mad Men, S3x09, 2009)
body.body:
![(source:tmdb.oreg)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/gaRTvTPn3U1czXlTpZAytUZwt6b.jpg)


**Wee Small Hours (S3x09)**

Airdate: 11 October 2009

Written by: Dahwi Waller & Matthew Weiner
Directed by: Scott Hornbacher

Running Time: 48 minutes


As the third season of *Mad Men* approaches its conclusion, the episodes begin to exhibit a marked variance in tone and mood, at least where the series’ protagonist, Don Draper, is concerned. The illusion of the all-powerful, invulnerable Don—already fractured by the forceful signing of his contract in [*Seven Twenty-Three*](https://peakd.com/hive-166847/@drax/television-review-seven-twenty-three-mad-men-s3x07-2009)—had been temporarily supplanted by the fantasy of a blissful, romanticised life during the Roman holiday of [*Souvenir*](https://peakd.com/hive-166847/@drax/television-review-souvenir-mad-men-s3x08-2009). That fantasy, notably facilitated by the benevolent patronage of Conrad Hilton, presented Hilton as a saviour, mentor, and the long-sought paternal role model Don craved. *Wee Small Hours*, the ninth episode, exists to shatter that particular illusion with a quiet, cumulative force, initiating a phase of profound professional and personal erosion that would define the remainder of the season. Directed by Scott Hornbacher, a producer making his directorial debut after working with Matthew Weiner on *The Sopranos*, the episode adopts a languid, nocturnal pace that perfectly mirrors its protagonist’s insomnia and restless moral drift.

One of the episode’s most structurally ambitious features is its framing within an unusually expansive historical period. It bookends its narrative with two pivotal events from the American civil rights movement: Martin Luther King’s March on Washington on 28 August 1963, and the funeral for the victims of the Birmingham church bombings on 18 September 1963. This three-week span provides a subtle, persistent hum of societal tension against which the characters’ personal crises play out, often in stark, unflattering contrast. Hornbacher’s direction handles this context with admirable restraint, allowing history to permeate the edges of the frame rather than dominate it, an approach that would be less successfully applied to the series’ more heavy-handed, slightly anachronistic references to the burgeoning Vietnam conflict.

The central professional relationship of the season, that between Don and Conrad Hilton, here reveals its corrosive underbelly. After bestowing perks and a veneer of heightened importance upon Don, Hilton emerges as the archetypal demanding, capricious client. He sees nothing untoward in pestering Don with phone calls every four hours, day and night, operating on a global tycoon’s schedule that acknowledges no human need for rest. The result is a Don Draper pushed to exhaustion, plagued by insomnia, and reverting to a familiar coping mechanism: aimless nocturnal driving. It is during one such insomniac pilgrimage that he encounters Suzanne Farrell, his children’s teacher, running along the roadside. The ensuing conversation in his car, charged with his obvious attraction, brilliantly displays subdued erotic tension and emotional vacancy. Don is not seeking connection but distraction, a pattern the episode meticulously dissects.

In a stroke of bitter irony, while Don contemplates this new adulterous avenue, his wife Betty is engaged in a parallel, if more cautiously orchestrated, betrayal. She initiates a correspondence with the politically ambitious Henry Francis, who responds by impulsively arriving at the Draper home—only to be seen by the family’s housekeeper, Carla. His hastily concocted cover story, involving a potential Republican fundraiser at the house, is seized upon by Betty with a mixture of relief and thrilling complicity. She successfully manipulates Don into agreeing to host the event. However, the fundraiser itself delivers a crushing humiliation: instead of Henry, his middle-aged female aide, Elsa Kitteridge (Ann Ryerson), appears. Feeling cheated and infantilised, Betty confronts Henry at his office. Their charged encounter, where they finally vocalise their mutual attraction, ends not in consummation but in abrupt, almost prudish, retreat. Betty, suddenly seeing offices and motel rooms as “tawdry”, pulls back, leaving the relationship in a state of frustrated limbo. 

A far more severe and consequential rejection forms the episode’s devastating core, unfolding within the offices of Sterling Cooper. The production of a television commercial for the vital Lucky Strikes account is supervised by Lee Garner Jr. (Darren Pettie), the boorish, arrogant son of the client’s owner. Salvatore Romano, the agency’s talented art director, is directing the spot. Garner Jr., having correctly intuited Sal’s hidden homosexuality, attempts to exploit it when they are alone in an editing room. Sal’s horrified, principled rejection of these advances is a moment of quiet dignity. The retaliation is swift and brutal: a drunken Lee Garner Jr. calls Harry Crane, demanding Sal’s firing and warning him not to tell Pete Campbell. Harry, in a catastrophic failure of moral courage, does nothing, hoping the matter will “blow over”. When Garner Jr. later storms out of a meeting upon seeing Sal still employed, the crisis can no longer be ignored. Don, informed of the situation by a devastated Sal, is faced with an ugly business reality. The Lucky Strikes account is simply too important; the client’s whims, however petty and cruel, must be obeyed. In a chillingly pragmatic decision, Don tells Sal he must go. The final image of Sal is heartbreaking: deceiving his wife Kitty about still having a job while speaking from a pay phone in a section of Central Park known for gay cruising. His professional annihilation coincides with his forced return to the shadows of a clandestine life.

This professional and personal erosion culminates in Don’s final humiliation via the very relationship that once elevated him. While discussing an advertising campaign, Conrad Hilton expounds on his mission to bring American democracy and the Hilton experience to every corner of the globe, “including the moon”. Don, sleep-deprived and increasingly disconnected, makes a fatal interpretive error. He delivers a beautiful, ambitious pitch about bringing Hilton to the world, but fails to literally include the moon as a proposed hotel site. Hilton, seeing his explicit wish ignored, storms out in disgust. Roger Sterling, ever the cynical pragmatist, later visits Don to deliver a stark warning: with two major clients now furious, his position is precarious. The father figure has become the wrathful judge, and Don’s creative genius is dismissed as insubordination.

The episode’s denouement finds Don attempting to reclaim some agency through familiar, toxic means. Using the pretext of another late-night call from Hilton, he instead calls Suzanne Farrell. Their ensuing late-night tryst is underscored by her sharp observation that targeting his children’s teacher represents a risky departure from his usual modus operandi—it is “too close to home”. She sleeps with him regardless, but the act feels less like a conquest than a symptom of his spiralling desperation. It is a hollow victory in a night of profound losses.

Where the series sometimes stumbles with clunky historical references, *Wee Small Hour handles the civil rights movement with far greater nuance. The events are not merely backdrop but serve as pointed characterisation tools, particularly in delineating the women in Don’s orbit. Suzanne speaks of teaching her pupils Martin Luther King’s “I Have a Dream” speech, a statement that evokes in Don a mixture of tacit approval and fascination with a woman who represents educated, principled independence. She is the antithesis of Betty, who, upon hearing the news of the Birmingham bombings, remarks to Carla with dismissive privilege, “Maybe it isn’t the time for civil rights.” The contrast couldn’t be clearer, framing Suzanne as a beacon of the future and Betty as an avatar of a wilfully ignorant past.

The firing of Salvatore Romano marked a significant behind-the-scenes milestone, making actor Bryan Batt the first regular cast member to be written out of the show. His contract was not renewed for Season 4. Series creator Matthew Weiner originally defended the shocking, unjust nature of Sal’s dismissal as a necessary illustration of the risks and injustices faced by gay men in the 1960s. While dramatically potent, this decision remains one of the series’ most controversial. Weiner later expressed public regret, calling the abandonment of Sal’s storyline “a missed opportunity,” and despite vague plans for a future cameo, nothing materialised. This meta-narrative of creative regret inevitably colours a modern viewing of the episode.

*Wee Small Hours* is a technically solid, often brilliantly acted episode. Hornbacher’s direction is assured, the historical framing is clever, and the parallel narratives of Betrayal are deftly interwoven. However, its overarching critical flaw is one of dramatic balance. The brutal, emotionally resonant termination of Salvatore Romano’s storyline is so powerful, so morally arresting, that it completely overwhelms the other narrative threads. Don’s troubles with Hilton, his pursuit of Suzanne, and Betty’s flirtation with Henry Francis all risk seeming like artificial ‘filler’ in comparison—well-executed subplots that simply cannot compete with the raw impact of a beloved character being sacrificed on the altar of period-accurate bigotry and corporate cowardice. 


RATING: 6/10 (++)
