body.title: Rabbits, Canal Bridges, and Woodland Tunnels
body.body:
https://images.hive.blog/DQmUMzm93AS4Txf2Bbm4W4Woj2R92K488CrDgvFCQbTLFE8/InCollage_20260601_130715682.jpg

This morning I set off to explore part of a woodland I had never visited before. After the recent spell of hot weather, it was good to wake to overcast skies.  

https://images.hive.blog/DQma5tamwaLgbHPwUSuRcknGH2dRK5XvS1439b9gJEU9pfb/20260601_091246.jpg

Hot weather tires me out after a while.  The air felt nice and cool, making it much easier to walk in. 

https://images.hive.blog/DQmb3jwSJPBKwLyNpiwhNJyPEX34MrJ5JFEsVDhM23xQRKN/20260601_090412.jpg

I liked the green foliage next to the old brickwork.  It was an interesting mix of nature and the built environment.

https://images.hive.blog/DQmbyhPgNaKi4mSiNyoyJy681GFyPR6vvFkAxKTh7XAxZPA/P6012019.JPG

https://images.hive.blog/DQmUcdVBeGeiETjXSG7M5YGdpW9jYFibLqZ2QDzMxAKJuMp/P6012029.JPG

Not long after entering the wood, a rabbit was quietly enjoying its breakfast in a clearing.  We made each other jump, and I expected it to run off, but it decided to carry on munching. 

https://images.hive.blog/DQmTFuSQvxHhmBmcKNxhMVMsoQkH6o8Ng6fzsi4uhKUaKF3/P6012016.JPG

https://images.hive.blog/DQmc8vMzxvjZqqojZpSQh4BiNnP6QfMYkQWdmHfKghhJGs9/P6012014.JPG

Along a hedgerow bordering the footpath, a coal tit flitted amongst the stems and leaves. I watched it carefully as it picked at seeds hidden amongst the foliage. I was surprised I managed to get so close to it, but it didn't seem too bothered by my presence.

https://images.hive.blog/DQmWEYHQmGVYcodJuaY9vYJZixevCvD1WdDHMC5VfL9HWFy/20260601_090433.jpg

There was a slight rain shower but it quickly passed.  

https://images.hive.blog/DQmahhXYKNneoce47WYYT9yUNQR4yn3h6eTNMhXHMNRxFiG/20260601_091320.jpg

https://images.hive.blog/DQmULuDRsrDqtvxyc4V3q5SD7BoPoTX46GCesCDp47mbJYS/20260601_091523.jpg

As I walked deeper into the wood, the trees formed lovely natural arches over the path. Their branches entwined with each other overhead, creating green tunnels. 

https://images.hive.blog/DQmaJ6RDQuCTDRanrefzeWfjnGvb9rWfhdLc6CJWw6RArkf/20260601_090832.jpg

There's no better smell than honeysuckle. It smelt really lovely and sweet. 

https://images.hive.blog/DQmR2UbgvLbZbNF8JnHLX7cwXBEpPv9AUYcQoGMWAEikhZz/20260601_091927.jpg

Sadly, there was one disappointing sight. Near the children's play area, several pieces of graffiti had been sprayed onto equipment. It reminded me of the bad side of human behaviour. 

https://images.hive.blog/DQmYyn5yuGi62Ki1yWa86rKnpVAcStHFhoNreCdBuz9zbis/20260601_092249.jpg

https://images.hive.blog/DQmQJ3EWrn5cwPjd9dbh8nbM3nYTUQ7YULAXCEcsBeB4rVo/20260601_092435.jpg

https://images.hive.blog/DQmP7cKuepo4kdm7Lk25Xrb1y6AHJT4zDpqZoh2dJqUuHKF/20260530_091452.jpg

Part of my walk took me along the canal towpath. It was a pretty stretch to follow. As I walked, I passed beneath several old bridges that crossed over the canal. The towpath was fairly quiet, with only a few people out enjoying the morning. After a while, I reached a point where I decided to turn around and retrace my steps. 

https://images.hive.blog/DQmPywgNg7aW9ZBM9ikcd5tx2zLCFM8wFuowbzmTdU54hKw/20260530_092223~2.jpg

Discovering a new woodland and spotting wildlife made it an enjoyable walk, and the sun eventually turned up.

https://images.hive.blog/DQmTQF6wQW4xj6B6wQh99WqmNgkL1JrpKsWChsLv5k5Lq4b/PaRgthAvamAmR7uZi4RENh3BWaKjnQbhHtF9iaSV1cVaeSir8SCZYpmzMLvBrDLdiD44L3w4RUXvxqnkBg2eqoHbbUCFgVMLCokxymJ6uR...g2EUvmwMbS8rDTmwiZZiXJVfaSEG5zu7KhSz75fp2aWUpTTXMModEMjmcJDocpskjENinHpDX2Xfhqs6PzWxPZxGDEgVmqwVo162Vb1AHTA1YxrG6iGLyJ3Dqw.gif

body.title: My Hive Goals for 2026 Week #22
body.body:
I have decided to start posting a weekly update on my progress toward [my 2026 goals](https://peakd.com/hive-167922/@jfang003/my-hive-goals-for-2026-lma) here on [Hive](https://leofinance.io/@leoglossary/leoglossary-what-is-hive). It helps me stay on track, and I can realize if I am behind on a goal at any point in time. It's the sixth month of the year so far, and there is plenty of time left in the year. Also, for everyone's note, the Saturday Savers has ended, but the Slothly Savers Club has started in its place. 

## Progress

![graph.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jfang003/23uFweFUy14AtiiWw7jPg7ygo8AYpbFNyAfzA9t6SS5zJ3uwUJo5Xgp4gPRpj7Cumgx2g.png)
Above are statistics that I have gotten from [HiveStats](https://hivestats.io/). This week is looking better than last week, and it all adds up over time, but the chart seems off again. Somee of the day shows almost no reewards, and they seemed to be bunched together in specific days.

### HP
I earned 131 [HP](https://leofinance.io/@leoglossary/leoglossary-hive-power-hp) earned throughout the week. I am checking this through the difference between the two endpoints on the graph on Hivestats. The numbers are looking decent this week, but I am not sure why the numbers are so off. I think the chart is just wrong due to what I mentioned above. The numbers have recovered since last week, so I wonder where things will go. I did power up 10 Hive yesterday for HPUD.

### HBD 

![HBD.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jfang003/23tkfuT2Hbn72HrRnKLRSSNHQKoDUkMsRud5PY1HsNyLoNZAwc75gQhsuLuiMD2bGEuor.png)
I earned 0 [HBD](https://leofinance.io/@leoglossary/leoglossary-hive-backed-dollar-hbd) this week. With the price of Hive lower, we have hit the debt limit. This means that we will be earning Hive instead of HBD. I won't be able to add to my HBD savings for a while, but the interest will help me towards that goal. When the Hive price is above the debt limit, I'll add to my savings. There isn't much I can do here, but at least that interest will add up. 

## Conclusion


![goal progress.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jfang003/23u6X11XH7o5fEbChLBDnBM3BXQgGFuB5pZtTuJdzAPJiFMvYKZydkdasTjKbwDmy5qEK.png)

My progress is looking decent for now. I need around 2% per week, so this week I met that standard. HBD is officially behind where I need to be now. However, without any HBD being earned, it might not be enough if that doesn't change by the end of the year. Other than that, nothing much has changed, and I am just slowly grinding away at my goals. The HBD goal isn't looking that great as I am behind, and I don't think we will be getting HBD anytime soon with the current Hive price. My HP goal is looking great, but my HBD isn't. I am not sure if I want to leave it as is or change some Hive into HBD later down the year. The HP is ahead, but the HBD isn't. At least I got the interest, so the progress is looking better than last week.

Do you have any goals for 2026? What is the progress towards your own goals? 

Feel free to leave a comment if you read my post. If you have any questions, feel free to ask, and I will do my best to answer.

body.title: Why South Indian Cuisine Is Winning Over Food Lovers Everywhere
body.body:
Street food culture in Britain has seen a subtle but dramatic transformation in the last decade that was driven by communities who are that bring their authentic regional dishes to new audiences. [South Indian cuisine in Manchester](https://www.primefoodproducts.co.uk/) is now an integral part of talked about food experiences in Manchester and has earned the respect of people who are sick of bland options and looking for something that has real depth. 



![23.jpg](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/e977184d508dde31702c4440f6ac881cb0e467a96f6f62a3d15ec41762904ce0)



South Indian cuisine is not one-dimensional it’s an extensive, varied assortment of regional cultures that span Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana Each with their own distinctive ingredients, cooking methods and flavor personalities. The thing that unites these cuisines is a culinary philosophy founded on balancerice, lentils coconut, curry leaves, tamarind and mustard seeds form the base of meals that are nutritious, light, and bursting with flavour.

### How South Indian Food Differs From What Most People Expect

For a lot of people who grew up in traditional British Indian restaurant tradition, South Indian food comes as an absolute surprise. It is a cuisine that relies heavily on rice-based dishes instead of wheat, so it is gluten-free in many of its famous dishes. Dosa is a crispy crepe, made fermented from lentil and rice batter. It is serving with coconut-based chutney, and Sambar, a stew of vegetables and lentils that is scented with dried tamarind and red chillies. 

Idli, a soft and steamed rice cake, appears simple, but it has incredible nutrition and digestion benefits because of the process of fermentation. Uttapam is a thick, savoury pancake that is topped with onions tomatoes along with green chillies. These meals aren’t simply different in the ingredients used but they are also a sign of an entirely different way of thinking about food, one that prioritizes the health of your gut, seasonal produce and spices as medicine rather than a spectacle.

### The Regional Variations That Make Every Plate a New Discovery

A single of the more thrilling aspects of pursuing the cuisine of Kerala is observing how drastically it changes across states. Kerala cuisine is characterized by the utilization of coconut in nearly every form — freshly grated, then pressed to make milk or boiled into oil -resulting in curries that are full of flavor in flavor, fragrant, and satisfying. Foods such as fish molee avial and Kerala the prawn curry are characterized by an identity of the coast that is different from other dishes across the continent. 

Tamil Nadu, by contrast is known for its spicy heat and intricate spices — Chettinad cuisine is thought to be among the most heavily spiced dishes across the entire country of India with kalpasi, marathi mokku and star anise, which are rarely seen in other regions. Andhra cooking increases the heat further by using fiery gongura-based recipes and rice-based dishes that have tangy flavours, earning an ardent following from those who are truly passionate about chilli. Karnataka has a softer more sweeter taste in its most famous dishes, including breakfast dishes and rice-based meals served with banana leaf.

### What to Order First and Why This Cuisine Rewards Exploration

Aiming at South Indian food with curiosity rather than trepidation is the best way to go. Breakfast menus alone -dosas, idlis the vadas and pongalprovides enough variety to keep food lovers entertained for weeks with no repetition. Rasam, a thin peppery soup that is often served with the full South Indian meal, is one of the best-loved dishes of all Indian cuisine, serving as a digestive and a cleanser of the palate, and also an extremely comforting broth. Biryani originates from Hyderabadi tradition. 

Hyderabadi tradition, which is technically as a cross-over from to the Deccan region, is now an international sensation in its own right, and is still a mainstay dish at celebrations. Filter coffee, which is brewed by using a traditional metal filter and topped with frosty milk, is just equally important to the culture in the same way as foodit’s the only way a South Indian meal feels complete without it. [South Indian foods in Manchester](https://www.primefoodproducts.co.uk/) is growing in recognition and popularity increasing awareness that this food has more than just delicious taste but also an intimate link to some of the world’s most ancient and most sophisticated cuisines. If you haven’t yet had the chance to explore it The journey starts with a simple dosa, and doesn’t stop until you’ve eaten it all.

body.title: Mi delicioso Almuerzo: Pollo al horno, gratinado con mozzarella [ESP/ENG]
body.body: # Mi delicioso Almuerzo: Pollo al horno, gratinado con mozzarella [ESP/ENG]\n\n<div class=\

>

Hola amigos amantes de la cocina y del buen comer que me leen en la comunidad de @hivefood, espero que todos hayan pasado un excelente fin de semana. Así mismo les deseo un feliz inicio de semana y de mes, ya entramos en le mes de junio, mes de los bonches, ya que tengo varios cumpleaños. Los invito a que sean bienvenidos a mi blog.

![20.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/23uFYMXcUzUY656DcqnpRq8vxronHNUcmhFRJibu9Wj8GHbqFBxhCMZEVSSLJMyKX8Mmq.jpg)

Hoy les traigo a la comunidad un delicioso y nutritivo almuerzo, cero de grasas  que prepara para degustarlo en mi almuerzo: Un deliciosos pollo al horno, gratinado con queso mozzarella.

![16.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/Eoc7WK91yXvw2rdhqfQZGcppWkMtxQDZQLFJgR9sTngZvc8D8x8syCQWqDgmMDMeMkb.jpg)

Esta receta la acompañe con arroz blanco, plátano y una rica crema de vegetales. como bebida tome agua, ya que la doctora me consiguió un pequeño problema con la toroide, por lo que estoy evitando un poco los azucare, evitando tomar tantos jugos y si lo hago lo preparo con una mínima cantidad. 

![18.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/EpCBSJsCMgCgZi4JNS8AREKtJxgE4Tayop9joFDVDAgDrKhvXLg5qSR85M9dYsjCtgC.jpg)

El pollo horneado en casa es una de las preparaciones más reconfortantes, saludables y versátiles. Destaca por ser jugoso por dentro y crujiente por fuera, es una receta bastante sencilla y fáciles de preparar con la especie que de nuestra preferencia y que por lo general siempre la tenemos en nuestra despensa, ideal para compartir en familia.

Les indicare la cantidad de ingredientes que utilice para esta preparación y el paso a paso de la receta.

# Ingredientes
* 2 muslos de pollo grande con su cuadril 
* Aliños verdes (celery, ajo porro y cilantro)
* 1 cucharada de salsa de soya
* Arroz blanco
* 1 plátano sancochado
* 1ají dulce, 3 dientes de ajo, sal y pimienta al gusto
* 1 cucharada de aceite y 2 revanadas de queso mozarela

![2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/Eos2K5nrpZjqPJ1uhS9tB3Be3oZ5UKDnr7pJvxgrAY5jehERSjXkwkENhts14D5moZX.jpg)

# Preparacion
Lo primero que hice fue quitarle la piel a los muslos, colocarlos en una refractaria y reservarlos con algo de sal.

![5.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/EpA4RG4n5Rmca4L1wVYJ489obtG7vQ5wXKiAcWG6UvhK74dyi5g8qYdw6STGLUGbmya.jpg)

A la par corte todo los aliños y los pase por la licuadora, este licuado se los agregue encima, de modo que esta crema medio liquida tapara los muslos, los introduje al horno y deje cocinar por 20 minutos con calor arriba y abajo.

![7.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/242DNg2nDwMAMNGQddQZFWPSeoZfizQdz84LaJURmPpY7G99NsmmKmQhEH9VPAerasyA9.jpg)|![8.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/244ob74weT6ZwDaUmHLFbJqM61oCwr37iYwHugzYZiejecus64uB5aEy6aMVbk1SictuS.jpg)
-|-

![9.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/EowHW4pCJRkHD7bJftKsRow1EvgpXSpjyjx1pcmMML8X8GdkzdFwEkQorbJYZB36U8n.jpg)|![13.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/EoGySam1ojD8cJJpHVD9TgJ8kKUhfVgZxUFrW6TNgHJUSR8GH8Dj3cZaniaWoQ9BTck.jpg)
-|-

Al transcurrir el tiempo de horneado, lo saque, revise el sazón, la textura y le coloque el queso mozzarella por encima, introduje nuevamente al horno y deje gratinar por 3 minutos, apague y emplate. Este platillo quedo super rico, con una textura muy suave y  lo acompañe con arroz, plátano sancochado y una deliciosa crema de verduras, de tomar agua.

![14.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/EogNiiZTBNdTNSx6pZjDeDdA6KtC2EcPe1cLHLYeo9y83Pp2mNnnDpShaYDgkkYmEo9.jpg)|![15.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/Eoe8iBYL6xmVhnsVbZq1zUvjwkoJgSSNxYLmMuGsesGyzgsKkbVe9MBMpRq4uaYpjPT.jpg)
-|-

![16.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/Eoc7WK91yXvw2rdhqfQZGcppWkMtxQDZQLFJgR9sTngZvc8D8x8syCQWqDgmMDMeMkb.jpg)|![19.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/EprVWFih5CUB5tq1vT6jZKD1zJ51YU931udrLKSE8rrU9Pz22ESML16tqd2Hdqn9nHs.jpg)
-|-

![18.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/EpCBSJsCMgCgZi4JNS8AREKtJxgE4Tayop9joFDVDAgDrKhvXLg5qSR85M9dYsjCtgC.jpg)

hasta aquí mi contenido, espero sea de su agrado y nos vemos en una nueva receta. saludos y bendiciones para todos.

* Fotos tomadas con Iphone 8 plus
* Portada diseñada con Canva

<div class=\
> # English Version # My Delicious Lunch: Baked Chicken, Topped with Mozzarella

> Hello, fellow food lovers and culinary enthusiasts who read my posts in the @hivefood community! I hope you all had a wonderful weekend. I also wish you a happy start to the week and the month—we’ve already entered June, the month of parties, since I have several birthdays coming up. I invite you to join me on my blog. ![20.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/23uFYMXcUzUY656DcqnpRq8vxronHNUcmhFRJibu9Wj8GHbqFBxhCMZEVSSLJMyKX8Mmq.jpg) Today I’m sharing a delicious and nutritious, fat-free lunch with the community—something I’m preparing to enjoy for my own lunch: a delicious baked chicken topped with mozzarella cheese. ![16.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/Eoc7WK91yXvw2rdhqfQZGcppWkMtxQDZQLFJgR9sTngZvc8D8x8syCQWqDgmMDMeMkb.jpg) I served this recipe with white rice, plantains, and a rich vegetable cream soup. For a drink, I had water, since the doctor found a small issue with my thyroid, so I’m cutting back a bit on sugar, avoiding too many juices, and if I do have them, I prepare them with a minimal amount of sugar. ![18.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/EpCBSJsCMgCgZi4JNS8AREKtJxgE4Tayop9joFDVDAgDrKhvXLg5qSR85M9dYsjCtgC.jpg) Homemade roasted chicken is one of the most comforting, healthy, and versatile dishes. It stands out for being juicy on the inside and crispy on the outside. It’s a fairly simple recipe that’s easy to prepare using your favorite spices—ingredients you usually always have on hand—and it’s perfect for sharing with the family. I’ll list the ingredients I used for this recipe and provide step-by-step instructions. # Ingredients * 2 large chicken thighs with drumettes * Green herbs (celery, leek, and cilantro) * 1 tablespoon soy sauce * White rice * 1 boiled plantain * 1 sweet pepper, 3 garlic cloves, salt and pepper to taste * 1 tablespoon oil and 2 slices of mozzarella cheese ![2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/Eos2K5nrpZjqPJ1uhS9tB3Be3oZ5UKDnr7pJvxgrAY5jehERSjXkwkENhts14D5moZX.jpg) # Preparation The first thing I did was remove the skin from the chicken thighs, place them in an ovenproof dish, and season them with a little salt. ![5.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/EpA4RG4n5Rmca4L1wVYJ489obtG7vQ5wXKiAcWG6UvhK74dyi5g8qYdw6STGLUGbmya.jpg) Meanwhile, chop all the seasonings and blend them in a blender. Pour this mixture over the chicken thighs so that the semi-liquid cream covers them. Place the dish in the oven and bake for 20 minutes with heat from both top and bottom. ![7.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/242DNg2nDwMAMNGQddQZFWPSeoZfizQdz84LaJURmPpY7G99NsmmKmQhEH9VPAerasyA9.jpg) |![8.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/244ob74weT6ZwDaUmHLFbJqM61oCwr37iYwHugzYZiejecus64uB5aEy6aMVbk1SictuS.jpg) -|- ![9.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/EowHW4pCJRkHD7bJftKsRow1EvgpXSpjyjx1pcmMML8X8GdkzdFwEkQorbJYZB36U8n.jpg) |![13.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/EoGySam1ojD8cJJpHVD9TgJ8kKUhfVgZxUFrW6TNgHJUSR8GH8Dj3cZaniaWoQ9BTck.jpg) -|- Once the baking time was up, I took it out, checked the seasoning and texture, and topped it with mozzarella cheese. I put it back in the oven and let it brown for 3 minutes, turned off the heat, and plated it. This dish turned out super delicious, with a very smooth texture, and I served it with rice, boiled plantains, and a delicious vegetable soup. ![14.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/EogNiiZTBNdTNSx6pZjDeDdA6KtC2EcPe1cLHLYeo9y83Pp2mNnnDpShaYDgkkYmEo9.jpg) |![15.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/Eoe8iBYL6xmVhnsVbZq1zUvjwkoJgSSNxYLmMuGsesGyzgsKkbVe9MBMpRq4uaYpjPT.jpg) -|- ![16.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/Eoc7WK91yXvw2rdhqfQZGcppWkMtxQDZQLFJgR9sTngZvc8D8x8syCQWqDgmMDMeMkb.jpg) |![19.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/EprVWFih5CUB5tq1vT6jZKD1zJ51YU931udrLKSE8rrU9Pz22ESML16tqd2Hdqn9nHs.jpg) -|- ![18.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/morepina/EpCBSJsCMgCgZi4JNS8AREKtJxgE4Tayop9joFDVDAgDrKhvXLg5qSR85M9dYsjCtgC.jpg) That’s all for my content today. I hope you enjoyed it, and I’ll see you in a new recipe. Greetings and blessings to all. * Photos taken with iPhone 8 Plus * Cover designed with Canva * Text translated with Deepl Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@morepina/mi-delicioso-almuerzo-pollo-al-horno-gratinado-con-mozzarella-espeng-6wp)

body.title: ‎Why I'm Happy Chelsea Are Holding On to Josh Acheampong ‎
body.body:
‎As a Chelsea fan, one thing I always enjoy is seeing young academy players getting a real chance to prove themselves. That's why the recent news about Chelsea rejecting offers for Josh Acheampong made me smile.
‎
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmXekJi7YDjBb262Yg6BLYEKDkLUfLtTYkbgWTsTyjkTuJ/GettyImages-2190756319-1024x683.jpg 

‎[Source](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/football/player/josh-acheampong-WGkASmNOCs7m22wU/)
‎
‎Football today can be quite ruthless. Young players often find themselves being loaned out repeatedly or sold before they get the opportunity to establish themselves in the first team. Because of that, it says a lot when a club decides to keep hold of a young player despite interest from several other teams.
‎
‎I remember watching Acheampong whenever he got the chance to play last season. Even though his appearances were limited, there was something about him that stood out. He looked calm on the ball, confident in his defending, and comfortable playing in different positions across the back line. For a player who is still only 20 years old, those are qualities that are tough to ignore.
‎
‎Like many Chelsea supporters, I sometimes found myself wondering why he was not getting more minutes. There were games where I felt he could have been given a chance, especially when the team was struggling with injuries and inconsistency. Still, I understand that development is not always a free ride path. Sometimes young players need time behind the scenes before they are ready for a bigger role.
‎
‎What makes this news even more encouraging is that Chelsea reportedly see him as one of the players they don't want to lose. Being mentioned alongside names like Cole Palmer and Reece James shows the level of belief the club has in him. That kind of trust is earned and not given.
‎
‎The new contract keeping him at the club until 2029 is another positive sign. To me, it suggests that Chelsea are looking beyond instant results and investing in players they believe can be important for years to come.
‎
‎With Xabi Alonso preparing for his first season in charge, I am curious to see how things unfold. A new manager often brings fresh opportunities, and this could be the perfect moment for Acheampong to establish himself as a regular member of the squad.
‎
‎I'd personally love to see him get more game time this season. Chelsea's academy has produced some fantastic talents over the years, and hopefully Acheampong can become the next success story. The ability is there, the club believes in him, and now it's all about taking the next step when the opportunity arrives.
‎
‎As fans, sometimes all we want is to see talented young players given a fair chance. Hopefully, Josh Acheampong gets exactly that.
‎

body.title: The Market Is Choosing Its Religion
body.body:
# The Market Is Choosing Its Religion

Somewhere between a war in the Middle East and a Jensen Huang product reveal, equity markets made a philosophical choice this week. They chose Nvidia.

New clashes in the Middle East and rising oil prices couldn't halt the rally at Monday's open. Instead, NVDA's stock climbed roughly 2% in pre-market trading after the company announced it was entering the personal computer processor market with a product integrating Arm architecture CPUs alongside Blackwell GPUs. The Middle East — a war that at its peak involved the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz and the shutdown of an estimated 10.5 million barrels per day of crude production across Iraq, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the UAE, Qatar, and Bahrain — apparently ranks somewhere below Jensen Huang's product roadmap in the hierarchy of things that move equities right now. Make of that what you will.

The Nvidia news was genuinely significant, but the market's *reaction* to it tells you more than the news itself. ARM surged 7.5%, while Qualcomm dropped 3.6% — a clean redistribution of expectation within the semiconductor stack. Nvidia also confirmed that its Vera data center CPU is now in full production, claiming it generates tokens 1.8 times faster than x86 architectures, with Huang calling it the company's \

The first customers read like a who's-who of the infrastructure build-out: OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceX/xAI, Dell, Oracle, and CoreWeave, with availability starting fall 2026. At a market cap of $5.45 trillion, Nvidia has become less a company than a load-bearing wall in the global economy.

Now here's the tension worth sitting with. While markets chase the AI supercycle upward, the macro ceiling is cracking.

Jerome Powell warned on Sunday against the \

while Neel Kashkari noted that even if the Strait of Hormuz were to fully reopen, supply chains and inflation could normalize far more slowly than markets expect. That's not hedging language — that's the Fed telling you, plainly, that the easy disinflationary trade is over. And markets are starting to price it: futures are now pricing rate *hikes*, not cuts. Read that again. We have gone, in the span of a few months of geopolitical shock and energy disruption, from a rate-cut narrative to a rate-hike reality. The velocity of that reversal deserves more attention than it's getting.

The ECB is the sharper story. Isabel Schnabel declined to specify an upper limit on the number of rate hikes ahead, insisting the ECB will remain data-driven. The hawks are running Frankfurt now, and the doves are losing the argument. Price subindices within German Services and Manufacturing PMIs have moved to multi-year highs, which makes the inflation picture sticky regardless of what Q2 GDP delivers. The ECB built its credibility fighting inflation in 2022 and 2023; it is not about to surrender it over a softening growth print. A June hike looks essentially priced. EUR/USD sat at 1.1651 on Monday — resilient, but quietly weighed down by the dollar's own hawkish reassertion.

Japan is the wild card that nobody wants to talk about directly. Japan's Q1 capital expenditure came in at 0.0% year-over-year, against an expected 4.0% — raising immediate questions about a downward GDP revision. That number should have been a stop sign. Instead, BOJ Governor Ueda is scheduled to speak Wednesday with the market hunting for signals on a June rate hike, though there's no internal consensus yet. The yen is above 158 against the dollar, and Japanese verbal intervention has been described by traders as weak, incapable of generating a sustainable rally without actual data to back it up. Ueda is in the worst possible position: his economy is softening at exactly the moment global pressure demands he tighten. Whatever he says Wednesday will be parsed with forensic intensity.

Underneath all of this sits the Friday NFP. The consensus forecast stands at 85,000 new jobs, with unemployment holding at 4.3%. That is a number that, two years ago, would have been called catastrophic. Today it sits right in the zone where the Fed can do nothing — too warm to cut, too cold to be confident the labor market holds. Powell needs clarity; the data keeps withholding it.

What's remarkable about this moment is the sheer number of regime inflection points arriving simultaneously. The ECB potentially hiking in June, BOJ wrestling with the same question from a structurally weaker position, the Fed watching its easing thesis dissolve in real time, a Middle East conflict that the World Bank assessed as delivering the largest oil supply shock on record — and equity markets at or near record highs because Nvidia announced a new laptop chip and something called Vera can run agent inference faster than Intel's architecture.

The cognitive dissonance here is not irrational, exactly. The AI infrastructure buildout is a decade-long structural story; the Middle East conflict has historically resolved faster than it disrupts. Markets are discounting machines, not historians. But discounting machines can overshoot on optimism just as badly as they overshoot on panic, and the current configuration — equity complacency sitting on top of a genuinely hostile rate environment — is the kind of setup that looks obvious in hindsight.

Watch Ueda Wednesday. Watch the JOLTS data Tuesday. Watch whether oil — which came into June having already pulled back from its April extremes — gets repriced upward on fresh clashes. The Nvidia narrative is seductive. It is also doing a great deal of heavy lifting for a market that would look considerably less confident if you stripped out a single stock.

Five trillion dollars is a lot of religion to put in one ticker.

这个不愉快的关于快递的事情又来了。

前天上午九点就到的快递，到今天还未收到。昨天我发现有异常，就联系快递员，谁知打了两个打通了没人接，我就觉得这估计有问题了。

然后接着给圆通快递客服打电话，客服查过之后说正在派送中，让我等。前天上午就显示派送中，不解决问题，还让我等。我把诉求又重复了一遍，客服查过以后，说让网点加急派送，然后挂了电话。

结果等到昨天下午也没等到，然后开始一直给总部打电话进行投诉，结果一样，让我等马上解决。还是等，等不到，接着打，一直未收到。其实以往的我不会这样做的，浪费时间和精力，但是，这些人的行为实在太可恶。每一个出来工作的成年人都要为自己的行为负责任，种任性的瓜，要结苦果的！

打到晚上10点结束，说明天上午一定解决。今天还在等，但是快递显示动了，又转到了妈妈驿站。弄的人哭笑不得，这究竟是想干啥了，这报复水平和手段也太低级了！我截图给总部，总部打电话，到11点多的时候一个电话打来，还是之前的那个驿站。我问她原因，她就说忘了！真是太可恶了！

我没让她进家，让她放下面快递柜。谁知道来之后我的快速就扔在那，气的我不打一处来。这时总部又来电，我投诉了一番，总部说，一定要让我那就接着等吧！

糟糕的心情，绝不饶恕。

body.title: [ENG/ESP] When life throws unexpected challenges your way, but you keep moving forward
body.body: > **Greetings, I hope you have a great day. Mine, like every day, will be wonderful… or at least I try to picture it that way, because I firmly believe that the way you see yourself has a huge impact on how things turn out. Today I want to share a little more of my daily life with you—even though it’s simple, it always brings some unexpected lesson or anecdote. Yesterday was a pretty damp day. It rained on and off during the early morning and also in the morning, leaving that smell of wet earth that is sometimes comforting and other times just complicates things. However, the rain didn’t stop work from going on as usual. When it’s time to work, it’s time, so my husband and I headed out as usual to carry out our routine at the Sunsol Unik hotel and then deliver a quote at the Parque Costa Azul shopping center. On the way, something unexpected happened. A water truck passed by us, and when it hit a rock, it flew straight into our windshield. The glass cracked immediately. The truck driver stopped and told us to find a place to replace it, saying he could help us with half the cost because he couldn’t afford more. We appreciated his honesty and kindness, and decided it was best to finish our tasks for the day first and then look for a place to replace the glass.**

> *Saludos, les deseo un día genial.   El mío, como cada día, será excelente… o al menos trato de visualizarlo así, porque creo firmemente que la manera en que uno se proyecta influye muchísimo en cómo se desarrolla todo. Hoy quiero compartirles un pedacito más de mi día a día, que aunque sencillo, siempre trae alguna enseñanza o anécdota inesperada. Ayer fue un día bastante húmedo. Llovió a intervalos durante la madrugada y también en la mañana, dejando ese olor a tierra mojada que a veces reconforta y otras veces solo complica las cosas. Sin embargo, la lluvia no impidió que el trabajo siguiera su curso. Cuando toca trabajar, toca, así que mi esposo y yo salimos como de costumbre para cumplir con nuestra rutina en el hotel Sunsol Unik y luego entregar un presupuesto en el centro comercial Parque Costa Azul. En el camino ocurrió algo que no esperábamos. Un camión de agua pasó por nuestro lado y, al pisar una piedra, esta salió disparada directo hacia nuestro parabrisas. El vidrio se cuarteó de inmediato. El conductor del camión se detuvo y nos dijo que buscáramos dónde reemplazarlo, que él podía ayudarnos con la mitad del costo, porque no tenía para más. Agradecimos su sinceridad y su intención, y decidimos que lo mejor era cumplir primero con nuestras tareas del día y luego dedicarnos a buscar dónde cambiar el vidrio.*
![photo_2026-06-02_00-21-52.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/23wqkoD72aNcTC1sUUtXTuZuUp43a46hWQhDRuxScPoas7PT8GWw89dpCF3EqTVLDbpuF.jpg) ![photo_2026-06-02_00-21-50.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EoGvwXWJwU4uiVAxu3eHJs9cXgvuw7iFCy4GupTb6tCEyjskDYFSJgFgeiQqmwUY15t.jpg) ![photo_2026-06-02_00-21-49.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/Eq7NKG4LU7pVJVoPkdmmu8jJhkUMxdV9FgEFXZfrgkC3rvPksdU31NCUzjAJ3VK3oHr.jpg) ![photo_2026-06-02_00-26-06.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EpJYX7FnpUs7dEpYPsFGrZ6cnkmE67CHQzWyAeqBkijCRMECS89c6ukeovv43ktQQBE.jpg)

> **We arrived at the Sunsol Unik Hotel and carried out our usual routine: chlorinating and disinfecting the main pool. Everything went very smoothly, and the levels were within the ideal range, which always gives us a sense of satisfaction and peace of mind. Knowing that the job is done right is a reward in itself.**

> *Llegamos al hotel Sunsol Unik y realizamos nuestra rutina de trabajo; la cloración y desinfección del tanque principal. Todo salió muy bien, los niveles quedaron dentro de los parámetros ideales, lo cual siempre nos da una sensación de satisfacción y tranquilidad. Saber que el trabajo está bien hecho es una recompensa en sí misma.*
![photo_2026-06-02_00-21-31.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/Eo6Jyymryaqf5K9ZnzoxVnCYCKNQVJkFZMD9otQcLskHejMop5jchp4GxFBJn56ta5W.jpg) ![photo_2026-06-02_00-21-30.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EprTcVNC6kwyA225vtrHXuPP148Jv8CQgQrwiHaiEjSyzUuLitzGgGLfRGUT4UzBk2p.jpg) ![photo_2026-06-02_00-21-29.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EqdAwb2c4oqqSScMPo1deLAtKpcQmJpqFeMGa83SzGPwhdbMogs4hBqDNvz84k5m4xL.jpg)

> **When we were done, we walked to the shopping center just a few meters away. We handed in the quote and took the opportunity to look around. We went up to the top floor to take an elevator, and from the balcony we could see some artists working on decorating a boat. It was beautiful to watch how, with patience and talent, they were transforming a simple structure into a piece full of color and life. Those kinds of moments, though brief, always fill my soul.**

> *Al terminar, caminamos hasta el centro comercial que queda a pocos metros. Entregamos el presupuesto y aprovechamos para dar una vuelta. Subimos a la planta alta para tomar una barquilla y desde el balcón pudimos ver a unos artistas trabajando en la decoración de un bote. Era hermoso ver cómo, con paciencia y talento, iban transformando una simple estructura en una pieza llena de color y vida. Ese tipo de momentos, aunque breves, siempre me llenan el alma.*
![photo_2026-06-02_00-21-36.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EpXK4Nm822c9k3b8dJ7hxivC9wVYNSwLVfBwJsx7EV44oS7wgqfpsh3nLkcAkPQogUm.jpg) ![photo_2026-06-02_00-21-35.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EprUW2kp4ZBiAeDbxVpkm6r6rbLAxukAeRWRAS6rWGRdu6toj4uXAc82PAsMa3DdEa7.jpg) ![photo_2026-06-02_00-21-32.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/Ep1XM6DhPsHaLX2WuC5jBY4k3sbx7m94coZ5by4RCtc9JCWDf1gyGd9bE9N35G2QXgU.jpg)
> **Then we got back to our mission for the day: finding a place to get the windshield repaired. We drove all over town, asking around, comparing prices, and listening to different options.**

> *Luego retomamos nuestra misión del día; buscar dónde arreglar el parabrisas. Fuimos de un lado a otro por la ciudad, preguntando, comparando precios, escuchando opciones.*
![photo_2026-06-02_00-21-47.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EpvhTxBS8eyBGdvEMP3LajCRif57TDexq3DdiTWZviRvZVzzDBcK1rZoP4RxqAL1m4B.jpg) ![photo_2026-06-02_00-21-44.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EptaUSa7yqtvv66EM8Exg1Q7dxgPdJbJD3XgNA7K92Nqrx52ZjPB4QSz1NWnd7ZZHXS.jpg) ![photo_2026-06-02_00-21-37.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EpGR7umm8qnGoBKTva9SR4QJZFiNpKJBi7gyQ143qZfuZfwqJjFZcChTEuB4Ytdu7gx.jpg)

> **We finally arrived at “Auto Parabrisas,” where we’d been told they’d likely have the windshield for our car model. And that’s exactly what happened. They had it in stock and gave us a quote of $190, which turned out to be the cheapest option. Now we have to come up with half that amount in a few days to get the problem fixed.**

> *Finalmente llegamos a “Auto Parabrisas”, donde nos habían dicho que probablemente sí tendrían el vidrio para nuestro modelo de auto. Y así fue. Lo tenían disponible y nos dieron un presupuesto de ciento noventa dólares, que resultó ser el más económico. Ahora nos toca reunir la mitad de ese monto en pocos días para poder resolver el problema.*
![photo_2026-06-02_00-21-41.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/Ep7udAEatqUTXzFbeN6x6PBoD28oTiHSL7JxaKJk7L6LUv8kcEuaNjVa5rpheAUU3U8.jpg) ![photo_2026-06-02_00-21-38.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EpQwL5Nthhuke2UecCtQtjDYZ5ozQzd6kU5szFtKLTXdwMrGinTXPCjg52FdwGMHKEU.jpg) ![photo_2026-06-02_00-21-23.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/EqHzNdpMuHvHKZN4R1FxhsqTrEbKLiFefLWWjGuyRcHNsqdLX3E899YSwMXreYmdmix.jpg) ![photo_2026-06-02_00-21-22.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/taniagonzalez/Eou7kTwT9KuxiQMDDhW7kgFGU12Q9hwAt7mtqQdCU4LqCeVenzFEwxiJ9Fav82RTHtf.jpg)

> **With all that information in hand, we headed home to analyze, discuss, and reach a consensus on how to handle this unexpected expense. Even so, we ended the day feeling satisfied that we’d completed our tasks and had a clear plan for resolving the issue. So, as always, I’ll see you throughout the week to share another little glimpse into my day-to-day life. See you soon. Bye.**

> *Con toda esa información en mano, regresamos a casa para analizar, debatir y llegar a un consenso sobre cómo afrontar este nuevo gasto inesperado. Aun así, cerramos el día con la satisfacción de haber cumplido con nuestras tareas y de tener un camino claro para resolver lo que se presentó. Así que, como siempre, los veré en el transcurso de la semana para contarles otro pedacito de mi día a día.   Hasta pronto.   Chao.*

body.title: The contribution of the sun to the world.
body.body: > https://images.pexels.com/photos/239861/pexels-photo-239861.jpeg [sourch]( https://www.pexels.com/photo/green-leafed-tree-beside-house-with-sun-ray-239861/ ) Our world is very beautiful and very mysterious. And the sun, which is about 150 million kilometers away from our earth, helps to make this mysterious world even more mysterious. In fact, although the distance from the sun to the earth is so great, the sun's responsibility to the earth is very important. So the sun performs its responsibility very well even from such a distance. Without the sun, our earth is completely immobile. Without the sun's contribution, our earth could not have been so beautiful. Without the sun's light, we would not have been able to see our earth so beautifully and would never have been able to enjoy the unique beauty of this earth. In fact, the sun has an unlimited contribution not only to see the beauty of the earth but also to make the beauty of this earth beautiful. Because of the sun's heat and light, many good things are created on the earth and many bad things are destroyed. The sun is seen as the absolute friend of our earth. The sun is very necessary not only for the earth but also for all living and non-living creatures and objects on this earth. We always understand the importance of the sun very well when the sun does not rise, that is, when the sky is cloudy, and when the sun's heat is low in winter, we understand the importance of the sun very well. If we pay a little attention, we can see that just as the heat of the sun causes us discomfort in summer, it also benefits and helps us a lot. No matter how hot it is or how sick we are due to the heat of the sun, if one day the sun does not rise and does not give heat, we have to face a lot of difficulties and start worrying when we see a cloudy sky. On the other hand, in winter, the heat of the sun is less, and when most of the days or more than half of the day the sky is cloudy and does not give the heat of the sun, then everyone feels very angry and needs the heat of winter. In fact, whether it is winter or hot, we need the heat of the sun and the light of the sun very much at all times. People who live in beautiful places on earth where the heat and light of the sun fall beautifully are very fortunate. We know that there are many places in this world where the light of the sun does not fall that way. There is not much heat, due to which those places are very cold. They are covered in snow. There are many places where the light of the sun is visible only for a few hours. Again, there are many places where the light of the sun is not visible for 6 months, let alone the heat. People living in these places face many difficulties and hardships. People living in these places know very well how much sunlight and heat are essential in our lives. We have seen different places on this earth where sunlight does not reach, plants cannot be born in any way. Similarly, animals and plants in this world cannot live well without sunlight and without it and do not get enough food sources. We are very fortunate that we were born in such a beautiful place on earth where we get enough sunlight and light. And because of this, we do not have to face so much hardship and hardship as those people who are born in those places on earth where not a single drop of sunlight and heat falls. body.body:
# Hello Hive




![1000224733.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/23wWpSuqUEaE8CYftiWCGDngJCG7sRHB9sFae3SztJTtVQ17bAJR7tWvn5GS5SPtonPdj.jpg)


It's another beautiful day and we are up early to face the business of the day. Yesterday was one of the most hectic times of some hardwork in the farm and I didn't even had the energy and time to check-in on hive. 

We started with planting the remaining parts of the lettuce we have been planting over the weekend. 
The lettuce seedlings we were planting got exhausted midway and we have to wait and order for more.


![1000224727.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/243q8yEGk6uSFgw5bJZpBQTewNnZaBcQqnHPdGKRVeyAixZYzp1EyS77dXErsDsDGGDQy.jpg)


Now the transplanting of the seedlings were completed yesterday and you can see the vast portion of land we were able to cover. This much quantity of lettuce hasn't been planted in this location before, hence once these particular veggies is ready the pepper here will enjoy some lettuce Salad. It is one of my favorite fruit dressing. 

![1000224725.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/23xebjHRNyhWLAFXpEnzPQZM14Bwjf89htHYYum4rCmQpZqp9X3TthBGWmPXBZ3EsBMTt.jpg)


This particular soil is a very fertile loamy clay soil hence almost everything planted here often flourish. Now these lettuce will be here for about 6-8weeks before they will be harvested up so that we can plant rice on the same plot of land.
Many a times we do not like mix cropping lettuce vegetables with other veggies on the same plot of land. Lettuce are often planted alone and since they do not take much time to produce, they get harvested promptly and the land is released to plant other crops. 


![1000224734.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/23u5xfViePVYK9ERNpMY472hqsnWcNuGsW6sL8jE4Y48E6p6aSYu6B8fdA5YWsgndtvXC.jpg)

![1000224735.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/EoChBf8zEb585ALyQ5ZHhkBY1d5CCgQ8bruMN3TTWwd1bUvghajz42Cr5FSFWbQhYMW.jpg)



Moving on we checked on the okro to ensure that there were no infections that can hinder the growth and productivity of the okro. 
From flowering to the emergence of the first sets of okro fruits 



Everything looks great and flourishing here and this is most likely due to quality of soil and the seeds planted because I remember vividly well how another farmer who planted some okro in another location in some not too distant time away has witnessed this much loss. The growth of the okro was arrested when they were barely 6 weeks. Everything happened suddenly and the crops changed coloration became red and burnt before they finally withered off.


![1000224735.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/EoChBf8zEb585ALyQ5ZHhkBY1d5CCgQ8bruMN3TTWwd1bUvghajz42Cr5FSFWbQhYMW.jpg)



But the condition here is different and everything looks good so far.
We did check the other veggies all round the farm to ensure that the pesticides we have applied was working 


Remember that we spotted some infection spreading out among the veggies which we had chosen to apply some pesticide during the weekend.
It was quite a long working day at the farm yesterday and having gotten home, we only ate our meals and slept off. 


![1000224732.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/monica-ene/23ywmCcpAoJEYPDVTvmwWWoaPNuupGekXMREHnfA6PwuwLedz9hj1eQqd2zCfsETrLrE6.jpg)


Thank God for grace and health to witness a new day and to set out for the days work.

Typically the people I know are already old money or they make money through management consulting and construction consulting. None of it are online. For me, being the odd one out, they scorn at how little I make through my online endeavors haha. 

Currently living in East-Java but I live in different places too, as our family has a couple of locations across different cities and provinces. So, I move around quite a lot. 

I never feel jealous of their wealth but more so about the inability of them to understand that what they have is enough, for a living at least. Style is different matter. Since I am so close to them, sometimes when they spend so frivolously, I feel sad knowing I could use those money to expand a few business or two. 


Since I have dual realities of life, In another version of myself and life, we're poor enough to not have any comparison 😅 but all I can say is that I still feel grateful we have a roof above our head though it's barely holding it up together.

body.title: Actitudes al descubierto # 18. La diferencia entre ayudar y acostumbrarse . [ES/EN]
body.body:
---

**Serie:** Actitudes al descubierto  
**Capítulo 18**  
**Título:** La diferencia entre ayudar y acostumbrarse  

---

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfRoAn1G4w5GPbz2jF3d3yLaDTU7yGcHJB6zRCLnawktF/tieubaotruong_man_7197469_640.jpg)
Fuente [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/man-feeding-birds-portrait-7197469/)

---

Hola, comunidad. Hoy continúo con la serie llamada *“Actitudes al descubierto”*, donde me propongo observar y compartir pequeños fragmentos del comportamiento humano en situaciones cotidianas. La idea no es juzgar, sino explorar cómo nuestros gestos, decisiones y reacciones reflejan actitudes y emociones que a veces pasan desapercibidas.

Hace unos días salí, como tantas veces, a buscar algo para llevar a la casa. En Cuba, incluso algo tan simple como comprar algunos productos del agro puede convertirse en una pequeña rutina diaria llena de recorridos, colas y espera.

Pasé por una placita de esas que todavía muchos seguimos llamando “estatales”, aunque hace tiempo funcionan mezclando productos de campesinos y vendedores que logran abastecerlas de diferentes maneras.

Había cola.

Nada fuera de lo normal.

Me quedé esperando y observando el movimiento de las personas, algo que suelo hacer bastante. Después de unos minutos vi a un señor mayor terminar sus compras. No lo conocía, pero inmediatamente noté que algo no estaba bien.

El hombre parecía perder estabilidad de repente.

No era exactamente una caída. Era como si el cuerpo dejara de responderle por unos segundos. Apenas podía caminar ni doblar bien las rodillas. Se quedó inmóvil, visiblemente desorientado.

Y entonces ocurrió algo interesante.

Un hombre que estaba más cerca reaccionó enseguida y pidió una silla que el placero tenía dentro del local. Otro ayudó a acercarla. Varias personas hicieron espacio alrededor. Entre todos lograron sentar al señor mientras intentaba recuperarse.

Nadie preguntó demasiado.

Simplemente ayudaron.

Durante unos minutos el lugar entero pareció detenerse alrededor de aquel desconocido.

Pero mientras eso ocurría, el placero comenzó a protestar.

Decía que aquella situación pasaba frecuentemente. Que el señor siempre venía solo, compraba y después le daban esos mareos. Hablaba con una mezcla de molestia y cansancio, como quien ya perdió sensibilidad ante algo que se repite demasiado.

Y aunque puedo entender que quizás para él aquello forme parte de una rutina incómoda, hubo algo en ese contraste que me hizo pensar bastante.

Mientras unas personas reaccionaban viendo a un ser humano vulnerable delante de ellas, otra parecía ver solamente un problema repetido.

Tal vez ahí está una de las cosas más peligrosas de la costumbre.

Cuando algo ocurre demasiadas veces, corremos el riesgo de dejar de mirar el sufrimiento que todavía existe dentro de esa escena.

Porque para quien observa todos los días, puede ser “el señor que siempre se marea”.

Pero para ese hombre, probablemente cada salida sigue siendo una batalla distinta.

Y según escuché después, vive solo.

No tiene a nadie que haga las compras por él.

No tiene otra opción.

Si no sale a buscar sus cosas, probablemente nadie lo hará.

Y entonces entendí algo que me dejó pensando el resto del día.

La empatía muchas veces aparece precisamente en quienes no tienen obligación de ayudar.

Porque ninguno de los que se acercó conocía realmente a aquel hombre. Nadie parecía esperar agradecimiento. No existía beneficio alguno en detenerse.

Simplemente reaccionaron al ver a alguien necesitando apoyo.

A veces creemos que la sensibilidad humana desaparece por completo entre tantos problemas cotidianos, cansancio y dificultades. Pero escenas pequeñas como esa recuerdan que todavía existen personas capaces de detenerse unos minutos por un desconocido.

Y quizá ahí es donde realmente se descubren las actitudes.

No en los grandes discursos.

Sino en esos instantes breves donde nadie sabe que está siendo observado.

---

En los próximos capítulos de *Actitudes al descubierto* continuaré compartiendo pequeñas escenas cotidianas donde las acciones más simples terminan revelando mucho más de lo que aparentan.

---

## English Version

---

**Series:** Attitudes Uncovered  
**Chapter 18**  
**Title:** The Difference Between Helping and Becoming Used to It  

---

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfRoAn1G4w5GPbz2jF3d3yLaDTU7yGcHJB6zRCLnawktF/tieubaotruong_man_7197469_640.jpg)
Source [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/photos/man-feeding-birds-portrait-7197469/)

---

Hello community. Today I continue with the series *“Attitudes Uncovered”*, where I observe and share small fragments of human behavior in everyday situations. The idea is not to judge, but to explore how our gestures, decisions, and reactions reflect attitudes and emotions that often go unnoticed.

A few days ago, I went out, as I often do, looking for something to bring home. In Cuba, even something as simple as buying agricultural products can become a daily routine filled with walking, waiting, and long lines.

I passed by one of those small markets that many people still call “state markets,” although nowadays they work through a mix of farmers and independent suppliers.

There was a line.

Nothing unusual.

I stayed there waiting and observing people moving around, something I tend to do often. After a few minutes, I saw an elderly man finish buying his groceries. I didn’t know him, but I immediately noticed something was wrong.

The man suddenly seemed to lose stability.

It wasn’t exactly a fall. It was more like his body stopped responding properly for a few moments. He could barely walk or bend his knees. He remained still, visibly disoriented.

And then something interesting happened.

A man standing nearby reacted immediately and asked for a chair that the market worker had inside the stand. Another person helped bring it over. Several people made space around the man. Together, they managed to sit him down while he tried to recover.

Nobody asked too many questions.

They simply helped.

For a few minutes, the entire place seemed to pause around that stranger.

But while all of this was happening, the market worker started complaining.

He said this situation happened frequently. That the elderly man always came alone, bought his things, and then got dizzy afterward. He spoke with a mixture of annoyance and exhaustion, like someone who had already lost sensitivity toward something repeated too many times.

And although I can understand that perhaps, for him, this had become part of an uncomfortable routine, there was something about that contrast that stayed in my mind.

While some people reacted by seeing a vulnerable human being in front of them, another person seemed to see only a repeated inconvenience.

Maybe that is one of the most dangerous things about routine.

When something happens too often, we risk stopping seeing the suffering that still exists inside the situation.

Because for someone watching it every day, he may simply become “the old man who always gets dizzy.”

But for that man, every trip outside is probably still a different battle.

And as I later heard, he lives alone.

There is nobody else to shop for him.

He has no other option.

If he does not go out to get his necessities, probably nobody will do it for him.

And then I understood something that stayed with me for the rest of the day.

Empathy often appears precisely in those who have no obligation to help.

Because none of the people who approached really knew that man. Nobody seemed to expect gratitude. There was no benefit in stopping.

They simply reacted after seeing someone who needed support.

Sometimes we believe human sensitivity has completely disappeared among so many daily problems, exhaustion, and difficulties. But small scenes like that remind us that there are still people capable of stopping for a few minutes to help a stranger.

And maybe that is where attitudes truly reveal themselves.

Not in big speeches.

But in those brief moments when nobody knows they are being observed.

---

In the next chapters of *Attitudes Uncovered*, I will continue sharing small everyday scenes where the simplest actions end up revealing much more than they seem to.

---

Thank you for reading.  
Special thanks to @bradleyarrow for supporting the community.

---

body.title: Interview with @CMON777, a player of “Guardians Of Glory” on Splinterlands [ES-EN]
body.body:
> This time, the post I’m sharing with you is completely different from what I usually post. I typically share insights about various aspects of the game, whether it’s gameplay or, more recently, the economy, but I also want to share a different kind of learning experience—and what better way than to “interview” the game’s most successful players, those with a track record of genuine experience who are, of course, willing to share with the community what they do—not just to have fun and play, but to make money while doing so. To that end, I’ve put together an “Interview” consisting of 10 very simple and general questions, but which can address many of the questions the community has, especially new users. So, if you’re just starting out in the game and have some questions that even I might not be able to fully explain through my tutorials—since there are many players who are better than me and have more experience—the idea is precisely for these types of players to share some insights about themselves and the game in general. > **The first interview is with the player whose username is @cmon777 from the guild “Guardians Of Glory,” whom I thanked for kindly agreeing to answer these questions. It’s also worth noting that these questions and answers will be in written form because my native language is Spanish, and although I have some command of written English, I don’t speak it. That’s why I’m using this format, but I would like it to be more like a “podcast” in the future.** **In the meantime, I hope you all find this content useful.** ![Separador.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lenonmc21/23u5taptEapzzNue7bMpgSFfTdVR9QsYdtt6rtQonQ5t8iCj5Bh3Xxf1yBs5u9aNdxzNy.png)
# Introduction by @cmon777
https://i.imgur.com/7u1AW7Q.png

> ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lenonmc21/23xAM9dE1gKF4WWiyyyS1ACpzm5bcjDiVdkq9U7jGcdg7vaWcT8LzRa9MLwf7pKJcJYdy.png) Before I begin and share the questions I asked and the answers I received, I should properly introduce the interviewee—as the title suggests—but I want to provide a little more context for those who aren’t familiar with him. So this section will be a bit of a mix, but the post is still about @cmon777’s experience in Splinterlands: ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lenonmc21/23tmBC5eMQVv2S84hZLjyP31e3LJz1uiet9K4mUdp2Ezmp3ZkRUCzEWnJpCtPZDdhxnFS.png) ![IMAGE 1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lenonmc21/EoJy8sgrbtAnYNVemWo916RVDJQagTwCuk5KNSXSByek8huMPTbeLegyyjcQqsyvSPj.png) First of all, it belongs to one of the strongest guilds in the entire game, an offshoot of “Kings of Glory” called “Guardians of Glory,” which has consistently ranked first among all guilds but is currently in third place. As such, these guilds undoubtedly bring together the elite of the game’s current player base. Finally, he’s a player who focuses on “Golden Card” decks, competes in the most competitive league of all—“Diamond”—and, as part of a team, is responsible for playing “Fray Wild,” so yes, he’s a specialist in playing “Wild Format” cards.
https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saydie/23u5xiwFjL73RxLkcbQBjfTdCWek7tXcDgYZzrgJ8aztjQtJvKRBNn3RFJSyFMvd3Yb4t.png
# \

> 

**1.)** Before discovering Splinterlands, did you already have experience with traditional or digital collectible card games (TCG/CCG) like Magic: The Gathering, Yu-Gi-Oh!, or Hearthstone? If so, what skills from those games have helped you here?

> **R:**No

---

**2.)** How did Splinterlands come into your life, and what exactly drew you to it at first and made you decide to stick with it and invest your time (and, possibly, money) in this ecosystem?

>**R:** Although I don’t come from the world of traditional or digital card games—the kind you mentioned—I have a lot of experience with other card games and video games in general. I had a computer when I was a kid; my first computer was an Apple in the late ’80s, then an Amiga, and after that, all the Intel Pentium models as they came out. I’ve always played a lot and never stopped. The games I played a lot were Command & Conquer 1 and 2... and then Age of Empires came along. I was totally addicted to Age of Empires 2 and played it online at nearly the highest level from the late ’90s through the mid-2000s. 
>
>Meanwhile, my other hobby was sports. Mainly tennis, but also soccer and basketball. At my tennis club, we played a lot of card games... for money, too... and I always wanted to play for money, because when there’s money on the line, people try harder, and that’s what I want. When I compete against someone, I want to be sure they’re giving it their all, because if there’s no money involved, most people don’t try hard, and then it gets boring. In 2007, I discovered online poker and gave it a try… and I loved it and became really good at it. 
>
>I played that game for about 10 years at the micro-stakes tables almost every day for hours on end. When I lost my job, it was my only source of income for a while... so I always stuck to the micro-stakes levels, because I basically needed to make money every month just to get by. I played at up to nine tables at a time for years, and at some point, it started to get boring, so I finally quit.
>
>After that, I lived solely on welfare, and in 2022, I searched YouTube for “making money with video games” or something like that… and that’s when I discovered cryptocurrency video games. Splinterlands was one of the games that came up, but I didn’t have any capital to invest, so I searched for “cryptocurrency poker”… and found ICE Poker. I introduced myself on the ICE Poker Discord, showing off my poker career stats to prove I’m an expert at this, looking for someone to take me on as an apprentice. A minute later, someone sent me a message and made me a great offer. I accepted that offer and went back to playing poker, while still keeping an eye on Splinterlands. At some point, I started transferring funds from my poker winnings to Splinterlands.
>
>And at some point, my poker winnings were so low that I stopped playing and focused solely on Splinterlands. I found Splinterlands particularly interesting because it’s a strategy game—that’s the kind of game I like—and also because it has a marketplace. And if it were just a card game like Hearthstone or MTG, I wouldn’t have been interested... it was the trading aspect and also the fact that you play for money. That’s how I got into Splinterlands and used my initial capital to buy cards on the market and try to sell them for more... basically, reselling cards... and also playing manually with a rented deck. It worked really well.
>
>I think I was a little lucky not to have discovered Splinterlands at its peak, like most people. The cards had already dropped significantly in value, and I knew I was getting in on a downward trend.

---

**3.)** Splinterlands stands out for its rules and mana mechanics. For a player at your level, what do you consider to be the most critical factor—or the most common mistake people make—when devising a strategy in a matter of seconds under very restrictive conditions?

> **R:** Maybe I don't take the time I need to fully understand the set of rules. I try to analyze the set of rules first and see which cards I have to complement it, before deciding which element to choose.

---

**4.)** If you had to choose a single card or summoner spell that perfectly defines your playstyle, or that you consider absolutely essential in the current meta, which one would it be and why?

> **R:** I don't play Modern, and I'm not up to date with the meta... Right now, I'm just managing my accounts and playing Brawls. Kelya and Quix are the ones I use the most.

---

**5.)** You've seen how the game has gone through different phases, from the classic editions (Alpha/Beta/Untamed) to the dynamics of Rebellion. What mechanical or economic change has forced you to reinvent your playstyle the most?

> **R:** No

---

**6.)** Staying competitive at the highest levels requires smart management. How do you currently manage your collection in terms of purchases, rentals, or delegations to maximize your daily and seasonal rewards?

> **R:** For rent only

---

**7.)** In all honesty, how would you assess the current balance in the game between entertainment value and financial incentives? Do you think the game is still fun in and of itself?

> **R:** It depends on what the game means to you... As for the auto-battle mode itself, while I think it's pretty good... there are games I prefer to play manually. I like managing my accounts and making money from them, too.

---

**8.)** If you had the power to modify or completely redesign a single game mechanic or economic system (whether it be the ranking system, how nodes work, the SPS, or the lands), which one would you choose, and what would you do with it?

> **R:** The economy... the fundamentals are very strong, but there are some things that really need to change. Not for my sake, but for the common good.

---

**9.)** What are your thoughts on the direction the development team is taking with the latest updates, and where do you think Splinterlands is headed in the medium and long term?

> **R:** It's not great, but it's not a hopeless situation either. If I had to explain it in more detail, it would take me a while... maybe later. This isn't the advice I want to give, but the advice I should give to new players so they don't ruin themselves... and I wish it were different

---

**10.)** For someone who just started playing today and might feel overwhelmed by the sheer number of cards, abilities, and the learning curve, what’s the most valuable piece of advice or starting strategy you’d give them to help them get by?

> **R:** It’s still possible to play Splinterlands and make money while doing so, with no risk, if you know how. I’m the only one who can give you good advice on this game... So the only good advice I can give you is to contact me before doing anything in the game. Otherwise, you WON’T succeed as a new player (or as a veteran).
>
>If you don't want to talk to me but still want to make money from this... without buying or renting anything (because you need to know exactly what to do)... you can make money for free without buying or renting cards by playing the battles (the team has also recently created a new building called \

so now you don't even need cards or spend money renting them... you just have to grab them from the library and win in the free duels, because others will pay). You can also play Frontier and earn cards you can use in Modern... earn a little without any investment. It won’t be much, but it’s a guaranteed profit with no investment... but if you want to earn a little more, etc.… you need me to guide you.
![Separador.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lenonmc21/23u5taptEapzzNue7bMpgSFfTdVR9QsYdtt6rtQonQ5t8iCj5Bh3Xxf1yBs5u9aNdxzNy.png)
# Final Thoughts https://i.imgur.com/a2tHTPH.png

> I hope you enjoyed this post. It was a pleasure to learn about @cmon777’s experience. As you can see, he’s a highly competitive player who’s focused on the game and maximizing his rewards—a player who rents out his gear and manages it flawlessly to make it all work. I hope to see in the comments what you think of this kind of initiative. If you’d like me to interview more players, I think it’s a great idea—you get to learn from the experts who know the game inside out, which is something new users definitely need. If you have any questions, feel free to comment on this post, and I’ll be happy to answer them.

Ademas cabe resaltar que estas preguntas y sus respuestas estarán escritas, debido a que, mi idioma nativo es el español y aunque manejo de cierta forma el Ingles escrito, no lo hablo, es por eso que uso este formato, pero, sí que me gustaría que fuera como una especie de “Podcast”, el cual puede ser más adelante.** **Mientras, espero que este contenido sea de utilidad para todos.** ![Separador.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lenonmc21/23u5taptEapzzNue7bMpgSFfTdVR9QsYdtt6rtQonQ5t8iCj5Bh3Xxf1yBs5u9aNdxzNy.png)
# Presentación de @cmon777
https://i.imgur.com/7u1AW7Q.png

> ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lenonmc21/23xAM9dE1gKF4WWiyyyS1ACpzm5bcjDiVdkq9U7jGcdg7vaWcT8LzRa9MLwf7pKJcJYdy.png) Antes de comenzar y colocar las preguntas que le hice y las respuestas que medio, debo presentar al entrevistado adecuadamente, ya que el titulo lo dice, pero, quiero darles un poco mas de contexto para el que no lo sepa. Así que esta sección será algo hibrida, pero, igual el post trata sobre la experiencia de @cmon777 en Splinterlands: ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lenonmc21/23tmBC5eMQVv2S84hZLjyP31e3LJz1uiet9K4mUdp2Ezmp3ZkRUCzEWnJpCtPZDdhxnFS.png) ![IMAGE 1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lenonmc21/EoJy8sgrbtAnYNVemWo916RVDJQagTwCuk5KNSXSByek8huMPTbeLegyyjcQqsyvSPj.png) Lo primero es que pertenece a uno de los “Gremios” mas fuertes de todo el juego, el cual es una extensión de “Kings Of Glory” llamado “Guardians Of Glory”, el cual ha estado en el primer lugar de todos los gremios, pero que justo ahora es el tercero, por lo que, estos gremios sin duda concentran la elite de los jugadores actuales del juego. Por último, es un jugador enfocado en cartas de “Lamina Dorada”, juega en la liga mas competitiva de todas que es “Diamante” y en equipo se encarga de jugar el “Fray Wild”, por lo que sí, es un especialista en jugar con cartas del “Formato Salvaje”.
https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saydie/23u5xiwFjL73RxLkcbQBjfTdCWek7tXcDgYZzrgJ8aztjQtJvKRBNn3RFJSyFMvd3Yb4t.png
# ¿Entrevista “Preguntas y Respuestas? https://i.imgur.com/a2tHTPH.png

> **1.)** Antes de descubrir Splinterlands, ¿ya tenías experiencia con juegos de cartas coleccionables tradicionales o digitales (TCG/CCG) como Magic: The Gathering, Yu-Gi-Oh! o Hearthstone? Si es así, ¿qué habilidades de esos juegos te han ayudado aquí? > **R:**No --- **2.)** ¿Cómo llegó Splinterlands a tu vida y qué fue exactamente lo que te atrajo al principio y te hizo decidir quedarte y dedicar tiempo (y, posiblemente, capital) a este ecosistema? >**R:** Aunque no provengo del ámbito de los juegos de cartas tradicionales o digitales, del tipo de juegos que has mencionado... tengo mucha experiencia en otros juegos de cartas y en los videojuegos en general. Ya tenía un ordenador de pequeño; mi primer ordenador fue un Apple a finales de los 80, luego un Amiga y, después, todos los Intel Pentium cuando salieron al mercado. Siempre he jugado mucho y nunca he dejado de hacerlo. Los juegos a los que jugaba mucho eran Command & Conquer 1 y 2... y luego llegó Age of Empires. Era totalmente adicto a Age of Empires 2 y lo jugué online casi al máximo nivel desde finales de los 90 hasta mediados de la década de 2000. > >Mientras tanto, mi otra afición eran los deportes. Principalmente el tenis, pero también el fútbol y el baloncesto. En mi club de tenis jugábamos mucho a los juegos de cartas... también por dinero... y siempre quise jugar por dinero, porque cuando hay dinero en juego la gente se esfuerza más y eso es lo que yo quiero. Cuando compito con alguien, quiero estar seguro de que se esfuerza al máximo, porque si no es por dinero la mayoría de la gente no se esfuerza y entonces se vuelve aburrido. En 2007 descubrí el póquer online y lo probé... y me encantó y me volví muy bueno en ello. > >Jugué a eso durante unos 10 años en las mesas de microapuestas casi todos los días durante horas. Cuando perdí mi trabajo, fue mi única fuente de ingresos durante un tiempo... así que siempre me quedé en los niveles de microapuestas, porque básicamente necesitaba cobrar cada mes para sobrevivir. Estuve jugando hasta en 9 mesas a la vez durante años y, en algún momento, empezó a aburrirme y finalmente lo dejé. > >Después de eso, viví solo de la ayuda social y, en 2022, busqué en YouTube «ganar dinero con los videojuegos» o algo así... y entonces descubrí los videojuegos con criptomonedas. Splinterlands fue uno de los juegos que apareció, pero no tenía capital para invertir, así que busqué «póquer con criptomonedas»... y encontré ICE Poker. Me presenté en el Discord de ICE Poker mostrando mis gráficos de mi carrera en el póquer para demostrar que soy un experto en esto, buscando a alguien que me aceptara como su aprendiz. Un minuto después, alguien me envió un mensaje y me hizo una gran oferta. Acepté esa oferta y volví a jugar al póquer, sin dejar de estar pendiente de Splinterlands. En algún momento empecé a transferir fondos de mis ganancias del póquer a Splinterlands. > >Y en algún momento, los beneficios del póquer eran tan bajos que dejé de jugar y me centré solo en Splinterlands.Splinterlands me resultaba especialmente interesante, porque es un juego de estrategia... ese es el tipo de juegos que me gustan y también porque tiene un mercado.Y si solo fuera un juego de cartas como Hearthstone o MTG, no me habría interesado... fue el aspecto del intercambio y también que se juega por dinero. Así es como me metí en Splinterlands y utilicé mi capital inicial para comprar cartas en el mercado e intentar venderlas por más... básicamente, revender cartas... y también jugando manualmente con un mazo alquilado. Funcionó muy bien. > >Creo que tuve un poco de suerte de no descubrir Splinterlands en su momento álgido, como la mayoría de la gente. Las cartas ya habían bajado mucho de valor y sabía que me estaba metiendo en una tendencia a la baja. --- **3.)** Splinterlands destaca por sus reglas y su mecánica de maná. Para un jugador de tu nivel, ¿cuál consideras que es el factor más crítico o el error más común que comete la gente al elaborar una estrategia en cuestión de segundos bajo condiciones muy restrictivas? > **R:** Quizás no me tomo el tiempo necesario para comprender bien el conjunto de reglas. Intento analizar primero el conjunto de reglas y qué cartas tengo para complementarlo, antes de decidir qué elemento elijo. --- **4.)** Si tuvieras que elegir una sola carta o invocador que definiera por completo tu estilo de juego, o que consideraras absolutamente indispensable en el meta actual, ¿cuál sería y por qué? > **R:** No juego en Modern y no estoy al día con el meta... Ahora mismo me dedico a gestionar mis cuentas y a jugar a Brawls. Kelya y Quix son los que más uso. --- **5.)** Has visto cómo el juego ha pasado por diferentes etapas, desde las ediciones clásicas (Alpha/Beta/Untamed) hasta la dinámica de Rebellion. ¿Cuál ha sido el cambio mecánico o económico que más te ha obligado a reinventar tu estilo de juego? > **R:** No --- **6.)** Mantenerse competitivo en los niveles altos requiere una gestión inteligente. ¿Cómo gestionas actualmente tu colección en términos de compras, alquileres o delegaciones para optimizar tus recompensas diarias y de temporada? > **R:** Solo alquilo --- **7.)** Con toda sinceridad, ¿cómo evalúas el equilibrio actual del juego entre el valor de entretenimiento y los incentivos económicos? ¿Crees que el juego sigue siendo divertido en sí mismo? > **R:** Depende de lo que signifique el juego para ti... En cuanto al modo de combate automático en sí, aunque creo que está bastante bien... hay juegos que prefiero jugar manualmente. Me gusta gestionar mis cuentas y también ganar dinero con ello. --- **8.)** Si tuvieras el poder de modificar o rediseñar por completo una única mecánica de juego o sistema económico (ya sea el sistema de clasificación, el funcionamiento de los nodos, el SPS o las tierras), ¿cuál elegirías y qué harías con ella? > **R:** La economía... los cimientos son muy buenos, pero hay algunas cosas que realmente hay que cambiar. No por mí, sino por el bien común. --- **9.)** ¿Cuál es tu opinión sobre la dirección que está tomando el equipo de desarrollo con las últimas actualizaciones, y hacia dónde crees que se dirige Splinterlands a medio y largo plazo? > **R:** No está bien, pero tampoco es una situación desesperada. Si tuviera que explicarlo con más detalle, me llevaría un rato... quizá más tarde. Este no es el consejo que quiero dar, sino el consejo que debería dar a los nuevos jugadores para que no se arruinen... y ojalá fuera diferente --- **10.)** Para alguien que acaba de empezar hoy y que podría sentirse abrumado por la gran cantidad de cartas, habilidades y la curva de aprendizaje, ¿cuál es el consejo más valioso o la estrategia inicial que le darías para ayudarle a sobrevivir? > **R:** Todavía es posible jugar a Splinterlands y ganar dinero mientras lo haces, sin ningún riesgo, si sabes cómo. El único que puede darte buenos consejos en este juego soy yo... Así que el único buen consejo que puedo darte es que te pongas en contacto conmigo antes de hacer nada en el juego. De lo contrario, NO tendrás éxito como jugador nuevo (ni como veterano). > >Si no quieres hablar conmigo y aun así quieres ganar dinero con esto... sin comprar ni alquilar nada (porque necesitas saber exactamente qué hacer)... puedes ganar dinero gratis sin comprar ni alquilar cartas jugando a las peleas (el equipo también ha creado recientemente un nuevo edificio llamado «la biblioteca», así que ahora ni siquiera necesitas cartas ni gastar dinero en alquilarlas... solo tienes que cogerlas de la biblioteca y ganar en las peleas gratis, porque otros pagarán). También puedes jugar a Frontier y ganar cartas que puedes usar en Modern... gana un poco sin ninguna inversión.
